domains.name: discovery
domains.description: Owns all data generated during drug discovery and target identification, including high-throughput screening (HTS) results, structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis, mechanism of action (MOA) studies, hit-to-lead progression, molecular targets, and early-stage compound optimization under GLP. Manages research data from electronic lab notebooks (ELN) in IDBS/Dotmatics, assay results, and compound libraries. Authoritative source for NCE (New Chemical Entity) and NBE (New Biological Entity) research data entering the development pipeline.
domains.references: ICH Q8 Pharmaceutical Development / GLP (21 CFR Part 58)

tables.name: molecular_target
tables.description: Master record for biological molecular targets identified during drug discovery, including proteins, enzymes, receptors, ion channels, and nucleic acids. Captures target class, gene name, UniProt/Ensembl identifiers, mechanism of action (MOA), therapeutic area relevance, target validation status, druggability assessment, and disease association. Authoritative SSOT for all target identification data entering the discovery pipeline from IDBS/Dotmatics ELN.

columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the molecular target record in the discovery data product. Primary key for all downstream joins and lineage tracking.
columns.reference: Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer — Internal PK Convention

columns.name: owning_org_unit_id

columns.name: patent_family_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_family. Business justification: Target-level IP strategy is managed at the patent family level for global coverage assessment. IP portfolio reports group target protection by family. molecular_target already links to a single patent

columns.name: patent_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: Molecular targets are patented inventions requiring patent protection tracking for freedom-to-operate analysis, portfolio management, and competitive intelligence in target selection decisions.

columns.name: primary_patent_claim_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_claim. Business justification: Specific patent claims cover target modulation methods; claim-level tracking required for FTO clearance, licensing negotiations, and assessing blocking IP in target validation stage gates.

columns.name: therapeutic_area_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.therapeutic_area. Business justification: Molecular targets are classified and prioritized within therapeutic area programs. Linking to the master therapeutic_area entity enables TA-level target portfolio reporting, competitive landscape anal

columns.name: competitive_landscape_summary
columns.description: Summary of known competitive programs targeting this molecular target, including approved drugs, clinical-stage compounds, and disclosed research programs from competitor organizations. Business-confidential intelligence used for portfolio strategy.
columns.reference: Internal Competitive Intelligence; FDA Orange Book; ClinicalTrials.gov

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this molecular target record was first created in the discovery data product. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); Databricks Lakehouse Audit

columns.name: discovery_program_code
columns.description: Internal program or project code under which this target is being investigated. Links the target to the broader drug discovery program for portfolio management, resource allocation, and P&L tracking.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA CO (Controlling / Project System); Internal Portfolio Management

columns.name: disease_association
columns.description: Specific disease or condition(s) associated with this molecular target, as supported by published literature or internal research data. May reference ICD-10/ICD-11 disease codes or MeSH disease terms.
columns.reference: WHO ICD-11; MeSH Disease Ontology; Open Targets Platform; DisGeNET

columns.name: druggability_assessment
columns.description: Scientific assessment of the target's amenability to small molecule or biologic modulation based on structural, biochemical, and computational analyses. Key input to portfolio prioritization and NCE/NBE strategy decisions.
columns.reference: ISPE Drug Discovery Guidelines; Hopkins & Groom Druggability Framework (Nature Reviews Drug Discovery)

columns.name: eln_notebook_reference
columns.description: Reference identifier to the primary Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) experiment record in IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics that documents the original target identification and characterization data. Provides full scientific audit trail.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; GLP (21 CFR Part 58); 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records)

columns.name: ensembl_gene_code
columns.description: Ensembl stable gene identifier (e.g., ENSG00000146648) for the gene encoding the molecular target. Used for genomic cross-referencing, variant analysis, and bioinformatics pipelines.
columns.reference: Ensembl Genome Browser (EMBL-EBI); ICH E15 Pharmacogenomics Definitions

columns.name: expression_tissue
columns.description: Primary tissue(s) or cell type(s) where this molecular target is expressed at therapeutically relevant levels, as determined by transcriptomic or proteomic profiling (e.g., liver, lung epithelium, T-cells). Informs tissue selectivity and delivery strategy.
columns.reference: Human Protein Atlas; GTEx; FANTOM5; ICH S6 Preclinical Safety for Biologics

columns.name: first_disclosed_date
columns.description: Date on which this molecular target was first formally disclosed or documented in the internal ELN or target identification database. Establishes the scientific priority date for IP purposes.
columns.reference: USPTO Patent Priority Date Rules; EPC Article 54 (Novelty); IDBS/Dotmatics ELN

columns.name: gene_name
columns.description: Official HGNC (HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee) approved gene symbol encoding the molecular target (e.g., EGFR, TP53, BRCA1). Standard identifier used in regulatory submissions and scientific publications.
columns.reference: HGNC — HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee; FDA Pharmacogenomics Guidance

columns.name: genetic_association_score
columns.description: Quantitative score (0.0000–1.0000) representing the strength of genetic evidence linking this target to the associated disease, derived from GWAS, Mendelian randomization, or Open Targets Platform data. Higher scores indicate stronger genetic validation.
columns.reference: Open Targets Platform; GWAS Catalog (EMBL-EBI); ICH E15 Pharmacogenomics

columns.name: last_reviewed_date
columns.description: Date of the most recent scientific or portfolio review of this target record. Ensures data currency and supports periodic target triage processes.
columns.reference: Internal Target Review SOP; GLP (21 CFR Part 58) Data Integrity Requirements

columns.name: moa_description
columns.description: Narrative description of the molecular mechanism by which modulation of this target is expected to produce a therapeutic effect. Captures agonism, antagonism, inhibition, activation, or allosteric modulation details as documented in ELN.
columns.reference: ICH E8 General Considerations for Clinical Studies; FDA Pharmacology Review Guidance

columns.name: moa_type
columns.description: Categorical classification of the pharmacological mechanism of action for compounds acting on this target. Used to group targets by intervention strategy in SAR analysis and portfolio reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: agonist|antagonist|inhibitor|activator|allosteric_modulator|degrader|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology MOA Classification; ICH E8

columns.name: modality
columns.description: Preferred drug modality for targeting this molecular target based on its structural and biochemical properties. Determines the NCE (New Chemical Entity) or NBE (New Biological Entity) classification of resulting compounds. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: small_molecule|biologic|antibody|peptide|oligonucleotide|cell_therapy|gene_therapy|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: FDA CDER/CBER Modality Classification; ICH Q6A/Q6B; EMA Biologics Guidelines

columns.name: novelty_status
columns.description: Classification of the target's novelty relative to the competitive landscape. Novel targets represent first-in-class opportunities; established targets have existing approved drugs; repurposed targets are being explored in new indications.
columns.reference: FDA Innovation and Drug Discovery Guidance; IP Strategy — Patent Filing (21 CFR Part 314)

columns.name: organism
columns.description: Biological organism in which the molecular target is expressed and studied. Typically Homo sapiens for human targets, but may include model organisms used in preclinical validation studies.
columns.reference: NCBI Taxonomy Database; ICH S5 Reproductive Toxicology; GLP Guidelines (21 CFR Part 58)

columns.name: patent_landscape_summary
columns.description: High-level summary of the patent landscape around this molecular target, including freedom-to-operate (FTO) considerations and known composition-of-matter or method-of-use patents. Supports IP strategy decisions.
columns.reference: USPTO; EPO; ICH Q11; 21 CFR Part 314 (NDA IP Certification)

columns.name: pathway_name
columns.description: Name of the primary biological signaling or metabolic pathway in which this target participates (e.g., PI3K/AKT/mTOR, RAS/MAPK, JAK/STAT). Supports pathway-based target clustering and polypharmacology analysis.
columns.reference: KEGG Pathway Database; Reactome Pathway Knowledgebase; WikiPathways

columns.name: pdb_code
columns.description: RCSB Protein Data Bank accession code for the primary 3D structure of this molecular target. Used by computational chemistry and structure-based drug design (SBDD) teams for molecular docking and virtual screening.
columns.reference: RCSB Protein Data Bank (PDB); wwPDB Guidelines

columns.name: prioritization_tier
columns.description: Portfolio prioritization tier assigned to this target by the Target Selection Committee, reflecting strategic importance, scientific confidence, and commercial potential. Tier 1 targets receive maximum resource allocation.
columns.reference: Internal Portfolio Review Process; ICH E8 General Considerations for Clinical Studies

columns.name: protein_structure_available
columns.description: Indicates whether a resolved 3D protein structure (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM, or NMR) is available for this target in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) or internal structural biology repository. Directly impacts structure-based drug design (SBDD) feasibility.
columns.reference: RCSB Protein Data Bank (PDB); ISPE Drug Discovery Guidelines

columns.name: safety_concern_description
columns.description: Narrative description of identified safety liabilities associated with modulation of this target (e.g., hERG channel activity, hepatotoxicity risk, immunosuppression). Populated only when safety_concern_flag is True.
columns.reference: ICH S7A/S7B; FDA Safety Pharmacology Guidance; EMA Preclinical Safety Guidelines

columns.name: safety_concern_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether known safety liabilities or toxicological concerns have been identified for this target based on literature, genetic association studies, or internal preclinical data. Triggers mandatory safety review before progression.
columns.reference: ICH S7A/S7B Safety Pharmacology; FDA Preclinical Safety Evaluation Guidance; GLP (21 CFR Part 58)

columns.name: selectivity_profile
columns.description: Assessment of the target's selectivity relative to related family members or off-target proteins. Informs compound design strategy to minimize off-target toxicity and maximize therapeutic index.
columns.reference: ICH S7A Safety Pharmacology Studies; FDA Pharmacology/Toxicology Review Guidance

columns.name: target_class
columns.description: Pharmacological class of the molecular target based on its biochemical function and structural family. Drives druggability assessment strategy and compound screening cascade design. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: GPCR|kinase|nuclear_receptor|ion_channel|protease|phosphatase|epigenetic_regulator|transcription_factor|transporter|other — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology Target Classification; ChEMBL Target Classification

columns.name: target_code
columns.description: Internally assigned alphanumeric business identifier for the molecular target, used as the externally-known unique code across systems (ELN, LIMS, CTMS). Distinct from the surrogate PK and from external database accession numbers.
columns.reference: Internal Master Data Management (MDM) Standard; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN

columns.name: target_engagement_assay
columns.description: Name or identifier of the primary biochemical or biophysical assay used to measure compound engagement with this target (e.g., HTRF binding assay, SPR, ITC, NanoBRET). Registered in LIMS (LabWare/SampleManager) and ELN.
columns.reference: LIMS — LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; GLP (21 CFR Part 58); IDBS/Dotmatics ELN

columns.name: target_name
columns.description: Human-readable scientific name of the molecular target (e.g., EGFR, BRAF, PD-L1, CDK4/6). Serves as the primary identity label used by research scientists and in ELN records within IDBS/Dotmatics.
columns.reference: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology; UniProt Protein Nomenclature Guidelines

columns.name: target_type
columns.description: Biological molecule type of the target (e.g., protein, enzyme, receptor, ion channel, nucleic acid). Determines the modality of drug intervention and screening assay design. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: protein|enzyme|receptor|ion_channel|nucleic_acid|lipid|carbohydrate|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology; ChEMBL Target Type Ontology

columns.name: uniprot_accession
columns.description: Universal Protein Resource (UniProt) accession number uniquely identifying the protein target in the global UniProtKB database. Enables cross-referencing with external biological databases and regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: UniProt Knowledgebase (UniProtKB); ICH M4 CTD Guidelines

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this molecular target record. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change detection, and audit trail maintenance per 21 CFR Part 11.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GDPR Article 5; Databricks Lakehouse Delta Lake

columns.name: validation_completion_date
columns.description: Date on which target validation studies were completed and the target was formally declared validated (in vitro or in vivo). Marks the transition from target identification to hit-to-lead progression stage.
columns.reference: ICH S7A/S7B; GLP (21 CFR Part 58); Internal Stage-Gate Process

columns.name: validation_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle stage of target validation, reflecting the level of scientific evidence supporting the target's role in disease. Drives go/no-go decisions for hit-to-lead progression. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: identified|hypothetical|validated_in_vitro|validated_in_vivo|clinically_validated|deprioritized — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH S7A/S7B Safety Pharmacology Guidelines; FDA Target Validation Guidance; IDBS/Dotmatics ELN Workflow

tables.name: compound
tables.description: Master record for all chemical and biological compounds in the discovery compound library, including NCEs (New Chemical Entities) and NBEs (New Biological Entities). Captures compound identity (IUPAC name, INN/USAN, registration number, CAS number), structural representation (molecular formula, molecular weight, SMILES, InChI), compound class (small molecule, biologic, peptide, ADC), source (synthesized, purchased, natural product), physicochemical properties (purity, physical state, storage conditions), and library membership. Authoritative SSOT for compound identity and structure across the discovery domain.

columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.therapeutic_area. Business justification: Compounds are classified by therapeutic area for portfolio management, IP strategy, and compound library organization. Linking to the master therapeutic_area entity enforces consistency across discove

columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.business_partner. Business justification: Vendor qualification and approved vendor list (AVL) compliance requires linking purchased/sourced compounds to their business partner record. 'vendor_name' is denormalized; the FK enables vendor audit

columns.name: cas_number
columns.description: Globally unique Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS) registry number assigned by the American Chemical Society to uniquely identify the chemical substance. Used for regulatory submissions, procurement, and cross-system compound lookup.
columns.reference: CAS Registry, ICH Q6A, FDA Substance Registration System (SRS)

columns.name: compound_class
columns.description: Broad classification of the compound by molecular modality. Drives regulatory pathway selection (NDA vs BLA), manufacturing strategy (chemical synthesis vs biologics), and analytical method requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: small_molecule|biologic|peptide|adc|oligonucleotide|cell_therapy|rna_therapy|gene_therapy — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH Q6A (small molecules), ICH Q6B (biologics), FDA CDER/CBER classification

columns.name: compound_name
columns.description: Internal working name or code name assigned to the compound during discovery (e.g., project code name such as 'ABC-1234'). Used as the primary human-readable label in ELN, LIMS, and CTMS systems before an INN or USAN is assigned.

columns.name: compound_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the compound within the discovery pipeline. 'Active' indicates the compound is under active research; 'promoted' indicates advancement to preclinical or clinical development; 'discontinued' indicates the compound has been deprioritized or terminated.
columns.reference: ICH Q8, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics, 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: controlled_substance_schedule
columns.description: U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) controlled substance schedule classification for the compound (Schedule I–V or not controlled). Determines handling, storage, procurement, and regulatory reporting requirements under the Controlled Substances Act.
columns.reference: DEA Controlled Substances Act (21 USC 812), 21 CFR Part 1308, DEA

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: System-generated timestamp recording when the compound record was first created in the data platform (Silver Layer). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH Q10, GDPR Article 5(2)

columns.name: discovery_stage
columns.description: Current stage of the compound within the drug discovery pipeline. Tracks progression from target identification through hit identification, hit-to-lead, lead optimization, and candidate selection before IND filing. Used for portfolio reporting and stage-gate decision making.
columns.reference: ICH Q8, ICH M3(R2), FDA IND Guidance 21 CFR Part 312, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: eln_reference_code
columns.description: Reference identifier linking this compound record to the originating experiment or notebook entry in the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Provides traceability from the compound master record back to the primary research data and synthesis records.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11, OECD GLP Principles, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: entity_type
columns.glossary_term: New Chemical Entity / New Biological Entity (NCE/NBE) Type
columns.description: Regulatory classification of the compound as a New Chemical Entity (NCE), New Biological Entity (NBE), biosimilar, fixed-dose combination, or prodrug. Determines regulatory exclusivity periods, patent strategy, and submission pathway under FDA, EMA, and ICH guidelines.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.108, EMA Guideline on NCE/NBE, ICH Q8

columns.name: glp_compliant
columns.description: Indicates whether the compound and its associated research data have been generated under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) conditions as required for regulatory submissions. GLP compliance is mandatory for safety pharmacology and toxicology studies supporting IND applications.
columns.reference: OECD Principles of GLP, 21 CFR Part 58, EMA GLP Directive 2004/10/EC

columns.name: hazard_classification
columns.description: Globally Harmonized System (GHS) hazard classification for the compound covering health, physical, and environmental hazards (e.g., 'Acute Toxicity Cat. 2, Carcinogen Cat. 1A'). Required for Safety Data Sheet (SDS) preparation, occupational health risk assessment, and EHS compliance.
columns.reference: GHS (UN Purple Book), OSHA HazCom 2012, REACH Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006, ICH Q3C

columns.name: hba_count
columns.description: Number of hydrogen bond acceptors (HBA) in the compound structure. Key Lipinski Rule of Five parameter (threshold: ≤ 10 HBAs) used in drug-likeness assessment and oral bioavailability prediction during hit-to-lead and lead optimization.
columns.reference: Lipinski Rule of Five, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines

columns.name: hbd_count
columns.description: Number of hydrogen bond donors (HBD) in the compound structure. Key Lipinski Rule of Five parameter (threshold: ≤ 5 HBDs) used in drug-likeness assessment and oral bioavailability prediction during hit-to-lead and lead optimization.
columns.reference: Lipinski Rule of Five, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines

columns.name: inchi
columns.description: IUPAC International Chemical Identifier (InChI) string providing a standardized, layered representation of the compound's chemical structure. Used for cross-system compound deduplication, registry lookups, and interoperability with external databases (PubChem, ChEMBL). Classified confidential as it encodes proprietary structural IP.
columns.reference: IUPAC InChI Trust, ICH Q6A, FDA SRS

columns.name: inchi_key
columns.description: Fixed-length 27-character hashed representation of the InChI string (InChIKey). Used as a compact, searchable identifier for compound lookup in external databases (PubChem, ChEMBL, CAS SciFinder) and for deduplication across compound registries.
columns.reference: IUPAC InChI Trust, FDA SRS, PubChem

columns.name: iupac_name
columns.glossary_term: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) Name
columns.description: Systematic chemical name of the compound following International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) nomenclature rules. Provides an unambiguous, internationally recognized chemical identity for regulatory submissions and scientific publications.
columns.reference: IUPAC 2013 Recommendations, ICH Q6A, FDA SRS

columns.name: last_reviewed_date
columns.description: Date on which the compound record was last reviewed by a qualified scientist or data steward for accuracy, completeness, and continued relevance in the discovery portfolio. Supports data governance and periodic compound library curation activities.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH Q10, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: library_membership
columns.description: Designation of the compound library or collection to which this compound belongs within the corporate compound library management system. Drives screening campaign design, compound availability, and resource allocation in HTS and fragment-based drug discovery programs.
columns.reference: ISPE GAMP 5, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics, LIMS - LabWare / SampleManager

columns.name: logp
columns.description: Logarithm of the octanol-water partition coefficient (LogP), a measure of the compound's lipophilicity. Critical SAR and ADME parameter used to predict membrane permeability, oral bioavailability, and CNS penetration. Lipinski Rule of Five threshold: LogP ≤ 5.
columns.reference: Lipinski Rule of Five, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: mechanism_of_action
columns.description: Described mechanism of action (MOA) of the compound — the biochemical interaction through which the compound produces its pharmacological effect (e.g., 'selective inhibitor of EGFR tyrosine kinase'). Critical for target validation, patent claims, and regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E8, FDA Pharmacology Review Guidance, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: molecular_formula
columns.description: Empirical molecular formula of the compound expressed using Hill notation (e.g., C21H30N2O5). Represents the elemental composition and is used in regulatory submissions, analytical method development, and structural verification.
columns.reference: IUPAC Hill System, ICH Q6A, FDA SRS

columns.name: molecular_weight
columns.description: Average molecular weight of the compound expressed in grams per mole (g/mol). Critical physicochemical property used in SAR analysis, ADME profiling, formulation development, and Lipinski Rule of Five drug-likeness assessment.
columns.reference: ICH Q6A, Lipinski Rule of Five, IUPAC

columns.name: physical_state
columns.description: Physical state of the compound at standard conditions (solid, liquid, gas, semi-solid). Determines handling procedures, formulation approach, and storage requirements. Captured in the ELN and LIMS at time of compound registration.
columns.reference: ICH Q6A, GMP 21 CFR Part 211, LIMS - LabWare / SampleManager

columns.name: purity_percent
columns.description: Measured chemical purity of the compound expressed as a percentage (0.00–100.00%). Determined by analytical methods such as HPLC or NMR. Critical quality attribute (CQA) for assay reliability, GLP compliance, and advancement decisions in hit-to-lead progression.
columns.reference: ICH Q6A, GLP (OECD Principles), 21 CFR Part 58, LIMS - LabWare / SampleManager

columns.name: registration_date
columns.description: Date on which the compound was formally registered in the corporate compound registry (IDBS/Dotmatics). Marks the official entry of the compound into the discovery compound library and initiates the compound lifecycle tracking.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11, OECD GLP Principles, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: registration_number
columns.description: Internally assigned unique registration number for the compound within the corporate compound registry (e.g., IDBS/Dotmatics compound registration system). Serves as the primary business identifier used across discovery, CMC, and regulatory workflows.
columns.reference: ICH Q6A, 21 CFR Part 312, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: rotatable_bond_count
columns.description: Number of rotatable bonds in the compound structure. Veber rule parameter (threshold: ≤ 10) used alongside TPSA to predict oral bioavailability and molecular flexibility in SAR and lead optimization analyses.
columns.reference: Veber Rules, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines

columns.name: smiles
columns.glossary_term: Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (SMILES) Notation
columns.description: Canonical SMILES (Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System) string representing the two-dimensional chemical structure of the compound. Used in cheminformatics, HTS data analysis, SAR modeling, and AI/ML-based drug discovery workflows. Classified confidential as it encodes proprietary structural IP.
columns.reference: Daylight SMILES Specification, ICH Q6A, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: solubility_aqueous_um
columns.description: Measured or predicted aqueous solubility of the compound expressed in micromolar (µM). Key ADME physicochemical property used in SAR analysis, formulation feasibility assessment, and drug-likeness profiling (Lipinski, Veber rules).
columns.reference: ICH Q6A, Lipinski Rule of Five, ADME Guidelines, LIMS

columns.name: source_type
columns.description: Origin classification of the compound indicating how it was obtained. Synthesized compounds are produced in-house; purchased compounds are acquired from external vendors or CROs; natural products are derived from biological sources. Impacts IP strategy and CMC documentation.
columns.reference: ICH Q11, FDA CMC Guidance, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: storage_condition
columns.description: Recommended storage conditions for the compound (e.g., '-20°C, under nitrogen, protected from light, desiccated'). Ensures compound stability and integrity in the compound library. Derived from stability data and referenced in CoA and compound library management SOPs.
columns.reference: ICH Q1A (Stability Testing), ICH Q6A, GMP 21 CFR Part 211.68, LIMS

columns.name: tpsa_angstrom2
columns.description: Topological Polar Surface Area (TPSA) of the compound expressed in square angstroms (Å²). Used to predict intestinal absorption, blood-brain barrier penetration, and oral bioavailability. Veber rule threshold: TPSA ≤ 140 Å² for oral drugs.
columns.reference: Veber Rules, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: System-generated timestamp recording when the compound record was last modified in the data platform. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and enables change detection for downstream data consumers and AI/ML pipelines.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH Q10, GDPR Article 5(2)

columns.name: usan
columns.description: United States Adopted Name (USAN) assigned by the USAN Council for the compound. Used in US regulatory submissions (NDA/BLA) and US commercial labeling. May differ slightly from INN.

columns.name: vendor_catalog_number
columns.description: Vendor-assigned catalog or product number for purchased compounds. Used for reorder, procurement traceability, and cross-referencing with vendor CoA and SDS documentation. Applicable only when source_type is 'purchased'.
columns.reference: ICH Q10, SAP S/4HANA MM Module, GMP 21 CFR Part 211

tables.name: assay
tables.description: Master record for biological and biochemical assays used in drug discovery screening and profiling. Captures assay name, assay type (biochemical, cell-based, phenotypic, ADME, toxicity), assay format (HTS, dose-response, selectivity), target association, assay technology platform (HTRF, AlphaScreen, SPR, NMR), assay validation status, GLP compliance flag, detection method, assay protocol reference, throughput capacity, and responsible scientist. Sourced from IDBS/Dotmatics ELN.

columns.name: assay_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the assay master record in the discovery domain. Primary key for the assay data product. Role classification: MASTER_RESOURCE.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN internal object model

columns.name: cost_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: Assay development and validation costs are tracked against cost centers for R&D budget reporting and financial controlling. Pharma finance teams require assay-level cost center assignment separate fro

columns.name: cro_business_partner_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.business_partner. Business justification: CRO vendor qualification and approved vendor list (AVL) management requires linking outsourced assays to their business partner record. 'cro_vendor_name' is a denormalized representation; the FK enabl

columns.name: licensing_agreement_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.licensing_agreement. Business justification: Assay technologies are frequently licensed from third parties (e.g., licensed cell lines, detection platforms, HTRF technology). The licensing agreement governs usage rights and royalty obligations. P

columns.name: molecular_target_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.molecular_target. Business justification: Assays are designed to screen against specific molecular targets. The assay table currently has target_name and target_class as denormalized STRING attributes. Adding molecular_target_id FK allows joi

columns.name: owning_org_unit_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.org_unit. Business justification: Assay ownership by org unit is required for GLP compliance scope assignment, budget allocation, and departmental capacity planning. 'owning_department' is a denormalized org unit reference that should

columns.name: patent_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: Proprietary assay methods are protected by method patents. IP teams track which patents cover which assays for licensing, FTO, and CRO outsourcing decisions. A pharma IP expert would expect assay-to-p

columns.name: therapeutic_area_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.therapeutic_area. Business justification: Assays are designed and maintained within therapeutic area programs. Linking to the master therapeutic_area entity enables TA-level assay resource allocation, capacity planning, and portfolio reportin

columns.name: assay_code
columns.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique code assigned to the assay within the ELN or LIMS (e.g., ASY-HTS0042). Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Used for cross-system referencing between IDBS/Dotmatics, LabWare LIMS, and SAP QM.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; LabWare LIMS; ICH Q2(R1)

columns.name: assay_name
columns.description: Full descriptive name of the assay as registered in the ELN (e.g., 'EGFR Kinase Inhibition HTRF Assay'). Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Used in scientific reports, regulatory submissions, and compound screening dashboards.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; ICH M10 (Bioanalytical Method Validation)

columns.name: assay_type
columns.description: Primary scientific classification of the assay based on its biological or chemical mode of measurement. Serves as the CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Drives downstream SAR analysis workflows and compound triage decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: biochemical|cell_based|phenotypic|ADME|toxicity|binding|functional — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH S7A/S7B (Safety Pharmacology); FDA Guidance on Drug Interaction Studies; IDBS Dotmatics assay taxonomy

columns.name: automation_compatible
columns.description: Indicates whether the assay has been adapted and validated for automated liquid handling platforms (e.g., Hamilton, Tecan, Beckman Coulter). Determines eligibility for inclusion in HTS screening campaigns and impacts throughput capacity planning.
columns.reference: ISPE GAMP 5; ANSI/SLAS Microplate Standards; IDBS E-WorkBook automation integration

columns.name: cell_line
columns.description: Name of the cell line used in cell-based assays (e.g., HEK293, HeLa, Jurkat, A549, MCF-7). Null for biochemical or cell-free assays. Required for assay reproducibility and cross-site comparability. Cell line authentication records are maintained in the ELN.
columns.reference: ATCC cell line standards; ISPE GAMP 5; ICH Q5D (Cell Substrates); LabWare LIMS biological material registry

columns.name: coefficient_of_variation_pct
columns.description: Percentage coefficient of variation (%CV) of the assay signal across replicate measurements, representing assay precision and reproducibility. Typically required to be ≤ 15% for HTS assays and ≤ 20% for bioanalytical assays per ICH Q2(R1). Stored from the assay validation run.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018

columns.name: concentration_unit
columns.description: Unit of measurement for compound concentrations used in the assay (e.g., nM, µM, mM). Standardizes concentration reporting across compound screening results and SAR analysis. Required for dose-response curve fitting and IC50/EC50 calculations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: nM|uM|mM|mg_mL|ug_mL|ng_mL|pM — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1); IUPAC nomenclature; LabWare LIMS unit registry

columns.name: cost_per_well_usd
columns.description: Estimated reagent and consumable cost per assay well in US dollars. Used for screening campaign cost modeling, budget planning, and make-vs-buy decisions for outsourcing to CROs. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA MM procurement data and lab supply records.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA CO (Cost Center Accounting); ICH Q10; ISPE Cost of Goods guidance

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the assay master record was first created in the ELN or data platform. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance and data lineage tracking.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); ICH Q10; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

columns.name: detection_method
columns.description: Physical or chemical detection principle used to measure the assay signal (e.g., fluorescence, luminescence, radioactivity, mass spectrometry). Distinct from technology_platform — platform is the instrument system, detection_method is the underlying measurement principle. Used for assay validation documentation and GLP compliance records. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fluorescence|luminescence|absorbance|radioactivity|mass_spectrometry|NMR|SPR|calorimetry — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance

columns.name: eln_notebook_reference
columns.description: Identifier of the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) experiment or notebook entry in IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics where the assay development and validation data are recorded. Provides direct traceability from the data product to the source scientific record.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP)

columns.name: first_used_date
columns.description: Date when the assay was first deployed for compound screening or profiling activities. Marks the operational start of the assay lifecycle. Used for assay age tracking, periodic revalidation scheduling, and portfolio lifecycle management.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook audit trail

columns.name: format
columns.description: Operational format describing how the assay is run in the screening workflow (e.g., High-Throughput Screening (HTS) primary screen, dose-response, selectivity panel). Determines throughput capacity planning and compound consumption requirements.
columns.reference: ISPE GAMP 5; IDBS E-WorkBook assay format taxonomy; ICH Q2(R1)

columns.name: glp_compliant
columns.description: Indicates whether the assay is conducted under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations as required for regulatory submissions (IND/NDA/BLA). GLP-compliant assays require full audit trails, validated equipment, and certified personnel. Critical for preclinical safety study data submitted to FDA/EMA.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); OECD Principles of GLP; EMA GLP Directive 2004/10/EC

columns.name: hit_threshold_unit
columns.description: Unit of measurement for the hit_threshold_value (e.g., percent inhibition, nM IC50). Ensures unambiguous interpretation of the hit-calling criterion across different assay types and readout formats.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH Q2(R1); IUPAC nomenclature

columns.name: hit_threshold_value
columns.description: Numerical threshold used to classify a compound as a 'hit' in primary screening (e.g., ≥ 50% inhibition at 10 µM). Defined during assay validation and used by automated hit-calling algorithms in the HTS data analysis pipeline. Critical for hit-to-lead progression decisions.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics hit-calling configuration; ICH Q2(R1); FDA HTS Guidance

columns.name: incubation_time_hours
columns.description: Standard incubation duration in hours for the assay reaction or cell treatment step. Critical for assay reproducibility and scheduling of automated liquid handling workflows. Stored from the validated assay protocol.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook protocol parameters; ISPE GAMP 5

columns.name: last_validated_date
columns.description: Date of the most recent formal validation or requalification of the assay per ICH Q2(R1) or fit-for-purpose qualification criteria. Used to trigger periodic revalidation workflows and to assess whether assay data is current for regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1); 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018

columns.name: lims_assay_code
columns.glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Assay ID
columns.description: Cross-reference identifier for this assay in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) — LabWare or Thermo Fisher SampleManager. Enables bidirectional traceability between the discovery data product and the LIMS assay execution records.
columns.reference: LabWare LIMS / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10

columns.name: multiplexed
columns.description: Indicates whether the assay measures multiple analytes or endpoints simultaneously in a single well or reaction (multiplexed assay). Multiplexed assays increase data density per compound and reduce reagent consumption. Relevant for assay cost modeling and data analysis pipeline configuration.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook multiplex assay configuration; LabWare LIMS

columns.name: outsourced_to_cro
columns.glossary_term: Outsourced to Contract Research Organization (CRO) Flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this assay is currently outsourced to an external Contract Research Organization (CRO) for execution. When true, the cro_vendor_name field captures the CRO identity. Impacts data governance, IP ownership, and regulatory audit trail requirements.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Oversight of Clinical Investigations (adapted for preclinical CRO oversight)

columns.name: plate_format
columns.description: Microplate format used in the assay (e.g., 96-well, 384-well, 1536-well). Determines reagent volumes, automation compatibility, and throughput capacity. Critical for liquid handling robot programming and compound dispensing protocols.
columns.reference: ANSI/SLAS Microplate Standards; ISPE GAMP 5; LabWare LIMS plate management

columns.name: protocol_reference
columns.description: Document identifier or URL reference to the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) or assay protocol document stored in the ELN (IDBS/Dotmatics) or document management system (Veeva Vault QualityDocs). Ensures traceability from assay execution to the governing protocol version.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); Veeva Vault QualityDocs; ISPE GAMP 5; ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System

columns.name: protocol_version
columns.description: Version number of the assay protocol document in effect at the time of assay execution (e.g., v1.0, v2.3). Required for GLP audit trails and regulatory submission traceability. Distinct from protocol_reference which is the document identifier.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); ICH Q10; Veeva Vault QualityDocs version control

columns.name: readout_type
columns.description: Primary quantitative output metric reported by the assay (e.g., IC50, EC50, Ki, Kd, percent inhibition, percent activation). Determines how compound activity data is interpreted in SAR analysis and hit-to-lead progression decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IC50|EC50|Ki|Kd|percent_inhibition|percent_activation|ratio|count|viability_pct — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: IUPAC pharmacology nomenclature; ChEMBL data standards; ICH M10

columns.name: regulatory_submission_eligible
columns.description: Indicates whether assay results generated using this assay are eligible for inclusion in regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA). Eligibility requires full validation per ICH Q2(R1) and GLP compliance where applicable. Governs data governance workflows for regulatory data packages.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312 (IND); 21 CFR Part 314 (NDA); ICH Q2(R1); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation

columns.name: retirement_date
columns.description: Date when the assay was formally retired and removed from active use. Null for active assays. Retirement is triggered by target deprioritization, supersession by a superior assay, or platform decommissioning. Required for data governance and historical data archival.
columns.reference: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); IDBS E-WorkBook lifecycle management

columns.name: signal_window
columns.description: Ratio of the maximum signal (positive control) to the minimum signal (negative control), quantifying the dynamic range of the assay. A signal window ≥ 2 is typically required for HTS qualification. Used in assay validation reports and Z-factor calculations.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1); Zhang JH et al. (1999) SLAS Discovery — Z-factor definition; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance

columns.name: species_origin
columns.description: Biological species from which the assay target, cells, or biological material is derived (e.g., human, mouse, rat, recombinant). Critical for translational relevance assessment and cross-species selectivity profiling. Impacts regulatory acceptability of preclinical data for IND submissions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: human|mouse|rat|rabbit|dog|monkey|in_vitro_recombinant — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH S5(R3) Reproductive Toxicology; ICH S7A/S7B; FDA IND Guidance

columns.name: technology_platform
columns.description: Detection technology or instrument platform used to execute the assay (e.g., HTRF, AlphaScreen, Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR), NMR, FRET, TR-FRET, Luminescence, Flow Cytometry). Critical for assay reproducibility assessment and equipment scheduling. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: HTRF|AlphaScreen|SPR|NMR|FRET|TR-FRET|luminescence|flow_cytometry|mass_spectrometry|fluorescence_polarization — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ISPE GAMP 5; ICH Q2(R1); LabWare LIMS instrument registry

columns.name: temperature_celsius
columns.description: Standard incubation or reaction temperature in degrees Celsius for the assay. Critical for assay reproducibility across sites and instruments. Deviations from this value are flagged as out-of-specification (OOS) events in the LIMS.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1); 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); LabWare LIMS environmental monitoring

columns.name: throughput_capacity
columns.description: Maximum number of compounds or samples that can be processed per day using this assay under standard HTS conditions. Serves as the MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Used for compound library screening campaign planning and resource scheduling in the discovery lab.
columns.reference: ISPE GAMP 5; IDBS E-WorkBook capacity planning module

columns.name: validation_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the assay with respect to its scientific and regulatory validation. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. 'validated' indicates full ICH Q2(R1) compliance; 'qualified' indicates fit-for-purpose qualification; 'development' indicates the assay is still being optimized. Governs whether assay results can be used in regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018

columns.name: z_prime_factor
columns.description: Statistical measure of assay quality (Z') calculated from positive and negative control variability. Values ≥ 0.5 indicate an excellent assay suitable for HTS. Stored as the validated Z' from the assay qualification run. Used to gate assay deployment for compound screening campaigns.
columns.reference: Zhang JH et al. (1999) A Simple Statistical Parameter for Use in Evaluation and Validation of High Throughput Screening Assays; ICH Q2(R1)

tables.name: hts_campaign
tables.description: Master record for High-Throughput Screening (HTS) campaigns executed against compound libraries. Captures campaign name, target or assay being screened, compound library used, screening format (primary, confirmatory, counter-screen), campaign status, start and end dates, number of compounds screened, hit rate, assay window (Z-prime factor), screening technology platform, CRO involvement flag, and campaign owner. Central operational entity for HTS execution tracking.

columns.name: hts_campaign_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the HTS campaign record in the discovery data product. Primary key for all downstream joins and lineage tracking.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics internal entity model; ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System

columns.name: assay_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.assay. Business justification: HTS campaigns execute screening using specific assays. The campaign currently has assay_format, assay_technology, target_name, target_class as denormalized attributes. Adding assay_id FK establishes t

columns.name: cost_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: HTS campaigns are major cost events requiring cost center allocation for financial tracking, budget management, and project costing. Enables campaign cost analysis, resource planning, and financial re

columns.name: cro_business_partner_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.business_partner. Business justification: Outsourced HTS campaigns require linking to the qualified CRO business partner for contract management, AVL compliance, and vendor performance tracking. 'cro_name' is a denormalized business partner n

columns.name: internal_order_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: HTS campaigns are cost-tracked R&D projects requiring internal order assignment for budget control, variance analysis, and cost-per-screen metrics essential to pharmaceutical screening operations and

columns.name: molecular_target_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.molecular_target. Business justification: hts_campaign has denormalized STRING fields target_name and target_class that duplicate data from the molecular_target master record. While hts_campaign already links to assay (which has molecular_tar

columns.name: project_id
columns.description: Reference to the parent drug discovery project under which this HTS campaign is executed. Links the campaign to the broader target identification and hit-to-lead program for portfolio tracking.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics project hierarchy; ICH Q10

columns.name: screening_plant_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.plant. Business justification: HTS campaigns are executed at specific screening facilities/plants; facility tracking is required for GMP compliance, capacity planning, and regulatory audit trails. Role prefix 'screening_' distingui

columns.name: therapeutic_area_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.therapeutic_area. Business justification: HTS campaigns are executed within therapeutic area programs and budgets. Linking to the master therapeutic_area entity enables TA-level campaign portfolio reporting, cost tracking, and strategic resou

columns.name: actual_end_date
columns.description: Date on which the HTS campaign screening execution was completed. Used to calculate campaign duration, throughput metrics, and to trigger downstream hit confirmation workflows.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: actual_start_date
columns.description: Date on which the HTS campaign screening execution actually commenced. Compared against planned_start_date to measure schedule variance and operational efficiency.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: assay_format
columns.description: Scientific format of the assay used in the campaign, indicating whether the screen measures biochemical activity (purified protein), cellular response, whole-organism phenotype, direct binding (biophysical), or fragment-based interactions. Critical for interpreting hit quality and SAR analysis.
columns.reference: NIH NCATS HTS Assay Guidance; ISPE Drug Discovery Guidelines

columns.name: assay_technology
columns.description: Specific detection technology or instrumentation platform used in the assay (e.g., HTRF, AlphaScreen, FRET, TR-FRET, FP, luminescence, absorbance, imaging). Determines data interpretation rules and quality thresholds. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: HTRF|AlphaScreen|FRET|TR-FRET|FP|luminescence|absorbance|imaging|SPR|ITC — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: SLAS (Society for Laboratory Automation and Screening) Technology Standards; ISPE GAMP 5

columns.name: campaign_code
columns.description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the HTS campaign, assigned by the ELN or LIMS system (e.g., HTS-EGFR-2024). Used for cross-system referencing in Dotmatics, LabWare, and project management tools.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics campaign numbering convention; LIMS - LabWare SampleManager

columns.name: campaign_description
columns.description: Free-text scientific description of the HTS campaign objectives, biological rationale, assay design, and any special conditions or deviations from standard protocols. Provides context for data interpretation and scientific review.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: campaign_name
columns.description: Human-readable descriptive name of the HTS campaign, typically including the target name and campaign purpose (e.g., 'EGFR Kinase Primary Screen Q1 2024'). Used in reports, dashboards, and scientific communications.

columns.name: campaign_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the HTS campaign, tracking progression from planning through execution to completion or cancellation. Drives operational dashboards and resource allocation decisions.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics workflow states; ICH Q10

columns.name: coefficient_of_variation_percent
columns.description: Percentage coefficient of variation of the neutral control wells across all campaign plates, measuring intra- and inter-plate reproducibility. Acceptable CV% thresholds are defined per assay type and are a key quality acceptance criterion.
columns.reference: SLAS Assay Quality Standards; ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures

columns.name: compounds_screened_count
columns.description: Total number of unique compounds tested in this HTS campaign. Key operational metric for campaign scope, resource planning, and hit rate denominator calculation.
columns.reference: SLAS HTS Metrics Guidelines; ISPE Drug Discovery Guidelines

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the HTS campaign record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GLP data integrity regulations.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GLP 21 CFR Part 58; ICH Q10

columns.name: cro_involved
columns.description: Indicates whether a Contract Research Organization (CRO) was engaged to execute or support this HTS campaign. Drives vendor management, data transfer agreement requirements, and IP ownership tracking.
columns.reference: ICH Q10; GLP 21 CFR Part 58; GDPR Article 28 (data processor agreements)

columns.name: data_quality_flag
columns.description: Overall data quality assessment for the HTS campaign based on Z' factor, CV%, plate failure rate, and control performance. Determines whether campaign data is accepted for hit identification and downstream SAR analysis.
columns.reference: SLAS Assay Quality Standards; ICH Q2(R1); GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: eln_notebook_reference
columns.description: Reference identifier linking this HTS campaign to the corresponding experiment record in the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Provides traceability to raw experimental data, protocols, and scientist sign-off records.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: failed_plate_count
columns.description: Number of assay plates that failed quality control criteria and were excluded from hit identification analysis. High failed plate counts may trigger campaign re-screening decisions.
columns.reference: SLAS Assay Quality Standards; GLP 21 CFR Part 58; ICH Q10

columns.name: glp_compliant
columns.description: Indicates whether this HTS campaign was conducted under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations. GLP compliance is required for studies intended to support regulatory submissions (IND/NDA). Non-GLP campaigns are exploratory research.
columns.reference: GLP - 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; FDA GLP Regulations

columns.name: hit_count
columns.description: Number of compounds that met or exceeded the hit threshold criteria in this campaign. Used to calculate hit rate and to scope confirmatory screening workload.
columns.reference: SLAS HTS Metrics Guidelines; ISPE Drug Discovery Guidelines

columns.name: hit_rate_percent
columns.description: Percentage of screened compounds that qualified as hits (hit_count / compounds_screened_count × 100). Key campaign quality metric used to assess assay selectivity, library quality, and target druggability. Stored as a raw business measurement, not a derived KPI.
columns.reference: SLAS HTS Metrics Guidelines; NIH NCATS HTS Best Practices

columns.name: hit_threshold_percent
columns.description: Percentage inhibition or activation threshold used to define a 'hit' in this campaign (e.g., ≥50% inhibition at screening concentration). Determines the stringency of hit identification and directly impacts hit count and hit rate.
columns.reference: SLAS HTS Best Practices; NIH NCATS Hit Criteria Guidelines

columns.name: lims_batch_code
columns.glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Batch ID
columns.description: Batch or run identifier assigned by the LIMS (LabWare or Thermo Fisher SampleManager) for the sample processing associated with this HTS campaign. Enables traceability of compound samples, plate preparation, and analytical results.
columns.reference: LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; 21 CFR Part 11; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: planned_start_date
columns.description: Scheduled start date for the HTS campaign as defined in the project plan. Used for resource scheduling, capacity planning, and tracking schedule adherence.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics project planning; ICH Q10

columns.name: plate_count
columns.description: Total number of assay plates processed during the campaign. Used for capacity planning, reagent consumption tracking, and quality control review scope.

columns.name: plate_format
columns.description: Microplate format used in the HTS campaign, defining the number of wells per plate. Determines throughput capacity, liquid handling requirements, and data volume per plate.

columns.name: positive_control_compound
columns.description: Name or identifier of the reference compound used as the positive control in the assay (known active compound). Defines the 100% inhibition/activation benchmark for data normalization and Z' factor calculation.
columns.reference: SLAS HTS Best Practices; GLP (Good Laboratory Practice) 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: screen_type
columns.description: Classification of the screening campaign by its scientific purpose in the HTS funnel. Primary screens test the full compound library; confirmatory screens re-test hits; counter-screens eliminate false positives; dose-response screens establish potency; selectivity screens assess off-target activity.
columns.reference: ISPE Drug Discovery Guidelines; NIH NCATS HTS Best Practices

columns.name: screening_concentration_um
columns.description: Single-point screening concentration in micromolar (µM) at which compounds are tested in the primary screen. Defines the activity threshold context for hit identification and is a critical parameter for hit rate comparability across campaigns.
columns.reference: SLAS HTS Best Practices; NIH NCATS Assay Guidance

columns.name: signal_to_background_ratio
columns.description: Ratio of the positive control signal to the background (negative control) signal, measuring the dynamic range of the assay. A higher S/B ratio indicates a more robust assay window. Complementary to Z' factor for assay quality assessment.
columns.reference: SLAS Assay Quality Standards; NIH NCATS HTS Assay Guidance

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the HTS campaign record. Required for data lineage tracking, change control auditing, and Silver layer incremental processing in the Databricks Lakehouse.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GLP 21 CFR Part 58; ICH Q10

columns.name: z_prime_factor
columns.description: Statistical measure of assay quality (Z' factor) calculated from positive and negative control signals, ranging from 0 to 1. A Z' ≥ 0.5 indicates an acceptable HTS assay window. Critical quality gate for campaign data acceptance per SLAS and NIH NCATS standards.
columns.reference: Zhang JH et al. (1999) J Biomol Screen; SLAS Assay Quality Standards; NIH NCATS

tables.name: screening_result
tables.description: Transactional record capturing individual compound screening results from HTS campaigns, dose-response assays, and selectivity panels. Captures compound, assay, and campaign references, plate/well position, raw signal, percent inhibition/activation, potency values (IC50/EC50/Ki), Hill slope, curve fit quality (R-squared), result classification (active, inactive, inconclusive, toxic, hit, confirmed hit, false positive), selectivity score, replicate number, run date, and data quality flags. Includes hit-to-lead eligibility determination. Distinct from in_vitro_study: screening_result covers primary and confirmatory screening at scale; in_vitro_study covers deeper mechanistic follow-up on selected compounds.

columns.name: screening_result_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each individual screening result record in the HTS or dose-response assay campaign. Primary key for the screening_result data product in the discovery domain.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; ICH M10 Bioanalytical Method Validation

columns.name: assay_id
columns.description: Reference to the assay definition used to generate this screening result, including assay type, target, and protocol version.
columns.reference: LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; GLP (Good Laboratory Practice) 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: hts_campaign_id
columns.description: Reference to the High-Throughput Screening (HTS) campaign or screening project under which this result was generated. Enables grouping of results by campaign for SAR analysis.

columns.name: molecular_target_id
columns.description: Reference to the biological molecular target (e.g., protein, enzyme, receptor) against which the compound was screened. Central to target identification and MOA studies.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH S9 Nonclinical Evaluation for Anticancer Pharmaceuticals

columns.name: primary_screening_compound_id
columns.description: Reference to the compound (NCE or NBE) that was screened in this assay run. Links to the compound master record in the compound library.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH Q6A Specifications for New Drug Substances

columns.name: coefficient_of_variation_pct
columns.description: Coefficient of variation (CV%) for replicate measurements of this compound in the assay run. Measures intra-assay reproducibility; high CV% triggers data quality review.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: compound_concentration_um
columns.description: Concentration of the compound tested in the assay well, expressed in micromolar (µM). Critical for dose-response curve fitting and potency determination.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1); GLP 21 CFR Part 58; LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this screening result record was first created in the system. Required for GLP audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic record compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GLP 21 CFR Part 58; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: curve_fit_r_squared
columns.description: Coefficient of determination (R²) from the dose-response curve fitting model. Values close to 1.0 indicate a high-quality fit. Used as a data quality gate for potency value acceptance.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: data_quality_flag
columns.description: Data quality status assigned to this screening result based on automated QC rules and manual review. 'flagged' indicates a potential issue requiring review; 'rejected' excludes the result from downstream analysis.
columns.reference: GLP 21 CFR Part 58; 21 CFR Part 11; LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; ICH Q2(R1)

columns.name: ec50_nm
columns.description: Half-maximal effective concentration (EC50) derived from dose-response curve fitting, expressed in nanomolar (nM). Key potency metric for agonist/activator compounds.
columns.reference: ICH S9; ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: eln_notebook_ref
columns.description: Reference identifier linking this screening result to the corresponding experiment entry in the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Provides traceability to the original experimental record.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GLP 21 CFR Part 58; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: hill_slope
columns.description: Hill slope (cooperativity coefficient) from the four-parameter logistic (4PL) dose-response curve fit. Values near 1 indicate simple binding; values significantly different from 1 may indicate cooperativity, aggregation, or assay artifacts.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: ic50_nm
columns.description: Half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) derived from dose-response curve fitting, expressed in nanomolar (nM). Key potency metric for inhibitory compounds in SAR analysis and hit-to-lead progression.
columns.reference: ICH S9; ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: instrument_code
columns.description: Identifier of the laboratory instrument (e.g., plate reader, liquid handler, mass spectrometer) used to generate the raw signal. Supports instrument qualification tracking and systematic error investigation per GLP.
columns.reference: GLP 21 CFR Part 58; 21 CFR Part 11; LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; ISPE GAMP 5

columns.name: is_hit_to_lead_eligible
columns.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this compound result meets the predefined criteria for progression into the hit-to-lead (H2L) phase, based on potency, selectivity, and data quality thresholds.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH Q6A; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: ki_nm
columns.description: Inhibition constant (Ki) representing the binding affinity of the compound to the target, expressed in nanomolar (nM). Derived from competitive binding or enzyme kinetics assays. Used in mechanistic SAR studies.
columns.reference: ICH S9; ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: lims_result_ref
columns.description: Reference identifier from the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) for this screening result record. Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational LIMS source system.
columns.reference: LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; 21 CFR Part 11; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: max_response_percent
columns.description: Maximum observed response (top asymptote) from the dose-response curve, expressed as a percentage of control. Indicates the efficacy ceiling of the compound at the target.

columns.name: min_response_percent
columns.description: Minimum observed response (bottom asymptote) from the dose-response curve, expressed as a percentage of control. Used to assess baseline signal and curve quality.

columns.name: pan_assay_interference_flag
columns.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the compound has been identified as a Pan-Assay Interference Compound (PAINS) — a compound that produces artifactual activity signals across multiple assays due to non-specific mechanisms. PAINS compounds are deprioritized in hit-to-lead.
columns.reference: Baell & Holloway (2010) J Med Chem; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: percent_activation
columns.description: Calculated percentage activation of the target relative to controls. Primary activity metric for agonist/activator HTS campaigns. Null for inhibition assays.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1); GLP 21 CFR Part 58; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: percent_inhibition
columns.description: Calculated percentage inhibition of the target activity relative to positive and negative controls on the same plate. Primary activity metric for inhibitory HTS campaigns. Null for activation assays.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1); GLP 21 CFR Part 58; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

columns.name: plate_barcode
columns.description: Unique barcode identifier of the physical assay plate on which the compound was tested. Used for traceability back to the physical plate in the LIMS and for QC investigations.
columns.reference: LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; GLP 21 CFR Part 58; ISPE GAMP 5

columns.name: plate_column
columns.description: Numeric column designation (1–24) of the well on the assay plate. Used for spatial analysis of plate effects and systematic error detection.
columns.reference: ANSI/SBS 1-2004 Microplate Standard; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: plate_row
columns.description: Row designation (A–P) of the well on the assay plate. Used for spatial analysis of plate effects and edge-effect QC.
columns.reference: ANSI/SBS 1-2004 Microplate Standard; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: quality_flag_reason
columns.description: Free-text or coded reason explaining why a data quality flag was applied (e.g., 'edge well effect', 'reagent lot failure', 'instrument malfunction', 'outlier replicate'). Required when data_quality_flag is 'flagged' or 'rejected'.
columns.reference: GLP 21 CFR Part 58; 21 CFR Part 11; LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager

columns.name: raw_signal_value
columns.description: Unprocessed instrument signal reading from the assay detector (e.g., fluorescence units, luminescence counts, absorbance). Preserved as the primary measurement for audit and reanalysis.
columns.reference: GLP 21 CFR Part 58; 21 CFR Part 11; LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager

columns.name: reagent_lot_number
columns.description: Lot identifier of the key assay reagent (e.g., enzyme, antibody, cell line passage) used in this assay run. Enables reagent lot correlation analysis for systematic variability investigation.
columns.reference: GLP 21 CFR Part 58; LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; cGMP 21 CFR Part 211

columns.name: replicate_number
columns.description: Sequential replicate index for this compound-assay combination within the same run (e.g., 1, 2, 3). Enables statistical aggregation across replicates and assessment of intra-assay variability.
columns.reference: ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: result_classification
columns.description: Scientific classification of the screening result based on activity thresholds and confirmatory data. Drives hit-to-lead progression decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|inactive|inconclusive|toxic|hit|confirmed_hit|false_positive|pan_assay_interference — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH Q6A; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: run_date
columns.description: Calendar date on which the assay run was executed. Used for temporal trending, reagent lot correlation, and GLP audit trail compliance.
columns.reference: GLP 21 CFR Part 58; LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager

columns.name: run_timestamp
columns.description: Precise date and time when the assay instrument reading was captured. Supports intra-day sequencing, instrument log correlation, and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic record compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records and Signatures; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: selectivity_score
columns.description: Quantitative selectivity score measuring the compound's specificity for the primary target versus off-target activities in a selectivity panel. Higher scores indicate greater selectivity. Used in SAR-driven lead optimization.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH S9; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

columns.name: signal_to_background_ratio
columns.description: Ratio of the positive control signal to the background (negative control) signal on the assay plate. A key plate-level QC metric; low S/B ratios indicate assay degradation or reagent failure.
columns.reference: GLP 21 CFR Part 58; LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; ISPE GAMP 5

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this screening result record. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks lakehouse.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GLP 21 CFR Part 58; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: well_position
columns.description: Alphanumeric well position on the assay plate (e.g., A01, H12, P24) indicating the exact location of the compound in the plate layout. Standard SBS/ANSI plate format.
columns.reference: ANSI/SBS 1-2004 Microplate Standard; LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager

columns.name: z_prime_factor
columns.description: Z' factor for the assay plate, a dimensionless statistical metric (range -∞ to 1) measuring assay quality based on signal window and variability. Z' ≥ 0.5 is the accepted threshold for a valid HTS assay plate.
columns.reference: Zhang JH et al. (1999) J Biomol Screen; GLP 21 CFR Part 58; LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager

tables.name: sar_study
tables.description: Master record for Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR) studies conducted to understand how structural modifications to a compound affect its biological activity. Captures study name, lead series identifier, target identifier, SAR hypothesis, key structural features analyzed, number of analogs synthesized, potency range observed, selectivity findings, ADME impact, study status, lead scientist, and ELN notebook reference from IDBS/Dotmatics. Core entity for medicinal chemistry optimization.

columns.name: sar_study_id
columns.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the SAR study record. Primary key for this entity.
columns.reference: ICH M10, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN internal object model

columns.name: assay_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.assay. Business justification: SAR (Structure-Activity Relationship) studies use specific assays to measure potency and selectivity of synthesized analogs. The study table currently has assay_type as a denormalized STRING attribute

columns.name: best_compound_id
columns.description: Reference to the single best-performing compound identified from this SAR study, based on the combination of potency, selectivity, and ADME profile. Candidate for progression to the next discovery stage.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics compound registry; ICH M4 CMC

columns.name: fto_analysis_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.fto_analysis. Business justification: FTO analyses are conducted on the chemical space explored in SAR studies to identify third-party IP blocking the series. IP and medicinal chemistry teams jointly review FTO before advancing a series.

columns.name: hts_campaign_id
columns.description: Reference to the originating High-Throughput Screening (HTS) campaign from which the hit compounds for this SAR study were identified. Provides lineage from HTS to lead optimization.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; LIMS; ICH M4

columns.name: indication_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.indication. Business justification: SAR studies are conducted to optimize compounds for specific disease indications. Linking to product.indication enables indication-level medicinal chemistry portfolio reporting and aligns SAR findings

columns.name: internal_order_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: SAR studies are discrete R&D activities requiring dedicated cost tracking via internal orders for financial planning, cost-per-analog analysis, and stage-gate decision support in medicinal chemistry o

columns.name: lead_series_id
columns.description: Reference to the lead chemical series under investigation in this SAR study. Links to the compound series master record in the compound library.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics compound library; ICH M4 CMC

columns.name: molecular_target_id
columns.description: Reference to the biological molecular target (e.g., protein, receptor, enzyme) that the SAR study is designed to modulate. Links to the target identification master record.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; UniProt; ChEMBL target ontology

columns.name: patent_family_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_family. Business justification: SAR studies generate composition-of-matter IP filed as patent families covering the chemical series. IP teams link SAR findings to patent families for prosecution strategy and portfolio reporting. sar

columns.name: project_id
columns.description: Reference to the parent drug discovery project under which this SAR study is conducted. Enables roll-up reporting at the project level.
columns.reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics project hierarchy; ICH M4

columns.name: therapeutic_area_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.therapeutic_area. Business justification: SAR studies are conducted within therapeutic area medicinal chemistry programs. Linking to the master therapeutic_area entity enables TA-level medicinal chemistry resource reporting and portfolio gove

columns.name: actual_completion_date
