columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.trademark. Business justification: Brand name selection and trademark filing is initiated at candidate nomination as part of commercial and regulatory strategy. Pharma brand teams begin trademark searches and filings at nomination. Tra

columns.name: validation_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to quality.validation. Business justification: Candidate nomination triggers CMC process validation planning as an IND-enabling activity. The nomination is the formal business event that initiates process/analytical validation protocols. A pharma

columns.name: cmc_feasibility_assessment
columns.glossary_term: Chemistry Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) Feasibility Assessment
columns.description: Assessment of the Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) feasibility for the nominated compound, evaluating synthetic accessibility, scalability, and formulation developability. Informs manufacturing strategy and go/no-go decision.
columns.reference: ICH M4Q (CMC); ICH Q8/Q9/Q10; 21 CFR Parts 210/211; ISPE GAMP Guidelines

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the candidate nomination record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver layer.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: decision_date
columns.description: Date on which the nomination committee rendered its formal decision (approved, deferred, or rejected) on the development candidate nomination. May differ from nomination_date if committee review takes multiple sessions.
columns.reference: ICH M4; Internal Stage-Gate Governance SOP

columns.name: deferral_reason
columns.description: Documented rationale for deferral or rejection of the development candidate nomination, capturing the scientific, safety, CMC, IP, or strategic basis for the committee's decision. Required for governance records and future re-nomination consideration.
columns.reference: ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 312; Internal Stage-Gate Governance SOP

columns.name: efficacy_summary
columns.description: Narrative summary of key in vitro and in vivo efficacy data supporting the nomination, including primary pharmacology results from High-Throughput Screening (HTS) and lead optimization assays. Sourced from LIMS and ELN records.
columns.reference: ICH M4S (Pharmacology); 21 CFR Part 312.23(a)(8)(i); GLP (21 CFR Part 58)

columns.name: eln_notebook_reference
columns.description: Reference identifier linking to the primary Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) experiment or project record in IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics that contains the supporting scientific data for this nomination. Ensures data provenance and GLP traceability.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GLP (21 CFR Part 58); OECD GLP Principles; ISPE GAMP 5

columns.name: estimated_ind_date
columns.glossary_term: Estimated Investigational New Drug (IND) Filing Date
columns.description: Projected target date for filing the Investigational New Drug (IND) application with the FDA (or equivalent CTA with EMA/MHRA) based on the approved nomination and preclinical development plan. Key pipeline milestone for portfolio planning.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312.23; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) 536/2014; ICH M3(R2)

columns.name: first_in_class
columns.description: Indicates whether the nominated development candidate represents a first-in-class mechanism of action with no approved drugs acting on the same molecular target. Informs competitive positioning, IP strategy, and regulatory designation eligibility.
columns.reference: FDA CDER Novel Drug Approvals; ICH M4; Internal IP Strategy SOP

columns.name: glp_compliant
columns.description: Indicates whether the key safety and pharmacology studies supporting this nomination were conducted in compliance with Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations. GLP compliance is required for IND-enabling studies submitted to regulatory authorities.
columns.reference: GLP (21 CFR Part 58); OECD GLP Principles; EMA GLP Directive 2004/10/EC

columns.name: handoff_date
columns.description: Date on which the nominated development candidate was formally handed off to the preclinical development team. Marks the transition from discovery to preclinical and initiates IND-enabling studies planning.
columns.reference: ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 312.23; Internal Pipeline Transition SOP

columns.name: ip_status
columns.description: Current status of intellectual property protection for the nominated development candidate, including patent filing status and Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) assessment outcome. Confidential business data critical for portfolio valuation and licensing strategy.
columns.reference: USPTO; EPO; ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 314.53; Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)

columns.name: moa_summary
columns.description: Narrative summary of the compound's Mechanism of Action (MOA) — how it interacts with the molecular target to produce the desired pharmacological effect. Sourced from ELN (IDBS/Dotmatics) and used in IND applications and regulatory submissions.

columns.name: modality
columns.description: The drug modality class of the nominated development candidate, distinguishing New Chemical Entities (NCE) from New Biological Entities (NBE) and advanced therapy types. Determines regulatory pathway (NDA vs BLA) and CMC strategy.
columns.reference: FDA CDER/CBER Classification; ICH M4Q; 21 CFR Parts 210/211/312

columns.name: nce_nbe_classification
columns.glossary_term: New Chemical Entity / New Biological Entity (NCE/NBE) Classification
columns.description: Classification of the nominated compound as a New Chemical Entity (NCE) — a small molecule not previously approved — or a New Biological Entity (NBE) — a biologic not previously approved. Determines regulatory exclusivity, data protection, and CMC requirements.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.108 (NCE Exclusivity); 42 USC 262 (Biologics); FDA CDER/CBER Classification

columns.name: nomination_committee
columns.description: Name or identifier of the governance committee responsible for reviewing and rendering the nomination decision (e.g., Drug Discovery Committee, Portfolio Review Board, R&D Leadership Team). Supports governance traceability.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; Internal R&D Governance Charter

columns.name: nomination_date
columns.description: The formal calendar date on which the development candidate was officially nominated for progression from discovery into preclinical development. This is the principal business event date for this milestone record.
columns.reference: ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 312.23; Internal Stage-Gate Milestone SOP

columns.name: nomination_number
columns.description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the development candidate nomination (e.g., DC-ONCO-2024-0042). Used in cross-functional communications, regulatory filings, and portfolio tracking systems such as IDBS/Dotmatics ELN.
columns.reference: ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 312.23; Internal Compound Numbering SOP

columns.name: nomination_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the development candidate nomination decision made by the nomination committee. Drives pipeline progression and resource allocation decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: approved|deferred|rejected|pending_review|withdrawn — promote to reference product if additional statuses are required]
columns.reference: ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 312; Internal Stage-Gate Governance SOP

columns.name: orphan_drug_eligible
columns.description: Indicates whether the nominated development candidate is potentially eligible for Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) based on the proposed indication affecting fewer than 200,000 patients in the US (or equivalent EU criteria). Triggers early regulatory strategy planning.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 316 (Orphan Drug Regulations); EMA Regulation (EC) No 141/2000; FDA OOPD

columns.name: portfolio_priority
columns.description: Strategic priority classification assigned to the nominated development candidate by the R&D portfolio governance committee, reflecting unmet medical need, competitive landscape, commercial potential, and scientific confidence. Drives resource allocation.
columns.reference: Internal R&D Portfolio Governance SOP; ICH M4

columns.name: regulatory_pathway
columns.description: Anticipated regulatory approval pathway for the development candidate based on the proposed indication and unmet medical need (e.g., Standard, Fast Track, Breakthrough Therapy Designation, Accelerated Approval). Drives regulatory strategy and timeline planning.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312; FDA FDASIA Section 902; FDA Guidance on Breakthrough Therapy; EMA PRIME Scheme

columns.name: safety_summary
columns.description: Narrative summary of early safety and tolerability findings from in vitro toxicology screens, genotoxicity assays, and any preliminary in vivo safety studies conducted under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP). Informs risk assessment for IND-enabling studies.
columns.reference: ICH M4S (Toxicology); ICH S7A/S7B; 21 CFR Part 312.23(a)(8)(ii); GLP (21 CFR Part 58)

columns.name: selectivity_profile
columns.description: Summary of the compound's selectivity against the primary target versus off-target proteins or receptors, derived from selectivity panel screening (e.g., kinase panel, GPCR panel). Informs safety risk and differentiation strategy.
columns.reference: ICH M4S; SAR Analysis SOP; EMA Guideline on Non-Clinical Safety Studies

columns.name: source_system
columns.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this candidate nomination record originated or was primarily authored (e.g., IDBS E-WorkBook, Dotmatics, LIMS). Supports data lineage and Silver layer provenance tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ISPE GAMP 5; Internal Data Governance Policy

columns.name: target_patient_population
columns.description: Description of the intended patient population for the proposed indication, including relevant biomarker stratification, disease stage, or demographic characteristics (e.g., adult patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC, pediatric patients with SMA). Informs clinical trial design.
columns.reference: ICH E8(R1); ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Enrichment Strategies; EMA Guideline on Stratified Medicine

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the candidate nomination record. Required for change tracking, audit compliance under 21 CFR Part 11, and incremental data pipeline processing.

domains.name: clinical
domains.description: Manages end-to-end clinical trial design, execution, and data management across all phases (I-IV). Covers investigational sites, principal investigators, trial protocols, case report forms (CRF), electronic data capture (EDC) from Medidata Rave, CTMS records from Oracle/Siebel, eTMF in Veeva Vault, and GCP-compliant execution. Includes patient enrollment, randomization, blinding, and intent-to-treat (ITT) analysis. Authoritative source for clinical efficacy and safety endpoints including ORR, PFS, OS, and QoL metrics. Supports IND/NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
domains.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP / 21 CFR Part 312 / EMA Clinical Trial Regulation

tables.name: trial
tables.description: Master record for each clinical trial (study) conducted by Pharmaceuticals, covering all phases (I–IV). Captures investigational product, therapeutic area, phase, study design (randomized, blinded, open-label), primary and secondary endpoints (ORR, PFS, OS, QoL), IND/CTA reference numbers, EudraCT/NCT identifiers, sponsor, CRO partner, planned vs. actual start/end dates, GCP compliance status, regulatory submission references (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA), overall trial lifecycle state, and key operational milestones (FPFV, LPLV, database lock, CSR completion, interim analysis dates) with planned vs. actual tracking and variance commentary. Authoritative SSOT for all trial-level metadata and timeline milestones consumed by regulatory submissions and eTMF in Veeva Vault.

columns.name: trial_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each clinical trial (study) record in the Pharmaceuticals data lakehouse. Primary key for the trial master record.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 312

columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Clinical trials should link to finance internal orders for trial budget tracking and cost allocation. This enables accurate R&D capitalization and trial cost management across the enterprise.

columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.post_approval_commitment. Business justification: FDA and EMA post-approval commitments (PMCs/PMRs) mandate specific clinical trials. Regulatory operations teams track which trial fulfills which PAC for agency status reporting. The post_approval_comm

columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Trials have primary regulatory jurisdiction countries. Required for regulatory authority mapping, submission planning (FDA, EMA, PMDA), country-specific compliance requirements, and trial registry sel

columns.name: royalty_agreement_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.royalty_agreement. Business justification: In-licensed compounds under royalty agreements trigger milestone-based royalty accruals upon clinical events (Phase 3 initiation, first patient dosed). Finance must link trial records to the governing

columns.name: sponsor_legal_entity_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Trials are sponsored by legal entities. Essential for financial consolidation, regulatory submissions (sponsor identification in CTD), contract management, and liability tracking. Core business relati

columns.name: strategy_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.strategy. Business justification: Regulatory strategy documents define the clinical development pathway, target indication, and filing sequence. Regulatory affairs teams must trace which trials execute against which strategy for globa

columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.therapeutic_area. Business justification: Trials are organized by therapeutic area for portfolio management, resource allocation, and regulatory strategy. Plain 'therapeutic_area' text column denormalizes the product.therapeutic_area master.

columns.name: actual_enrollment
columns.description: Actual number of patients enrolled (consented and randomized or assigned to treatment) as tracked in Oracle/Siebel CTMS and Medidata Rave EDC. Updated in real-time during trial execution. Used for enrollment rate monitoring and milestone tracking.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); ClinicalTrials.gov results reporting; 21 CFR 312.33

columns.name: actual_primary_completion_date
columns.glossary_term: Actual Primary Completion Date (Last Patient Last Visit)
columns.description: Actual date on which the last patient completed the primary endpoint assessment (LPLV). Recorded in CTMS and Medidata Rave. Triggers database lock procedures and Clinical Study Report (CSR) preparation.
columns.reference: FDAAA 801; ICH E3 Structure and Content of CSR; 21 CFR 312.33

columns.name: actual_start_date
columns.glossary_term: Actual Trial Start Date (First Patient First Visit)
columns.description: Actual date on which the first patient was enrolled and received the first dose (FPFV). Recorded in Oracle/Siebel CTMS and Medidata Rave. Compared against planned_start_date to calculate enrollment delay variance.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR 312.33 Annual Report; ClinicalTrials.gov results reporting

columns.name: analysis_population
columns.description: Statistical analysis population used for the primary endpoint analysis. Intent-to-Treat (ITT) is the regulatory gold standard for confirmatory trials. Per Protocol (PP) is used as a sensitivity analysis. Defined in the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP).
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1) Section 5.2; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle; EMA Reflection Paper on Missing Data

columns.name: blinding_type
columns.description: Level of blinding applied to the trial to minimize bias. Double-blind is the gold standard for Phase 3 confirmatory trials. Open-label is common in oncology and rare disease studies. Impacts GCP compliance requirements and unblinding procedures.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.7; 21 CFR 312.23

columns.name: control_type
columns.description: Type of control arm used in the trial. Placebo-controlled is standard for regulatory approval; active comparator is required when placebo is unethical. Historical control is used in rare disease single-arm studies.
columns.reference: ICH E10 Choice of Control Group; 21 CFR 314.126; EMA Guideline on Choice of Non-Inferiority Margin

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the trial master record was first created in the clinical data lakehouse Silver layer. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED field for audit trail and data lineage purposes. Populated automatically on insert.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); ICH E6(R2) Audit Trail; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

columns.name: csr_completion_date
columns.description: Date on which the Clinical Study Report (CSR) was finalized and approved per ICH E3 guidelines. The CSR is a mandatory component of NDA/BLA/MAA regulatory submissions. Tracked in Veeva Vault eTMF.
columns.reference: ICH E3 Structure and Content of Clinical Study Reports; 21 CFR 314.50; EMA Module 5 CTD

columns.name: cta_reference
columns.description: Regulatory authority-assigned Clinical Trial Authorisation reference number for trials conducted in EU/EEA, UK (MHRA), or other ex-US jurisdictions. Supports multi-regional trial tracking.
columns.reference: EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014; MHRA Clinical Trials Regulations; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: database_lock_date
columns.description: Date on which the clinical trial database was locked in Medidata Rave EDC following data cleaning, query resolution, and medical review sign-off. Marks the point after which no further data changes are permitted without formal unblinding procedures. Critical milestone for regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: eclinical_system_study_reference
columns.glossary_term: Electronic Data Capture (EDC) System Study Identifier
columns.description: Study identifier assigned in Medidata Rave EDC system. Used to cross-reference clinical data collected in Rave with CTMS records and the trial master record. Enables data lineage tracing from source EDC to the Silver layer.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; Medidata Rave Study Configuration

columns.name: etmf_vault_reference
columns.glossary_term: Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) Vault Document ID
columns.description: Veeva Vault eTMF study-level document identifier linking this trial master record to the corresponding eTMF study folder. Enables direct navigation to trial documentation for regulatory inspection readiness.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8 (Essential Documents); TMF Reference Model; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: eudract_number
columns.glossary_term: European Union Drug Regulating Authorities Clinical Trials (EudraCT) Number
columns.description: Unique identifier assigned by the European Clinical Trials Database (EudraCT / CTIS) for trials conducted in the European Economic Area. Required for EMA regulatory submissions and MAA dossiers.
columns.reference: EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014; EMA EudraCT/CTIS

columns.name: gcp_compliance_status
columns.description: Current GCP compliance status of the trial based on internal quality oversight, audit findings, and regulatory inspection outcomes. Critical findings may trigger clinical holds. Tracked in MasterControl/TrackWise QMS and Veeva Vault.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Inspections; PIC/S GCP Guide

columns.name: ind_number
columns.description: FDA-assigned IND application number under which this trial is conducted. Links the trial to the regulatory submission record. Required for all Phase I–III trials in the US. May reference multiple INDs for combination studies.

columns.name: interim_analysis_date
columns.description: Planned date for the pre-specified interim efficacy or futility analysis reviewed by the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB). Relevant for adaptive trials and trials with early stopping rules. Defined in the Statistical Analysis Plan.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1) Section 4.5; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; DSMB Charter

columns.name: irb_approval_status
columns.glossary_term: Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Ethics Committee Approval Status
columns.description: Status of IRB/Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) approval for the trial protocol. Mandatory before any patient enrollment. Tracked per jurisdiction. Suspension triggers immediate halt of enrollment per GCP requirements.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 3 (IRB/IEC); 21 CFR Part 56; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 4

columns.name: is_adaptive_design
columns.description: Indicates whether the trial employs a pre-specified adaptive design allowing modifications to the trial or statistical procedures based on interim data analysis. Requires additional FDA/EMA guidance compliance per ICH E20.
columns.reference: ICH E20 Adaptive Designs; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs (2019); EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

columns.name: is_pediatric_study
columns.description: Indicates whether the trial includes a pediatric population (patients under 18 years). Triggers Pediatric Study Plan (PIP/PSP) requirements under FDA PREA and EMA Paediatric Regulation. Impacts regulatory strategy and labeling.
columns.reference: FDA PREA (Pediatric Research Equity Act); EMA Paediatric Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006; ICH E11(R1)

columns.name: nct_number
columns.description: Unique public registry identifier assigned by ClinicalTrials.gov (U.S. National Library of Medicine). Mandatory for trials subject to FDAAA 801 registration requirements. Used in regulatory submissions and public disclosure.
columns.reference: FDAAA 801; 42 CFR Part 11; ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol Registration and Results System

columns.name: phase
columns.description: Regulatory development phase of the clinical trial per ICH and FDA/EMA classification. Phase 1/2 and 2/3 denote seamless adaptive designs. Phase 4 denotes post-marketing studies. Drives regulatory strategy and submission planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: phase_1|phase_1_2|phase_2|phase_2_3|phase_3|phase_4|not_applicable — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E8(R1); 21 CFR 312.21; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials in Small Populations

columns.name: planned_enrollment
columns.description: Target number of patients to be enrolled in the trial as specified in the approved protocol and IND/CTA. Basis for site activation planning, supply chain forecasting, and budget allocation in SAP.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1) Sample Size; 21 CFR 312.23(a)(6); EMA Scientific Advice

columns.name: planned_primary_completion_date
columns.glossary_term: Planned Primary Completion Date (Last Patient Last Visit)
columns.description: Planned date for Last Patient Last Visit (LPLV) for the primary endpoint assessment. Registered in ClinicalTrials.gov as the Primary Completion Date. Drives regulatory submission timeline planning for NDA/BLA/MAA.
columns.reference: FDAAA 801; ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol Registration; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: planned_start_date
columns.glossary_term: Planned Trial Start Date (First Patient First Visit)
columns.description: Planned date for First Patient First Visit (FPFV) — the target date for the first patient to be enrolled and dosed. Used for milestone planning, CRO contracting, and supply chain scheduling. Tracked against actual FPFV for variance analysis.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle/Siebel CTMS milestone tracking; CTMS milestone definitions

columns.name: primary_endpoint
columns.description: The principal clinical outcome measure that the trial is powered to demonstrate (e.g., 'Overall Survival (OS)', 'Progression-Free Survival (PFS)', 'Objective Response Rate (ORR)', 'Complete Remission Rate'). Defined in the protocol and statistical analysis plan. Drives regulatory approval decisions.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); ICH E8(R1); FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints; EMA Guideline on Endpoints

columns.name: regulatory_submission_type
columns.description: Type of regulatory submission associated with this trial's data package. IND for US investigational studies; NDA/BLA for US marketing applications; MAA for EU; CTA for clinical trial authorisation. Links to the regulatory.submission domain. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IND|NDA|BLA|MAA|sNDA|sBLA|CTA — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 21 CFR Parts 312, 314, 601; EU CTR 536/2014; ICH M4 CTD

columns.name: short_title
columns.description: Abbreviated or acronym-based title used for internal operational reference, CTMS displays, and cross-functional communications (e.g., 'MONARCH-3', 'KEYNOTE-522').
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle/Siebel CTMS study naming conventions

columns.name: sponsor_protocol_number
columns.description: Internal protocol identifier assigned by Pharmaceuticals as the trial sponsor. Used as the primary cross-system reference in Oracle/Siebel CTMS, Medidata Rave EDC, Veeva Vault eTMF, and SAP. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this master record.

columns.name: study_design_type
columns.description: Fundamental design classification of the clinical trial. Determines statistical analysis plan requirements, randomization procedures, and regulatory acceptability. Adaptive designs require additional ICH E20 compliance documentation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: randomized|non_randomized|single_arm|crossover|adaptive|basket|umbrella — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles; ICH E20 Adaptive Designs; 21 CFR 312.23

columns.name: title
columns.description: Full official title of the clinical trial as registered in ClinicalTrials.gov and EudraCT/CTIS. Used in regulatory submissions, eTMF, and public disclosures. Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL for this master record.

columns.name: trial_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the clinical trial. Drives operational workflows, regulatory reporting obligations, and eTMF archival triggers. 'on_hold' indicates a clinical hold per 21 CFR 312.42. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS for this master record.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 312.42 (Clinical Hold); ICH E6(R2); ClinicalTrials.gov status definitions

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the trial master record was last modified in the Silver layer. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED field. Used for incremental data pipeline processing and change data capture (CDC) in Databricks.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); ICH E6(R2) Audit Trail; Databricks Delta Lake CDC

tables.name: protocol
tables.description: Formal clinical trial protocol document master, representing each approved version of the study protocol. Tracks protocol number, version, amendment history and rationale, approval date, IRB/IEC approval reference, study objectives (primary, secondary, exploratory), inclusion/exclusion criteria, dosing regimen, visit schedule (schedule of assessments), randomization design (scheme type, stratification factors, allocation ratio, blinding method), statistical analysis plan reference, sample size justification, and GCP compliance attestation. Linked to the parent trial and managed in Veeva Vault eTMF. Each amendment creates a new versioned protocol record with change justification.
tables.reference: Protocol Document (Veeva Vault eTMF / ICH E6 GCP)

columns.name: protocol_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each versioned clinical trial protocol record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for the protocol data product.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 312

In pharma partnerships, a licensee may run a protocol under a distinct licensing agreement from

Regulatory teams must link the protocol to the PAC to report fulfillment status to FDA/EMA, confirm the study design

columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.project. Business justification: Clinical protocols are authored against a specific discovery project. IND/CTA filings and regulatory submissions require tracing the protocol to its originating discovery project for portfolio governa

columns.name: regulatory_application_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.application. Business justification: Protocols are written to support specific regulatory applications (IND, NDA, BLA). Regulatory teams must track which protocols support which applications for submission planning, health authority meet

columns.name: specification_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to quality.specification. Business justification: Clinical protocols must reference the approved IMP quality specification to define acceptable product parameters (potency, purity, storage) per IMPD/IND requirements. This link supports regulatory sub

columns.name: submission_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: Protocol amendments must be submitted to health authorities (FDA IND amendment, EMA CTA amendment). Regulatory operations teams track which submission corresponds to each protocol version for amendmen

columns.name: therapeutic_area_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.therapeutic_area. Business justification: Protocol design, endpoint selection, and statistical methodology are TA-specific. Plain 'therapeutic_area' text column denormalizes the master. Medical affairs and regulatory teams filter protocols by

columns.name: trial_id
columns.description: Reference to the parent clinical trial to which this protocol version belongs. Links the protocol to the overarching study record in the CTMS.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS

columns.name: allocation_ratio
columns.description: Ratio of subjects assigned to each treatment arm (e.g., 1:1, 2:1, 1:1:1). Directly impacts sample size calculations and statistical power. Documented in the randomization section of the protocol.

columns.name: amendment_number
columns.description: Sequential integer counter for protocol amendments. Zero (0) indicates the original protocol; each subsequent amendment increments by one. Supports amendment history tracking and regulatory submission traceability.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.1; FDA Guidance on Protocol Amendments; 21 CFR 312.30

columns.name: amendment_rationale
columns.description: Documented justification for protocol changes introduced in this amendment version. Required by regulatory agencies to assess the impact of changes on subject safety, data integrity, and study validity. Null for original protocol (amendment_number = 0).
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.1; 21 CFR 312.30; EMA Guideline on Protocol Amendments

columns.name: amendment_type
columns.description: Classification of the amendment's regulatory significance. 'Substantial' amendments require prior regulatory authority approval; 'non_substantial' require notification only; 'administrative' are minor corrections. Determines regulatory submission pathway.
columns.reference: EU Clinical Trial Regulation 536/2014; EMA Guideline on Substantial Modifications; 21 CFR 312.30

columns.name: approval_date
columns.description: Date on which the sponsor's internal governance (e.g., Clinical Development Committee) formally approved this protocol version for implementation. Distinct from IRB/IEC approval; triggers eTMF filing in Veeva Vault.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.11; Veeva Vault eTMF; SOPs

columns.name: blinding_method
columns.description: Level of masking applied to the trial to prevent bias. Double-blind masks both subject and investigator; open-label has no masking. Critical for GCP compliance and regulatory acceptance of efficacy data.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.7; ICH E9(R1); 21 CFR 312

columns.name: clinicaltrials_gov_number
columns.description: National Clinical Trial (NCT) identifier assigned by ClinicalTrials.gov upon trial registration. Mandatory for FDA-regulated trials under FDAAA 801 and required for publication in peer-reviewed journals per ICMJE policy.
columns.reference: FDAAA 801; ICMJE Clinical Trial Registration Policy; WHO ICTRP

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this protocol record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity standards.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: design_type
columns.description: Structural design of the clinical trial. Determines how treatment arms are organized and how subjects are allocated. Informs statistical analysis plan and regulatory review strategy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: parallel|crossover|factorial|single_arm|basket|umbrella|platform — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E8(R1); ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance

columns.name: dosing_regimen
columns.description: Description of the investigational product dose, route of administration, frequency, and duration for each treatment arm (e.g., Drug X 200mg IV Q3W for 12 cycles). Directly linked to CMC and IND/NDA/BLA submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.6; ICH M4E (CTD Module 5); 21 CFR 312.23

columns.name: effective_date
columns.description: Date from which this protocol version is operationally effective at investigational sites. For amendments, this is the date sites must implement the changes. Drives site notification and training requirements.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.1; 21 CFR 312.30; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation

columns.name: eudract_number
columns.description: European Union Drug Regulating Authorities Clinical Trials (EudraCT) registration number assigned by EMA for clinical trials conducted in the EU/EEA. Required for MAA submissions and EU Clinical Trial Regulation compliance.
columns.reference: EU Clinical Trial Regulation 536/2014; EMA EudraCT Database; EMA GCP Guideline

columns.name: exclusion_criteria
columns.description: Conditions or characteristics that disqualify a subject from enrollment (e.g., prior therapy, comorbidities, contraindications). Complements inclusion criteria to define the eligible study population.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.5; 21 CFR 312.23; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation

columns.name: exploratory_objectives
columns.description: Hypothesis-generating objectives not powering the study, such as biomarker analyses, translational research endpoints, or health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) assessments. Supports future study design and RWE generation.

columns.name: gcp_compliance_attestation
columns.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this protocol version has been formally attested as compliant with ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice guidelines. Required for regulatory submissions and audit readiness.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR 312; EMA GCP Guideline; PIC/S GCP Guide

columns.name: inclusion_criteria
columns.description: Eligibility criteria that subjects must meet to be enrolled in the trial (e.g., age range, diagnosis, performance status, biomarker positivity). Defines the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) population. Stored as structured free text per protocol.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.5; 21 CFR 312.23; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation

columns.name: ind_number
columns.description: FDA-assigned Investigational New Drug (IND) application number under which this protocol is filed. Links the protocol to the regulatory submission record. Required for US clinical trial conduct under 21 CFR Part 312.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 312.23; FDA IND Application; eCTD Module 5

columns.name: irb_approval_date
columns.description: Date on which the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) granted approval for this protocol version. Milestone date for site activation and GCP compliance documentation.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 3.1; 21 CFR 56.109; EU Clinical Trial Regulation 536/2014

columns.name: irb_approval_reference
columns.glossary_term: Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) Approval Reference
columns.description: Reference number or identifier of the IRB/IEC approval for this protocol version. Required for GCP compliance and site activation. Tracked in Veeva Vault eTMF under the Trial Master File structure.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 3; 21 CFR 56; EU Clinical Trial Regulation 536/2014

columns.name: phase
columns.description: Regulatory development phase of the clinical trial as defined by ICH and FDA guidelines. Determines the study objectives, patient population size, and regulatory pathway (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA).
columns.value_regex: Phase I|Phase I/II|Phase II|Phase II/III|Phase III|Phase IV
columns.reference: ICH E8(R1); 21 CFR 312.21; FDA Guidance for Industry

columns.name: planned_sample_size
columns.description: Total number of subjects planned for enrollment as determined by the sample size justification in the protocol. Based on statistical power calculations for the primary endpoint. Drives site activation and enrollment planning.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.5; ICH E6(R2) Section 6.9; FDA Statistical Guidance

columns.name: primary_endpoint
columns.description: The principal clinical outcome measure used to evaluate the primary objective (e.g., Overall Survival (OS), Progression-Free Survival (PFS), Objective Response Rate (ORR)). Drives sample size calculation and statistical analysis plan.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials

columns.name: primary_objective
columns.description: The principal scientific and clinical objective of the trial as stated in the protocol. Defines the primary endpoint and the key question the study is designed to answer (e.g., demonstrate superiority in Overall Survival).
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.2; ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles

columns.name: protocol_number
columns.description: Sponsor-assigned unique protocol identifier used across all regulatory submissions, eTMF filings, and CTMS records. Externally known identifier referenced in IND/NDA/BLA/MAA dossiers.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6; 21 CFR 312.23; Veeva Vault eTMF

columns.name: protocol_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of this protocol version. 'draft' indicates work-in-progress; 'under_review' indicates IRB/IEC or sponsor review; 'approved' indicates fully authorized for use; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a newer amendment; 'retired' indicates withdrawn.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Veeva Vault QualityDocs Lifecycle States

columns.name: randomization_scheme
columns.description: Method used to randomly allocate subjects to treatment arms. Stratified randomization accounts for prognostic factors; adaptive randomization adjusts allocation ratios based on accumulating data. Documented in the protocol and statistical analysis plan.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) Section 6.7; FDA Guidance on Randomization

columns.name: sample_size_justification
columns.description: Narrative description of the statistical assumptions and power calculations supporting the planned sample size, including assumed effect size, alpha level, power, and dropout rate. Required by ICH E9(R1) and regulatory agencies.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.5; FDA Statistical Guidance; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials

columns.name: sap_reference
columns.description: Document identifier or version reference for the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) associated with this protocol version. The SAP details the pre-specified statistical methods for analyzing primary and secondary endpoints per ICH E9(R1).
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) Section 6.9; FDA Statistical Guidance

columns.name: short_title
columns.description: Abbreviated or lay-language title of the protocol used in operational communications, CTMS displays, and site-facing materials. Distinct from the full regulatory title.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS

columns.name: stratification_factors
columns.description: Clinical or demographic variables used to stratify randomization to ensure balanced treatment arms (e.g., disease stage, ECOG performance status, geographic region, biomarker status). Stored as free text per protocol specification.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Stratified Randomization

columns.name: study_type
columns.description: Broad classification of the study design indicating whether the trial involves an active intervention, passive observation, or special access program. Aligns with ClinicalTrials.gov and EudraCT registration categories.
columns.reference: ICH E8(R1); ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol Registration; EudraCT

columns.name: title
columns.description: Full official title of the clinical trial protocol as it appears on the protocol document and regulatory submissions. Typically includes the investigational product name, indication, and study design descriptor.

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this protocol record. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity. Enables change detection in the Silver Layer lakehouse pipeline.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: veeva_vault_doc_reference
columns.description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault eTMF where the authoritative protocol document is stored. Enables direct traceability from the data product record to the source document in the electronic Trial Master File.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; Veeva Vault eTMF; TMF Reference Model

columns.name: version_number
columns.description: Sequential version identifier for this protocol document (e.g., 1.0, 2.0, 2.1). Each approved amendment increments the version. Used to distinguish original protocol from subsequent amendments.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.1; Veeva Vault eTMF Document Versioning

columns.name: visit_schedule_summary
columns.description: High-level description of the Schedule of Assessments (SoA) including number of study visits, key assessment windows, and follow-up duration. Detailed SoA is maintained in the protocol appendix and Medidata Rave EDC configuration.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.4; Medidata Rave EDC; CTMS Visit Schedule

tables.name: investigational_site
tables.description: Master record for each clinical investigational site (hospital, clinic, research center) participating in one or more trials. Captures site name, address, country, site number, IRB/IEC of record, site activation milestones (feasibility, selection, SIV, FPFV target), site closure date, enrollment capacity, GCP inspection history, site status (selected, activated, enrolling, on-hold, closed), regulatory authority jurisdiction, and CRA assignment for site initiation and ongoing oversight. Serves as the geographic and operational anchor for site-level enrollment, monitoring, and IMP accountability activities.
tables.reference: Site Master File (ICH E6 GCP / CTMS)

columns.name: investigational_site_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the investigational site record in the clinical data lakehouse. Primary key for this master record.

columns.name: country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Sites are physically located in countries. Essential for regulatory authority jurisdiction determination, IRB/IEC requirements, site selection strategy, country-level enrollment tracking, and GCP comp

columns.name: distribution_network_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to supply.distribution_network. Business justification: Sites receive IMP through specific distribution nodes (depots/warehouses); GDP compliance requires documented supply chain routing. Clinical supply management uses this for shipment planning, temperat

columns.name: hco_master_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.hco_master. Business justification: An investigational site is hosted by a healthcare organization. Linking to hco_master enables site feasibility analysis, HCO-level performance benchmarking, contracting, and Sunshine Act reporting at

columns.name: health_authority_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.health_authority. Business justification: Sites must comply with jurisdiction-specific regulations and inspection requirements. Site qualification, GCP inspection readiness, and regulatory compliance tracking require knowing which health auth

columns.name: managing_org_unit_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.org_unit. Business justification: Investigational sites are managed by regional or country clinical operations org units responsible for site monitoring, budget oversight, and performance reporting. Pharma clinical ops teams require t

columns.name: masterdata_address_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.address. Business justification: Sites have standardized physical addresses. Required for site management, investigational product shipments, monitoring visit planning, regulatory documentation (site lists in submissions), and geoloc

columns.name: site_business_partner_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.business_partner. Business justification: Investigational sites are registered as business partners (vendors) in pharma masterdata for site fee payments, investigator grant processing, and vendor qualification audits. This is a standard accou

columns.name: site_internal_order_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Sites incur costs tracked via internal orders for site activation, monitoring, patient recruitment, and investigator fees. Essential for trial budget management, site payment processing, and cost-per-

columns.name: site_legal_entity_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Sites are owned/operated by legal entities (hospitals, research institutions, private practices). Required for clinical trial agreements (CTAs), payment processing, insurance/liability coverage, and r

columns.name: closure_date
columns.description: Date on which the site close-out visit was completed and the site was formally closed. All essential documents must be archived in eTMF (Veeva Vault) by this date.

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the investigational site record was first created in the clinical data lakehouse. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity standards.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: enrolled_subject_count
columns.description: Actual number of subjects who have been randomized and enrolled at this site to date. Compared against enrollment_target to assess site performance and trigger enrollment support actions.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave EDC; CTMS Oracle/Siebel

columns.name: enrollment_target
columns.description: Planned number of subjects to be enrolled at this site as agreed between the sponsor and principal investigator. Used for enrollment forecasting, site performance benchmarking, and IMP supply planning.

columns.name: etmf_site_folder_reference
columns.glossary_term: Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) Site Folder ID
columns.description: Reference identifier for the site-level folder in the Veeva Vault eTMF system. Links the site master record to its essential document archive for GCP inspection readiness and regulatory submission support.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; Veeva Vault eTMF; 21 CFR Part 312.62

columns.name: feasibility_date
columns.description: Date on which the site feasibility assessment was completed, confirming the site's capability, patient population, and infrastructure to conduct the trial. First milestone in the site activation timeline tracked in CTMS.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; CTMS Oracle/Siebel Site Milestone

columns.name: fpfv_actual_date
columns.glossary_term: First Patient First Visit (FPFV) Actual Date
columns.description: Actual date on which the first patient first visit (FPFV) occurred at this site. Compared against fpfv_target_date to measure site activation performance and enrollment timeline adherence.

columns.name: fpfv_target_date
columns.glossary_term: First Patient First Visit (FPFV) Target Date
columns.description: Planned date for the first patient first visit (FPFV) at this site, representing the target enrollment start. Used for enrollment forecasting and site performance tracking against the clinical development timeline.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); CTMS Oracle/Siebel Enrollment Milestone

columns.name: gcp_inspection_status
columns.description: Current GCP inspection status of the investigational site by a regulatory authority (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA). Critical for site risk assessment, regulatory submission support, and pre-approval inspection (PAI) readiness.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312.68; EMA GCP Inspection Procedure; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19.3; PIC/S

columns.name: investigational_site_status
columns.description: Current operational lifecycle status of the investigational site within the clinical program. Drives CRA monitoring schedules, IMP shipment eligibility, and enrollment reporting. Values: selected (identified for participation), activated (SIV complete, ready to enroll), enrolling (actively screening/randomizing subjects), on_hold (enrollment paused), closed (no further activity), terminated (early discontinuation).
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.62; CTMS Oracle/Siebel

columns.name: irb_iec_approval_expiry_date
columns.description: Date on which the current IRB/IEC approval for the trial protocol at this site expires. Triggers renewal workflow; enrollment must be suspended if approval lapses without renewal.

columns.name: irb_iec_approval_number
columns.description: Official approval reference number issued by the IRB/IEC for the clinical trial protocol at this site. Mandatory for site activation and must be filed in the eTMF (Veeva Vault) prior to first patient first visit (FPFV).

columns.name: irb_iec_name
columns.glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Name
columns.description: Name of the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) of record responsible for ethical oversight of clinical trial activities at this site. Required for GCP compliance and eTMF documentation in Veeva Vault.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 3; 21 CFR Part 56; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014

columns.name: is_gcp_trained
columns.glossary_term: Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Training Confirmed Indicator
columns.description: Indicates whether all required site staff have completed GCP training as documented in the eTMF (Veeva Vault) prior to site activation. Mandatory pre-condition for site initiation per ICH E6(R2).

columns.name: is_lead_site
columns.description: Indicates whether this site is designated as the lead or coordinating site for a multi-center trial. Lead sites often host the coordinating investigator and serve as the primary regulatory contact.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014

columns.name: last_gcp_inspection_date
columns.glossary_term: Last Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Inspection Date
columns.description: Date of the most recent GCP inspection conducted at this site by a regulatory authority. Used to assess inspection recency and site compliance history for NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312.68; ICH E6(R2); EMA GCP Inspection Procedure

columns.name: lplv_actual_date
columns.glossary_term: Last Patient Last Visit (LPLV) Actual Date
columns.description: Actual date on which the last patient last visit (LPLV) occurred at this site, marking the end of active patient participation. Triggers site close-out visit scheduling and IMP reconciliation.

columns.name: regulatory_authority_jurisdiction
columns.description: Primary regulatory authority with jurisdiction over the investigational site's clinical trial activities. Determines applicable GCP guidelines, inspection readiness requirements, and submission standards (IND/NDA/BLA/MAA). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|OTHER — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 21 CFR Parts 312, 314; EMA Regulation (EU) No 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: screen_failure_count
columns.description: Number of subjects who were screened but failed to meet eligibility criteria at this site. Used to calculate screen failure rate and assess protocol feasibility and patient population fit.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave EDC; CTMS Oracle/Siebel

columns.name: selection_date
columns.description: Date on which the sponsor formally selected the site for participation in the clinical trial, following feasibility review. Marks transition to site status 'selected' in CTMS.

columns.name: site_type
columns.description: Classification of the investigational site by institutional category, used for site selection strategy, feasibility analysis, and enrollment benchmarking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: academic_medical_center|community_hospital|private_clinic|research_center|cro_managed|veterans_affairs|pediatric_center — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); CTMS Oracle/Siebel Site Classification

columns.name: siv_date
columns.description: Date on which the Site Initiation Visit (SIV) was conducted by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA). Confirms site readiness, staff training, and IMP accountability procedures. Required before first patient enrollment.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19.2; 21 CFR Part 312.62; CTMS Oracle/Siebel

columns.name: time_zone
columns.description: IANA time zone identifier for the investigational site (e.g., America/New_York, Europe/London). Used for accurate timestamp alignment of EDC data from Medidata Rave, adverse event reporting timelines, and CRA scheduling.
columns.reference: IANA Time Zone Database; ICH E2B(R3) ICSR Reporting

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the investigational site record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11, and incremental data pipeline processing.

tables.name: principal_investigator
tables.description: Master record for each Principal Investigator (PI) and sub-investigator responsible for conducting a clinical trial at a site. Captures investigator name, medical license number, specialty, GCP training certification date, CV reference, financial disclosure status, delegation log reference, and regulatory authority registration. Distinct from the HCP domain (which covers commercial HCP engagement) — this entity is specifically scoped to GCP-regulated trial conduct roles.

columns.name: principal_investigator_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the principal investigator or sub-investigator master record in the clinical domain. Serves as the primary key for this entity across all downstream clinical data products.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice (GCP); 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: contract_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.contract. Business justification: Each principal investigator's trial participation is governed by a signed investigator agreement (contract). Direct FK enables financial disclosure tracking, FMV compliance validation, and OIG/SAM scr

columns.name: ctms_investigator_id
columns.glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Investigator ID
columns.description: Source system identifier for this investigator as recorded in Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS. Used for cross-system reconciliation and lineage tracing back to the operational CTMS record.
columns.reference: Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: hcp_master_id
columns.description: FK to hcp.hcp_master.hcp_master_id — Principal investigators are HCPs — linking PI records to HCP master enables unified view of an HCPs relationship with the company across clinical, commercial, and medical affairs activities.

columns.name: health_authority_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.health_authority. Business justification: Principal investigators are registered with and subject to debarment checks by specific health authorities (FDA debarment list, EMA disqualification register). Regulatory compliance teams must link ea

columns.name: investigational_site_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.investigational_site. Business justification: A Principal Investigator (PI) record in a CTMS is fundamentally associated with a specific investigational site — the PI conducts the trial at that site. The principal_investigator table carries per-s

columns.name: investigator_business_partner_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.business_partner. Business justification: Principal investigators receive investigator grants and honoraria requiring registration as business partners for payment processing, financial disclosure compliance (Sunshine Act), and vendor qualifi

columns.name: license_country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: PIs hold medical licenses in specific countries. Required for regulatory compliance verification, license validation against country-specific medical boards, Form FDA 1572 validation, and investigator

columns.name: reporter_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.reporter. Business justification: Principal Investigators are primary reporters of trial SAEs/SUSARs to sponsors. Linking PI identity to PV reporter records enables causality assessment tracking, follow-up correspondence, and regulato

columns.name: therapeutic_area_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.therapeutic_area. Business justification: Site feasibility assessments and investigator qualification processes match PIs to trials by therapeutic area expertise. Plain 'therapeutic_area_expertise' text column denormalizes the master. Clinica

columns.name: country
columns.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country where the investigator primarily practices and conducts clinical trial activities. Determines applicable regulatory framework (FDA, EMA, PMDA, NMPA, etc.).
columns.reference: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; ICH E6(R2); EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) 536/2014

columns.name: cv_document_reference
columns.description: Reference identifier or URL pointing to the investigator's current curriculum vitae stored in Veeva Vault eTMF. The CV is a mandatory eTMF document (TMF Reference Model artifact 01.01) required for regulatory submissions and site qualification.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8.2.10; TMF Reference Model v3.0 (DIA); Veeva Vault eTMF

columns.name: delegation_log_reference
columns.description: Reference identifier pointing to the investigator's delegation of authority log stored in Veeva Vault eTMF or site trial master file. The delegation log documents which trial tasks have been assigned to sub-investigators and site staff, as required by GCP.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1.5, 8.3.22; TMF Reference Model v3.0; 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: email
columns.description: Primary professional email address of the investigator used for trial-related communications, protocol amendments, and safety notifications. Distinct from personal email; should be institutional or practice-based.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 4; HIPAA Privacy Rule

columns.name: fda_debarment_check_date
columns.description: Date on which the investigator was last verified against the FDA Debarment List and the Office of Inspector General (OIG) exclusion database. Mandatory pre-engagement check and periodic re-verification per sponsor SOPs.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312.70; FDA Debarment List; OIG Exclusion Database; FDCA Section 306

columns.name: financial_disclosure_date
columns.description: Date on which the investigator's financial disclosure form (FDA Form 3454 or 3455) was most recently submitted or updated. Required for NDA/BLA submissions to FDA.

columns.name: financial_disclosure_status
columns.description: Status of the investigator's financial disclosure form (FDA Form 3454/3455) as required under 21 CFR Part 54. Indicates whether the investigator has disclosed financial interests that could affect trial integrity. 'Disclosed' means the form has been submitted and reviewed.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 54 (Financial Disclosure by Clinical Investigators); FDA Guidance on Financial Disclosure

columns.name: first_name
columns.description: Legal given name of the principal investigator or sub-investigator as it appears on their medical license and regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.53; GDPR Article 4

columns.name: form_1572_date
columns.description: Date on which the investigator signed FDA Form 1572 (Statement of Investigator) for the most recent trial engagement. Form 1572 is a legal commitment by the investigator to comply with FDA regulations and GCP. Required for all IND-regulated trials in the US.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312.53(c); FDA Form 1572; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: gcp_training_date
columns.glossary_term: Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Training Certification Date
columns.description: Date on which the investigator most recently completed GCP training as required by ICH E6(R2). Mandatory for trial participation; triggers re-training alerts when approaching the validity window (typically 2-3 years).
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1.3; 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Directive 2005/28/EC

columns.name: gcp_training_expiry_date
columns.glossary_term: Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Training Expiry Date
columns.description: Date on which the current GCP training certification expires. Investigators with expired GCP training must not conduct trial activities. Drives compliance monitoring and site qualification workflows.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1.3; FDA GCP Guidance; EMA GCP Directive 2005/28/EC

columns.name: gcp_training_provider
columns.description: Name of the organization or platform that delivered the GCP training (e.g., CITI Program, TransCelerate, sponsor-internal training). Supports audit trail for regulatory inspections.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA GCP Guidance; MHRA GCP Inspection findings

columns.name: investigator_role
columns.description: GCP-defined role of the individual at the investigational site: Principal Investigator (PI) who bears overall responsibility, Sub-Investigator (sub-I) who assists under PI supervision, or Coordinating Investigator who coordinates multi-site activities.

columns.name: investigator_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the investigator record. 'Active' indicates the investigator is qualified and currently engaged in trial conduct. 'Disqualified' reflects FDA or regulatory authority debarment or disqualification actions.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312.70 (Disqualification of Clinical Investigators); FDA Debarment List

columns.name: irb_registration_number
columns.glossary_term: Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Ethics Committee Registration Number
columns.description: Registration number of the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) with which the investigator's site is registered. Required for FDA-regulated trials under 21 CFR Part 56 and ICH E6(R2).
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 56 (Institutional Review Boards); ICH E6(R2) Section 3; OHRP IRB Registration

columns.name: is_debarred
columns.description: Indicates whether the investigator is currently listed on the FDA Debarment List or OIG exclusion database. A value of True immediately disqualifies the investigator from participating in any FDA-regulated clinical trial.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312.70; FDCA Section 306; OIG Exclusion Database

columns.name: last_name
columns.description: Legal family name of the principal investigator or sub-investigator as it appears on their medical license and regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.53; GDPR Article 4

columns.name: license_expiry_date
columns.description: Date on which the investigator's medical license expires. Triggers re-qualification workflows to ensure continued GCP-compliant trial conduct. Null if the license has no expiry.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.53; GCP compliance monitoring

columns.name: license_issuing_authority
columns.description: Name of the regulatory or professional body that issued the medical license (e.g., California Medical Board, General Medical Council UK, Ordre des Médecins France). Required for cross-border trial conduct verification.

columns.name: medical_license_number
columns.description: State or national medical license number issued by the relevant licensing authority. Required for regulatory submissions and site qualification. Uniquely identifies the investigator's right to practice medicine.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312.53(c); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1.1; State Medical Board regulations

columns.name: medical_specialty
columns.description: Primary board-certified or recognized medical specialty of the investigator (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Cardiology, Neurology). Used to match investigator expertise to trial therapeutic area and protocol requirements.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS); UEMS (European Union of Medical Specialists)

columns.name: middle_name
columns.description: Middle name or initial of the investigator as recorded on official credentials. Used for disambiguation when first and last names are not unique.

columns.name: npi_number
columns.description: 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) assigned by CMS to US-based healthcare providers. Used for US-specific investigator identification, cross-referencing with HCP databases, and commercial engagement separation.
columns.reference: HIPAA Administrative Simplification (45 CFR Part 162); CMS NPI Registry; NPPES

columns.name: orcid_identifier
columns.description: Persistent digital identifier (ORCID iD) assigned to the investigator by the ORCID registry. Used to uniquely identify researchers across publications, grant applications, and clinical trial registries (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov).
columns.reference: ORCID Standard; ICH E6(R2); ClinicalTrials.gov registration requirements

columns.name: phone
columns.description: Primary professional phone number for the investigator, used for urgent safety communications, protocol queries, and site monitoring contact. Includes country code for international trials.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 4; 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: prior_trial_count
columns.description: Total number of GCP-regulated clinical trials in which the investigator has previously served as PI or sub-investigator. Key feasibility metric used by sponsors and CROs during site selection.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); TransCelerate Investigator Registry; FDA Guidance on Site Selection

columns.name: professional_title
columns.description: Highest relevant professional or academic degree held by the investigator (e.g., MD, PhD, PharmD). Used in regulatory submissions and delegation logs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MD|DO|PhD|MD-PhD|PharmD|MBBS|MBChB|DVM|Other — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.53

columns.name: qualification_verified_date
columns.description: Date on which the sponsor or CRO last verified the investigator's qualifications, credentials, and GCP training as part of the site qualification or re-qualification process. Supports audit trail for regulatory inspections.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; 21 CFR Part 312.53; FDA Pre-Approval Inspection (PAI) readiness

columns.name: record_created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the principal investigator master record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and GCP-compliant record management per 21 CFR Part 11.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); ICH E6(R2) Section 8; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: record_updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the principal investigator master record was most recently modified. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity requirements.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; ALCOA+ data integrity principles

columns.name: regulatory_authority_registration_number
columns.description: Identifier assigned by a national regulatory authority for the investigator's registration to conduct clinical trials (e.g., FDA investigator registration number, EudraCT investigator ID, MHRA registration). Required for IND/NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312.53; EudraCT; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) 536/2014; MHRA

columns.name: sub_specialty
columns.description: Secondary or sub-specialty area of clinical expertise (e.g., Hematologic Oncology, Pediatric Immunology). Provides finer-grained matching for complex or rare disease trials.

columns.name: years_of_clinical_trial_experience
columns.description: Number of years the investigator has been conducting GCP-regulated clinical trials. Used during site feasibility assessments to evaluate investigator experience relative to protocol complexity.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; FDA Guidance on Investigator Qualifications; TransCelerate Site and Investigator Quality Tolerance Limits

tables.name: clinical_enrollment
tables.description: Transactional record capturing each subject's complete enrollment and randomization journey within a clinical trial. Tracks screening number, subject number, enrollment date, informed consent confirmation, eligibility assessment (inclusion/exclusion criteria verification), screen failure reason, randomization date, randomization code, treatment arm assignment, stratification factors, blinding status, allocation ratio, block size reference, unblinding event details (if applicable), and enrollment/randomization status (screened, screen-failed, enrolled, randomized, withdrawn, completed). Supports ITT, modified ITT, and per-protocol population definitions. Authoritative SSOT for all subject-level randomization data including scheme parameters and individual assignments. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM (Randomization and Trial Supply Management) and Oracle CTMS.
tables.reference: Subject Enrollment Record (Medidata Rave EDC / ICH E9)

columns.name: clinical_enrollment_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each subject enrollment and randomization record within a clinical trial. Primary key for the enrollment data product in the Databricks Silver Layer.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: dispensed_inventory_lot_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to supply.inventory_lot. Business justification: Subject-level IMP accountability requires knowing which inventory lot was dispensed to each enrolled subject. GCP IMP accountability logs and pharmacovigilance lot traceability per subject are regulat

columns.name: investigational_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.investigational_product. Business justification: Enrolled subjects are assigned to specific investigational product kits at randomization. While enrollment has treatment_arm_code, linking to investigational_product provides the actual IMP kit assign

columns.name: investigational_site_id
columns.description: Reference to the investigational site where the subject was screened and enrolled. Corresponds to the site record in Oracle CTMS / Medidata Rave.

columns.name: medicinal_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Tracks which medicinal product each subject received. Required for product-specific safety reporting (ICH E2A), efficacy analysis by product, and regulatory queries about subject exposure in multi-pro

columns.name: patient_id
columns.description: Reference to the clinical trial subject (patient) record. Links to the subject master record sourced from Medidata Rave EDC.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); HIPAA 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164; GDPR Article 9

columns.name: protocol_id
columns.description: Reference to the specific protocol version under which the subject was enrolled. A trial may have multiple protocol amendments; this captures the version active at enrollment.

columns.name: rems_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.rems. Business justification: REMS programs (e.g., iPLEDGE, Clozapine REMS) require individual patient enrollment and compliance tracking. Each clinical enrollment in a REMS-governed trial must link to the REMS program for FDA-man

columns.name: trial_id
columns.description: Reference to the parent clinical trial under which this subject was screened and enrolled. Links to the trial master record in Oracle CTMS.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014

columns.name: allocation_ratio
columns.description: The ratio of subjects allocated to each treatment arm as defined in the randomization scheme (e.g., '1:1', '2:1', '1:1:1'). Determines the probability of assignment to each arm. Sourced from the RTSM randomization schedule.
columns.reference: ICH E9 Section 2.3; ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

columns.name: blinding_status
columns.description: Indicates the current blinding state of the subject's treatment assignment. 'blinded' = treatment assignment concealed; 'open_label' = treatment known from outset; 'unblinded' = previously blinded assignment has been revealed. Critical for data integrity and regulatory compliance.
columns.reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Blinding

columns.name: block_size
columns.description: The number of subjects per randomization block used in the blocked randomization scheme. Confidential as knowledge of block size could compromise blinding. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM randomization parameters.
columns.reference: ICH E9 Section 2.3; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; FDA Guidance on Randomization

columns.name: completion_date
columns.description: Date on which the subject completed all protocol-required study procedures and follow-up visits. Populated only when enrollment_status = completed. Used for study close-out and final analysis datasets.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC CDASH Standard; ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol Registration

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this enrollment record was first created in the source system (Medidata Rave RTSM or Oracle CTMS). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2) GCP guidelines.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

columns.name: ctms_subject_key
columns.glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Subject Key
columns.description: The natural/business key for this subject enrollment record as assigned by Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS. Used for cross-system reconciliation between CTMS and Medidata Rave EDC. Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

columns.name: data_lock_flag
columns.description: Flag indicating whether the subject's enrollment and randomization data has been locked for analysis (database lock). True = data locked and frozen for statistical analysis; False = data still open for query resolution or updates. Critical for regulatory submission readiness.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data; CDISC Standards

columns.name: eligibility_confirmed
columns.description: Flag indicating whether the subject has been confirmed as meeting all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria as defined in the trial protocol. True = eligible; False = not eligible or assessment pending. Drives enrollment decision in RTSM.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria

columns.name: enrollment_date
columns.description: Date on which the subject was formally enrolled into the clinical trial following eligibility confirmation. Represents the principal business event timestamp for the enrollment transaction. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC CDASH Standard

columns.name: enrollment_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the subject within the enrollment and randomization workflow. Drives Intent-to-Treat (ITT), modified ITT, and Per-Protocol (PP) population definitions. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM and Oracle CTMS. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: screened|screen_failed|enrolled|randomized|withdrawn|completed|discontinued — promote to reference product if additional statuses are required]
columns.reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: informed_consent_confirmed
columns.description: Flag indicating whether a valid, signed Informed Consent Form (ICF) has been confirmed for this subject prior to any study procedures. True = ICF confirmed; False = ICF not confirmed or pending. Mandatory GCP compliance check.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50.25; EMA Regulation (EU) No 536/2014

columns.name: informed_consent_date
columns.description: Date on which the subject signed the Informed Consent Form (ICF), confirming voluntary participation in the trial. Must precede any study-specific procedures per GCP requirements. Critical for regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50; EMA Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Article 29; GDPR Article 7

columns.name: itt_population_flag
columns.description: Flag indicating whether the subject is included in the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis population. True = subject is part of the ITT population (all randomized subjects regardless of protocol adherence). Drives primary efficacy analysis per ICH E9.
columns.reference: ICH E9 Section 5.2; ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands; 21 CFR Part 314; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle

columns.name: mitt_population_flag
