Business justification: The BOM defines the exact composition of the investigational product including API, excipients, and packaging components. Regulatory submissions (IND, IMPD) and clinical supply management require BOM

columns.name: budget_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.budget. Business justification: IMP supply budgets (manufacturing, packaging, labeling, cold-chain distribution) are tracked separately from clinical operations budgets. Pharma supply finance analysts require investigational_product

columns.name: compound_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.compound. Business justification: IND filings, CMC documentation, and pharmacovigilance require traceability from clinical investigational products back to discovery compound registration records. Essential for regulatory submissions

columns.name: dmf_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.dmf. Business justification: Manufacturing processes, specifications, and control strategies for investigational products are documented in Drug Master Files. CMC regulatory strategy requires linking IMP to the supporting DMF for

columns.name: drug_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_product. Business justification: Investigational products ARE drug products in clinical testing. Critical for IMP accountability, regulatory traceability (21 CFR 312), linking clinical batches to commercial formulations, and CMC-clin

columns.name: drug_substance_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_substance. Business justification: The IMPD/IND CMC section requires linking the investigational product to its registered drug substance (API). QC release, stability studies, and GMP compliance tracking all reference the drug_substanc

columns.name: exclusivity_period_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.exclusivity_period. Business justification: IP and regulatory teams track which exclusivity designations (orphan drug, pediatric, data exclusivity) are being pursued through development of each investigational product. This drives clinical prog

columns.name: formulation_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.formulation. Business justification: IMP batch records must trace to specific formulations for comparability protocols, bridging studies, and regulatory compliance (ICH Q5E). Essential when formulation changes occur during development or

columns.name: hta_submission_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to market.hta_submission. Business justification: The specific investigational product formulation, dose, and route evaluated in the trial is the product under HTA assessment. Market access teams must link the exact IMP to the HTA submission to ensur

columns.name: inn_registry_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.inn_registry. Business justification: Investigational products are identified by INN (International Nonproprietary Name) as the authoritative substance identity for regulatory submissions (IND, IMPD, EudraCT). Pharma regulatory affairs re

columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.137

columns.name: gmp_certificate_reference

columns.reference: EU GMP Annex 13; PIC/S GMP Guide; 21 CFR Parts 210-211; ICH Q7

columns.name: imp_code
columns.description: Sponsor-assigned alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this IMP or comparator within the trial supply system. Used for dispensation tracking and accountability logs in Oracle CTMS and SAP MM.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; EU IMPD Guideline; 21 CFR Part 312.23

columns.name: impd_reference
columns.description: Reference number or document identifier for the Investigational Medicinal Product Dossier (IMPD) submitted to EU competent authorities. Supports EMA/MHRA CTA submissions.
columns.reference: EU Directive 2001/20/EC; EMA IMPD Guideline; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: ind_number
columns.description: FDA-assigned Investigational New Drug (IND) application number under which this IMP is authorized for clinical investigation in the United States. Links to the regulatory.application record.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312; FDA IND Guidance; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: kit_number
columns.description: Unique identifier for the IMP dispensation kit as labeled and shipped to the investigational site. Used for kit-level accountability tracking and IWRS-driven dispensation in Oracle CTMS.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; EU GMP Annex 13; Oracle CTMS IMP Module

columns.name: manufacture_date
columns.description: Date on which the IMP batch was manufactured. Used to calculate shelf life, retest dates, and to verify GMP compliance of the batch at time of dispensation.
columns.reference: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.137; ICH Q1A Stability Guideline

columns.name: matching_placebo_code

columns.name: mechanism_of_action

columns.name: product_type

columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 1.33; EU IMPD Guideline; 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: quantity_destroyed

columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8.3.15; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 312.62

columns.name: quantity_dispensed
columns.description: Total quantity of this IMP dispensed to trial subjects from this batch, expressed in the dispensation unit (e.g., tablets, vials, mL). Core field for IMP accountability log per ICH E6(R2) Section 8.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8.3.15; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 312.62

columns.name: quantity_returned
columns.description: Total quantity of this IMP returned by trial subjects or sites, expressed in the dispensation unit. Used to calculate compliance rates and reconcile IMP accountability per GCP requirements.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8.3.15; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 312.62

columns.name: retest_date
columns.description: Date by which the IMP batch must be retested to confirm continued suitability for use, particularly for drug substances with defined retest periods rather than expiry dates. Supports stability management.
columns.reference: ICH Q1A(R2) Stability Guideline; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.137

columns.name: storage_condition

columns.reference: ICH Q1A(R2); EU GDP Guidelines; 21 CFR Part 211.142; WHO TRS 961

columns.name: supply_status
columns.description: Current status of this IMP record in the trial supply lifecycle: available (at site, ready for dispensation), dispensed (issued to subject), returned (received back from subject), destroyed, quarantine (hold pending investigation), or expired.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; EU GMP Annex 13; SAP MM Inventory Management

columns.name: updated_timestamp

tables.name: trial_endpoint
tables.description: Transactional record capturing the formal assessment of primary and secondary clinical endpoints for each subject at defined timepoints. Captures endpoint name (ORR, PFS, OS, QoL, DOR), assessment date, assessment method (RECIST, BICR, investigator assessment), result value, unit, response category, and adjudication committee review status. Feeds directly into efficacy analyses for NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
tables.reference: Efficacy Endpoint Record (RECIST / ICH E9 / CDISC ADaM)

columns.name: trial_endpoint_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each trial endpoint assessment record in the clinical lakehouse silver layer.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: protocol_id
columns.description: Reference to the specific protocol version governing this endpoint assessment, ensuring traceability to the approved study design.

columns.description: Reference to the parent clinical trial under which this endpoint assessment was conducted. Links to the trial master record in the CTMS.

columns.description: Date on which the independent adjudication committee completed its review and issued a final determination for this endpoint assessment.
columns.reference: FDA Guidance on Independent Radiological Review; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: adjudication_required
columns.description: Indicates whether this endpoint assessment requires review by an independent adjudication committee (e.g., BICR, DSMB, IRC) due to discordance between investigator and central read, or per protocol mandate.
columns.reference: FDA Guidance on Independent Radiological Review; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: adjudication_result
columns.description: Final response category or concordance determination issued by the independent adjudication committee after review. Overrides investigator assessment when discordant, per protocol rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CR|PR|SD|PD|NE|concordant|discordant — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: FDA Guidance on Independent Radiological Review; RECIST 1.1

columns.name: adjudication_status
columns.description: Current status of the independent adjudication committee review for this endpoint assessment. Tracks workflow from pending through completed adjudication, supporting BICR and IRC processes.
columns.reference: FDA Guidance on Independent Radiological Review; ICH E6(R2); Veeva Vault eTMF

columns.name: assessment_date
columns.description: Calendar date on which the endpoint assessment was performed. This is the principal real-world event date for the endpoint record, distinct from data entry or audit timestamps.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312; Medidata Rave EDC

columns.name: assessment_method
columns.description: Standardized methodology used to evaluate the endpoint (e.g., RECIST 1.1 for solid tumor response, iRECIST for immunotherapy, BICR for blinded independent central review, RANO for CNS tumors). Critical for regulatory submission credibility. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: RECIST_1.1|iRECIST|BICR|investigator|RANO|mRECIST|PCWG3|Cheson|IWG — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: RECIST 1.1 (Eisenhauer et al. 2009); FDA Guidance on Radiological Imaging; EMA Oncology Guidelines

columns.name: assessment_status
columns.description: Current workflow status of the endpoint assessment record: planned (scheduled but not yet performed), completed (data captured and verified), missed (visit occurred but assessment not done), not_done (subject not available), or invalid (data quality issue).
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave EDC; CDISC SDTM

columns.name: baseline_value
columns.description: Baseline measurement value for the endpoint at study entry (e.g., sum of longest diameters at baseline for RECIST). Used to calculate percent change from baseline and determine response categories.

columns.name: best_overall_response
columns.description: Best overall response achieved by the subject across all assessment timepoints up to and including this assessment, per RECIST or applicable criteria. Used in ORR and DOR calculations for regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: RECIST 1.1; FDA Guidance on Oncology Endpoints; ICH E9(R1)

columns.name: censoring_reason
columns.description: Reason for censoring a subject in time-to-event analyses when the endpoint event has not occurred (e.g., lost to follow-up, withdrawal of consent, initiation of new anticancer therapy, end of study). Required for regulatory-grade survival analyses. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: lost_to_followup|withdrawal|new_anticancer_therapy|end_of_study|administrative|death_other_cause — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Survival Analysis; CDISC SDTM

columns.name: confirmed_response
columns.description: Indicates whether the response (CR or PR) has been confirmed by a subsequent assessment at least 4 weeks later, as required by RECIST 1.1 for ORR determination in regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: RECIST 1.1; FDA Guidance on Oncology Endpoints

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this endpoint assessment record was first created in the clinical data system. Required for GCP audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2).
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

columns.name: data_lock_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this endpoint record has been locked as part of the clinical database lock process prior to unblinding and statistical analysis. Locked records are immutable for regulatory submission purposes.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Database Lock

columns.name: edc_record_reference
columns.description: Source system record identifier from Medidata Rave EDC, enabling traceability from the lakehouse silver layer back to the originating EDC record for audit and reconciliation purposes.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave EDC

columns.name: endpoint_category
columns.description: Classification of the endpoint as primary, secondary, exploratory, or safety per the study protocol. Primary endpoints drive the primary efficacy analysis for NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials

columns.name: endpoint_code
columns.description: Standardized alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the endpoint definition within the study (e.g., EP001, PFS_PRIMARY). Sourced from the study protocol and EDC configuration in Medidata Rave.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles; Medidata Rave EDC

columns.name: endpoint_name
columns.description: Full descriptive name of the clinical endpoint being assessed (e.g., Objective Response Rate, Progression-Free Survival, Overall Survival, Duration of Response, Quality of Life). Aligns with protocol-defined endpoint nomenclature.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints

columns.name: endpoint_type
columns.description: Functional type of the endpoint indicating the nature of the measurement: efficacy (ORR, PFS, OS), safety (AE rate), pharmacokinetic (PK), pharmacodynamic (PD), biomarker, or patient-reported outcome (PRO/QoL). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: efficacy|safety|pharmacokinetic|pharmacodynamic|biomarker|patient_reported|composite — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Biomarker Qualification

columns.name: evaluable_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the subject is considered evaluable for this specific endpoint at this timepoint, based on protocol-defined evaluability criteria (e.g., minimum number of prior assessments, no major protocol deviations).
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); Study Protocol Evaluability Criteria

columns.name: event_date
columns.description: Date on which the endpoint event (progression, death, response) occurred. For censored subjects, this is the last known event-free date. Used in time-to-event analyses for PFS and OS.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Survival Analysis; CDISC SDTM

columns.name: event_occurred
columns.description: Indicates whether the endpoint event (e.g., disease progression, death) has occurred for time-to-event endpoints such as PFS and OS. False indicates censoring. Critical for Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Survival Analysis; CDISC SDTM

columns.name: itt_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this subject's endpoint assessment is included in the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis population, the primary analysis population for most regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on ITT Principle; 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: nadir_value
columns.description: Lowest (nadir) measurement value recorded for the subject across all prior assessments. Used in RECIST PD determination (≥20% increase from nadir) and DOR calculations.

columns.name: percent_change_from_baseline
columns.description: Percentage change in the endpoint measurement from the baseline value to the current assessment value. Directly used in waterfall plots and response determination per RECIST criteria.
columns.reference: RECIST 1.1; FDA Guidance on Oncology Endpoints; ICH E9(R1)

columns.name: pp_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this subject's endpoint assessment is included in the Per Protocol (PP) analysis population, used as a sensitivity analysis alongside ITT in regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Populations

columns.name: query_open
columns.description: Indicates whether there is an open data query (discrepancy) raised against this endpoint record in the EDC system (Medidata Rave). Open queries must be resolved before database lock.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave EDC; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: response_category
columns.description: Categorical tumor response classification per the applicable assessment criteria: Complete Response (CR), Partial Response (PR), Stable Disease (SD), Progressive Disease (PD), or Not Evaluable (NE). Directly feeds ORR calculation for NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
columns.reference: RECIST 1.1; iRECIST; FDA Guidance on Oncology Endpoints; ICH E9(R1)

columns.name: result_value
columns.description: Numeric result of the endpoint assessment (e.g., tumor size in mm, PFS duration in months, QoL score). This is the principal quantitative outcome for the endpoint record. Null for categorical-only endpoints.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); Medidata Rave EDC; CDISC SDTM

columns.name: time_to_event_days
columns.description: Duration in days from the study reference date (e.g., randomization date) to the endpoint event or censoring date. Used directly in PFS, OS, and DOR analyses for NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Survival Analysis; CDISC SDTM

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this endpoint assessment record was most recently modified. Required for GCP audit trail compliance and data integrity monitoring under 21 CFR Part 11.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

Sourced from central lab data transfers into Medidata Rave. Distinct from manufacturing LIMS results — this is trial-specific clinical lab data.

columns.description: Reference to the scheduled or unscheduled study visit during which the specimen was collected. Aligns with the visit schedule defined in the trial protocol and captured in Medidata Rave CRF.

columns.name: clinically_significant_flag
columns.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the laboratory result has been assessed by the investigator as clinically significant. Corresponds to CDISC CDASH/SDTM LBCLSIG. A clinically significant abnormal result may trigger an adverse event report or protocol-defined action.
columns.reference: CDISC CDASH LB domain (LBCLSIG); ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Guidelines

columns.name: collection_date
columns.description: Date on which the biological specimen was collected from the trial subject. Used for study day calculation, protocol deviation assessment, and time-point alignment in efficacy and safety analyses. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBDTC (date portion).
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBDTC); ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: collection_timestamp
columns.description: Full date and time of specimen collection from the trial subject, including timezone offset. Used for precise PK/PD time-point calculations and timed lab assessments (e.g., fasting glucose, post-dose PK samples). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBDTC (full datetime).
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBDTC); ICH E6(R2) GCP; ISO 8601

columns.name: comments
columns.description: Free-text comments or notes associated with the laboratory result, including laboratory annotations, investigator comments on abnormal results, or data management notes. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBCOMM. Used for contextual interpretation of results.
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBCOMM); ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: data_entry_status
columns.description: Status of the Case Report Form (CRF) data entry for this laboratory result in Medidata Rave EDC. Tracks the data management workflow from initial entry through verification and database lock. Used for data cleaning and trial master file completeness tracking.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; Medidata Rave data management workflow

columns.name: entered_timestamp
columns.description: Date and time when the laboratory result was entered or imported into the Medidata Rave EDC system. Used for audit trail compliance per 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2) to demonstrate timely data entry and GCP compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18; Medidata Rave audit trail

columns.name: fasting_status
columns.description: Indicates whether the subject was fasting at the time of specimen collection. Relevant for metabolic panels (glucose, lipids) where fasting status affects reference ranges and result interpretation. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBFAST.
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBFAST); ICH E3

columns.name: lab_type
columns.description: Indicates whether the laboratory result was generated by a central laboratory (contracted central lab with standardized methods across all sites) or a local laboratory (site-specific lab). Central lab results are preferred for primary efficacy and safety endpoints due to standardization.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC SDTM LB domain

columns.name: loinc_code
columns.glossary_term: Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes (LOINC) Code
columns.description: Standardized LOINC code identifying the laboratory test or observation. Enables cross-study, cross-site, and cross-system harmonization of lab test definitions. Required for regulatory submissions and interoperability with central lab data transfers.
columns.reference: LOINC v2.77 (Regenstrief Institute); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog; CDISC CDASH/SDTM LB domain

columns.name: normal_flag
columns.description: Flag indicating whether the result is within, below, or above the laboratory's normal reference range. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBNRIND. Values: normal, low, high, critically_low, critically_high. Used in safety data listings and shift tables for regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBNRIND); ICH E3; CTCAE v5.0; FDA Data Standards Catalog

columns.name: out_of_range_flag
columns.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the result value falls outside the laboratory's defined reference range (either below lower limit or above upper limit). Distinct from clinical significance — a result can be out of range but not clinically significant. Used for automated data quality checks and safety signal detection.
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain; ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

columns.name: panic_value_flag
columns.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the result meets the laboratory's criteria for a panic (critical) value requiring immediate notification to the investigator or site. Supports GCP-compliant safety monitoring and timely SAE/AE reporting obligations.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312.32; CTCAE v5.0; CAP (College of American Pathologists) guidelines

columns.name: protocol_deviation_flag
columns.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this laboratory result is associated with a protocol deviation (e.g., specimen collected outside the protocol-defined time window, incorrect specimen type collected). Used for ITT/PP population analysis and regulatory submission deviation summaries.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Protocol Deviations

columns.name: query_flag
columns.description: Boolean flag indicating whether an open data query (discrepancy) exists for this laboratory result record in Medidata Rave EDC. Used by data managers to track unresolved data issues requiring site clarification before database lock.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; Medidata Rave query management

columns.name: rave_record_reference
columns.description: Source system record identifier from Medidata Rave EDC for this laboratory result entry. Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail back to the originating EDC system.

columns.name: reference_range_high
columns.description: Upper bound of the laboratory's normal reference range for this test, applicable to the subject's demographic group (age, sex). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTNRHI. Used for normal/abnormal flagging and shift table generation.
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSTNRHI); ICH E3; CTCAE v5.0

columns.name: reference_range_low
columns.description: Lower bound of the laboratory's normal reference range for this test, applicable to the subject's demographic group (age, sex). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTNRLO. Used for normal/abnormal flagging and shift table generation.
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSTNRLO); ICH E3; CTCAE v5.0

columns.name: reported_timestamp
columns.description: Date and time when the laboratory result was officially reported and transmitted by the laboratory to the sponsor or EDC system. Used for turnaround time monitoring, GCP compliance (timely reporting of critical values), and data transfer reconciliation.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; CAP turnaround time standards

columns.name: result_status
columns.description: Current status of the laboratory result record reflecting its lifecycle in the EDC and central lab workflow. Values: preliminary (initial result), final (verified and released), corrected (amended after initial release), cancelled (result voided), pending (awaiting analysis). Corresponds to HL7 observation status.
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain; HL7 FHIR Observation.status; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: result_unit_standard
columns.description: Standardized unit of measure for the laboratory result after conversion to a common unit for cross-site and cross-study comparability. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTRESU. Enables pooled analyses and regulatory submission datasets.
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSTRESU); UCUM; ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

columns.name: result_value
columns.description: The reported result value for the laboratory test as a string to accommodate both numeric and character results (e.g., '5.4', '>100', 'POSITIVE', 'NEGATIVE', 'TRACE'). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBORRES. Stored as STRING to preserve original reported value including qualifiers.
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBORRES); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

columns.name: result_value_numeric
columns.description: Numeric representation of the laboratory result value after standardization and unit conversion. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTRESN. Used for quantitative statistical analyses, shift tables, and outlier detection. Null for non-numeric results.
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSTRESN); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

columns.name: study_day
columns.description: Relative study day of specimen collection calculated from the subject's first dose date (Day 1). Negative values indicate pre-dose assessments. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBDY. Used for time-course analyses, PK/PD modeling, and protocol compliance assessment.
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBDY); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

columns.name: test_category
columns.description: Broad classification of the laboratory test panel or category (e.g., hematology, chemistry, urinalysis, coagulation). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBCAT variable. Used for grouping and filtering in safety data review and regulatory submissions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: hematology|chemistry|urinalysis|coagulation|immunology|microbiology|pharmacokinetics|other — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBCAT); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

columns.name: test_name
columns.description: Human-readable name of the laboratory test performed (e.g., Hemoglobin, Serum Creatinine, ALT, White Blood Cell Count). Sourced from the central lab data transfer file and mapped to the CRF lab panel definition in Medidata Rave.
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBTEST); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

columns.name: test_subcategory
columns.description: More granular sub-classification of the laboratory test within its category (e.g., liver function tests within chemistry, CBC within hematology). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSCAT variable.
columns.reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSCAT); ICH E3

columns.name: toxicity_grade
columns.glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Toxicity Grade
columns.description: Toxicity grade assigned to the laboratory abnormality per the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grading scale (Grade 1=Mild, Grade 2=Moderate, Grade 3=Severe, Grade 4=Life-threatening, Grade 5=Death). Used for safety signal detection, dose modification decisions, and regulatory safety reporting.
columns.reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E3; FDA Safety Reporting Guidance; 21 CFR Part 312.32

columns.name: verified_timestamp
columns.description: Date and time when the laboratory result was verified (source data verified, SDV) by the clinical monitor or data manager in Medidata Rave. Required for GCP audit trail and trial master file completeness.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18.3; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring

tables.name: trial_milestone
tables.description: Transactional record tracking key operational milestones for each clinical trial, including FPFV (First Patient First Visit), LPLV (Last Patient Last Visit), database lock date, CSR completion date, regulatory submission date, and interim analysis dates. Captures planned vs. actual dates, milestone status, responsible function, and variance commentary. Supports portfolio-level trial timeline management and regulatory commitment tracking.

columns.name: trial_milestone_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each trial milestone record in the clinical trial management system. Primary key for the trial_milestone data product.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: approval_id

columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Milestones are often country-specific (country-level regulatory submissions, country site activations, country database locks). Required for country-level trial planning, regulatory timeline tracking,

columns.name: investigational_site_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.investigational_site. Business justification: Many trial milestones are site-specific, including FPFV (First Patient First Visit) per site, LPLV (Last Patient Last Visit) per site, and site activation/closure dates. Linking trial_milestone to inv

columns.name: lifecycle_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.lifecycle. Business justification: Trial milestones (FPFV, DBL, CSR completion, NDA submission) are the primary triggers for product lifecycle stage-gate decisions. Portfolio governance and R&D leadership use this link to automatically

columns.name: patent_term_extension_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_term_extension. Business justification: Patent Term Extension (PTE/SPC) applications require precise regulatory review period dates derived from clinical trial milestones (IND filing, NDA approval). IP counsel directly references trial mile

columns.name: plan_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to supply.plan. Business justification: Trial milestone slippage (e.g., FPFV delay, protocol amendment) directly triggers supply plan revisions in S&OP. Linking trial_milestone to supply plan enables supply planners to re-baseline productio

columns.name: production_order_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to manufacturing.production_order. Business justification: Clinical milestones (FPFV, enrollment targets, database lock) trigger and constrain clinical supply production orders. Essential for supply forecasting, campaign planning, manufacturing slot allocatio

columns.name: protocol_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.protocol. Business justification: Trial milestones are defined in the protocol and tracked per protocol version. Protocol amendments may change milestone definitions or timelines. Linking trial_milestone to protocol enables tracking w

columns.name: regulatory_submission_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: Clinical milestones (database lock, CSR completion, final study report) are prerequisites for regulatory submissions. Regulatory operations teams track submission readiness and PDUFA timelines based o

columns.name: responsible_org_unit_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.org_unit. Business justification: Trial milestones are owned by specific org units (regulatory affairs, clinical ops, data management) accountable for delivery. responsible_function is a denormalized plain-text attribute. Linking to o

columns.name: trial_id
columns.description: Reference to the parent clinical trial to which this milestone belongs. Links the milestone record to the trial protocol and study-level metadata.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS Trial entity

columns.name: actual_date
columns.description: The confirmed date on which the milestone was achieved. Populated only upon milestone completion. Used to calculate variance against planned_date and to update regulatory commitment trackers.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) No 536/2014

columns.name: approval_timestamp
columns.description: Date and time when the milestone completion or date change was formally approved. Supports electronic audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP inspection readiness.
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); EMA GCP Inspections

columns.name: approved_by
columns.description: Name or identifier of the individual who formally approved the milestone completion or date change. Supports GCP audit trail requirements and electronic signature compliance under 21 CFR Part 11.
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GCP guidelines

columns.name: comments
columns.description: General free-text comments or notes associated with this milestone record, capturing additional context not covered by structured fields. Used by clinical operations teams for internal communication and audit trail documentation.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS notes field

columns.name: completion_evidence_type
columns.description: Type of documentation used to confirm milestone completion (e.g., signed memo, system-generated log from Medidata Rave, regulatory authority letter, DSMB report). Required for GCP inspection readiness and audit trail completeness.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EMA GCP Inspections

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Date and time when this milestone record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under GCP and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

columns.name: database_lock_type
columns.description: Specifies the type of database lock associated with this milestone, where applicable: interim (for interim analysis), final (for primary analysis), or partial (for a subset of sites or data). Populated only for database lock milestones. Supports data management planning.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave EDC database lock procedures; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: etmf_document_reference
columns.glossary_term: Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) Document Reference
columns.description: Reference identifier linking this milestone to the corresponding evidence document stored in Veeva Vault eTMF (e.g., milestone completion evidence, signed confirmation letter). Supports GCP audit trail and inspection readiness.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; Veeva Vault eTMF; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EMA eTMF guidance

columns.name: forecast_date
columns.description: The current best estimate of when the milestone will be achieved, updated dynamically as the trial progresses. Distinct from planned_date (baseline) and actual_date (confirmed completion). Supports rolling forecast and portfolio timeline management.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; Kinaxis RapidResponse planning conventions

columns.name: health_authority
columns.description: The regulatory health authority to which this milestone is committed or reported (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA). Relevant when is_regulatory_commitment is True. Supports multi-regional regulatory commitment tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation; PMDA; MHRA; NMPA

columns.name: ind_number
columns.description: The FDA-assigned Investigational New Drug (IND) application number associated with the clinical trial. Required for regulatory commitment tracking and FDA correspondence. Nullable for non-US trials.
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; IND application requirements

columns.name: interim_analysis_number
columns.description: Sequential number identifying which interim analysis this milestone represents (e.g., 1 for IA1, 2 for IA2). Populated only when is_interim_analysis is True. Supports tracking of multiple pre-specified interim analyses within a single trial.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance; DSMB charter

columns.name: is_critical_path
columns.description: Indicates whether this milestone lies on the critical path of the clinical trial project plan. Critical path milestones directly impact the overall trial completion date and receive elevated monitoring priority in portfolio management.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); ISPE GAMP 5; Oracle Siebel CTMS project planning

columns.name: is_interim_analysis
columns.description: Indicates whether this milestone represents an interim analysis event (e.g., a pre-specified interim efficacy or futility analysis). When True, additional blinding and DSMB (Data Safety Monitoring Board) governance controls apply.
columns.reference: ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance; DSMB charter requirements

columns.name: is_regulatory_commitment
columns.description: Indicates whether this milestone represents a formal commitment made to a health authority (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA) as part of an approval condition, post-approval commitment, or REMS requirement. When True, triggers mandatory regulatory commitment tracking workflows.
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Post-Authorisation Commitments; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: milestone_category
columns.description: Indicates whether the milestone is a planned internal target, a contractual obligation (e.g., with a CRO/CMO), a regulatory commitment (e.g., FDA/EMA post-approval commitment), or an internal management checkpoint. Drives escalation and governance workflows.
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Post-Authorisation Commitments; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: milestone_code
columns.description: Standardized alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the milestone type within the organization's CTMS (e.g., FPFV, LPLV, DBL, CSR, IND_SUB). Used for cross-trial portfolio reporting and regulatory commitment tracking.
columns.reference: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: milestone_name
columns.description: Full descriptive name of the clinical trial milestone (e.g., 'First Patient First Visit', 'Last Patient Last Visit', 'Database Lock', 'Clinical Study Report Completion', 'Regulatory Submission'). Human-readable label used in portfolio dashboards and regulatory commitment trackers.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) No 536/2014

columns.name: milestone_sequence
columns.description: Integer defining the chronological order of this milestone within the trial's project plan. Used to enforce milestone sequencing logic, detect out-of-order completions, and render Gantt-style timeline visualizations.
columns.reference: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2); project management best practices

columns.name: milestone_status
columns.description: Current operational status of the milestone in its lifecycle. 'at_risk' indicates the milestone is projected to miss its planned date. 'delayed' indicates the actual date has passed the planned date without completion. Used for portfolio-level trial timeline management and escalation triggers.
columns.reference: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: milestone_type
columns.description: Categorical classification of the milestone by functional area: enrollment (patient-facing), data_management (EDC/database activities), analysis (statistical/interim), regulatory (submission-related), safety (DSMB/safety review), or operational (site/logistics). Supports portfolio-level filtering and reporting.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS milestone category taxonomy

columns.name: notification_sent
columns.description: Indicates whether stakeholder notifications (e.g., to regulatory affairs, clinical operations leadership, CRO partners) have been dispatched upon milestone completion or delay detection. Supports automated workflow orchestration.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS workflow management

columns.name: planned_date
columns.description: The originally baselined target date for achieving this milestone, as defined in the clinical trial protocol or project plan. Used as the reference point for variance calculation and regulatory commitment tracking.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: predecessor_milestone_code
columns.description: The milestone_code of the immediately preceding milestone that must be completed before this milestone can begin. Enables dependency-aware critical path analysis and automated scheduling in the CTMS.
columns.reference: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2); project management standards

columns.name: region
columns.description: Geographic region associated with this milestone for regional portfolio reporting and regulatory tracking. Used when a milestone applies to a specific region rather than a single country or globally.
columns.value_regex: North America|Europe|Asia Pacific|Latin America|Middle East Africa|Global
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA; EMA; PMDA; NMPA regional regulatory frameworks

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Date and time when this milestone record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements under GCP and 21 CFR Part 11, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks lakehouse.
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

columns.name: variance_commentary
columns.description: Free-text narrative explaining the reason for any deviation between planned and actual/forecast milestone dates. Captures context not covered by variance_reason_code, including mitigation actions taken. Required for regulatory commitment reporting to FDA/EMA.
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) No 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: variance_days
columns.description: Signed integer representing the difference in calendar days between the actual (or forecast) date and the planned date. Positive values indicate delay; negative values indicate early completion. Stored as a business field to support regulatory commitment reporting without requiring runtime calculation.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Post-Authorisation Commitments

columns.name: variance_reason_code
columns.description: Standardized code categorizing the root cause of any milestone variance. Used for portfolio-level trend analysis and process improvement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: site_activation_delay|enrollment_shortfall|protocol_amendment|regulatory_hold|safety_event|data_quality|resource_constraint|vendor_delay|other — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ISPE GAMP 5

tables.name: biospecimen
tables.description: Transactional record for each biological specimen (tissue biopsy, blood draw, urine, CSF) collected from a trial subject at protocol-defined timepoints. Captures specimen type, collection date, collection visit, tube/container type, volume/quantity, processing method, storage temperature, biobank location, shipment tracking to central lab, LOINC/SNOMED coding, chain-of-custody audit trail, and associated assay results reference. Critical for oncology trials requiring RECIST tumor assessments, pharmacogenomic stratification, companion diagnostic validation, and translational research endpoints. Sourced from LIMS integration with Medidata Rave EDC.

columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Biomarker studies, PK/PD analysis, and translational research require linking specimens to the product being tested. Essential for dose-response modeling, bioequivalence studies, and supporting produc

columns.name: anatomical_site
columns.description: The anatomical location from which the specimen was collected, such as left arm, liver, or lung. Particularly important for tissue biopsies and tumor samples.

columns.name: collection_method

columns.name: consent_biobank_flag

tables.name: site_activation
tables.description: This association product represents the Site Activation (Trial Site) between investigational_site and trial. It captures the full operational lifecycle of a specific investigational site's participation in a specific clinical trial — from site selection and IRB approval through site initiation, enrollment performance, and formal site closure. Each record links one investigational_site to one trial and holds all per-trial-per-site attributes that exist only in the context of that site-trial pairing, including enrollment milestones, IRB/IEC approval details, GCP inspection status, and eTMF folder references. This is the authoritative SSOT for site-level trial operational data consumed by CTMS, eTMF, and clinical operations reporting.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical operations, an investigational site participates in MULTIPLE clinical trials over its lifetime, and each clinical trial is conducted across MULTIPLE investigational sites simultaneously. This is the foundational operational reality of multi-site clinical trials. The business actively manages each site-trial pairing as a distinct operational entity — called a 'trial site' or 'site activation' — with its own enrollment targets, IRB approvals, SIV dates, FPFV milestones, and closure dates that are specific to that site-trial combination and belong to neither the site master record nor the trial master record alone.

columns.description: Primary key for the site_activation association

columns.description: Foreign key linking to the investigational site participating in this trial activation

columns.name: trial_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to the clinical trial for which this site has been activated

columns.name: closure_date
columns.description: Date on which the site close-out visit was completed and the site was formally closed for this specific trial. The same site may have different closure dates across different trials.

columns.name: enrolled_subject_count
columns.description: Actual number of subjects who have been randomized and enrolled at this site for this specific trial. Per-trial-per-site metric that cannot reside on the site master record.

columns.name: enrollment_target
columns.description: Planned number of subjects to be enrolled at this site for this specific trial, as agreed between the sponsor and site. Belongs to the site-trial pairing, not the site master, because the same site may have different enrollment targets across different trials.

columns.name: etmf_site_folder_reference
columns.description: Reference identifier for the site-level folder in the Veeva Vault eTMF system for this specific trial. Each trial generates a separate eTMF site folder per site, making this a site-trial-level reference.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault eTMF; ICH E6(R2) Section 8

columns.name: fpfv_actual_date
columns.description: Actual date on which the first patient first visit occurred at this site for this trial. Used to calculate FPFV variance against target for operational reporting.

columns.name: fpfv_target_date
columns.description: Planned date for the First Patient First Visit (FPFV) at this site for this trial. A key activation milestone specific to the site-trial combination.

columns.name: gcp_inspection_status
columns.description: Current GCP inspection status of this site for this specific trial by a regulatory authority. Inspection outcomes are trial-specific and must be tracked at the site-trial level.

columns.name: investigational_site_status
columns.description: Current operational lifecycle status of this site within this specific trial. A site may be actively enrolling in one trial while on-hold in another, confirming this is a site-trial-level attribute.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CTMS industry standard

columns.name: irb_iec_approval_expiry_date
columns.description: Date on which the current IRB/IEC approval for this trial protocol at this site expires. Renewal is required per trial, making this a site-trial-level attribute.

columns.name: irb_iec_approval_number
columns.description: Official approval reference number issued by the IRB/IEC for this specific trial protocol at this site. Each trial requires a separate IRB/IEC approval at each site.

columns.name: irb_iec_name
columns.description: Name of the Institutional Review Board or Independent Ethics Committee that approved this trial at this site. May differ by trial if a site uses different ethics committees for different protocols.

columns.name: last_gcp_inspection_date
columns.description: Date of the most recent GCP inspection at this site for this trial. Trial-specific inspection history belongs to the site activation record.

columns.name: lplv_actual_date
columns.description: Actual date of the Last Patient Last Visit at this site for this trial, marking the end of active enrollment and data collection at this site.

columns.name: screen_failure_count
columns.description: Number of subjects screened but failing eligibility criteria at this site for this specific trial. Varies by trial protocol and site population.

columns.name: selection_date
columns.description: Date on which the sponsor formally selected this site for participation in this specific trial. Marks the beginning of the site activation lifecycle for this site-trial pairing.

columns.name: siv_date
columns.description: Date on which the Site Initiation Visit (SIV) was conducted by the CRA for this site-trial combination. A mandatory GCP milestone before first patient enrollment.

tables.name: submission
tables.description: Master record and single source of truth for all regulatory submissions (filing events) to health authorities including original applications, supplements, amendments, responses to information requests, and annual reports. Each submission represents a discrete eCTD sequence filed under a parent application. Tracks submission type, sequence number, dossier format (eCTD), submission date, target agency, eCTD lifecycle operation (new, replace, append, delete), submission medium, validation status, regulatory pathway, priority designation, and current lifecycle status. Includes document-level composition tracking with CTD module/section assignment (Modules 1-5), individual document metadata (title, type, version, author, status, file format, checksum), version control, and dossier completeness assessment aligned with ICH M4 (CTD structure) and M8 (eCTD technical specification). SSOT for regulatory submission identity, lifecycle, sequence tracking, dossier content, and document inventory in Veeva Vault RIM.
