columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 601 (FDA BLA); EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH Q5 Biologics Guidelines

columns.name: breakthrough_designation_program
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority offers a breakthrough therapy designation or equivalent expedited development program (e.g., FDA Breakthrough Therapy, EMA PRIME scheme, MHRA Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway). Drives early engagement strategy.
columns.reference: FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation (21 CFR Part 312.82); EMA PRIME Guideline; MHRA ILAP

columns.name: dmf_accepted
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority accepts Drug Master File (DMF) submissions for confidential disclosure of manufacturing, processing, packaging, and storage information for drug substances and excipients.
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 314.420 (DMF); EMA Active Substance Master File (ASMF) Guideline; ICH Q7

columns.name: ectd_required
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority mandates submission in Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) format as per ICH M8 guideline. Drives submission formatting and Veeva Vault RIM configuration.
columns.reference: ICH M8 eCTD Guideline; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA eCTD Specification v3.2.2

columns.name: effective_date
columns.description: Date from which this health authority record is considered valid and active for use in regulatory submissions and compliance activities. Supports temporal validity management in the regulatory master data.
columns.reference: Internal Master Data Governance; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: external_agency_code
columns.description: Official external identifier assigned to the health authority by an industry body or cross-reference system (e.g., DUNS number, ISO organization code, or identifier from a regulatory intelligence database). Supports cross-system reconciliation.
columns.reference: ISO 6523 Organization Identifier; DUNS; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: gmp_inspection_authority
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority has the mandate and capability to conduct Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) inspections of pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities. Drives inspection readiness and compliance programs.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Parts 210/211 (FDA cGMP); EMA GMP Guidelines; PIC/S PE 009; ICH Q7

columns.name: ich_member
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority is a full member or observer of the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH). ICH membership signals alignment with harmonized technical guidelines for drug registration.
columns.reference: ICH Governance; ICH Members and Observers List

columns.name: icsr_reporting_required
columns.glossary_term: Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) Reporting Required
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority requires Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) submissions for pharmacovigilance and adverse event reporting. Drives Argus Safety / Oracle AERS configuration for expedited and periodic safety reporting.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) ICSR Guideline; FDA 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010; PMDA PV Regulations

columns.name: ind_accepted
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority accepts Investigational New Drug (IND) applications or their local equivalent for clinical trial authorization. Drives IND filing strategy for global clinical development programs.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312 (FDA IND); ICH E6 GCP; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation EU 536/2014

columns.name: jurisdiction_type
columns.description: Scope of regulatory jurisdiction exercised by the health authority — federal (e.g., FDA within the US), national (e.g., MHRA for UK), regional (e.g., state-level agencies), supranational (e.g., EMA for EU member states), or international (e.g., WHO).
columns.reference: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System; 21 CFR Parts 210/211

columns.name: language_of_submission
columns.description: Official language(s) required for regulatory submissions to this health authority (e.g., 'English' for FDA/EMA/MHRA, 'Japanese' for PMDA, 'Chinese (Simplified)' for NMPA). Drives translation and localization planning for global submissions.
columns.reference: ICH M4 CTD Guideline; PMDA Submission Requirements; NMPA Technical Guidelines

columns.name: local_representative_required
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority requires a local regulatory representative, marketing authorization holder, or in-country agent to be designated for submissions and post-approval activities. Critical for market access planning in jurisdictions like Japan (PMDA) and China (NMPA).
columns.reference: PMDA Pharmaceutical Affairs Act; NMPA Drug Registration Regulations; EMA Directive 2001/83/EC Article 8

columns.name: mutual_recognition_agreements
columns.description: Comma-separated list of Mutual Recognition Agreements (MRA) or equivalence arrangements the health authority has with other regulatory bodies (e.g., 'FDA-EMA MRA', 'PIC/S Member'). Impacts GMP inspection reliance and submission strategy.
columns.reference: FDA-EMA MRA (2017); PIC/S Mutual Recognition; ICH Q10

columns.name: nda_accepted
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority accepts New Drug Application (NDA) submissions or their local equivalent (e.g., MAA for EMA, J-NDA for PMDA) for marketing authorization of small molecule drugs.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314 (FDA NDA); EMA Directive 2001/83/EC; ICH M4 CTD

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text field for capturing additional regulatory context, special requirements, recent guidance updates, or operational notes specific to this health authority. Maintained by the Regulatory Affairs team.
columns.reference: Internal Regulatory Affairs SOP; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: orphan_drug_program
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority operates an orphan drug designation program providing incentives (e.g., market exclusivity, fee waivers, protocol assistance) for rare disease treatments. Relevant for oncology and rare disease therapeutic areas.
columns.reference: FDA Orphan Drug Act (21 CFR Part 316); EMA Regulation (EC) No 141/2000; PMDA Orphan Drug Designation

columns.name: pai_conducted
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority conducts Pre-Approval Inspections (PAI) of manufacturing facilities as part of the marketing authorization review process. Drives inspection readiness planning.
columns.reference: FDA PAI Program (21 CFR Parts 210/211); EMA GMP Inspection Programme; PIC/S Guidelines

columns.name: primary_contact_email
columns.description: Official primary contact email address for regulatory correspondence with the health authority. Used for submission inquiries, meeting requests, and formal communications.
columns.reference: GDPR Article 4; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6 GCP

columns.name: primary_contact_phone
columns.description: Official primary telephone number for the health authority's regulatory affairs contact office. Includes country dialing code.

columns.name: priority_review_duration_days
columns.description: Expedited or priority review clock duration in calendar days for applications granted priority review designation at this health authority (e.g., 180 days for FDA Priority Review, 150 days for EMA accelerated assessment). Supports regulatory strategy for breakthrough therapies.
columns.reference: FDA PDUFA VI Priority Review Goals; EMA Accelerated Assessment Guideline; MHRA Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway

columns.name: psur_required
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority requires Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSUR) or Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Reports (PBRER) as part of post-marketing pharmacovigilance obligations. Aligns with ICH E2C(R2) guideline.
columns.reference: ICH E2C(R2) PBRER/PSUR Guideline; EMA Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010; FDA PADER Requirements

columns.name: record_created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this health authority master record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GDPR.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); GDPR Article 5; SOX Compliance

columns.name: record_updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this health authority master record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and data currency validation under 21 CFR Part 11.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); GDPR Article 5; SOX Compliance

columns.name: region
columns.description: Geopolitical or regulatory region associated with the health authority (e.g., 'North America', 'European Union', 'Asia Pacific', 'Latin America', 'Middle East & Africa'). Supports regional regulatory strategy planning and submission portfolio management.
columns.reference: ICH M4 eCTD Guideline; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: regulatory_framework
columns.description: Primary regulatory framework or legislation governing the health authority's operations (e.g., '21 CFR Parts 210/211/312/314' for FDA, 'Directive 2001/83/EC and Regulation 726/2004' for EMA, 'Pharmaceutical Affairs Act' for PMDA). Critical for compliance mapping.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Parts 210; 211; 312; 314; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH Guidelines

columns.name: rems_applicable
columns.glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Applicable
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority has a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) or equivalent risk management program framework applicable to submissions. Relevant for FDA and analogous risk management programs at other agencies.
columns.reference: FDA REMS Program (21 CFR Part 314.520); EMA Risk Management Plan (RMP) Guideline

columns.name: standard_review_duration_days
columns.description: Standard regulatory review clock duration in calendar days for a standard marketing authorization application at this health authority (e.g., 365 days for FDA standard NDA review, 210 days for EMA centralized procedure). Used for regulatory timeline planning.
columns.reference: FDA PDUFA VI Goals; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 6; ICH M4 CTD

columns.name: submission_portal_url
columns.description: Official URL of the health authority's electronic submission portal (e.g., FDA ESG gateway, EMA CESP portal, PMDA eCTD gateway). Used by regulatory affairs teams to route and track electronic submissions.
columns.reference: FDA Electronic Submissions Gateway (ESG); EMA CESP; ICH M8 eCTD

columns.name: veeva_vault_agency_code
columns.description: Agency identifier code as configured in Veeva Vault Regulatory Information Management (RIM) system. Used to link this master record to submission tracking, dossier management, and regulatory correspondence workflows in Veeva Vault.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM Configuration; Internal RIMS Data Governance

tables.name: application
tables.description: Master record for a regulatory application (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, ANDA, 510k) representing the formal dossier filed with a health authority for a specific drug product. Tracks application number assigned by the agency, application type, applicant entity, lead product, therapeutic indication, regulatory pathway, orphan designation status, priority review status, PDUFA/action date, and overall approval status. One application may have multiple submissions (original + supplements).

columns.name: application_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the regulatory application record in the data platform. Primary key for the application entity.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314; ICH M4 eCTD Guidance

columns.name: access_strategy_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to market.access_strategy. Business justification: Regulatory applications drive market access strategy development; access teams plan reimbursement pathways, HTA submissions, and launch sequencing based on application status and approval timelines fo

columns.name: atc_classification_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: ATC classification in regulatory applications determines therapeutic category for health authority review, pricing negotiations, and reimbursement decisions. Required for CTD Module 1 and health econo

columns.name: drug_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_product. Business justification: NDA/BLA/MAA applications are filed for a specific drug product formulation (dosage form, strength, route). Regulatory teams need this link for CMC section tracking and application-to-formulation trace

columns.name: exclusivity_period_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.exclusivity_period. Business justification: Applications track data_exclusivity_expiry_date and market_exclusivity_expiry_date as denormalized plain attributes. Application-level exclusivity planning (NCE, orphan, pediatric) requires a proper F

columns.name: finance_internal_order_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Regulatory applications should link to finance internal orders for regulatory program budget tracking and cost allocation. This enables accurate tracking of regulatory affairs costs by application and

columns.name: health_authority_id
columns.description: FK to regulatory.health_authority

columns.name: indication_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.indication. Business justification: Applications are filed for specific therapeutic indications. application.therapeutic_indication is a denormalized text field; normalizing via FK to product.indication enables indication-level applicat

columns.name: inn_registry_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.inn_registry. Business justification: Regulatory applications must reference INN for active substance identification, therapeutic classification, and global regulatory intelligence. Essential for NDA/BLA/MAA submissions and competitive la

columns.name: legal_entity_id
columns.description: Reference to the legal entity (company or affiliate) that is the named applicant/sponsor on the regulatory application.

columns.name: licensing_agreement_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.licensing_agreement. Business justification: Applications for in-licensed assets are governed by licensing agreements specifying field of use, territory, and regulatory diligence obligations. Regulatory milestone payments (filing, approval) are

columns.name: medicinal_product_id
columns.description: Reference to the lead drug product (Drug Product / Drug Substance) associated with this regulatory application.

columns.name: patent_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: NDA/BLA applications must declare patent information for Orange Book listing per 21 CFR 314.53. Business process: patent declaration at application submission, lifecycle management, and generic entry

columns.name: acceptance_date
columns.description: Date on which the health authority formally accepted the application for substantive review (i.e., filing acceptance / validation date). Marks the start of the official review clock.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.101; EMA Validation Procedures; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: agency_application_number
columns.description: The official application number assigned by the health authority upon receipt of the submission (e.g., NDA 123456, BLA 761234, EMA/H/C/004321). This is the externally-known business identifier for the application.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: applicant_name
columns.description: The full legal name of the company or entity listed as the applicant/sponsor on the regulatory application as filed with the health authority.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.50(a); EMA Application Form; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: application_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the regulatory application as tracked in the regulatory information management system. Drives workflow and reporting across regulatory affairs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|submitted|under_review|approved|refused|withdrawn|on_hold — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Procedural Guidance

columns.name: application_type
columns.description: Classification of the regulatory application type filed with the health authority. IND = Investigational New Drug, NDA = New Drug Application, BLA = Biologics License Application, ANDA = Abbreviated New Drug Application, MAA = Marketing Authorization Application, sNDA/sBLA = supplemental applications, 510k = medical device premarket notification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IND|NDA|BLA|ANDA|MAA|sNDA|sBLA|510k — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 21 CFR Parts 312, 314, 601; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH M4

columns.name: approval_date
columns.description: Date on which the health authority granted formal approval or marketing authorization for the application. Null if not yet approved.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.105; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: breakthrough_therapy_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the FDA has granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation (BTD) for this application, enabling intensive FDA guidance and rolling review.

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: The timestamp when this regulatory application record was first created in the data platform, sourced from Veeva Vault RIM or the regulatory information management system.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5(2); Veeva Vault RIM Audit Trail

columns.name: dosage_form
columns.description: The pharmaceutical dosage form of the drug product covered by this application (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, lyophilized powder for solution). Aligns with CMC section of the dossier.
columns.reference: ICH Q6A; FDA Dosage Form Terminology; EMA EDQM Standard Terms

columns.name: ectd_sequence_number
columns.glossary_term: Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Sequence Number
columns.description: The four-digit eCTD sequence number of the original submission (sequence 0000) as assigned in the eCTD lifecycle. Used to track the dossier version in Veeva Vault RIM and agency systems.
columns.reference: ICH M8 eCTD Guideline; FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide; EMA eCTD Guideline

columns.name: fast_track_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the FDA has granted Fast Track Designation for this application, facilitating more frequent interactions with FDA and eligibility for rolling review.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312.80; FDA Fast Track Guidance 2018

columns.name: lead_division_code
columns.description: The FDA Office/Division or EMA Committee (e.g., CDER, CBER, CHMP, COMP) responsible for reviewing this application. Determines the review team and applicable guidance documents.
columns.reference: FDA CDER/CBER Organization; EMA Committee Structure; 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: new_molecular_entity_flag
columns.glossary_term: New Chemical Entity (NCE) / New Molecular Entity (NME) Flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the active ingredient in this application is a New Chemical Entity (NCE) or New Molecular Entity (NME) that has not previously been approved by the health authority, conferring 5-year data exclusivity in the US.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.108; Hatch-Waxman Act; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

columns.name: orphan_designation_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the drug product has received Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) from the FDA or EMA for the indication covered by this application, conferring market exclusivity and fee waivers.
columns.reference: FDA Orphan Drug Act (21 CFR Part 316); EMA Regulation (EC) No 141/2000

columns.name: pai_outcome
columns.description: The outcome classification of the Pre-Approval Inspection (PAI) conducted at the manufacturing site. VAI = Voluntary Action Indicated; OAI = Official Action Indicated (may delay approval).
columns.reference: FDA PAI Compliance Program 7346.832; 21 CFR Parts 210, 211; PIC/S

columns.name: pai_required_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether a Pre-Approval Inspection (PAI) of the manufacturing facility has been required or triggered as part of the review of this application.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Parts 210, 211; FDA PAI Compliance Program 7346.832; PIC/S

columns.name: pdufa_action_date
columns.glossary_term: Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) Action Date
columns.description: The target action date committed by the FDA under the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA), or equivalent agency action deadline (e.g., EMA opinion date, PMDA review deadline). Critical milestone for commercial planning.
columns.reference: PDUFA VII (FDA); EMA Procedural Guidance; 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: post_approval_commitment_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the approval of this application is subject to post-approval commitments or post-marketing requirements (PMRs/PMCs) imposed by the health authority.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.81; FDA FDAAA 2007; EMA Post-Authorization Measures

columns.name: priority_review_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the application has been granted Priority Review designation by the health authority, entitling it to a shorter review clock (6 months for FDA vs. standard 10 months).
columns.reference: FDA PDUFA; 21 CFR Part 312.80; EMA Accelerated Assessment Guideline

columns.name: reference_product_name
columns.glossary_term: Reference Listed Drug (RLD) / Reference Product Name
columns.description: For ANDA (generic) or biosimilar applications, the name of the reference listed drug (RLD) or reference biological product against which the application is filed. Null for original NDA/BLA applications.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.94 (ANDA); 42 USC 262(k) (Biosimilar); FDA Orange Book

columns.name: regulatory_pathway
columns.description: The regulatory review pathway designated for this application. Determines review timelines, eligibility criteria, and post-approval commitments. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: standard|priority_review|accelerated_approval|breakthrough_therapy|fast_track|conditional_approval|exceptional_circumstances — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312.80 (Fast Track); FDA FDASIA 2012 (Breakthrough Therapy); EMA Conditional Marketing Authorization Guideline

columns.name: rems_required_flag
columns.glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Required Flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the FDA has required a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program as a condition of approval for this application, due to serious safety concerns.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.520; FDA REMS Guidance; FDAAA 2007

columns.name: rolling_review_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority has granted rolling review, allowing submission and review of completed dossier sections before the full application is submitted.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312.80; EMA Rolling Review Procedure; FDA Fast Track Guidance

columns.name: route_of_administration
columns.description: The route by which the drug product is administered to patients (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular). Defined in the CMC and clinical sections of the dossier.
columns.reference: ICH Q6A; FDA Route of Administration Terminology; EMA EDQM Standard Terms

columns.name: submission_date
columns.description: The date on which the original regulatory application dossier was formally submitted to the health authority. This is the principal business event date for the application lifecycle.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.101; EMA Procedural Guidance; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: submission_format
columns.description: The format in which the regulatory dossier was submitted to the health authority. eCTD (Electronic Common Technical Document) is the current standard; NeeS and paper are legacy formats.
columns.reference: ICH M8 eCTD Guideline; FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide; EMA eCTD Guideline

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: The timestamp when this regulatory application record was most recently modified in the data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5(2); Veeva Vault RIM Audit Trail

columns.name: vault_document_reference
columns.description: The unique document or object identifier assigned to this application record in Veeva Vault RIM, enabling traceability back to the source system of record for the regulatory dossier.

tables.name: submission_sequence
tables.description: Tracks individual eCTD submission sequences within a regulatory application, representing each discrete filing event (original submission, amendment, response to information request, annual report, supplement). Captures sequence number, submission date, submission type (original, class I/II supplement, CBE, PAS), eCTD lifecycle operation (new, replace, append), submission medium, and validation status. Aligns with ICH M8 eCTD technical specification.

columns.name: submission_sequence_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each eCTD submission sequence record within the regulatory application lifecycle.

columns.name: application_id
columns.description: Reference to the parent regulatory application (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, etc.) to which this submission sequence belongs.
columns.reference: ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification; 21 CFR Part 314; EMA eCTD Guidance

columns.name: health_authority_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.health_authority. Business justification: Submission sequences are filed with specific health authorities. The submission_sequence table has health_authority_code (STRING) which is a denormalized reference. Replacing with health_authority_id

columns.name: rims_submission_id
columns.glossary_term: Regulatory Information Management System (RIMS) Submission ID
columns.description: The native submission record identifier from the source Regulatory Information Management System (RIMS), specifically Veeva Vault RIM, used for cross-system traceability and reconciliation.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM Data Model; ICH M8; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: acknowledgement_date
columns.description: Date on which the health authority formally acknowledged receipt of the submission sequence. Triggers the start of the regulatory review clock for applicable submission types.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.101; EMA Procedural Guidance; ICH M8

columns.name: approval_timestamp
columns.description: Date and time at which the submission sequence was formally approved for filing by the authorized signatory, capturing the electronic signature event per 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); Veeva Vault RIM Electronic Signature Audit Trail

columns.name: approved_by
columns.description: Name or employee identifier of the authorized signatory or regulatory affairs head who approved this submission sequence for filing with the health authority.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6 GCP; Veeva Vault RIM Electronic Signature; SOPs for Regulatory Submissions

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Date and time at which this submission sequence record was first created in the data platform, serving as the audit trail creation marker per 21 CFR Part 11 and data governance requirements.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); ICH E6 GCP

columns.name: cro_cmo_involvement
columns.description: Indicates whether a Contract Research Organization (CRO) or Contract Manufacturing Organization (CMO) contributed data or documents to this submission sequence. Relevant for supply chain transparency and regulatory accountability.
columns.reference: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System; FDA Guidance on Contract Manufacturing; EMA GMP Guidelines

columns.name: ctd_module
columns.description: The primary Common Technical Document (CTD) module addressed by this submission sequence. M1 = Regional Administrative; M2 = Summaries; M3 = Quality (CMC); M4 = Nonclinical; M5 = Clinical. Used for content classification and routing.
columns.reference: ICH M4 CTD Guideline; ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification; FDA CTD Guidance

columns.name: ecdt_lifecycle_operation
columns.description: The eCTD document lifecycle operation applied in this sequence, indicating how the submitted documents relate to prior sequences. Values: new (first submission of a document), replace (supersedes a prior document), append (adds to a prior document), delete (removes a prior document). Aligns with ICH M8 eCTD lifecycle attribute.
columns.reference: ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification v4.0; FDA eCTD Guidance for Industry

columns.name: ecdt_version
columns.description: The version of the Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) specification used to structure and validate this submission sequence (e.g., 3.2.2 for legacy, 4.0 for ICH M8 compliant submissions).
columns.reference: ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification v4.0; FDA eCTD Guidance for Industry; EMA eCTD Guidance

columns.name: gateway_tracking_number
columns.description: Unique tracking or acknowledgement number assigned by the health authority's electronic submission gateway (e.g., FDA ESG acknowledgement number, EMA CESP submission ID) upon receipt of the eCTD package. Used for submission traceability and correspondence.
columns.reference: FDA Electronic Submissions Gateway (ESG) Technical Specification; EMA CESP User Guide

columns.name: information_request_ref
columns.description: Reference identifier for the health authority information request, deficiency letter, or complete response letter (CRL) that this submission sequence is responding to. Null if not a response submission.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.110; EMA List of Outstanding Issues (LOI) Procedure; MHRA Deficiency Letter Process

columns.name: is_resubmission
columns.description: Indicates whether this submission sequence is a formal resubmission following a Complete Response Letter (CRL) or refusal, as opposed to an original or routine amendment filing.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.110; FDA Guidance on Resubmission of NDA/BLA; EMA Re-examination Procedure

columns.name: package_size_mb
columns.description: Total file size of the eCTD submission package in megabytes. Used for submission logistics planning, gateway transmission monitoring, and compliance with health authority file size limits.
columns.reference: FDA ESG Technical Specification; EMA CESP Submission Size Guidelines

columns.name: pdufa_goal_date
columns.glossary_term: Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) Goal Date
columns.description: The target action date committed by the FDA under the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) for completing review of this submission. Applicable to NDA/BLA submissions filed with the FDA. Null for non-FDA or non-PDUFA submissions.
columns.reference: PDUFA VII Performance Goals and Procedures; 21 CFR Part 314; FDA CDER PDUFA Guidance

columns.name: priority_designation
columns.description: Regulatory priority designation applicable to this submission, which may affect review timelines and PDUFA goal dates. Examples: Priority Review, Breakthrough Therapy, Accelerated Approval, Orphan Drug, Fast Track (FDA); PRIME (EMA). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: standard|priority|breakthrough|accelerated|orphan|fast_track|prime|conditional — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: FDA PDUFA VII; 21 CFR Part 312.82 (Fast Track); FDA Breakthrough Therapy Guidance; EMA PRIME Scheme

columns.name: regulatory_action_date
columns.description: The date on which the health authority issued a formal regulatory action (approval, complete response letter, refusal, approvable letter) in response to this submission sequence.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.110; EMA Opinion Date Guidance; ICH M8

columns.name: regulatory_action_type
columns.description: The type of formal regulatory decision issued by the health authority for this submission sequence. Approval = marketing authorization granted; Complete Response = FDA letter requesting additional information; Approvable/Not Approvable = legacy FDA designations; Refusal = EMA/MHRA refusal of marketing authorization; Withdrawal = application withdrawn.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.110; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; MHRA Guidance on Regulatory Decisions

columns.name: regulatory_procedure_type
columns.description: The regulatory procedure under which this submission is filed, particularly relevant for EMA submissions. Centralized = EMA centralized procedure; Decentralized = DCP across multiple EU member states; Mutual Recognition = MRP; National = single country national procedure. Null for FDA submissions.
columns.reference: EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; EMA Directive 2001/83/EC; MHRA Guidance on Regulatory Procedures

columns.name: review_clock_start_date
columns.description: The date on which the regulatory review clock officially begins for this submission sequence, as determined by the health authority. May differ from acknowledgement_date for submissions requiring filing review or completeness assessment.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.101; PDUFA Performance Goals; EMA Procedural Guidance

columns.name: sequence_number

columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA Post-Authorisation Measures; FDAAA 2007

columns.name: regulatory_region
columns.description: Regulatory region or jurisdiction grouping for the approval. Used for regional reporting and portfolio management (US=FDA, EU=EMA, JP=PMDA, CN=NMPA, UK=MHRA, CA=Health Canada, AU=TGA, ROW=Rest of World). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: US|EU|JP|CN|UK|CA|AU|ROW — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH M4; FDA 21 CFR; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

columns.name: review_division
columns.description: The specific review division or committee within the health authority responsible for evaluating and granting this approval (e.g., FDA CDER Division of Oncology Products, EMA CHMP, PMDA Review Division).
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314; FDA CDER Organization; EMA CHMP Rules of Procedure

columns.name: submission_type
columns.description: Type of regulatory submission that led to this approval. NDA (New Drug Application), BLA (Biologics License Application), MAA (Marketing Authorization Application), ANDA (Abbreviated NDA), sNDA/sBLA/sMAA (supplemental submissions). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NDA|BLA|MAA|ANDA|sNDA|sBLA|sMAA|NDS|SNDS|510k — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314; 21 CFR Part 601; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this approval record was last modified. Audit trail field for data governance and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.

columns.name: veeva_vault_document_reference
columns.description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault RIM (Regulatory Information Management) system where the approval certificate, approval letter, and associated regulatory documents are stored. Enables direct traceability to the source system of record.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11; EMA eSubmission Guidelines

tables.name: ha_interaction
tables.description: Single source of truth for ALL formal interactions and communications with health authorities including Type A/B/C meetings (FDA), scientific advice (EMA), pre-submission meetings, advisory committee meetings, and all written correspondence (information requests, complete response letters, deficiency letters, acknowledgment letters, approval letters, agency queries, and general regulatory correspondence). Captures interaction type, format (in-person, teleconference, written), direction (inbound/outbound), dates, participants, discussion topics, agreed outcomes, response deadlines, follow-up actions, correspondence tracking numbers, document references, and response timeline compliance. Consolidates both meeting-based and written communications into a single chronological record per application. SSOT for all health authority communications — no separate correspondence product exists. Sourced from Veeva Vault RIM correspondence and meeting modules.
tables.reference: FDA Type A/B/C Meeting / EMA Scientific Advice

columns.name: ha_interaction_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each health authority interaction record in the silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this data product. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — represents a discrete formal communication or meeting event with a health authority, with its own lifecycle, participants, and outcomes.

columns.name: application_id
columns.description: Reference to the regulatory application (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, or other submission) to which this health authority interaction is associated. Links the interaction to its parent regulatory dossier for chronological record-keeping.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 312; 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

columns.name: brand_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand. Business justification: Health authority meetings shape brand development strategy. Commercial incorporates agency feedback and agreed development plans into brand positioning and launch planning.

columns.name: country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: ha_interaction.jurisdiction is a plain-text denormalization of country. HA interactions are jurisdiction-specific regulatory meetings; a proper FK enables interaction tracking by country, regulatory i

columns.name: health_authority_id
columns.description: Reference to the health authority entity (FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA, NMPA, etc.) that is the counterparty in this interaction. Serves as the PARTY_REFERENCE for this transaction header.
columns.reference: ICH M4; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

columns.name: medicinal_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Health authority interactions (Type A/B/C meetings, queries, advisory committees) are conducted for specific medicinal products. ha_interaction.product_name is a denormalized text field; normalizing v

columns.name: safety_signal_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.safety_signal. Business justification: Health authority meetings (Type C, scientific advice) frequently discuss emerging safety signals and required regulatory actions. Real business process: signal detection → request meeting → discuss be

columns.name: submission_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: HA interactions (information requests, Type A/B/C meetings, queries) are frequently tied to a specific regulatory submission. The ha_interaction table already carries ectd_sequence_number and submissi

columns.name: agency_contact_name
columns.description: Name of the primary health authority contact or reviewer assigned to this interaction (e.g., FDA project manager, EMA rapporteur, PMDA reviewer). Enables relationship management and continuity tracking across interactions.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA PDUFA Meeting Management Guidance

columns.name: agency_reference_number
columns.description: The official reference or tracking number assigned by the health authority to this specific interaction or correspondence (e.g., FDA meeting request confirmation number, EMA scientific advice case number, MHRA correspondence reference). Distinct from the company's internal interaction_reference_number.
columns.reference: FDA PDUFA Meeting Management Guidance; EMA Scientific Advice Procedure; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: agreed_outcomes_summary
columns.description: Summary of agreements, agency positions, commitments, and conclusions reached during or resulting from this health authority interaction. For meetings, captures agreed minutes content. For written correspondence, captures the agency's decision or position. Critical for regulatory strategy and post-meeting action tracking.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA Meeting Minutes Guidance; EMA Scientific Advice Outcome

columns.name: briefing_document_reference
columns.description: Document reference number or Veeva Vault document ID for the briefing document, background package, or information package submitted to the health authority in preparation for or in response to this interaction. Links to the eTMF/RIM document management system.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA Guidance for Industry: Formal Meetings; eCTD ICH M4

columns.name: confidentiality_level
columns.description: Data classification level assigned to this interaction record based on the sensitivity of the regulatory strategy and agency communications content. Restricted: contains highly sensitive regulatory strategy or unpublished clinical data. Confidential: standard regulatory correspondence. Internal: general meeting logistics. Public: post-approval public communications.
columns.reference: GDPR Article 5; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10; Company Data Classification Policy

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this health authority interaction record was first created in the silver layer data product. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED field for this transaction header. Populated automatically at ingestion time.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Conventions

columns.name: direction
columns.description: Indicates the direction of the communication: inbound (initiated by the health authority, e.g., information request, deficiency letter), outbound (initiated by the company, e.g., meeting request, response letter), or bilateral (mutual, e.g., formal meeting). Essential for tracking response obligations and deadlines.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.47; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

columns.name: discussion_topics_summary
columns.description: A structured summary of the key topics, questions, and agenda items discussed or addressed in this health authority interaction. For meetings, captures the agenda items. For written correspondence, summarizes the subject matter. Business-confidential as it contains regulatory strategy information.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA Meeting Minutes Guidance; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: ectd_sequence_number
columns.glossary_term: Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Sequence Number
columns.description: The eCTD sequence number of the submission associated with this interaction (e.g., the sequence number of the meeting request package or response submission filed in the eCTD dossier). Four-digit zero-padded number per ICH M8 eCTD specification. Null if the interaction is not associated with a formal eCTD submission.
columns.reference: ICH M8 eCTD Specification; FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide; EMA eCTD Guidance

columns.name: follow_up_actions_required
columns.description: Indicates whether this interaction generated one or more follow-up action items that require tracking and completion (e.g., additional data requests, protocol amendments, label negotiations, post-approval commitments). Drives workflow routing in the regulatory affairs team.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA Meeting Minutes Guidance; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: follow_up_due_date
columns.description: The deadline by which all follow-up actions arising from this interaction must be completed. Null if follow_up_actions_required is False or if no specific deadline was established. Used for regulatory affairs workload planning and compliance monitoring.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA Meeting Minutes Guidance

columns.name: health_authority_division
columns.description: The specific division, office, or committee within the health authority responsible for this interaction (e.g., FDA CDER Office of Oncology Products, EMA Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP), PMDA Office of New Drug I). Enables granular tracking of agency relationships and division-specific regulatory strategies.
columns.reference: FDA CDER/CBER Organizational Structure; EMA Committee Structure; ICH M4

columns.name: interaction_date
columns.description: The principal real-world date on which the interaction occurred — the meeting date for in-person/teleconference interactions, or the date a written communication was received or sent. Serves as the BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP (date precision) for this transaction. For written correspondence, this is the document date on the letter or communication.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: interaction_format
columns.description: The modality or format through which the health authority interaction took place. Distinguishes between in-person meetings, teleconferences, videoconferences, hybrid formats, and written-only communications. Critical for meeting management and regulatory strategy documentation.
columns.reference: FDA Guidance for Industry: Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: interaction_reference_number
columns.description: Externally-known tracking number or correspondence control number assigned to this interaction, either by the health authority (e.g., FDA meeting request number, EMA procedure number) or by the company's RIMS/Veeva Vault RIM system. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this transaction. Used for cross-referencing with agency correspondence and eCTD submissions.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA PDUFA Meeting Management Guidance; EMA Scientific Advice Procedure

columns.name: interaction_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the health authority interaction record. Tracks the workflow from initial drafting through scheduling, execution, and closure. 'Overdue' indicates a response deadline has been missed. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS for this transaction header. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|submitted|scheduled|in_progress|completed|cancelled|overdue — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA PDUFA Meeting Management Guidance

columns.name: interaction_type
columns.description: Classification of the health authority interaction by formal category. Covers FDA meeting types (Type A, Type B, Type B EOP, Type C), EMA scientific advice, pre-submission meetings, advisory committee meetings, written correspondence types (information request, complete response letter, deficiency letter, acknowledgment letter, approval letter, agency query, general correspondence), and PAI interactions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: type_a_meeting|type_b_meeting|type_b_eop_meeting|type_c_meeting|scientific_advice|pre_submission_meeting|advisory_committee|information_request|complete_response_letter|deficiency_letter|acknowledgment_letter|approval_letter|agency_query|general_correspondence|pai_interaction — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: FDA Guidance for Industry: Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants; EMA Scientific Advice and Protocol Assistance Procedure; ICH Q8/Q9/Q10

columns.name: meeting_category
columns.glossary_term: FDA Meeting Category / EMA Scientific Advice Category
columns.description: For meeting-type interactions, the formal FDA meeting category (Type A: dispute resolution/clinical hold; Type B: pre-IND, end-of-phase, pre-NDA/BLA; Type C: all others) or EMA scientific advice category. Drives PDUFA response timeline obligations. Set to 'not_applicable' for written correspondence interactions.
columns.reference: FDA Guidance for Industry: Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants (PDUFA VI); EMA Scientific Advice and Protocol Assistance

columns.name: minutes_document_reference
columns.description: Document reference number or Veeva Vault document ID for the official meeting minutes or written record of the interaction outcome. For written correspondence, references the agency letter or response document. Null for interactions where minutes are not yet finalized.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA Meeting Minutes Guidance; EMA Scientific Advice Outcome Letter

columns.name: pai_related
columns.description: Indicates whether this interaction is associated with a Pre-Approval Inspection (PAI) by the health authority, including inspection scheduling, outcome discussions, or corrective action follow-up. Enables filtering of PAI-related regulatory communications.
columns.reference: FDA PAI Guidance; 21 CFR Parts 210/211; EMA GMP Inspection Procedures

columns.name: participant_count
columns.description: Total number of participants (combined company and agency attendees) in this interaction. Applicable primarily to meeting-type interactions. Used for meeting logistics and engagement analytics.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA Meeting Management Guidance

columns.name: pdufa_clock_impact
columns.description: Indicates whether this interaction has an impact on the PDUFA review clock (e.g., a complete response letter resets the clock; an information request may pause it). True if the interaction affects the regulatory review timeline clock. Applicable to FDA interactions only; False or null for non-FDA interactions.
columns.reference: FDA PDUFA VI Commitment Letter; 21 CFR Part 314.102; FDA Guidance on Review Clock

columns.name: rems_related
columns.glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Related Flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this health authority interaction is related to a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program, including REMS design, modification, assessment, or compliance discussions. Enables filtering of REMS-specific regulatory communications.
columns.reference: FDA REMS Guidance; 21 CFR Part 314.520; FDAAA Section 505-1

columns.name: response_due_date
columns.description: Regulatory deadline by which the company must respond to an inbound health authority communication (e.g., information request, deficiency letter, complete response letter). Critical for compliance monitoring and PDUFA/EMA clock management. Null for outbound-only interactions.
columns.reference: FDA PDUFA; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; 21 CFR Part 314.110

columns.name: response_submitted_date
columns.description: Actual date on which the company submitted its response to the health authority for inbound communications. Compared against response_due_date to assess timeline compliance. Null if no response has been submitted yet.
columns.reference: FDA PDUFA; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: response_timeline_compliant
columns.description: Indicates whether the company's response to this health authority interaction was submitted within the required regulatory deadline (response_due_date). True if response_submitted_date is on or before response_due_date. Null if no response is required or if the response has not yet been submitted.
columns.reference: FDA PDUFA; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; 21 CFR Part 314.110

columns.name: scheduled_date
columns.description: The originally scheduled or planned date for the interaction, particularly for meetings. Distinct from interaction_date (actual occurrence date) to enable tracking of rescheduling events and planning accuracy. Applicable primarily to meeting-type interactions.
columns.reference: FDA Guidance for Industry: Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: source_system_record_reference
columns.description: The native record identifier from the source system of record (Veeva Vault RIM correspondence or meeting module document ID) from which this interaction record was ingested. Enables traceability back to the operational system for audit and reconciliation purposes.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records; ICH Q10

columns.name: submission_date
columns.description: Date on which the company submitted the meeting request, briefing document, or written correspondence to the health authority. Used to calculate agency review timelines and PDUFA clock start dates. Distinct from interaction_date (when the meeting/response occurred).
columns.reference: FDA PDUFA Meeting Management Guidance; EMA Scientific Advice Procedure; 21 CFR Part 312.47

columns.name: therapeutic_area
columns.description: The therapeutic area or disease indication relevant to this health authority interaction (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Enables cross-portfolio analytics and regulatory strategy alignment by therapeutic area.
columns.reference: ATC Classification; ICH E8; FDA CDER Therapeutic Area Guidance

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this health authority interaction record was last modified in the silver layer data product. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED field for this transaction header. Updated on every write operation to support change data capture and audit trail requirements.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Conventions

tables.name: dmf
tables.description: Drug Master File (DMF) registry tracking all DMFs filed with health authorities for APIs, excipients, packaging materials, and manufacturing sites. Captures DMF number, DMF type (Type I-V), holder name, subject of DMF, filing date, last annual update date, authorization letters issued, and associated products referencing the DMF. Supports CMC regulatory strategy and third-party supplier qualification. Aligns with 21 CFR 314.420 and EMA DMF guidelines.

columns.name: dmf_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the Drug Master File (DMF) record in the regulatory data product. Primary key for the dmf entity.

columns.name: drug_master_file_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.drug_master_file. Business justification: regulatory.dmf and intellectual.drug_master_file represent the same business artifact from regulatory filing and IP/licensing perspectives respectively. CMC regulatory strategy and IP protection coord

columns.name: drug_substance_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_substance. Business justification: DMFs (Drug Master Files) are regulatory filings submitted to health authorities specifically for drug substances (APIs), not finished products. Regulatory CMC review, DMF authorization letters, and cr

columns.name: health_authority_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.health_authority. Business justification: Drug Master Files are filed with specific health authorities (FDA, EMA, etc.). Currently dmf has only an incoming FK from dossier_document, making it nearly siloed. Adding health_authority_id links DM

columns.name: holder_business_partner_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.business_partner. Business justification: DMF holders are often external suppliers or CMOs who are business partners in the ERP/MDM system. Linking DMF to business_partner enables supplier qualification tracking, GMP certificate management, a

columns.name: holder_legal_entity_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: DMF holders are legal entities that own drug master files. Regulatory compliance requires tracking the legal entity for authorization letters, annual updates, and cross-referencing in NDAs/ANDAs. Hold

columns.name: manufacturing_plant_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.plant. Business justification: dmf.manufacturing_site_name is a plain-text denormalization of the plant. DMFs are site-specific regulatory filings; a proper FK to masterdata.plant enables GMP inspection scheduling, PAI readiness tr

columns.name: manufacturing_site_country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: DMF manufacturing site jurisdiction determines applicable GMP standards, inspection authority, and regulatory pathway. Critical for CMC assessment and supply chain risk management. Manufacturing_site_

columns.name: patent_family_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_family. Business justification: DMFs for drug substances and manufacturing processes reference the patent family protecting the CMC subject matter. Regulatory CMC strategy requires knowing which patent family covers the DMF to asses

columns.name: site_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to manufacturing.site. Business justification: Drug Master Files are filed for specific manufacturing sites — the DMF covers the manufacturing process at a named site. dmf.manufacturing_site_name is a denormalized text field; replacing with site_i

columns.name: submission_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: Drug Master Files are filed with health authorities via regulatory submissions. The DMF filing event is a submission, and subsequent amendments are also filed as submissions. Linking dmf to its origin

columns.name: amendment_count
columns.description: Total number of amendments submitted to the health authority for this DMF since the original filing date. Reflects the change history and regulatory maintenance activity for the DMF.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

columns.name: authorization_letter_date
columns.glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Authorization Letter Date
columns.description: Date on which the most recent Letter of Authorization (LoA) was issued by the DMF holder to the referencing applicant. Null if no authorization letter has been issued.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420(d); FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

columns.name: authorization_letter_issued
columns.glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Authorization Letter Issued
columns.description: Indicates whether the DMF holder has issued a Letter of Authorization (LoA) to the referencing applicant, granting the health authority permission to review the confidential DMF contents in support of an NDA, BLA, or ANDA submission.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420(d); FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

columns.name: cmc_section
columns.description: Identifies the specific Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) section of the eCTD/CTD dossier (Module 3) to which this DMF contributes. Used to map DMF content to the corresponding CTD section in NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
columns.reference: ICH M4Q (CTD Module 3); ICH Q11; 21 CFR 314.420

columns.name: confidentiality_commitment
columns.description: Indicates whether the DMF holder has provided a formal confidentiality commitment to the referencing company, ensuring that proprietary manufacturing information disclosed in the DMF will not be shared beyond the regulatory review context.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry; GDPR Article 28

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this DMF record was first created in the regulatory data product. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); ICH Q10

columns.name: deficiency_letter_received
columns.glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Deficiency Letter Received
columns.description: Indicates whether the health authority has issued a deficiency letter (also known as a Complete Response Letter or information request) identifying gaps or issues in the DMF that must be addressed before the referencing application can be approved.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry; EMA DMF Guidelines

columns.name: deficiency_response_due_date
columns.glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Deficiency Response Due Date
columns.description: Deadline by which the DMF holder must respond to a deficiency letter issued by the health authority. Null if no deficiency letter has been received. Critical for regulatory timeline management.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

columns.name: dmf_number
columns.description: Official DMF number assigned by the health authority (e.g., FDA) upon receipt of the filing. Serves as the externally-known unique identifier for the DMF across regulatory submissions and CMC dossiers.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance; EMA DMF Guidelines

columns.name: dmf_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the DMF with the health authority. Active indicates the DMF is in good standing and available for reference; withdrawn indicates the holder has withdrawn the filing; closed indicates the authority has closed the file.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry; EMA DMF Guidelines

columns.name: dmf_type
columns.description: Classification of the DMF per FDA categorization: Type I (Manufacturing Site, Facilities, Operating Procedures, and Personnel), Type II (Drug Substance, Drug Substance Intermediate, and Material Used in Their Preparation, or Drug Product), Type III (Packaging Material), Type IV (Excipient, Colorant, Flavor, Essence, or Material Used in Their Preparation), Type V (FDA-Accepted Reference Information).
columns.value_regex: Type I|Type II|Type III|Type IV|Type V
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

columns.name: ectd_sequence_number
columns.glossary_term: Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Sequence Number
columns.description: Four-digit eCTD sequence number of the most recent submission lifecycle for this DMF. Used to track the current version of the eCTD dossier in the health authority's document management system.
columns.reference: ICH M8 (eCTD); FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide

columns.name: filing_date
columns.description: Date on which the DMF was originally submitted and received by the health authority. Establishes the official filing date of record for regulatory and IP purposes.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

columns.name: gmp_certificate_expiry_date
columns.glossary_term: Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Certificate Expiry Date
columns.description: Expiry date of the current GMP certificate associated with the manufacturing site in the DMF. Used to trigger renewal activities and assess supplier qualification status.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Parts 210-211; EMA GMP Guidelines; PIC/S; cGMP

columns.name: gmp_certificate_number
columns.description: Certificate number of the current Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) certificate issued by a competent authority for the manufacturing site referenced in the DMF. Supports supplier qualification and PAI readiness.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Parts 210-211; EMA GMP Guidelines; PIC/S; cGMP

columns.name: internal_owner
columns.description: Name or employee identifier of the internal regulatory affairs professional responsible for managing this DMF relationship, tracking updates, and coordinating authorization letters with the DMF holder.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; Veeva Vault RIM; ICH Q10

columns.name: last_amendment_date
columns.glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Last Amendment Date
columns.description: Date of the most recent amendment submitted to the health authority for this DMF. Used to assess currency of the DMF content and identify DMFs requiring review.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

columns.name: last_annual_update_date
columns.glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Last Annual Update Date
columns.description: Date of the most recent annual update submitted to the health authority to confirm the DMF remains current and accurate. FDA requires annual updates under 21 CFR 314.420(c). Failure to update may result in DMF inactivation.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420(c); FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

columns.name: next_annual_update_due_date
columns.glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Next Annual Update Due Date
columns.description: Calculated due date for the next mandatory annual update submission to the health authority. Used for proactive compliance tracking and regulatory calendar management.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420(c); FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

columns.name: pai_status
columns.description: Current status of the Pre-Approval Inspection (PAI) for the manufacturing site or process covered by this DMF. PAI is conducted by FDA or other health authorities prior to approval of an NDA/BLA referencing this DMF. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: not_initiated|scheduled|completed|passed|failed|pending_response — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 21 CFR Parts 210-211; FDA PAI Guidance; EMA GMP Inspection Procedures

columns.name: strategic_importance
columns.description: Internal classification of the strategic importance of this DMF to the company's product portfolio and supply chain. Critical indicates sole-source supplier for a marketed product; high indicates key supplier for pipeline assets; medium/low for non-critical materials.
columns.reference: ICH Q10; FDA Supply Chain Guidance; Internal CMC Regulatory Strategy

columns.name: subject
columns.description: Detailed description of the subject matter covered by the DMF, such as the specific API, excipient, packaging component, or manufacturing site. Aligns with the 'Subject of DMF' field in FDA eCTD submissions.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA eCTD Guidance; ICH M4 (CTD)

columns.name: submission_format
columns.description: Format in which the DMF was submitted to the health authority: eCTD (Electronic Common Technical Document), paper, or NeeS (Non-eCTD Electronic Submission). FDA mandates eCTD for most submissions since 2017.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA eCTD Guidance; ICH M8 (eCTD)

columns.name: title
columns.description: Official title or subject description of the DMF as submitted to the health authority, describing the substance, material, site, or process covered by the filing.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this DMF record in the regulatory data product. Supports change tracking, audit trail compliance, and data freshness monitoring.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); ICH Q10

columns.name: veeva_vault_document_reference
columns.glossary_term: Veeva Vault Regulatory Information Management (RIM) Document ID
columns.description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault RIM (Regulatory Information Management System) corresponding to this DMF record. Enables traceability between the data product and the source system of record for regulatory document management.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures)

columns.name: withdrawal_date
columns.description: Date on which the DMF was formally withdrawn by the holder or closed by the health authority. Null for active DMFs. Used to manage the lifecycle of supplier relationships and assess impact on referencing applications.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

tables.name: label
tables.description: Single source of truth for approved product labeling (prescribing information, package insert, patient information leaflet, SmPC) and complete change history across all markets and languages. Tracks current label version, effective date, approval date, market/country, language, label type, content sections, and lifecycle status. Maintains full amendment history including change reason (safety update, new indication, dosage modification, black box warning), change type (agency-initiated, company-initiated), regulatory basis, affected sections, submission reference, and implementation status across markets. SSOT for both current approved labeling and all historical label changes — no separate label change product exists. Integrates with Veeva Vault PromoMats and RIM.

columns.name: black_box_warning
columns.description: Indicates whether this label version contains an FDA Boxed Warning (Black Box Warning) — the most serious warning required by the FDA for drugs with significant risk of serious or life-threatening adverse effects. True = boxed warning present; False = no boxed warning.

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: safety_update|new_indication|dosage_modification|contraindication_update|drug_interaction_update|pediatric_labeling|geriatric_labeling|pregnancy_labeling|administrative_update — promote to reference product]

columns.name: change_type
columns.description: Classification of the type of change that resulted in this label version. Agency-initiated: required by health authority; Company-initiated: proposed by the marketing authorization holder; Labeling Supplement: formal supplement submission; Prior Approval Supplement (PAS): requires FDA approval before implementation; Changes Being Effected (CBE): can be implemented before FDA approval; Annual Report: minor changes reported annually. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: agency_initiated|company_initiated|labeling_supplement|prior_approval_supplement|cbee|annual_report — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Post-Authorisation Procedures; FDA Labeling Supplement Guidance

columns.name: dosage_form
columns.description: Pharmaceutical dosage form of the drug product as stated on this label (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, solution, cream). Reflects the finished dosage form (FDF) classification per the approved label.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 201.56; EMA SmPC Section 3; ICH M4; WHO Pharmaceutical Dosage Forms

columns.name: ectd_sequence_number
columns.glossary_term: Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Sequence Number
columns.description: The eCTD sequence number of the regulatory submission dossier in which this label version was submitted to the health authority. Four-digit zero-padded sequence number per eCTD specification (e.g., 0001, 0025). Enables direct traceability to the eCTD submission package.
columns.reference: ICH M8 eCTD Specification; FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide; EMA eCTD Guideline; 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: effective_date
columns.description: Date from which this label version is commercially effective and must be used on marketed product packaging. May differ from approval date due to implementation timelines or transition periods.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 201.56; EMA SmPC Guideline; FDA Labeling Guidance; ICH M4

columns.name: implementation_deadline
columns.description: Regulatory or company-mandated deadline by which the new label version must be implemented on marketed product packaging. Critical for compliance tracking, especially for safety-driven label changes with mandatory implementation timelines.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Variation Regulation; FDA Safety Labeling Changes Guidance

columns.name: implementation_status
columns.description: Operational status of the label implementation across markets and packaging lines. Pending: implementation not yet started; In Progress: packaging/artwork updates underway; Implemented: new label in use on marketed product; Overdue: implementation deadline passed without completion; Not Applicable: label change does not require physical implementation.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 201; EMA SmPC Guideline; GDP Guidelines; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: is_current_version
columns.description: Indicates whether this label record represents the currently approved and active version for the given product, market, language, and label type combination. True = current approved version; False = historical/superseded version. Enables efficient querying of the current label without date-range filtering.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Post-Authorisation Procedures

columns.name: label_number
columns.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the label document, typically assigned by the regulatory information management system (RIMS) or Veeva Vault RIM (e.g., LBL-2024-00123). Used for cross-system traceability.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA Structured Product Labeling (SPL); 21 CFR Part 201

columns.name: label_type
columns.description: Classification of the label document by its regulatory format and intended audience. Prescribing Information (PI) and Package Insert (PI) are US formats; Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC) is the EU/EMA format; Patient Information Leaflet (PIL) is the patient-facing EU document; Medication Guide and Instructions for Use (IFU) are FDA-specific formats.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 201; EMA Guideline on SmPC; ICH M4; FDA Labeling Guidance

columns.name: language_code
columns.description: IETF BCP 47 / ISO 639 language code for the language of this label version (e.g., en, fr, de, ja, zh-CN). Supports multi-language label management across global markets.
columns.reference: ISO 639; IETF BCP 47; EMA SmPC Guideline; ICH M4

columns.name: lifecycle_status
columns.description: Current state of the label version within its regulatory lifecycle. Draft: in preparation; Under Review: submitted to health authority or under internal review; Approved: currently approved and in force; Superseded: replaced by a newer version; Withdrawn: removed from market; Archived: historical record retained for compliance.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Post-Authorisation Procedures; ICH Q10

columns.name: marketing_authorization_number
columns.description: The marketing authorization (MA) or product license number assigned by the health authority for the approved drug product in the relevant market (e.g., NDA 123456 for FDA, EU/1/24/1234 for EMA centralized procedure). Links the label to the formal marketing authorization.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.105; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; MHRA Human Medicines Regulations 2012; PMDA Pharmaceutical Affairs Law

columns.name: ndc_code
columns.description: FDA-assigned National Drug Code (NDC) for the drug product associated with this label. The NDC is a unique 10-digit, 3-segment number identifying the labeler, product, and trade package size. Applicable for US market labels only.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 207; FDA NDC Directory; FDA Labeling Guidance

columns.name: product_name
columns.description: Brand/trade name of the drug product as it appears on this label version. Captured directly on the label record to preserve the exact name at the time of approval, which may differ from the current master product name.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 201.10; EMA SmPC Section 1; ICH M4; WHO INN Programme

columns.name: regulatory_basis
columns.description: The regulatory or scientific basis justifying this label version change (e.g., 'Post-market safety study PMSS-2024-001', 'PSUR cycle 5 findings', 'FDA safety communication dated 2024-03-15', 'Pediatric study per PREA'). Provides the evidentiary foundation for the label amendment.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Variation Regulation; FDA PREA; ICH E2C(R2) PSUR Guideline

columns.name: rems_required
columns.glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Required Flag
columns.description: Indicates whether a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program is required for this drug product as referenced in this label version. True = REMS required; False = no REMS requirement.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.520; FDA REMS Guidance; FDAAA Section 505-1

columns.name: route_of_administration

columns.name: strength

columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 201.56; EMA SmPC Section 3; ICH M4; USP

columns.name: superseded_date

columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Post-Authorisation Procedures; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: therapeutic_area
columns.description: Primary therapeutic area or disease area for which the drug product is approved as reflected in this label (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular, Neurology). Supports portfolio-level label analytics and regulatory reporting.

columns.name: updated_timestamp

columns.name: version_number

columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Guideline on Summary of Product Characteristics

Critical for pharmacovigilance-driven label updates and post-approval lifecycle management.

columns.name: implementation_status

columns.name: initiator_type

columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.70; FDA Labeling Guidance; EMA GVP Module IX; ICH E2D

columns.name: is_black_box_warning

columns.name: is_pv_driven

tables.name: post_approval_commitment

Monitors compliance with FDA PMR/PMC requirements under FDAAA and EMA post-authorization measures. Provides both executive-level commitment status and operational task-level progress tracking in a single entity. SSOT for all regulatory obligation tracking — no separate action-level product exists.

tables.name: dmf_cross_reference
tables.description: This association product represents the formal Cross-Reference Authorization between a Drug Master File (DMF) and a regulatory application. It captures the operational record of a sponsor's authorization to cite a specific DMF within a specific application, including the Letter of Authorization (LoA) lifecycle, FDA-assigned cross-reference identifiers, and access grant status. Each record links one DMF to one regulatory application and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this specific DMF-application cross-reference relationship, in accordance with 21 CFR 314.420 and FDA DMF guidance.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical regulatory practice, a single DMF (e.g., an API Drug Master File) is formally cross-referenced by multiple NDA/BLA/ANDA applications from one or more sponsors, and a single application routinely references multiple DMFs (e.g., one for the API, one for the excipient, one for the packaging material, one for the manufacturing site). This cross-referencing process is a formally managed business activity: the DMF holder must issue a Letter of Authorization (LoA) to each referencing applicant, the FDA tracks each cross-reference explicitly, and each authorization has its own lifecycle, reference number, and correspondence history. The relationship is not derivable from transactional joins — it is an operational record that regulatory affairs professionals actively create, update, and manage.

It is a denormalized summary that can be computed from the dmf_cross_reference association table (COUNT of application_id grouped by dmf_id). Storing it on the DMF entity creates a maintenance burden and data integrity risk. It should be removed from dmf and derived from this association.]
