columns.description: Indicates whether the node is qualified and authorized to handle clinical trial investigational medicinal products (IMPs) in addition to commercial supply. Clinical supply nodes must comply with GCP and GMP requirements.
columns.reference: GCP ICH E6(R2); GMP 21 CFR Part 312; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014

columns.name: cold_chain_certified
columns.description: Indicates whether the node holds a valid cold chain certification from a recognized body (e.g., IATA CEIV Pharma, GDP cold chain qualification). Required for handling temperature-sensitive biologics, vaccines, and specialty medicines.
columns.reference: IATA CEIV Pharma; GDP Guidelines (EU 2013/C 343/01); WHO TRS 961; ICH Q1A(R2)

columns.name: controlled_substance_authorized
columns.description: Indicates whether the node is authorized by the DEA (or equivalent national authority) to store and distribute controlled substances. Nodes without this authorization cannot be assigned to controlled substance distribution lanes.
columns.reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301; UN Convention on Psychotropic Substances; INCB

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this distribution network node record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.

columns.name: dea_registration_number
columns.description: DEA registration number authorizing the node to handle Schedule I–V controlled substances. Required for US-based nodes handling controlled pharmaceutical products. Null for non-US nodes or nodes not handling controlled substances.
columns.reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301; DEA 21 CFR Part 1304

columns.name: effective_end_date
columns.description: Date on which this distribution network node is scheduled to cease operations or be decommissioned. Null for currently active nodes with no planned end date. Used for network transition planning.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; Kinaxis RapidResponse; GDP Guidelines (EU 2013/C 343/01)

columns.name: effective_start_date
columns.description: Date from which this distribution network node became or is scheduled to become operationally active in the supply network. Used for time-phased network planning and historical network topology analysis.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; Kinaxis RapidResponse; GDP Guidelines (EU 2013/C 343/01)

columns.name: gdp_authorization_expiry_date
columns.glossary_term: Good Distribution Practice (GDP) Authorization Expiry Date
columns.description: Date on which the GDP wholesale distribution authorization expires. Supply planning systems must alert when expiry is approaching to prevent distribution through unauthorized nodes.

columns.name: gdp_authorization_number
columns.description: Official GDP wholesale distribution authorization number issued by the competent regulatory authority (e.g., MHRA, national competent authority). Required for regulatory traceability and audit purposes.

columns.name: gdp_authorization_status
columns.description: Current GDP authorization status of the node as required by EU GDP Guidelines (2013/C 343/01) and equivalent national regulations. Authorized nodes are eligible to handle medicinal products. Expired or suspended nodes must be excluded from active distribution lanes.
columns.reference: GDP Guidelines (EU 2013/C 343/01); MHRA GDP Guidelines; WHO Technical Report Series No. 957

columns.name: handling_time_days
columns.description: Number of calendar days required for internal processing activities at the node (receiving, quality inspection, pick/pack, dispatch preparation). Added to lead times in supply planning calculations.
columns.reference: Kinaxis RapidResponse; SAP S/4HANA WM; Blue Yonder

columns.name: hazmat_capable
columns.description: Indicates whether the node is certified to store and handle hazardous materials including cytotoxic compounds, flammable solvents, and other regulated substances. Relevant for oncology API and certain excipient handling.
columns.reference: IATA DGR; IMDG Code; 49 CFR (US DOT Hazmat); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119

columns.name: inbound_lead_time_days
columns.description: Standard number of calendar days required for inbound shipments to arrive at this node from its upstream supply source. Used as a planning parameter in Kinaxis RapidResponse and SAP APO/IBP for replenishment scheduling.
columns.reference: Kinaxis RapidResponse; Blue Yonder; SAP APO/IBP

columns.name: last_updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this distribution network node record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, audit trail, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.

columns.name: multi_temperature_capable
columns.description: Indicates whether the node can simultaneously handle multiple temperature zones (e.g., both ambient and refrigerated storage). Enables assignment of mixed-temperature product portfolios to a single node in supply network planning.
columns.reference: ICH Q1A(R2); GDP Guidelines (EU 2013/C 343/01); Kinaxis RapidResponse

columns.name: network_tier
columns.description: Hierarchical tier classification of the node within the distribution network topology. Tier 1 = primary manufacturing/central DC; Tier 2 = regional DC; Tier 3 = local/last-mile node. Drives network optimization and replenishment hierarchy in supply planning.
columns.reference: Kinaxis RapidResponse; Blue Yonder; SAP APO/IBP

columns.name: node_code
columns.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this distribution network node across supply chain planning systems (Kinaxis RapidResponse, Blue Yonder, SAP APO/IBP). Used as the business key for cross-system integration and network lane definitions.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; Kinaxis RapidResponse; Blue Yonder

columns.name: node_name
columns.description: Human-readable name of the distribution network node (e.g., 'Frankfurt Regional DC', 'Chicago 3PL Hub', 'Singapore Manufacturing Site'). Used in supply chain planning dashboards and network topology reports.

columns.name: node_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the distribution network node. Inactive or suspended nodes are excluded from supply planning runs. Nodes under qualification are pending GDP or regulatory authorization review.
columns.reference: GDP Guidelines (EU 2013/C 343/01); 21 CFR Part 211; SAP S/4HANA MM

columns.name: node_type
columns.description: Classification of the network node by its functional role in the pharmaceutical supply chain. Drives planning logic, GDP compliance requirements, and lane eligibility in Kinaxis RapidResponse and SAP APO/IBP. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: manufacturing_site|distribution_center|3pl_node|wholesaler|direct_to_pharmacy|clinical_depot|hospital_pharmacy|specialty_pharmacy — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: GDP Guidelines (EU 2013/C 343/01); SAP S/4HANA MM; Kinaxis RapidResponse

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text field for capturing operational notes, special handling instructions, or qualifications relevant to this distribution network node. Examples include specific GDP deviation history, special import/export restrictions, or infrastructure constraints.

columns.name: operator_type
columns.description: Classification of the entity operating the distribution node. Distinguishes between internally operated sites and third-party operators such as 3PL (Third-Party Logistics), CMO (Contract Manufacturing Organization), CDMO (Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization), or wholesalers.
columns.reference: GDP Guidelines (EU 2013/C 343/01); SAP S/4HANA MM; Kinaxis RapidResponse

columns.name: outbound_lead_time_days
columns.description: Standard number of calendar days required for outbound shipments to depart this node and reach the next downstream node or customer. Used for delivery commitment and supply planning in Kinaxis RapidResponse.
columns.reference: Kinaxis RapidResponse; Blue Yonder; SAP APO/IBP

columns.name: pallet_capacity
columns.description: Maximum number of standard pallets (EUR/ISO pallet) the node can accommodate simultaneously. Used for operational capacity planning and inbound/outbound throughput modeling in supply network planning tools.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA WM; Kinaxis RapidResponse; ISO 6780 (Flat Pallets)

columns.name: quarantine_zone_available
columns.description: Indicates whether the node has a dedicated physical quarantine zone for holding materials pending quality release, investigation, or returns processing. Required for GDP-compliant nodes handling pharmaceutical products.
columns.reference: GDP Guidelines (EU 2013/C 343/01); 21 CFR Part 211.84; SAP S/4HANA QM

columns.name: region
columns.description: Internal geographic region classification for the node (e.g., 'EMEA', 'APAC', 'North America', 'LATAM'). Used for regional supply planning segmentation in Kinaxis RapidResponse and Blue Yonder.
columns.reference: Kinaxis RapidResponse; Blue Yonder; SAP APO/IBP

columns.name: sap_plant_code
columns.description: Four-character SAP plant code assigned to this distribution network node in SAP S/4HANA MM/WM/PP modules. Used for cross-system integration between supply planning tools (Kinaxis, Blue Yonder) and SAP ERP for inventory and production order management.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; SAP S/4HANA WM; SAP APO/IBP

columns.name: sap_storage_location_code
columns.description: SAP storage location code within the plant, representing the primary storage location for this node in SAP S/4HANA WM. Used for inventory posting, goods receipt, and goods issue transactions.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA WM; SAP S/4HANA MM

columns.name: serialization_capable
columns.description: Indicates whether the node is equipped to scan, verify, and process serialized pharmaceutical packaging as required by DSCSA (US) and EU FMD (Falsified Medicines Directive) track-and-trace regulations.
columns.reference: DSCSA (Drug Supply Chain Security Act); EU FMD Directive 2011/62/EU; 21 CFR Part 203

columns.name: storage_capacity_m3
columns.description: Total physical storage capacity of the node measured in cubic meters. Used for capacity planning, network optimization, and inventory allocation decisions in Kinaxis RapidResponse and SAP WM.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA WM; Kinaxis RapidResponse; Blue Yonder

columns.name: temperature_zone
columns.description: Primary temperature storage zone capability of the node. Defines the cold-chain handling classification: ambient (15–25°C), CRT (Controlled Room Temperature, 15–30°C), refrigerated (2–8°C), frozen (-20°C), or ultra-low temperature (-80°C). Critical for product-to-node assignment in supply planning.
columns.reference: ICH Q1A(R2); USP <1079>; GDP Guidelines (EU 2013/C 343/01); WHO TRS 961

columns.name: warehouse_zone_count
columns.description: Number of distinct storage zones configured within the node (e.g., quarantine zone, approved stock zone, returns zone, controlled substance vault). Reflects the physical warehouse layout complexity in SAP WM.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA WM; GDP Guidelines (EU 2013/C 343/01); 21 CFR Part 211.68

tables.name: clinical_supply_order
tables.description: Supply order for investigational medicinal products (IMPs), comparators, and ancillary supplies destined for clinical trial sites. Captures IMP material code, protocol number, study site, randomization kit number, ordered quantity, blinding requirements, expiry date, cold-chain requirements, import/export permit references, and order status. Distinct from commercial sales orders due to IND/CTA regulatory requirements, blinding, and randomization constraints.

columns.name: clinical_supply_order_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the clinical supply order record in the lakehouse Silver layer. Primary key for this entity.

columns.name: batch_record_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to manufacturing.batch_record. Business justification: QP release for clinical trial supplies requires the batch record to be directly referenced on the clinical supply order. EU GMP Annex 13 and FDA 21 CFR Part 312 mandate batch record traceability for i

columns.name: compound_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.compound. Business justification: Clinical trials order specific investigational compounds identified in IND/CTA applications. Essential for clinical supply chain management linking discovery assets to trial execution, regulatory subm

columns.name: courier_business_partner_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.business_partner. Business justification: clinical_supply_order.courier_name is a denormalized plain-text field. Linking to masterdata.business_partner enables courier qualification tracking, GDP compliance verification, and clinical supply c

columns.name: destination_country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: clinical_supply_order.destination_country_code is a denormalized plain-text field. Linking to masterdata.country enables import permit validation, clinical trial regulatory compliance checks, and coun

columns.name: distribution_network_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to supply.distribution_network. Business justification: clinical_supply_order has supply_depot_code as a free-text string identifying the supply depot from which the IMP is shipped. Adding distribution_network_id → distribution_network.distribution_network

columns.name: drug_product_id

columns.name: patent_id

columns.name: patient_enrollment_id

columns.name: plan_id

IND/CTA regulatory submissions and QP release require direct traceability from the clinical supply order to the production order

columns.name: unit_of_measure_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.unit_of_measure. Business justification: clinical_supply_order.quantity_unit_of_measure is a denormalized plain-text UOM. Linking to masterdata.unit_of_measure enforces 3NF and ensures validated UOM master data for IRT system reconciliation

columns.name: actual_delivery_date
columns.description: The date on which the clinical supply was confirmed as received at the investigational site. Compared against required_delivery_date to assess supply chain performance and site readiness.

columns.name: approved_quantity
columns.description: The quantity of IMP or ancillary supply formally approved for fulfilment after clinical supply review. May differ from ordered_quantity due to stock availability, protocol amendments, or QP release constraints.
columns.reference: EU GMP Annex 13; ICH Q10; 21 CFR Parts 210/211

columns.name: blinding_type
columns.description: Specifies the blinding methodology applied to this supply order as defined in the clinical protocol. Determines labelling, packaging, and handling requirements for the IMP to maintain trial integrity.
columns.reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) GCP; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: cancellation_reason
columns.description: Free-text description of the reason for cancellation when order_status is 'Cancelled'. Captures business justification for audit trail and supply planning analysis (e.g., protocol amendment, site closure, stock recall).
columns.reference: ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 11; EU GMP Annex 13

columns.name: cold_chain_required
columns.description: Indicates whether this supply order requires cold-chain logistics (True) due to temperature-sensitive IMP storage and transport conditions. Triggers cold-chain packaging, monitoring, and carrier selection in the distribution workflow.
columns.reference: GDP Guidelines (EU) 2013/C 343/01; WHO Technical Report Series No. 961 Annex 9; 21 CFR Parts 210/211

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: The date and time when this clinical supply order record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and EU Annex 11.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; EU Annex 11; ICH Q10

columns.name: dispensing_unit
columns.description: Description of the dispensing unit configuration for the IMP as packaged for clinical trial use (e.g., 'Blinded kit of 28 tablets', '1 vial 10mg/mL'). Supports site pharmacist dispensing and accountability records.
columns.reference: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Parts 210/211; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: export_permit_number
columns.description: Reference number of the export permit or authorisation issued by the originating country's regulatory authority for the shipment of IMP across international borders for clinical trial purposes.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312; EU Regulation 536/2014; GDP Guidelines (EU) 2013/C 343/01

columns.name: import_permit_number
columns.description: Reference number of the import permit issued by the relevant national regulatory authority (e.g., FDA, EMA member state, PMDA) authorising the importation of the IMP into the destination country for clinical trial use.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312; EU Regulation 536/2014; PMDA Clinical Trial Notification; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: ind_cta_number
columns.glossary_term: Investigational New Drug (IND) / Clinical Trial Authorisation (CTA) Number
columns.description: The regulatory filing reference number (IND number in the US per 21 CFR Part 312, or CTA number in the EU per Regulation 536/2014) under which this clinical supply order is authorised. Required for import/export permit applications and regulatory compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 312 (IND); EU Regulation 536/2014 (CTA); ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: irt_system_reference
columns.description: Reference number or transaction ID from the Interactive Response Technology (IRT) / Interactive Web Response System (IWRS) that triggered or confirmed this supply order. Links the supply event to the randomization and drug management system.
columns.reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; EU GMP Annex 13

columns.name: is_blinded
columns.description: Indicates whether this supply order is subject to blinding requirements (True) or is open-label (False). Used as a quick filter for blinding compliance checks and supply handling procedures.
columns.reference: ICH E9; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: last_updated_timestamp
columns.description: The date and time when this clinical supply order record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Required for change control audit trail under 21 CFR Part 11 and EU Annex 11.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; EU Annex 11; ICH Q10

columns.name: order_date
columns.description: The calendar date on which the clinical supply order was formally placed or submitted by the clinical supply team. This is the principal business event date for the order.
columns.reference: ICH Q10; SAP MM Purchase Order Date

columns.name: order_number
columns.description: Externally-known, human-readable order reference number assigned by the clinical supply management system (e.g., Kinaxis RapidResponse or SAP MM) to uniquely identify this supply order across systems and with third-party logistics providers.
columns.reference: ICH Q10; SAP MM Purchase Order Number convention

columns.name: order_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the clinical supply order, tracking progression from initial creation through fulfilment or cancellation. Drives supply chain workflow in Kinaxis RapidResponse / SAP MM. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Draft|Submitted|Approved|In Preparation|Shipped|Delivered|Cancelled|On Hold — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH Q10; SAP MM Order Status; GDP Guidelines (EU) 2013/C 343/01

columns.name: order_type
columns.description: Classification of the supply order by the nature of the material being ordered. IMP = investigational medicinal product; Comparator = approved reference drug; Placebo = matching placebo; Ancillary = non-IMP study supplies; Open-Label Extension = OLE phase supply; Rescue Medication = emergency/rescue supply.
columns.reference: EU GMP Annex 13; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: ordered_quantity
columns.description: The quantity of IMP or ancillary supply units requested in this order, expressed in the unit of measure defined on the IMP material master (e.g., vials, tablets, kits).
columns.reference: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Parts 210/211; ICH Q10

columns.name: priority_level
columns.description: Priority classification of the clinical supply order indicating the urgency of fulfilment. Emergency orders may be triggered by unplanned site demand, protocol deviations, or patient safety requirements.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ICH Q10; GDP Guidelines (EU) 2013/C 343/01

columns.name: qp_release_date
columns.description: The date on which the Qualified Person (QP) formally certified and released the IMP batch for clinical use. Required for EU GMP Annex 13 compliance and batch disposition records.
columns.reference: EU GMP Annex 13; EU Directive 2001/20/EC; EMA GMP Guidelines

columns.name: qualified_person_release
columns.description: Indicates whether the IMP batch included in this order has been certified and released by a Qualified Person (QP) as required by EU GMP Annex 13 and Directive 2001/20/EC before dispatch to the clinical site.
columns.reference: EU GMP Annex 13; EU Directive 2001/20/EC; EMA GMP Guidelines

columns.name: randomization_kit_number
columns.description: The unique kit number assigned by the Interactive Response Technology (IRT) or randomization system to the blinded supply kit. Links the physical supply to the randomization schedule and subject assignment. Critical for blinded trial integrity.
columns.reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; EU GMP Annex 13

columns.name: required_delivery_date
columns.description: The date by which the clinical supply must arrive at the investigational site to support the trial schedule. Used for supply chain planning and lead-time management in Kinaxis RapidResponse.

columns.name: shipment_date
columns.description: The date on which the clinical supply was physically dispatched from the originating depot or manufacturing site. Used for GDP compliance, transit time tracking, and delivery performance monitoring.

columns.name: shipped_quantity
columns.description: The actual quantity of IMP or ancillary supply physically dispatched from the manufacturing site or depot. May differ from approved_quantity due to last-minute stock adjustments or partial shipments.
columns.reference: GDP Guidelines (EU) 2013/C 343/01; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Parts 210/211

columns.name: shipping_country_code
columns.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country from which the clinical supply is dispatched. Used for import/export compliance, customs documentation, and GDP route planning.
columns.reference: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; GDP Guidelines (EU) 2013/C 343/01; 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: storage_temperature_max_c
columns.description: The maximum permissible storage and transport temperature in degrees Celsius for the IMP in this order, as specified in the IMP dossier and CoA. Used to configure cold-chain monitoring thresholds and excursion alerts.
columns.reference: ICH Q1A(R2); GDP Guidelines (EU) 2013/C 343/01; WHO TRS 961 Annex 9

columns.name: storage_temperature_min_c
columns.description: The minimum permissible storage and transport temperature in degrees Celsius for the IMP in this order, as specified in the IMP dossier and CoA. Used to configure cold-chain monitoring thresholds.
columns.reference: ICH Q1A(R2); GDP Guidelines (EU) 2013/C 343/01; WHO TRS 961 Annex 9

columns.name: tracking_number
columns.description: The courier or logistics provider's shipment tracking reference number, enabling real-time monitoring of the clinical supply in transit. Supports GDP compliance and cold-chain excursion investigation.

tables.name: product_recall
tables.description: Pharmaceutical product recall event record initiated by regulatory authority mandate or voluntary company action. Captures recall number, recall class (Class I, II, III per FDA), affected NDC, affected lot numbers, recall scope (market, distribution level), recall reason, regulatory agency notification date, press release date, customer notification status, quantity recovered, and recall closure date. Supports lot traceability and regulatory reporting obligations under 21 CFR Part 7.

columns.name: product_recall_id
columns.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the pharmaceutical product recall event record. Primary key for the product_recall data product in the supply domain.

columns.description: Foreign key linking to market.coverage_decision. Business justification: Product recall regulatory process requires notifying payers and suspending affected coverage decisions. Market access teams must identify which coverage decisions are impacted by a recall for regulato

columns.name: legal_entity_id

columns.description: Foreign key linking to manufacturing.master_batch_record. QA must identify all batches produced under that MBR version fo

columns.name: material_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.material. Business justification: Recalls must link to material master for affected specifications, regulatory data, distribution history. Critical for recall scope determination, effectiveness checks, regulatory reporting, and custom

columns.name: medicinal_product_id
columns.description: Reference to the master product record for the pharmaceutical product subject to the recall. Links to the product master data entity for product name, formulation, and therapeutic area details.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module; Master Data

columns.name: packaging_configuration_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.packaging_configuration. Business justification: Recalls in pharma are often packaging-configuration-specific (e.g., a specific blister pack size with a defective closure). FDA/EMA recall notifications require precise packaging identification. Direc

columns.name: patient_access_program_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to market.patient_access_program. Business justification: When a product recall is initiated, patient access programs dispensing the recalled product must be immediately suspended and enrolled patients notified. Patient safety compliance requires direct trac

columns.name: pv_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.pv_product. Business justification: Product recalls are often triggered by safety signals (ICSRs, SUSARs) and require coordination between supply chain and pharmacovigilance for regulatory authority notifications (FDA, EMA). Links recal

columns.name: reimbursement_policy_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to market.reimbursement_policy. Business justification: Regulatory recall notifications must identify affected reimbursement policies for suspension or amendment. Health authorities and payers require traceability from recall events to active reimbursement

columns.name: safety_signal_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.safety_signal. Business justification: Product recalls in pharma are formally triggered by validated safety signals. Regulatory agencies (FDA, EMA) require traceability from recall action back to the originating safety signal. PV and suppl

columns.name: site_id
columns.description: Reference to the manufacturing site where the affected lots were produced. Enables traceability back to the production facility for root cause investigation and regulatory inspection purposes.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 211; SAP S/4HANA PP Module; GDP Guidelines

columns.name: sku_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.sku. Business justification: Product recalls in pharma are executed at SKU level — the specific market pack (country, strength, pack size) determines customer notification scope and regulatory reporting. sku_code is denormalized;

columns.name: trial_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.trial. Business justification: Recall management requires identifying all active clinical trials using the recalled product/lot. Linking product_recall to trial enables recall teams to notify sponsors, pause dosing, and file regula

columns.name: affected_markets
columns.description: Comma-separated list of ISO 3-letter country codes (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU) identifying the countries or markets where the recalled product was distributed and where recall actions must be executed.
columns.reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; 21 CFR Part 7; EMA Recall Guidance

columns.name: cold_chain_required
columns.description: Indicates whether the recalled product requires cold-chain handling (temperature-controlled logistics) during the recovery and return process. Critical for biologics, vaccines, and temperature-sensitive drug products.
columns.reference: GDP Guidelines; WHO Cold Chain Guidelines; 21 CFR Part 211.142

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: The timestamp when the product recall record was first created in the system. Audit trail field supporting 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance and data lineage tracking.

columns.name: customer_notification_date
columns.description: The date on which direct customers (wholesalers, distributors, hospitals, pharmacies) were formally notified of the recall via recall notification letters or electronic communications.

columns.name: customer_notification_status
columns.description: Current status of the customer notification process indicating whether recall notification letters have been sent to all affected customers in the distribution chain.

columns.name: distribution_level
columns.description: The level in the distribution chain to which the recall extends. Consumer: product reached end patients/consumers; Retail: product at retail pharmacy level; Wholesale: product at wholesale distributor level; Hospital: product at hospital/clinic level; User: product at healthcare professional level.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7.3(k); FDA Recall Depth Definitions

columns.name: effectiveness_check_level
columns.description: FDA-defined effectiveness check level indicating the depth and percentage of consignees to be audited to verify recall notification receipt and product return. Level A: 100% of consignees; Level B: some percentage; Level C: 10% of consignees; Level D: 2% of consignees; Not Required: for certain recall types.
columns.value_regex: Level A|Level B|Level C|Level D|Not Required
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7.42(b); FDA Recall Effectiveness Check Guidance

columns.name: expiration_date_range
columns.glossary_term: Expiration Date Range of Affected Lots
columns.description: The expiration date range (e.g., '2024-01 to 2025-06') covering all affected lot numbers included in the recall. Assists customers and distributors in identifying recalled product on shelves and in inventory.

columns.name: gdp_compliance_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the recall execution is being conducted in compliance with Good Distribution Practice (GDP) guidelines, including proper documentation, chain of custody, and temperature-controlled handling of recovered product where applicable.
columns.reference: EU GDP Guidelines 2013/C 343/01; WHO GDP Guidelines; PIC/S

columns.name: health_hazard_assessment
columns.description: Summary of the health hazard evaluation conducted by the company's medical and regulatory teams to assess the risk to patients from the defective product. Supports recall classification and regulatory submission under 21 CFR Part 7.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7.41; FDA Health Hazard Evaluation

columns.name: initiating_agency
columns.description: The regulatory authority or company entity that initiated or mandated the recall. Identifies whether the recall was company-initiated (voluntary) or directed by a specific regulatory body such as FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, or NMPA. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|Company — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7; EMA Recall Guidance; MHRA Recall Guidance

columns.name: last_updated_timestamp
columns.description: The timestamp when the product recall record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and enables change tracking for regulatory inspection readiness.

columns.name: ndc_code
columns.description: The National Drug Code (NDC) of the affected drug product in the standard 5-4-2 format. Uniquely identifies the labeler, product, and package configuration of the recalled pharmaceutical product as registered with the FDA.

columns.name: press_release_date
columns.description: The date on which the company issued a public press release or public notification regarding the recall. Required for Class I and certain Class II recalls to inform consumers and healthcare professionals.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7; FDA Press Release Requirements

columns.name: product_disposition
columns.description: The approved method for disposing of recovered recalled product. Options include destruction, return to manufacturer, reprocessing, relabeling (where permitted), or quarantine pending further evaluation.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7; 21 CFR Part 211.204; GDP Guidelines

columns.name: quantity_distributed
columns.description: Total quantity of the affected product that was distributed to the market prior to the recall initiation, expressed in the standard unit of measure (e.g., units, bottles, vials). Used to calculate recall effectiveness and track recovery progress.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7.53; FDA Recall Effectiveness Checks

columns.name: quantity_recovered
columns.description: Total quantity of the recalled product that has been physically returned, destroyed, or otherwise accounted for as of the last update. Used to calculate recall effectiveness percentage and support regulatory reporting.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7.53; FDA Recall Effectiveness Checks

columns.name: quantity_uom
columns.description: Unit of measure applicable to quantity_distributed and quantity_recovered fields (e.g., EA=Each, BT=Bottle, VL=Vial, AMP=Ampoule, PKG=Package, KG=Kilogram, L=Liter). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|BT|VL|AMP|PKG|KG|L — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

columns.name: recall_class
columns.description: FDA-defined classification indicating the severity of the health hazard associated with the recalled product. Class I: serious adverse health consequences or death; Class II: temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences; Class III: unlikely to cause adverse health consequences.

columns.name: recall_closure_date
columns.description: The date on which the recall was formally closed or terminated by the regulatory authority or the company after all recall activities, effectiveness checks, and documentation requirements were completed.

columns.name: recall_effectiveness_pct
columns.description: Percentage of distributed product that has been successfully recovered or accounted for, calculated as (quantity_recovered / quantity_distributed) * 100. Key metric for FDA recall effectiveness checks and regulatory reporting under 21 CFR Part 7.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7.53; FDA Recall Effectiveness Guidance

columns.name: recall_initiated_date
columns.description: The date on which the recall was formally initiated by the company or ordered by the regulatory authority. Represents the principal business event timestamp for the recall lifecycle.

columns.name: recall_notes
columns.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, regulatory correspondence summaries, or contextual information relevant to the recall event that is not captured in structured fields.

columns.name: recall_number
columns.description: Externally-assigned recall identification number issued by the regulatory authority (e.g., FDA recall number) or internally assigned by the company for voluntary recalls. Serves as the primary business identifier for tracking and referencing the recall event across regulatory submissions and communications.

columns.name: recall_reason_code
columns.description: Standardized code categorizing the root cause or reason for the recall (e.g., contamination, labeling error, sub-potency, sterility failure, foreign particulate). Aligns with FDA recall reason taxonomy for regulatory reporting and trend analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Contamination|Labeling Error|Sub-Potency|Super-Potency|Sterility Failure|Foreign Particulate|Stability Failure|Packaging Defect|Microbial Contamination|Other — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7; FDA Recall Reason Codes

columns.name: recall_reason_description
columns.description: Detailed narrative description of the specific defect, violation, or safety concern that triggered the recall. Provides the full technical and regulatory context beyond the recall reason code, including root cause findings from CAPA investigations.

columns.name: recall_scope
columns.description: Geographic scope of the recall indicating whether the recall covers the entire national market, specific regions, international markets, or is limited to a specific manufacturing or distribution site.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7; EMA Recall Guidance; GDP Guidelines

columns.name: recall_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the recall event. Pending: recall initiated but not yet active; Active: recall in progress with field corrections underway; Monitoring: recall effectiveness checks ongoing; Terminated: FDA has terminated the recall; Closed: all recall activities completed and documented.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7.55; FDA Recall Status Definitions

columns.name: recall_strategy
columns.description: Description of the recall strategy approved by the regulatory authority or company, including the depth of recall, communication methods, effectiveness check methodology, and disposition instructions for recovered product.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7.42; FDA Recall Strategy Guidance

columns.name: recall_type
columns.description: Categorization of the recall initiation type. Voluntary recalls are company-initiated; Mandatory recalls are ordered by a regulatory authority; Market Withdrawal involves minor violations not subject to legal action; Stock Recovery involves products not yet distributed to the market.

columns.name: regulatory_notification_date
columns.description: The date on which the company formally notified the relevant regulatory authority (e.g., FDA, EMA) of the recall initiation. Critical compliance milestone tracked under 21 CFR Part 7 and equivalent international regulations.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 7.46; EMA Recall Notification Requirements

columns.name: regulatory_submission_ref
columns.description: Reference number or identifier for the regulatory submission (e.g., NDA, BLA, MAA) associated with the recalled product. Links the recall event to the product's regulatory dossier for compliance tracking in RIMS.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314; 21 CFR Part 601; Veeva Vault RIM

tables.name: serialization_record
tables.description: Unit-level and case-level serialization record for pharmaceutical finished goods compliant with DSCSA (Drug Supply Chain Security Act) and EU FMD (Falsified Medicines Directive) requirements. Captures serial number, GTIN, NDC, lot number, expiry date, aggregation hierarchy (unit→case→pallet), commissioning event, decommissioning event, verification status, and trading partner transaction history. Enables end-to-end track-and-trace across the pharmaceutical supply chain.

columns.name: serialization_record_id
columns.description: Primary key for serialization_record

columns.name: batch_record_id

columns.name: brand_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand. Business justification: Serialization compliance (DSCSA, FMD) is brand-specific; commercial teams use serialization data for product authentication, counterfeit prevention, and market-specific regulatory reporting. Links tra

columns.name: business_partner_id
columns.description: Reference to the trading partner (manufacturer, wholesaler, distributor, pharmacy) that currently holds legal ownership of the serialized unit. Updated at each DSCSA transaction event (Transfer of Ownership). Core to DSCSA chain-of-custody tracking.
columns.reference: DSCSA (21 CFR Part 203) Section 582(b); GDP Guidelines (2013/C 343/01)

tables.name: recall_lot_scope
tables.description: This association product represents the operational scoping event between a product_recall and a specific inventory_lot in pharmaceutical recall management. It captures the per-lot tracking required by FDA 21 CFR Part 7 effectiveness checks, recording the affected quantity, recovery status, disposition method, and notification state for each individual lot included in a recall action. Each record links one product_recall to one inventory_lot and carries attributes that exist only in the context of that specific recall-lot pairing — they cannot reside on the recall header (which is aggregate) or the inventory lot (which reflects current inventory state).. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical recall operations, a single recall event explicitly targets multiple specific inventory lots (e.g., all lots of NDC 12345-678-90 manufactured between Jan–Jun 2024), and a single inventory lot can be subject to multiple recalls across its lifecycle (e.g., a lot recalled for labeling deficiency and later for contamination). The FDA's recall effectiveness check process requires tracking each affected lot individually with its own recovery status, disposition, and notification record. This is an operationally managed relationship — recall coordinators actively create, update, and close records per lot — not an analytical derivation.

columns.glossary_term: Recall Lot Scope - Recall Lot Scope Id
columns.description: Primary key for the recall_lot_scope association

columns.name: inventory_lot_id
columns.glossary_term: Recall Lot Scope - Inventory Lot Id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to the specific inventory lot included within the scope of this recall action.

columns.name: product_recall_id
columns.glossary_term: Recall Lot Scope - Product Recall Id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to the parent product recall event that initiated the scope of this lot inclusion.

columns.name: affected_quantity_per_lot
columns.description: The quantity of this specific inventory lot that falls within the scope of the recall. Distinct from product_recall.quantity_distributed, which is the aggregate across all lots. Required for per-lot effectiveness check reporting to the FDA.

columns.name: disposition_per_lot
columns.description: The approved disposition method for this specific lot as determined by quality review. May differ from the recall-level product_disposition on the parent recall record if lot-specific conditions (e.g., cold chain break, partial quantity) warrant a different disposition decision.

columns.name: notification_sent_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the holder or custodian of this specific inventory lot has been formally notified of the recall. Tracked per lot because lots may be held at different locations (3PL, distributor, hospital) requiring separate notification actions.

columns.name: recovery_date
columns.description: The date on which this specific inventory lot was physically recovered, confirmed destroyed, or otherwise resolved within the recall process. Per-lot date required for FDA effectiveness check documentation.

columns.name: recovery_status
columns.description: Current recovery status for this specific lot within the recall. Tracked independently per lot as different lots may be at different stages of recovery simultaneously. Cannot reside on inventory_lot (which reflects current inventory state) or product_recall (which is aggregate).

domains.name: pharmacovigilance
domains.description: Owns all post-market safety surveillance and adverse event management. Collects, processes, and reports individual case safety reports (ICSR), serious adverse events (SAE), suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions (SUSAR), periodic safety update reports (PSUR), risk management plans (RMP), and signal detection records. Integrates with Argus Safety/Oracle AERS. Supports mandatory regulatory reporting to FDA, EMA, and other health authorities per PV regulations.
domains.references: ICH E2A-E2F / 21 CFR Part 312.32 / EMA GVP Modules

tables.name: icsr
tables.description: Individual Case Safety Report — the primary transactional record in pharmacovigilance. Captures all adverse event/adverse drug reaction reports from healthcare professionals, patients, literature, clinical trials, and spontaneous sources. Stores case identifiers (worldwide unique case ID), report type (spontaneous, literature, clinical trial, solicited, SAE), source channel, seriousness criteria, listedness assessment, causality assessment, narrative, regulatory clock start date, case processing status, and submission compliance. For literature-sourced cases, stores publication reference (PMID/DOI). For clinical trial cases, stores reconciliation status with EDC, dechallenge/rechallenge results, and site details. Includes version history tracking (initial, follow-up, nullification) with full audit trail per ICH E2B and 21 CFR Part 314. Includes de-identified patient demographics (age, sex, weight, medical history) per GDPR/HIPAA. Includes intake triage, minimum criteria validation, duplicate assessment outcome, and case assignment. SSOT for all individual safety cases. Supports regional requirements for FDA (MedWatch), EMA (EudraVigilance), PMDA (J-ICSR), NMPA, and TGA reporting. SLA-critical: 7-day and 15-day regulatory reporting deadlines.
