columns.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.investigator. Business justification: IND/CTA SAE reporting regulations require identification of the responsible investigator. The investigator record carries GCP certification, protocol deviation history, and 1572 status — all required

columns.name: master_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.hcp_master. Business justification: SAE reports in clinical trials identify the site investigator who reported the event. Essential for query resolution, site communication, medical review, and regulatory inspection readiness per GCP re

columns.name: patient_id
columns.description: Reference to the patient or clinical trial subject associated with this SAE. Links to the master patient/subject record for demographic and medical history context.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); ICH E6(R2) GCP; HIPAA; GDPR Article 9

columns.name: processing_org_unit_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.org_unit. Business justification: SAE reports are processed and owned by specific PV org units (regional safety teams). Org unit assignment is required for GCP audit trails, regulatory submission accountability, workload management, a

columns.name: project_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.project. Business justification: SAE reports must be associated with the discovery/development project for aggregate safety analysis, DSUR preparation, and clinical program oversight. Safety operations teams routinely query SAEs by p

columns.name: pv_product_id
columns.description: Reference to the suspect medicinal product (drug substance or drug product) associated with the SAE. Links to the product master for INN, ATC code, formulation, and regulatory approval details.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) element B.4; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 314.81

columns.name: reporter_id
columns.description: Reference to the healthcare professional, patient, or other reporter who submitted the SAE. Links to the reporter master record for qualification, contact, and reporter type details.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) element A.2; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: sales_rep_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.sales_rep. Business justification: SAE reports received via field sales reps must be tracked to the collecting rep for follow-up obligations, AE reporting compliance audits, and rep training records. Pharma companies are required to tr

columns.name: submission_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: SAE reports under clinical trials are filed under the IND/CTA regulatory submission. Linking sae_report to regulatory.submission enables IND safety reporting compliance tracking per 21 CFR 312.32, tyi

columns.name: susar_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.susar. Business justification: The sae_report table has an is_susar boolean flag indicating that certain SAE reports qualify as SUSARs. When is_susar=true, the SAE report should be directly linked to the corresponding SUSAR record

columns.name: trial_id
columns.description: Reference to the clinical trial or study in which the SAE occurred. Links to the clinical trial master record for protocol, phase, and IND/CTA details. Null for spontaneous post-market reports.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: visit_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.visit. Business justification: SAE reports from clinical trials are identified at a specific visit. Linking sae_report to the visit enables EDC-safety reconciliation and source data verification (SDV), a GCP requirement. sae_report

columns.name: case_number
columns.description: Externally-known alphanumeric case identifier assigned by the pharmacovigilance system (Argus Safety/Oracle AERS) upon initial receipt of the SAE. Used for cross-system tracking, regulatory submissions, and reconciliation with EDC systems such as Medidata Rave.
columns.reference: ICH E2D; Argus Safety Case Number; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: causality_assessment
columns.description: Medical assessment of the causal relationship between the suspect medicinal product and the SAE, based on WHO-UMC or investigator assessment criteria. Drives SUSAR classification and regulatory reporting obligations.
columns.reference: WHO-UMC Causality Categories; ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2); EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the SAE report record was first entered into the pharmacovigilance safety database (Argus Safety/Oracle AERS). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: dechallenge_result
columns.description: Outcome observed when the suspect drug was withdrawn or dose reduced (dechallenge). A positive dechallenge (event resolved on withdrawal) supports a causal relationship. Required field in ICH E2B(R3) ICSR submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) element B.4.k.18.1; ICH E2A; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: edc_case_reference
columns.description: Case or subject reference number from the clinical trial EDC system (e.g., Medidata Rave subject ID or AE sequence number) used to reconcile the SAE record between the safety database and the clinical database.
columns.reference: ICH E2D; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave

columns.name: edc_reconciliation_status
columns.description: Status of reconciliation between this SAE record in the pharmacovigilance safety database (Argus Safety) and the corresponding record in the clinical trial EDC system (Medidata Rave). Required per ICH E2D guidance to ensure consistency between clinical and safety databases.
columns.reference: ICH E2D; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave-Argus Safety reconciliation SOP

columns.name: is_fatal
columns.description: Indicates whether the SAE resulted in the death of the patient. Triggers mandatory expedited 7-day reporting to health authorities and escalation to senior medical review.
columns.reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2D; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: is_susar
columns.glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Indicator
columns.description: Indicates whether this SAE has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR), requiring expedited 7-day (fatal/life-threatening) or 15-day reporting to health authorities and notification to investigators.
columns.reference: ICH E2A; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; EU CT Regulation 536/2014

columns.name: listedness
columns.description: Assessment of whether the adverse reaction is listed (expected) in the current Reference Safety Information (RSI) such as the Investigator Brochure or SmPC. Determines whether the event qualifies as unexpected for SUSAR classification.
columns.reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 312.32

columns.name: meddra_pt_code
columns.description: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term code assigned to the primary SAE event term. Standard coding used for regulatory submissions, signal detection, and aggregate safety analysis.
columns.reference: MedDRA v26+; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; FDA FAERS

columns.name: meddra_pt_name
columns.description: Human-readable MedDRA Preferred Term label corresponding to the meddra_pt_code. Displayed in safety reports, regulatory submissions, and signal detection outputs.
columns.reference: MedDRA v26+; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: meddra_soc_code
columns.description: MedDRA System Organ Class code representing the highest-level anatomical or physiological classification of the SAE. Used for aggregate safety reporting and PSUR tabulations.
columns.reference: MedDRA v26+; ICH E2B(R3); ICH E2C(R2) PSUR

columns.name: medical_review_status
columns.description: Current status of the medical officer review of the SAE case. Tracks progression from initial triage through physician causality assessment and case narrative approval.
columns.reference: ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety workflow

columns.name: narrative
columns.description: Free-text medical narrative summarizing the SAE case including patient history, event description, clinical course, treatment, and outcome. Contains protected health information (PHI). Submitted as part of the ICSR to health authorities.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) element H.1; ICH E2D; HIPAA; GDPR Article 9; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: onset_date
columns.description: Date on which the serious adverse event first began or was first observed by the patient or healthcare professional. Used to calculate time-to-onset from first drug exposure.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) element A.1.7; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: outcome
columns.description: Clinical outcome of the SAE at the time of reporting or case closure. Drives case narrative, aggregate safety reporting, and benefit-risk assessment in PSUR/PBRER.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) element B.2.i.7.2; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: patient_age_at_onset
columns.glossary_term: Patient Age at Adverse Event Onset
columns.description: Age of the patient in years at the time the serious adverse event began. Used for demographic analysis, signal detection, and population-specific risk assessment.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) element B.1.2.2; HIPAA; GDPR Article 9

columns.name: patient_sex
columns.description: Biological sex of the patient as recorded at the time of the SAE. Used for demographic stratification in signal detection and aggregate safety reporting (PSUR/PBRER).
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) element B.1.2.1; HIPAA; GDPR Article 9

columns.name: receipt_date
columns.description: Date on which the company first received valid minimum information about the SAE (Day 0 for regulatory reporting clock). SLA-critical: initial SAE notification must be processed within 24 hours of site awareness per ICH E2D.
columns.reference: ICH E2D; ICH E2A; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: rechallenge_result
columns.description: Outcome observed when the suspect drug was re-administered after the initial adverse event (rechallenge). A positive rechallenge (event recurred) strongly supports causality. Required field in ICH E2B(R3) ICSR submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) element B.4.k.18.2; ICH E2A; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: regulatory_submission_date
columns.description: Actual date on which the ICSR/SUSAR was submitted to the health authority. Compared against regulatory_submission_due_date to assess compliance with reporting timelines.
columns.reference: ICH E2A; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; EudraVigilance

columns.name: regulatory_submission_due_date
columns.description: Deadline by which the SAE/SUSAR must be submitted to the relevant health authority (FDA, EMA, etc.). Calculated from receipt_date based on applicable reporting timeline (7-day for fatal/life-threatening SUSAR; 15-day for other SUSARs; 30-day for non-expedited).
columns.reference: ICH E2A; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; EU CT Regulation 536/2014

columns.name: report_status
columns.description: Current workflow state of the SAE report from initial receipt through medical review, causality assessment, and regulatory submission. Drives SLA monitoring and submission queue management.
columns.reference: ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety workflow states

columns.name: report_type
columns.description: Classification of the SAE report by its originating source. Determines applicable regulatory reporting timelines and submission pathways (e.g., 7-day vs 15-day expedited reporting).
columns.reference: ICH E2D; ICH E2A; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: seriousness_criteria
columns.description: One or more ICH E2A seriousness criteria met by this event: death, life-threatening, hospitalization (initial or prolonged), disability/incapacity, congenital anomaly/birth defect, or medically important event. Multiple criteria may apply. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: death|life_threatening|hospitalization|prolonged_hospitalization|disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_important — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2D; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: site_awareness_date
columns.description: Date on which the investigational site or sponsor first became aware of the SAE. Used to calculate the 24-hour initial notification SLA and the 7/15-day regulatory reporting clock per ICH E2A and GCP requirements.
columns.reference: ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: time_to_onset_days
columns.description: Number of days between the first dose of the suspect medicinal product and the onset of the SAE. Key pharmacovigilance metric used in signal detection, aggregate analysis, and benefit-risk evaluation.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; FDA FAERS

columns.name: treatment_description
columns.description: Free-text description of the treatment(s) administered to manage the SAE, including concomitant medications, procedures, or interventions. Captured in the case narrative.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: treatment_given
columns.description: Indicates whether specific treatment was administered to the patient in response to the SAE. Relevant for case narrative, medical review, and aggregate safety reporting.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) element B.2.i.8; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the SAE report record. Supports audit trail, version control, and reconciliation workflows per 21 CFR Part 11.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: worldwide_unique_case_number
columns.description: Globally unique case identifier formatted per ICH E2B(R3) standard (country code + organisation identifier + local case number). Required for electronic ICSR submissions to FDA, EMA, and other health authorities.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA GVP Module VI

tables.name: pv_submission
tables.description: Regulatory submission record for all pharmacovigilance reports submitted to health authorities worldwide. Covers expedited individual case reports (7-day fatal/life-threatening, 15-day serious), periodic aggregate reports (PSUR, PBRER, PADER, DSUR), and ad-hoc safety communications. Stores submission type, target authority, submission date, acknowledgement status, error handling, submission format (E2B R2/R3 XML, eCTD), gateway/portal details, submission reference number, resubmission history, and compliance status. Supports all major regulatory gateways including EudraVigilance (EVWEB/gateway), FAERS (FDA), MHRA Sentinel, PMDA gateway, and NMPA. Tracks authority-specific technical requirements (E2B R3 for EMA, E2B R2 for some national authorities). SLA-critical: regulatory deadline compliance with automatic escalation.
tables.reference: ICH E2B / FDA MedWatch / EMA EudraVigilance

columns.name: pv_submission_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each pharmacovigilance regulatory submission record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 314; EMA EudraVigilance Technical Specifications

columns.name: application_id
columns.description: Reference to the regulatory application (NDA, BLA, MAA, IND) under which this pharmacovigilance submission is filed. Links to the regulatory.application product. Enables traceability between safety submissions and the marketing authorisation or investigational application.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.81; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: approval_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.approval. Business justification: Periodic safety reports (PSURs, PADERs) and signal-driven submissions pertain to specific marketing approvals. Linking pv_submission to approval enables authority-level benefit-risk tracking tied to t

columns.name: brand_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand. Business justification: Regulatory safety submissions (ICSRs, PSURs, SUSARs) must reference commercial brand for health authority tracking, compliance audit trails, and brand-level submission history. Essential for regulator

columns.name: drug_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_product. Business justification: Submission-level product tracking: pv_submission records regulatory submissions to health authorities. Linking to drug_product enables product-level submission tracking for regulatory intelligence, co

columns.name: health_authority_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.health_authority. Business justification: Every PV submission targets a specific health authority. pv_submission.health_authority_code is a denormalized plain attribute. A proper FK enables authority-specific PV submission compliance dashboar

columns.name: original_submission_pv_submission_id
columns.description: Self-referencing identifier pointing to the original pv_submission_id when this record represents a resubmission, follow-up, or amendment. Null for original submissions. Enables reconstruction of the full resubmission history chain.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.7; EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide

columns.name: primary_pv_icsr_id
columns.description: Reference to the Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) that is the subject of this submission, when submission_type is an ICSR variant. Links to the source safety case record in Argus Safety / Oracle AERS. Null for aggregate report submissions (PSUR, PBRER, DSUR).
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR 314.81; EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety Data Model

columns.name: psur_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.psur. Business justification: Some PV submissions are for PSUR reports (submission_type indicates report type). Add psur_id FK (nullable - only populated for PSUR submission types). This links the submission transaction to the PSU

columns.name: pv_product_id
columns.description: Reference to the medicinal product (Drug Product / Drug Substance) that is the subject of the safety report or aggregate submission. Links to the master product record.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k; EMA Product Dictionary; FDA NDC Directory

columns.name: responsible_org_unit_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.org_unit. Business justification: PV submissions are executed by specific regulatory affairs or PV org units. Org unit ownership is required for submission workload reporting, regulatory deadline accountability, and inspection readine

columns.name: rmp_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.rmp. Business justification: Some PV submissions are for RMP reports. Add rmp_id FK (nullable - only populated for RMP submission types). Remove rmp_version as it normalizes to rmp.version_number.

columns.name: sae_report_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.sae_report. Business justification: SAE reports generate regulatory submissions. Add sae_report_id FK (nullable - only populated for SAE submission types). This links the submission transaction to the SAE master record.

columns.name: safety_signal_id
columns.description: Reference to the pharmacovigilance safety signal record that prompted or is associated with this submission, where applicable. Links to the signal detection and management record. Null for routine ICSR submissions not linked to a formal signal.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module IX; ICH E2E; FDA Guidance on Safety Reporting

columns.name: submission_country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Submission target country determines format (E2B R2/R3, CIOMS), gateway (EudraVigilance, FDA ESG, MHRA Yellow Card), and timelines. Operational requirement for submission routing and compliance tracki

columns.name: submission_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: PV submissions (E2B transmissions, PSURs, RMPs) are formal regulatory submissions tracked in the regulatory dossier. Linking pv_submission to regulatory.submission enables reconciliation of PV transmi

columns.name: submitting_legal_entity_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: The legal entity making a PV submission is a core regulatory requirement — health authorities require MAH legal entity identification on all submissions. sender_organisation and sender_identifier are

columns.name: susar_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.susar. Business justification: SUSAR records generate regulatory submissions (expedited reporting). Add susar_id FK (nullable - only populated for SUSAR submission types). One SUSAR can have multiple submissions (initial + follow-u

columns.name: trial_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.trial. Business justification: Expedited IND safety reports (15-day reports) are submitted to health authorities in the context of a specific clinical trial per FDA 21 CFR 312.32. Linking pv_submission to trial enables regulatory t

columns.name: variation_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.variation. Business justification: Safety-driven variations (urgent safety restrictions, Type II variations) generate pv_submission records for authority notification. Linking pv_submission to variation enables end-to-end tracking of s

columns.name: acknowledgement_code
columns.description: Technical acknowledgement code returned by the health authority gateway per HL7 v2 / E2B messaging standards. AA = Application Accept; AE = Application Error; CA = Commit Accept; CE = Commit Error; TA = Technical Accept; TE = Technical Error. Drives automated error handling and resubmission workflows.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) Implementation Guide; HL7 v2 Acknowledgement Codes; EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules

columns.name: acknowledgement_date
columns.description: Timestamp when the technical acknowledgement (ACK) message was received from the health authority gateway confirming successful receipt of the submission. Distinct from substantive acceptance. Used for SLA compliance evidence.
columns.reference: EMA EudraVigilance Gateway Technical Specifications; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; ICH E2B(R3) Implementation Guide

columns.name: argus_case_number
columns.description: The case number from the Argus Safety / Oracle AERS pharmacovigilance system that is the source of record for this submission. Enables direct traceability from the submission record back to the full safety case in the operational PV system.
columns.reference: Argus Safety / Oracle AERS; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: authority_case_number
columns.description: The case or report reference number assigned by the receiving health authority upon acceptance of the submission (e.g., EudraVigilance case number, FDA FAERS case ID). Used for follow-up queries and regulatory correspondence. Populated after authority acceptance.
columns.reference: EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; PMDA E2B Transmission Guide

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this pharmacovigilance submission record was first created in the data platform. Audit trail field for data lineage and 21 CFR Part 11 / Annex 11 electronic records compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; EU Annex 11; GDPR Article 5(1)(f); ICH Q10

columns.name: date_of_first_receipt
columns.description: The date the company first received the minimum valid safety information constituting a reportable case (Day 0 for regulatory clock purposes). This is the anchor date from which the 7-day or 15-day expedited reporting deadline is calculated for ICSRs. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.4.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.4; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1)

columns.name: days_to_deadline
columns.description: Number of calendar days remaining between the current date and the regulatory_deadline at the time of last record update. Negative values indicate overdue submissions. Used for SLA monitoring dashboards and automatic escalation triggers. Note: this is a snapshot value captured at record update time, not a live calculation.
columns.reference: ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 314.81

columns.name: error_code
columns.description: Structured error code returned by the health authority gateway or E2B validation engine upon rejection or technical failure (e.g., EudraVigilance business rule error code, FAERS conformance error code). Enables automated error categorisation and routing to the appropriate remediation team.
columns.reference: EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; ICH E2B(R3) Validation Rules

columns.name: gateway_portal
columns.description: The specific electronic gateway or web portal used to transmit this submission to the health authority. Determines technical format and protocol requirements. EudraVigilance Gateway and EVWEB are EMA channels; FAERS Gateway is the FDA channel for ICSRs; MHRA Sentinel is the UK post-Brexit channel. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EUDRAVIGILANCE_GATEWAY|EUDRAVIGILANCE_EVWEB|FAERS_GATEWAY|MHRA_SENTINEL|PMDA_GATEWAY|NMPA_GATEWAY|VIGIBASE_WHO|DIRECT_EMAIL|PAPER — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: EMA EudraVigilance Technical Specifications; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; MHRA Sentinel System Guidance; PMDA E2B Transmission Guide

columns.name: is_expedited
columns.description: Indicates whether this submission is subject to expedited regulatory reporting requirements (7-day or 15-day clock). True = expedited; False = periodic/non-expedited. Drives SLA escalation logic and compliance monitoring.
columns.reference: ICH E2D; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1); EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: is_on_time
columns.description: Indicates whether the submission was transmitted on or before the regulatory_deadline. True = submitted on time; False = submitted late. Key compliance KPI field populated at time of submission. Used for regulatory compliance reporting and CAPA tracking.
columns.reference: ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 314.81; PIC/S GVP Guidelines

columns.name: is_susar
columns.glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this submission relates to a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) from a clinical trial, which carries specific expedited reporting obligations to both health authorities and investigators under ICH E2A and GCP regulations.
columns.reference: ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2) GCP; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 312.32; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014

columns.name: message_format
columns.description: The technical format standard used for the submission message. E2B_R2_XML = ICH E2B(R2) XML format (used by some national authorities); E2B_R3_XML = ICH E2B(R3) XML format (required by EMA EudraVigilance and FDA from 2022); ECTD = Electronic Common Technical Document format (for aggregate reports); PDF = portable document format for ad-hoc communications; PAPER = legacy paper submission.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R2); ICH E2B(R3); ICH M8 eCTD; EMA EudraVigilance Technical Specifications; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide

columns.name: regulatory_deadline
columns.description: The mandatory regulatory deadline date by which this submission must be transmitted to the health authority, calculated from the date of first receipt (Day 0) of the safety information. For expedited ICSRs: Day 7 (fatal/life-threatening) or Day 15 (serious). For PSURs/PBRERs: per approved data lock point schedule. SLA-critical field used for automatic escalation.
columns.reference: ICH E2D; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1); EMA GVP Module VI; ICH E2C(R2)

columns.name: rejection_reason
columns.description: Free-text or structured description of the reason(s) for rejection returned by the health authority gateway or authority reviewer when submission_status is REJECTED. Includes E2B validation error codes and human-readable explanations. Used for root cause analysis and CAPA.
columns.reference: EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; ICH E2B(R3) Implementation Guide

columns.name: report_period_end
columns.glossary_term: Report Period End Date (Data Lock Point)
columns.description: End date of the data collection period (Data Lock Point, DLP) for aggregate reports (PSUR, PBRER, PADER, DSUR). Defines the cut-off date for safety data included in the report. Null for individual case (ICSR) submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E2C(R2); ICH E2F; EMA GVP Module VII; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)

columns.name: report_period_start
columns.description: Start date of the data collection period covered by this submission. Applicable primarily to aggregate reports (PSUR, PBRER, PADER, DSUR) defining the International Birth Date (IBD) or period start. Null for individual case (ICSR) submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E2C(R2); ICH E2F; EMA GVP Module VII; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)

columns.name: report_type_qualifier
columns.description: Qualifier indicating whether this is an initial report, a follow-up update to a previously submitted case, or a nullification (withdrawal) of a previously submitted report. Corresponds directly to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.2 field.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.2; EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide

columns.name: responsible_qppv
columns.description: Name or identifier of the Qualified Person for Pharmacovigilance (QPPV) responsible for this submission under EU GVP regulations. The QPPV bears legal accountability for the completeness and accuracy of pharmacovigilance submissions to the EMA and EU member states.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module I; EU Directive 2001/83/EC Article 104; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: resubmission_count
columns.description: Number of times this submission has been resubmitted to the health authority following a rejection or technical error. Zero indicates the original submission was accepted without resubmission. Used to track submission quality and identify systemic data quality issues.
columns.reference: EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; ICH E2B(R3) Implementation Guide

columns.name: submission_date
columns.description: The principal real-world timestamp when the pharmacovigilance report was transmitted to the health authority gateway or portal. This is the legally significant submission event time used for regulatory deadline compliance calculations.
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314.81; EMA GVP Module VI; ICH E2D; 21 CFR Part 312.32

columns.name: submission_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the pharmacovigilance submission workflow. DRAFT = in preparation; PENDING = queued for transmission; SUBMITTED = transmitted to health authority gateway; ACKNOWLEDGED = technical acknowledgement received from gateway; ACCEPTED = substantively accepted by authority; REJECTED = rejected with errors requiring correction; RESUBMITTED = corrected and resubmitted after rejection; WITHDRAWN = voluntarily withdrawn by the company. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DRAFT|PENDING|SUBMITTED|ACKNOWLEDGED|ACCEPTED|REJECTED|RESUBMITTED|WITHDRAWN — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; ICH E2B(R3) Implementation Guide

columns.name: submission_type
columns.description: Classification of the pharmacovigilance submission by regulatory report type. ICSR_EXPEDITED_7DAY = fatal/life-threatening Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) requiring 7-calendar-day reporting; ICSR_EXPEDITED_15DAY = serious ICSR requiring 15-calendar-day reporting; ICSR_NON_EXPEDITED = non-expedited periodic ICSR; PSUR = Periodic Safety Update Report; PBRER = Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report; PADER = Periodic Adverse Drug Experience Report; DSUR = Development Safety Update Report. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ICSR_EXPEDITED_7DAY|ICSR_EXPEDITED_15DAY|ICSR_NON_EXPEDITED|PSUR|PBRER|PADER|DSUR|AD_HOC_SAFETY_COMM|REMS_ASSESSMENT|SUSAR — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E2D; ICH E2C(R2); ICH E2F; 21 CFR 314.81; EMA Guideline on Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) Module VI

columns.name: submission_version
columns.description: Sequential version number of this submission for a given safety case or aggregate report. Version 1 = initial submission; Version 2+ = follow-up or amendment submissions. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.2 (report type: initial/follow-up/nullification).
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.2; EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide

columns.name: transmission_reference
columns.description: Unique message transmission identifier assigned by the health authority gateway at the point of receipt (e.g., EudraVigilance message ID, FAERS transmission reference). Distinct from the authority_case_number; this is the technical envelope identifier used for gateway-level tracing and acknowledgement matching.
columns.reference: EMA EudraVigilance Gateway Technical Specifications; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; ICH E2B(R3) A.1.0.1

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this pharmacovigilance submission record was most recently modified in the data platform. Audit trail field for data lineage and 21 CFR Part 11 / Annex 11 electronic records compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; EU Annex 11; GDPR Article 5(1)(f); ICH Q10

tables.name: psur
tables.description: Periodic aggregate safety report master record covering PSUR, PBRER (ICH E2C R2), PADER (FDA), and DSUR (development phase) for each product-indication combination. Captures data lock point, reporting interval, international birth date (IBD), cumulative exposure data, interval and cumulative case summaries, signal summary, benefit-risk evaluation conclusion, and submission status per applicable authority. Tracks preparation milestones, author assignments, medical review, QC, and approval workflow. Supports EU PSUR single assessment (PSUSA) process, FDA PADER requirements, and ICH DSUR for investigational products. Includes structured benefit-risk assessment sections. SLA-critical: fixed regulatory submission deadlines based on IBD.
tables.reference: ICH E2C(R2) PBRER / EU PSUR Single Assessment

columns.name: psur_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the PSUR/PBRER/PADER/DSUR master record in the pharmacovigilance data lakehouse.
columns.reference: ICH E2C(R2); FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA Guideline on PSUR

columns.name: application_id
columns.description: Reference to the marketing authorisation application (NDA/BLA/MAA) or investigational application (IND) under which this periodic safety report is submitted.
columns.reference: ICH E2C(R2); FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

columns.name: approval_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.approval. Business justification: PSURs are tied to specific marketing approvals. The approval record contains approval_date (international birth date reference), approved_indication, and conditions the PSUR must address. Direct link

columns.name: atc_classification_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: PSURs are structured around ATC classifications for benefit-risk assessment and PSUSA grouping. ATC code is a core PSUR data element per ICH E2C(R2) and EMA PSUSA procedures. Linking psur to atc_class

columns.name: drug_substance_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_substance. Business justification: ICH E2C regulatory requirement: PSUR is a substance-based periodic safety report. Linking psur to drug_substance is fundamental to PSUR structure — the report covers all formulations of the active sub

columns.name: health_authority_id
columns.description: Reference to the primary health authority (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA) to which this PSUR is submitted. Determines applicable regulatory requirements and submission format.

tables.name: safety_signal
tables.description: Safety signal record representing a new or evolving safety concern identified through signal detection activities. Captures signal source (spontaneous database, literature, clinical trial, real-world data), detection method (disproportionality analysis, clinical review, machine learning), MedDRA-coded term, signal strength metrics (PRR, ROR, EBGM, IC), and signal status lifecycle (new, under evaluation, validated, refuted, closed). Includes formal assessment records: methodology, data sources reviewed, benefit-risk impact evaluation, proposed label change recommendation, regulatory action required, PRAC/PSUR referral status, and final disposition. Each signal supports multiple assessment iterations. Tracks the full signal management workflow from detection through triage, validation, prioritization, assessment, and closure or regulatory action per GVP Module IX. SLA-critical: PRAC rapporteur notification timelines.

columns.name: label_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.label. Business justification: Safety signals with label_change_recommended=true must reference the specific label version to be updated. This enables signal management workflow to directly identify and queue the affected label for

columns.name: molecular_target_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.molecular_target. Business justification: Safety signal validation requires molecular target review. Signal assessment committees evaluate target biology, pathway, tissue expression, and known class effects to determine if the signal is mecha

columns.name: owning_org_unit_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.org_unit. Business justification: Safety signals are assessed and owned by specific PV org units (signal management team, therapeutic area safety team). Org unit ownership is required for signal triage workflow, PRAC notification acco

columns.name: patent_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: Safety signal management requires IP teams to assess whether a label change triggered by a signal affects patent claims or exclusivity. Signal closure reports and regulatory action decisions reference

columns.name: project_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.project. Business justification: Safety signals are managed at the development project level for portfolio safety reviews, DSUR signal sections, and go/no-go decisions on clinical progression. Signal management teams routinely aggreg

columns.name: pv_product_id
columns.description: Reference to the medicinal product (drug substance or drug product) associated with this safety signal. Links to the master product entity for the implicated compound.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX; ICH E2C(R2); EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: submission_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: Safety signals requiring regulatory action result in formal submissions (label changes, variations, PSUR referrals). Linking safety_signal to the resulting regulatory submission enables end-to-end sig

columns.name: trial_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.trial. Business justification: Safety signals detected from clinical trial data must be traceable to the originating trial for PRAC notification and signal triage (GVP Module IX). safety_signal has source_reference_number as text b

columns.name: analysis_period_end_date
columns.description: End date of the data analysis period used for signal detection. Together with analysis_period_start_date, defines the cumulative or interval data window reviewed.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; ICH E2C(R2)

columns.name: analysis_period_start_date
columns.description: Start date of the data analysis period used for signal detection. Defines the temporal window of adverse event data reviewed to identify the signal.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; ICH E2C(R2)

columns.name: assessment_summary
columns.description: Narrative summary of the formal signal assessment findings, including methodology applied, data sources reviewed, clinical interpretation, and conclusions. Supports regulatory dossier preparation and PRAC submissions.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; ICH E2C(R2); EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: benefit_risk_impact
columns.description: Overall benefit-risk impact determination resulting from the signal assessment. Indicates whether the signal changes the benefit-risk balance of the product as favorable, unfavorable, uncertain, or neutral.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX; ICH E2C(R2) PBRER; EMA Benefit-Risk Methodology; GVP Module I

columns.name: closure_date
columns.description: Date on which the safety signal was formally closed following completion of all assessment activities and regulatory actions. Represents the end of the signal management lifecycle.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the safety signal record was first created in the pharmacovigilance system (Argus Safety / Oracle AERS). Used for audit trail and data lineage compliance per 21 CFR Part 11.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GVP Module IX; ICH E6(R2) GCP

columns.name: data_source_database
columns.description: Name of the specific pharmacovigilance database or data source from which the signal was detected (e.g., FDA FAERS, WHO VigiBase, EudraVigilance, company spontaneous database, published literature). Supports traceability of signal origin.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; FDA FAERS

columns.name: detection_method
columns.description: Methodology used to identify the safety signal. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: disproportionality_analysis|clinical_review|machine_learning|literature_review|spontaneous_report|regulatory_authority — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; ICH E2C(R2)

columns.name: detection_timestamp
columns.description: Date and time when the safety signal was first detected or identified, representing the principal real-world event time. Critical for SLA tracking of PRAC rapporteur notification timelines and regulatory reporting deadlines.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; 21 CFR 314.81; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: ebgm_value
columns.description: Empirical Bayes Geometric Mean (EBGM) — a Bayesian disproportionality metric used in the FDA FAERS database analysis. EBGM ≥2 is a commonly applied threshold for signal detection.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX; FDA FAERS Signal Detection; DuMouchel EBGM Method

columns.name: fatal_case_count
columns.description: Number of fatal outcome cases among the cases contributing to this safety signal. Fatal cases receive highest priority in signal triage and may trigger expedited regulatory notification.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management; GVP Module IX; 21 CFR 312.32

columns.name: ic_value
columns.description: Information Component (IC) — a Bayesian disproportionality metric used by the WHO Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) VigiBase. Positive IC values indicate a drug-event association stronger than expected by chance.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX; WHO UMC VigiBase IC Method; Bate et al. IC Algorithm

columns.name: label_change_recommended
columns.description: Indicates whether the signal assessment has resulted in a formal recommendation to update the product label (SmPC, USPI, or equivalent). Triggers regulatory submission activities.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX; 21 CFR 314.70; EMA SmPC Guideline; ICH E2C(R2)

columns.name: meddra_pt_code
columns.glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term Code
columns.description: MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) code representing the primary adverse event or medical concept associated with this safety signal. Standardized coding per MedDRA hierarchy for regulatory submissions and signal tracking.
columns.reference: MedDRA Version Current; ICH M1 MedDRA Guideline; GVP Module IX; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: meddra_pt_name
columns.glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term Name
columns.description: Human-readable MedDRA Preferred Term name corresponding to the meddra_pt_code. Provides the standardized medical terminology label for the safety signal event.
columns.reference: MedDRA Version Current; ICH M1 MedDRA Guideline; GVP Module IX

columns.name: meddra_soc_code
columns.glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) Code
columns.description: MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) code for the primary adverse event, providing the highest-level classification in the MedDRA hierarchy. Used for signal clustering and therapeutic area analysis.
columns.reference: MedDRA Version Current; ICH M1 MedDRA Guideline; GVP Module IX

columns.name: prac_notification_date
columns.glossary_term: Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee (PRAC) Rapporteur Notification Date
columns.description: Actual date on which the PRAC rapporteur was notified of the safety signal. Compared against prac_notification_due_date to assess SLA compliance.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010

columns.name: prac_notification_due_date
columns.glossary_term: Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee (PRAC) Rapporteur Notification Due Date
columns.description: SLA-critical deadline by which the PRAC rapporteur must be notified of the validated safety signal per EMA regulatory requirements. Drives escalation workflows and compliance monitoring.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010

columns.name: priority_level
columns.description: Triage priority assigned to the safety signal based on clinical seriousness, signal strength, and public health impact. Drives SLA timelines for assessment completion and regulatory notification.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; FDA PDUFA VI Commitments

columns.name: prr_value
columns.description: Proportional Reporting Ratio (PRR) — a disproportionality analysis metric quantifying the ratio of the proportion of reports for a drug-event combination versus all other drugs. Values >2 with chi-squared >4 and ≥3 cases typically indicate a signal.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; Evans et al. PRR Method; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: psur_referral_flag
columns.glossary_term: Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) Referral Flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this safety signal has been referred for inclusion and evaluation in the next Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) / Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER).
columns.reference: GVP Module VII PSUR; ICH E2C(R2); EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: regulatory_action_required
columns.description: Indicates whether the safety signal assessment has determined that a regulatory action is required (e.g., label update, DHPC, REMS modification, product withdrawal). Drives downstream regulatory affairs workflows.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; 21 CFR 314.81; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: regulatory_action_type
columns.description: Type of regulatory action determined to be required based on the signal assessment outcome. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: label_update|rems_modification|dhpc|psur_referral|product_withdrawal|contraindication_addition|none — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: GVP Module IX; 21 CFR 314.70; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; FDA REMS Guidance

columns.name: rmp_update_required
columns.glossary_term: Risk Management Plan (RMP) Update Required Flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the signal assessment outcome requires an update to the product's Risk Management Plan (RMP). Triggers regulatory affairs and pharmacovigilance team coordination.
columns.reference: GVP Module V Risk Management Systems; EMA/838713/2011 Rev 2; Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010

columns.name: ror_value
columns.description: Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) — a disproportionality analysis metric representing the odds of a specific adverse event being reported for a drug versus all other drugs. Complements PRR in signal detection.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; van Puijenbroek ROR Method; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: serious_case_count
columns.description: Number of Serious Adverse Event (SAE) cases among the total cases contributing to this signal. Serious cases include fatal, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, or congenital anomaly outcomes per ICH E2A.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management; GVP Module IX; 21 CFR 312.32

columns.name: signal_description
columns.description: Detailed narrative description of the safety signal including the nature of the concern, clinical context, patient population affected, and initial evidence summary. Supports signal triage and assessment documentation.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; ICH E2C(R2); EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: signal_number
columns.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique identifier assigned to the safety signal upon creation in Argus Safety / Oracle AERS. Used for cross-system referencing, regulatory correspondence, and PRAC rapporteur notifications.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: signal_source_type
columns.description: Classification of the data source from which the safety signal was detected. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: spontaneous_database|literature|clinical_trial|real_world_data|social_media|health_authority — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; ICH E2C(R2); FDA Guidance on Signal Detection

columns.name: signal_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the safety signal per GVP Module IX workflow: new (detected, not yet triaged), under_evaluation (active assessment in progress), validated (confirmed as a genuine safety concern), refuted (assessed and dismissed), closed (final disposition reached and documented).
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; ICH E2C(R2)

columns.name: signal_title
columns.description: Concise, human-readable title describing the safety signal, typically formatted as [Drug Name] and [Adverse Event Term]. Used in regulatory correspondence, PRAC submissions, and internal safety committee communications.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: signal_type
columns.description: Classification of the signal as new (not previously known), strengthened (existing signal with increased evidence), weakened (existing signal with decreased evidence), or refuted (previously identified signal now dismissed).
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: source_reference_number
columns.description: Reference number or identifier from the originating data source (e.g., FAERS case number, EudraVigilance report ID, literature PubMed ID, clinical trial NCT number) that triggered or contributed to the signal detection.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; FDA FAERS; EudraVigilance; WHO VigiBase

columns.name: triage_date
columns.description: Date on which the safety signal was formally triaged by the pharmacovigilance team to determine priority and assign for full assessment. Marks the transition from detection to active evaluation.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the safety signal record. Supports audit trail requirements and tracks signal assessment progression through the lifecycle.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GVP Module IX; ICH E6(R2) GCP

columns.name: validation_date
columns.description: Date on which the safety signal was formally validated as a genuine safety concern following initial assessment. Triggers downstream regulatory notification and benefit-risk evaluation activities.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; ICH E2C(R2)

tables.name: pv_product
tables.description: Pharmacovigilance product master — the authoritative PV-domain view of medicinal products under safety surveillance. Captures product name, INN, ATC code, MAH (Marketing Authorization Holder), authorization numbers per country/region, formulation, route of administration, reference safety information document reference, international birth date (IBD), PSMF reference, QPPV assignment, and PV system governance metadata. Distinct from the commercial product catalog — this is the PV-specific product registration used for case processing, signal detection, PSUR scheduling, and regulatory reporting. Includes PSMF-level metadata: PV system description, organizational structure for pharmacovigilance, contracted party references, and compliance status per EU GVP Module II.
tables.reference: EMA XEVMPD / FDA SPL Product Listing

columns.name: pv_product_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the pharmacovigilance product master record. Primary key for the pv_product entity within the Databricks Silver Layer.
columns.reference: ICH E2D; EU GVP Module VI

columns.name: approval_id

Replaces text atc_code with proper master data refer

columns.name: brand_id

columns.name: brand_plan_id

columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.inn_registry. Business justification: International Nonproprietary Name (INN) is WHO standard for substance identification in pharmacovigilance. Required for duplicate case detection, substance-level signal detection, and regulatory submi

columns.name: labeling_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.labeling. Business justification: Listedness determination: PV teams must reference the current approved label to assess whether an adverse reaction is listed. Linking pv_product to labeling enables direct traceability to the label ve

columns.name: mah_legal_entity_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Marketing Authorization Holder (MAH) is the legal entity responsible for pharmacovigilance obligations. Required for regulatory submissions, liability determination, and safety reporting accountabilit

columns.name: masterdata_ndc_code_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.ndc_code. Business justification: US market products require NDC linkage for FDA FAERS submissions, product identification in US ICSRs, and recall coordination. Essential for US pharmacovigilance operations and regulatory compliance.

columns.name: medicinal_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Core bridge between PV product master and commercial product master. Required for regulatory identifier reconciliation (NDC, EMA product number), lifecycle status alignment, product discontinuation im

columns.name: molecular_target_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.molecular_target. Business justification: Products are defined by their molecular targets. Essential for class effect analysis, mechanism-based safety monitoring, and portfolio-level risk assessment. When safety signals emerge for one product

columns.name: patent_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: PV products must track primary patents for lifecycle management, regulatory submissions, and understanding formulation/composition when assessing adverse events. Essential for innovator product safety

columns.name: project_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.discovery_project. Business justification: Links marketed products to originating discovery projects for institutional knowledge and retrospective analysis. When serious safety issues arise, teams review original project rationale, target sele

columns.name: rems_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.rems. Business justification: When pv_product.rems_required=true, the product is enrolled in a REMS program. Linking pv_product to the specific rems record enables PV teams to access REMS program requirements during signal assessm

columns.name: responsible_org_unit_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.org_unit. Business justification: Each PV product is managed by a specific PV org unit (therapeutic area safety team). Product-to-org-unit assignment is required for PSMF maintenance, QPPV delegation, signal detection ownership, and P

columns.name: submission_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: pv_product represents the PV view of a product under a marketing authorization. Linking to the primary regulatory submission enables PSMF maintenance and product-level submission history tracking, a c

columns.name: argus_product_code
columns.description: Native product identifier from the Argus Safety / Oracle AERS pharmacovigilance system. Used for cross-system reconciliation and traceability between the Silver Layer PV product master and the operational PV case processing system.
columns.reference: Oracle Argus Safety Product Configuration; ICH E2B(R3) integration

columns.name: authorization_type
columns.description: Type of regulatory marketing authorisation application under which the product is approved (e.g., NDA — New Drug Application, BLA — Biologics License Application, MAA — Marketing Authorisation Application). Determines submission pathway and reporting requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NDA|BLA|MAA|ANDA|NDS|other — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 21 CFR 314; 21 CFR 601; EU Directive 2001/83/EC; ICH M4

columns.name: controlled_substance_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the product contains a controlled substance subject to DEA scheduling requirements. True = controlled substance; False = not a controlled substance. Impacts PV reporting and distribution controls.
columns.reference: DEA Controlled Substances Act; 21 CFR 1308; EU Directive 2011/62/EU

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the PV product master record was first created in the pharmacovigilance system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GVP Module II.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; EU GVP Module II; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: ema_product_number
columns.description: EMA-assigned product number for centrally authorised products in the EU. Used for EudraVigilance submissions, PSUR repository submissions, and EU regulatory correspondence.
columns.reference: EU GVP Module VI; EudraVigilance Access Policy; EMA/816573/2011

columns.name: eudravigilance_mp_code
columns.description: EudraVigilance Medicinal Product Dictionary (EVMPD) identifier assigned by EMA for the product. Required for electronic ICSR submissions to EudraVigilance and EU regulatory reporting.
columns.reference: EU GVP Module VI; EudraVigilance Data Analysis System; Regulation (EC) 726/2004

columns.name: expedited_reporting_required
columns.description: Indicates whether this product is subject to expedited (7-day or 15-day) Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) reporting obligations to health authorities. Drives case processing timelines in Argus Safety.
columns.reference: ICH E2D; EU GVP Module VI Section 6.3; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1); 21 CFR 312.32

columns.name: international_birth_date
columns.description: International Birth Date (IBD) — the date of first marketing authorisation granted worldwide for the active substance. Serves as the reference date for PSUR/PBRER data lock point scheduling per ICH E2C(R2).
columns.reference: ICH E2C(R2) Section 2.1; EU GVP Module VII; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)

columns.name: orphan_designation_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the product holds an orphan drug designation for a rare disease indication. True = orphan designation granted; False = no orphan designation. Affects PV reporting thresholds and PSUR requirements.
columns.reference: EU Regulation 141/2000; 21 CFR 316; FDA Orphan Drug Act

columns.name: product_type
columns.description: Classification of the medicinal product by its scientific/regulatory category (e.g., small molecule, biologic, vaccine, gene therapy, cell therapy, combination product). Drives applicable regulatory framework and PV requirements.
columns.reference: ICH S6(R1); EU GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 3.2(e)

columns.name: psmf_reference
columns.description: Reference identifier linking this product to the applicable Pharmacovigilance System Master File (PSMF) that describes the PV system governing this product. Mandatory for EU GVP Module II compliance.
columns.reference: EU GVP Module II; Directive 2001/83/EC Article 104; EMA/816573/2011

columns.name: psur_due_date
columns.glossary_term: Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) Next Due Date
columns.description: Next scheduled due date for submission of the Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) or Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER) to the relevant health authority. Calculated from IBD and submission frequency.
columns.reference: ICH E2C(R2) Section 2.1; EU GVP Module VII; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(ii)

columns.name: psur_frequency
columns.glossary_term: Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) Submission Frequency
columns.description: Regulatory-mandated frequency for Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) / Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER) submission for this product. Drives the PSUR scheduling calendar.
columns.reference: ICH E2C(R2); EU GVP Module VII; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(ii)

columns.name: pv_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the product within the pharmacovigilance system. Drives case processing eligibility, signal detection inclusion, and PSUR scheduling. Active = currently under PV surveillance; Suspended = temporarily halted; Withdrawn = marketing authorisation withdrawn; Under_review = under regulatory review; Archived = historical record only.
columns.reference: EU GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 314.81; Argus Safety product configuration

columns.name: rems_required
columns.glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Required Flag
columns.description: Indicates whether a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) is required by the FDA for this product. True = REMS is mandated; False = REMS not required. Applicable to US-authorised products only.

columns.name: rmp_required
columns.description: Indicates whether a Risk Management Plan (RMP) is required for this product by the applicable health authority. True = RMP is mandated; False = RMP not required. Drives risk minimisation activity tracking.
columns.reference: EU GVP Module V; EMA/838713/2011; 21 CFR 505-1 (REMS)

columns.name: signal_detection_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this product is currently included in the active signal detection and management programme. True = included in signal detection runs; False = excluded (e.g., archived or withdrawn products).
columns.reference: EU GVP Module IX; ICH E2E; FDA Guidance on Signal Detection

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the PV product master record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GVP Module II.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; EU GVP Module II; SOX

tables.name: suspect_drug
tables.description: Suspect and concomitant drug record within an ICSR. Captures drug name (verbatim and WHO Drug Dictionary coded), drug role (suspect, concomitant, interacting), dose, frequency, route, indication, start/stop dates, action taken (drug withdrawn, dose reduced, dose not changed, unknown), dechallenge result, rechallenge result, and batch/lot number. One ICSR may have multiple suspect and concomitant drugs. Enables product-level case aggregation for signal detection, line listing generation, and exposure-based analyses.

columns.name: suspect_drug_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the suspect or concomitant drug record within an Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR). Primary key of this entity.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Guideline on Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) Module VI

columns.name: icsr_id
columns.description: Reference to the parent Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) to which this suspect or concomitant drug record belongs. One ICSR may contain multiple drug records.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: inventory_lot_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to supply.inventory_lot. Business justification: PV case processing requires tracing a suspect drug's implicated batch to the actual inventory_lot for distribution scope assessment, cold chain compliance review, and batch recall decisions. Regulator

columns.name: investigational_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.investigational_product. Business justification: The suspect drug in a trial ICSR is the investigational product. Linking enables batch-level traceability for causality assessment and potential recall decisions per ICH E2B R3. suspect_drug has verba
