columns.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.hcp_master. Business justification: Tracking prescribing physician for suspect drugs enables prescriber-pattern analysis in signal detection, targeted DHPC distribution, and prescriber follow-up for dechallenge/rechallenge outcomes. Cri

columns.name: masterdata_ndc_code_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.ndc_code. Business justification: US ICSRs require NDC-level product identification for FDA submissions. Enables precise product matching, regulatory compliance, and integration with FDA Structured Product Labeling (SPL) for listednes

columns.name: material_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.material. Business justification: Suspect drugs must link to material master for batch traceability, quality investigations, and manufacturing deviation correlation. Enables root cause analysis when batch_lot_number indicates potentia

columns.name: pv_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.pv_product. Business justification: Suspect drugs in ICSRs should link to the PV product master for authoritative product data. Add pv_product_id FK. Remove product_name, inn_name, atc_code as they normalize to pv_product (verified pv_p

columns.name: treatment_exposure_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to patient.treatment_exposure. Business justification: Batch/lot-level safety investigations require tracing a PV suspect drug record to the specific treatment_exposure (lot_number, dose_administered, administration_date). This link is essential for batch

columns.name: action_taken
columns.description: Action taken with the suspect or concomitant drug in response to the adverse event (e.g., drug withdrawn, dose reduced, dose not changed, unknown). Critical for dechallenge assessment and causality evaluation. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.8.
columns.value_regex: drug withdrawn|dose reduced|dose increased|dose not changed|unknown|not applicable
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: coding_status
columns.description: Status of the WHO Drug Dictionary coding process for this drug record: coded (coding complete), pending (awaiting coding), not coded (unable to code), auto-coded (coded by automated system), or manually coded (coded by a pharmacovigilance specialist).
columns.reference: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD); Argus Safety; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: country_of_administration
columns.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country where the drug was administered to the patient. Used for regional signal detection and regulatory reporting stratification.
columns.reference: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: cumulative_dose_amount
columns.description: Total cumulative dose of the drug received by the patient from start to stop date (or to the date of the adverse event). Used in dose-response analyses and exposure-based signal detection. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.5a.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.5a; EMA GVP Module IX

columns.name: cumulative_dose_unit
columns.description: Unit of measurement for the cumulative dose amount (e.g., mg, g, IU). Must be interpreted in conjunction with cumulative_dose_amount. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.5b.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.5b; UCUM; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: dechallenge_result
columns.description: Outcome observed after the drug was withdrawn or dose reduced (dechallenge): whether the adverse event improved or resolved. A positive dechallenge supports causality. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.9.i.3.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i.3; WHO-UMC Causality Assessment; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: dosage_form
columns.description: Physical form of the drug product administered to the patient (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, patch, solution). Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.9.2. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|injection|solution|patch|cream|powder|suspension|inhaler|suppository — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.9.2; EDQM Standard Terms; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: dose_amount
columns.description: Numeric quantity of the drug administered per dose as reported. Must be interpreted in conjunction with dose_unit. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.1a.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.1a; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: dose_unit
columns.description: Unit of measurement for the dose amount (e.g., mg, mcg, g, mg/kg, IU, mL). Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.1b. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mg|mcg|g|mg/kg|IU|mL|mg/mL|% — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.1b; UCUM (Unified Code for Units of Measure); EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: dosing_frequency
columns.description: Frequency at which the drug was administered (e.g., once daily, twice daily, weekly). Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.3. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: once daily|twice daily|three times daily|four times daily|weekly|biweekly|monthly|as needed|continuous|every 8 hours — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.3; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: drug_role
columns.description: Role of the drug in the adverse event case: suspect (primary drug under investigation), concomitant (taken alongside but not suspected), interacting (suspected drug-drug interaction), or treatment (used to treat the adverse event). Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.1.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: drug_sequence_number
columns.description: Sequential number identifying the position of this drug record within the parent ICSR, used for ordering and referencing multiple drugs in a single case (e.g., drug 1, drug 2). Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.1.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.1; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: expiry_date
columns.description: Expiry date of the drug product batch administered to the patient. Used in product quality investigations to assess whether an expired product may have contributed to the adverse event. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.8.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.137; cGMP

columns.name: indication
columns.description: Medical condition or disease for which the drug was prescribed or taken, coded using MedDRA terminology. Supports indication-stratified signal detection and benefit-risk assessment. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.7.r.2b.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.7.r.2b; MedDRA; EMA GVP Module IX

columns.name: indication_verbatim
columns.description: Indication for drug use as reported verbatim by the reporter, prior to MedDRA coding. Preserved for traceability and coding audit. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.7.r.2a.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.7.r.2a; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: is_blinded
columns.description: Indicates whether the drug identity is blinded (True) in the context of a clinical trial (e.g., randomized controlled trial where the patient or investigator does not know the assigned treatment). Affects SUSAR reporting and unblinding procedures.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.2.5; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: is_company_product
columns.description: Indicates whether the drug is a product owned or marketed by the reporting company (True) or a competitor/third-party product (False). Determines regulatory reporting obligations and case ownership.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: parent_drug_code
columns.description: WHO Drug Dictionary parent drug code representing the active moiety or parent compound, used to group drug products sharing the same active substance for aggregate signal detection and PSUR analyses.
columns.reference: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD); ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module IX

columns.name: rechallenge_result
columns.description: Outcome observed after the drug was reintroduced following dechallenge (rechallenge): whether the adverse event recurred. A positive rechallenge is strong evidence of causality. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.9.i.4.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i.4; WHO-UMC Causality Assessment; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: record_created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this suspect or concomitant drug record was first created in the pharmacovigilance system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module VI.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: record_updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this suspect or concomitant drug record was last modified in the pharmacovigilance system. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module VI.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: route_of_administration
columns.description: Route by which the drug was administered to the patient (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, topical). Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.10.2. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intramuscular|topical|inhalation|transdermal|intrathecal — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.10.2; EDQM Standard Terms; FDA 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: source_system_drug_code
columns.description: Identifier of this drug record in the originating pharmacovigilance source system (e.g., Argus Safety case drug ID or Oracle AERS drug sequence identifier). Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the system of record.
columns.reference: Argus Safety / Oracle AERS; ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: Date on which the patient started taking the drug. Used to calculate drug exposure duration and temporal relationship to adverse event onset. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.4.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.4; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: stop_date
columns.description: Date on which the patient stopped taking the drug. Nullable if the drug was ongoing at the time of the report. Used to calculate exposure duration and assess dechallenge timing. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.5.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.5; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: time_to_onset_days
columns.description: Number of days between the drug start date and the onset of the adverse event. A key temporal metric for causality assessment and signal detection algorithms (e.g., disproportionality analysis).
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); WHO-UMC Causality Assessment; EMA GVP Module IX

columns.name: verbatim_drug_name
columns.description: Drug name exactly as reported by the reporter (patient, healthcare professional, or other source) before any coding or standardization. Preserved for traceability and audit. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.2.2.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.2.2; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: who_drug_code
columns.description: Unique alphanumeric code assigned by the WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD) to the coded medicinal product. Used for product-level case aggregation, line listing, and signal detection analytics.
columns.reference: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD); ICH E2B(R3) G.k.2.3.r.1

columns.name: who_drug_name
columns.glossary_term: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD) Coded Drug Name
columns.description: Standardized drug name as coded against the WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD), representing the preferred term for the medicinal product. Enables cross-case aggregation and signal detection.
columns.reference: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD); ICH E2B(R3) G.k.2.3; EMA GVP Module IX

tables.name: reporter
tables.description: Reporter master data — the individual or organization who submitted an adverse event report. Captures reporter type (healthcare professional, patient/consumer, lawyer, regulatory authority, literature), qualification (physician, pharmacist, nurse, dentist, consumer), country, institution, anonymized reporter identifier (per GDPR/HIPAA), contact preference for follow-up, and reporter reliability assessment. Enables reporter-level case aggregation, duplicate detection, follow-up management, and compliance with ICH E2B reporter data requirements. Distinct from HCP master — this is the PV-specific reporter identity used solely for case processing.

columns.name: reporter_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the pharmacovigilance reporter record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for the reporter master data entity.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety Reporter Entity

columns.name: country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Reporter country determines follow-up feasibility, data privacy regulations (GDPR vs others), contact protocols, and language requirements. Operational necessity for case management and regulatory com

columns.name: hco_master_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.hco_master. Business justification: Reporters (pharmacists, hospital physicians) are affiliated with HCOs. Linking reporter to hco_master supports institutional-level reporting pattern analysis, follow-up management, and GDPR data stewa

columns.name: master_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.hcp_master. Business justification: When reporter is HCP (is_hcp flag), linking to hcp_master enables license verification, specialty validation for causality assessment, NPI matching for regulatory submissions, and structured follow-up

columns.name: master_reporter_id
columns.description: Reference to the canonical/master reporter record when this record has been identified as a duplicate. Null if this record is itself the master. Supports deduplication and case re-linking workflows in the PV system.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety Duplicate Management

columns.name: masterdata_address_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.address. Business justification: Structured address linkage enables standardized contact management, duplicate reporter detection, and GDPR compliance (right to erasure). Replaces fragmented address fields with master data reference

columns.name: anonymized_reporter_code
columns.description: Privacy-compliant pseudonymous identifier assigned to the reporter in lieu of personal identifiers, enabling case aggregation and follow-up management without exposing PII. Mandatory under GDPR and HIPAA for PV processing.
columns.reference: GDPR Article 4 & Article 25; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; ICH E2B(R3) A.1.7

columns.name: argus_reporter_code
columns.description: Source system identifier for the reporter as assigned by Argus Safety / Oracle AERS. Used for lineage tracing and deduplication against the operational PV system.
columns.reference: Argus Safety / Oracle AERS Reporter Master; ICH E2B(R3) A.1.7

columns.name: consent_date
columns.description: Date on which the reporter provided or withdrew consent to be contacted for follow-up. Required for GDPR audit trail demonstrating lawful basis for processing personal data.

columns.name: consent_to_contact
columns.description: Indicates whether the reporter has provided explicit consent to be contacted for follow-up queries regarding the adverse event report. Mandatory consent gate under GDPR Article 7 before any follow-up communication is initiated.
columns.reference: GDPR Article 7; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.508; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: contact_preference
columns.description: Preferred channel for follow-up communication as indicated by the reporter. Drives the follow-up workflow in Argus Safety. 'no_contact' indicates the reporter has declined further contact, which must be respected per GDPR consent obligations.
columns.reference: GDPR Article 7; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety Follow-up Workflow

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the reporter record was first created in the PV system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records in regulated pharmaceutical environments.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; GDPR Article 30

columns.name: department
columns.description: Department or unit within the reporter's organization (e.g., Oncology Ward, Clinical Pharmacology, Drug Safety). Supports routing of follow-up queries to the correct organizational unit.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.4; Argus Safety Reporter Master

columns.name: duplicate_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this reporter record has been identified as a potential or confirmed duplicate of another reporter record. Duplicate reporters must be resolved before case processing to prevent double-counting in aggregate safety analyses.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; FDA 21 CFR §314.81; Argus Safety Duplicate Detection

columns.name: email
columns.description: Primary email address of the reporter for electronic follow-up correspondence. Classified as restricted PII. Used only for PV case follow-up; not shared with commercial systems. Consent-gated per GDPR.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.6; GDPR Article 4 & Article 6; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

columns.name: family_name
columns.description: Last/family name of the individual reporter. Stored in restricted classification per GDPR and HIPAA. Used for follow-up correspondence and duplicate detection. May be withheld or anonymized per reporter consent.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.3b; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

columns.name: fax
columns.description: Fax number of the reporter or their institution, used for formal follow-up correspondence in jurisdictions where fax remains a regulatory-accepted communication channel (e.g., Japan PMDA submissions).
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.6; PMDA Pharmacovigilance Guidelines

columns.name: first_report_date
columns.description: Date on which the reporter submitted their first adverse event report to the company. Used for longitudinal reporter relationship analysis and tenure-based reliability assessment.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety Reporter Master; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: follow_up_deadline
columns.description: Target date by which a follow-up response from the reporter is required to meet regulatory submission timelines (e.g., 15-day expedited reporting for SUSARs and SAEs). Calculated based on initial receipt date and applicable regulatory clock.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR §312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR Part 314.81

columns.name: follow_up_required
columns.description: Indicates whether outstanding follow-up queries have been sent to this reporter and a response is pending. Drives the follow-up management workflow in Argus Safety to ensure timely case completion within regulatory timeframes.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; FDA 21 CFR §312.32; Argus Safety Follow-up Workflow

columns.name: gdpr_erasure_date
columns.description: Date on which the GDPR Right to Erasure request was processed and PII fields were anonymized. Null if no erasure request has been received. Required for GDPR compliance audit trail.
columns.reference: GDPR Article 17 & Article 30; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: gdpr_erasure_requested
columns.description: Indicates whether the reporter has submitted a Right to Erasure (Right to be Forgotten) request under GDPR Article 17. When true, PII fields must be anonymized while retaining the anonymized case record for pharmacovigilance regulatory obligations under GDPR Article 17(3)(c).
columns.reference: GDPR Article 17; EMA GVP Module VI; ICH E2B(R3)

columns.name: given_name
columns.description: First/given name of the individual reporter. Stored in restricted classification per GDPR and HIPAA. Used for follow-up correspondence and duplicate detection. May be withheld or anonymized per reporter consent.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.3a; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

columns.name: is_hcp
columns.description: Indicates whether the reporter is a qualified Healthcare Professional (HCP). HCP-reported cases carry higher regulatory weight and may trigger expedited 15-day reporting obligations to FDA, EMA, and other health authorities.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.2; FDA 21 CFR §314.81; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR Part 312.32

columns.name: language_code
columns.description: ISO 639-1 or ISO 639-2 language code representing the reporter's preferred communication language. Used to route follow-up correspondence to appropriately qualified multilingual PV staff and to select translated follow-up letter templates.
columns.reference: ISO 639-1; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: last_report_date
columns.description: Date of the most recent adverse event report submitted by this reporter. Used to identify active versus dormant reporters and to support follow-up prioritization.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety Reporter Master; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: license_number
columns.description: Professional license or registration number of the HCP reporter (e.g., medical license, pharmacy registration). Used to verify reporter qualification and credibility. Stored as confidential business data.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.2; FDA MedWatch 3500A; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text field for PV case processor notes regarding the reporter, such as communication history, special handling instructions, or context about the reporter's relationship to the case. Not transmitted in regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: Argus Safety Reporter Master; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: organization_name
columns.description: Name of the institution, hospital, clinic, regulatory authority, or company from which the reporter submitted the adverse event report. Relevant for institutional reporters and regulatory authority submissions.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.4; EMA GVP Module VI; FDA 21 CFR §314.81

columns.name: phone
columns.description: Primary telephone number of the reporter for follow-up contact. Classified as restricted PII. Stored in E.164 international format where possible. Used exclusively for PV case follow-up activities.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.6; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

columns.name: qualification
columns.description: Professional qualification of the reporter, particularly relevant for Healthcare Professional (HCP) reporters. Determines the clinical credibility weighting of the report and regulatory classification. ICH E2B(R3) field A.2.1.2. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: physician|pharmacist|nurse|dentist|other_health_professional|consumer|unknown — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.2; EMA GVP Module VI; FDA MedWatch 3500A

columns.name: regulatory_authority_code
columns.description: Identifier of the regulatory authority (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA) when the reporter is a regulatory body. Used to route mandatory ICSR submissions and track authority-initiated follow-up requests.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.1.4; FDA 21 CFR §314.81; EMA GVP Module VI; MHRA Yellow Card; PMDA Guidelines

columns.name: reliability_score
columns.description: Internal PV team assessment of the reporter's historical reliability based on completeness and accuracy of prior submissions. Used to weight signal detection analysis and prioritize follow-up resources. Assigned by the PV case processor.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module VI; ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety Reporter Assessment

columns.name: reporter_status
columns.description: Current operational status of the reporter record within the PV system. Inactive or blocked reporters are excluded from new case assignments. Supports duplicate detection and data quality management.
columns.reference: Argus Safety Reporter Master; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: reporter_type
columns.description: Classification of the reporter by their relationship to the adverse event. Drives regulatory reporting obligations and follow-up workflows. ICH E2B(R3) field A.2.1.1. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: healthcare_professional|patient_consumer|lawyer|regulatory_authority|literature|other — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.1; FDA 21 CFR §314.81; EMA GVP Module VI

columns.name: source_type
columns.description: Classification of the original source through which the adverse event report was received. Determines regulatory handling requirements; e.g., literature-sourced reports require medical literature monitoring per GVP Module VI. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: spontaneous|literature|clinical_trial|regulatory_authority|solicited|other — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.1.4; EMA GVP Module VI; FDA 21 CFR §314.81

columns.name: specialty
columns.description: Medical or clinical specialty of the HCP reporter (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Neurology). Supports signal detection analysis by therapeutic area and enables targeted follow-up by medically qualified personnel.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety Reporter Master

columns.name: total_reports_submitted
columns.description: Cumulative count of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) submitted by this reporter. Used for duplicate detection, reporter profiling, and reliability assessment. Updated upon each new case linkage.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety Reporter Aggregation

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the reporter record. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GDPR Article 30 record-keeping obligations.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; GDPR Article 30

tables.name: pv_action
tables.description: Pharmacovigilance action record capturing regulatory and safety actions taken in response to validated signals, PSUR findings, RMP updates, or authority requests. Action types include: labeling updates (CCDS, SmPC, USPI changes), DHPC (Dear Healthcare Professional Communication), restricted indication, market suspension/withdrawal, REMS modification, RMP update trigger, and PASS study initiation. Tracks action type, triggering event, responsible party, target completion date, authority notification requirement, implementation evidence, and effectiveness assessment. Links signals, PSURs, and RMPs to their downstream regulatory consequences.
tables.reference: GVP Module XVI / FDA REMS / EMA RMP Action

columns.name: pv_action_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the pharmacovigilance action record. Primary key for this entity. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — represents a discrete regulatory/safety action with a defined lifecycle triggered by a validated signal, PSUR finding, RMP update, or health authority request.
columns.reference: ICH E2E Pharmacovigilance Planning; 21 CFR Part 314; EMA GVP Module V

columns.name: action_country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: PV actions (DHPC distributions, label updates) are scoped to specific markets/countries. The market_scope field is a plain-text denormalization of country. A proper FK enables country-specific regulat

columns.name: adverse_event_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to patient.adverse_event. Business justification: Risk minimization actions (DHCP letters, label updates, REMS) must be traceable to the triggering clinical adverse event for CAPA documentation and health authority inspection readiness. pv_action.tri

columns.name: approval_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.approval. Business justification: PV actions may result in approval condition modifications, suspension, or withdrawal. Linking pv_action to the affected approval enables tracking of approval-level safety actions, required for benefit

columns.name: brand_plan_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand_plan. Business justification: PV actions (label changes, DHPC distributions, REMS updates) must be tracked against brand plans so commercial teams can assess strategic impact and update promotional plans. Brand plan owners are for

columns.name: copay_program_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.copay_program. Business justification: PV actions implementing REMS or restricted distribution requirements can mandate suspension or modification of copay programs for restricted drugs. Commercial operations teams need this link to execut

columns.name: hco_master_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.hco_master. Business justification: PV actions such as DHCP letters and risk minimization measures are directed at healthcare organizations. Linking pv_action to hco_master enables tracking which HCOs received safety communications — re

columns.name: health_authority_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.health_authority. Business justification: PV actions include authority notifications (DHPC, urgent safety restrictions). pv_action.notified_authorities is a plain attribute. A proper FK to health_authority enables authority-specific action tr

columns.name: icsr_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.icsr. Business justification: PV actions (label updates, DHPC distributions, REMS programs) can be triggered directly by individual ICSRs — particularly serious, unexpected, fatal cases that require immediate regulatory action. Th

columns.name: internal_order_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Safety actions (label updates, REMS implementation, DHPC distribution, risk communication campaigns) generate implementation costs tracked via internal orders. Finance captures costs for regulatory su

columns.name: inventory_lot_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to supply.inventory_lot. Business justification: PV actions such as lot quarantine, destruction orders, or restricted distribution target specific inventory lots. Formally linking pv_action to inventory_lot enables GMP compliance tracking, lot dispo

columns.name: investigator_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.investigator. Business justification: PV actions triggered by clinical trial safety signals (protocol amendments, investigator notifications, unblinding decisions) must be linked to the responsible investigator. This supports GCP complian

columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.invoice. Business justification: PV actions such as DHPC distribution, label update printing, REMS program implementation, and effectiveness surveys are executed by external vendors who invoice for services. Linking pv_action to invo

columns.name: label_change_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.label_change. Business justification: PV actions of type 'label update' directly produce label change records. Linking pv_action to label_change enables end-to-end traceability from safety signal action to implemented label change, requir

columns.name: label_id

When a safety action requires notifying a partner (licensee, c

columns.reference: EMA XEVMPD; FDA NDC Directory; ICH E2B(R3)

columns.description: Foreign key linking to market.reimbursement_policy. Business justification: PV actions such as label updates, DHPC issuance, or REMS implementation directly trigger reimbursement policy revisions — payers must update coverage criteria and prior authorization requirements. Tra

columns.name: rmp_id
columns.description: Reference to the Risk Management Plan (RMP) associated with or updated by this pharmacovigilance action. Nullable when the action is not RMP-driven.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module V; ICH E2E; FDA REMS Guidance

columns.name: sae_report_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.sae_report. Business justification: SAE events can trigger PV actions (regulatory notifications, safety measures). Add sae_report_id FK (nullable - only when action is triggered by SAE). The triggering_event_type field indicates the tri

columns.name: safety_signal_id
columns.description: Reference to the validated safety signal that triggered this pharmacovigilance action. Links the action to its upstream signal detection record for traceability and regulatory reporting.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module IX; ICH E2E; FDA Guidance on Signal Detection

columns.name: submission_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: PV actions (label updates, DHPC, REMS modifications) result in regulatory submissions. Linking pv_action to the resulting regulatory submission enables tracking of action-to-submission timelines, a ke

columns.name: susar_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.susar. Business justification: SUSAR events can trigger PV actions (label changes, regulatory notifications). Add susar_id FK (nullable - only when action is triggered by SUSAR). The triggering_event_type field indicates the trigge

columns.name: trial_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.trial. Business justification: Regulatory PV actions (label updates, DHPC, protocol amendments) are often triggered by safety findings from a specific clinical trial. Linking pv_action to trial enables traceability from regulatory

columns.name: variation_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.variation. Business justification: Safety-driven PV actions result in Type II variations (EU) or Prior Approval Supplements (US). Linking pv_action to the resulting variation enables tracking of safety-driven variation timelines and re

columns.name: action_description
columns.description: Detailed narrative description of the pharmacovigilance action, including the specific risk minimization measures to be implemented, rationale, and expected patient safety impact. Captured from Argus Safety case narrative or Veeva Vault RIM action record.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module V; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 314.81

columns.name: action_number
columns.description: Externally-known business identifier for the PV action, formatted as PVA-{YYYY}-{NNNNNN}. Used in regulatory correspondence, authority notifications, and cross-system tracking within Argus Safety/Oracle AERS and Veeva Vault RIM.
columns.reference: ICH E2E; EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314.81

columns.name: action_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the pharmacovigilance action, tracking progression from initiation through completion or cancellation. Drives workflow routing in safety management systems.
columns.reference: ICH E2E; EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: action_type
columns.description: Classification of the regulatory or safety action being taken. Includes labeling updates (CCDS/SmPC/USPI changes), Dear Healthcare Professional Communication (DHPC), restricted indication, market suspension/withdrawal, Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) modification, Risk Management Plan (RMP) update trigger, and Post-Authorization Safety Study (PASS) initiation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: labeling_update|dhpc|restricted_indication|market_suspension|market_withdrawal|rems_modification|rmp_update|pass_initiation — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module V; FDA REMS Guidance; ICH E2C(R2); 21 CFR Part 314.81

columns.name: actual_completion_date
columns.description: Date on which the pharmacovigilance action was fully implemented and closed. Compared against target_completion_date to assess timeliness and regulatory compliance. Nullable until action is completed.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314.81; ICH E2E

columns.name: argus_case_number
columns.description: Source system case or action number from Argus Safety/Oracle AERS, the operational system of record for pharmacovigilance. Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the source PV system.
columns.reference: Argus Safety/Oracle AERS; 21 CFR Part 11; EMA GVP Module I

columns.name: authority_notification_date
columns.description: Date on which the relevant health authority (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA, etc.) was formally notified of this pharmacovigilance action. Nullable when notification is not required or not yet submitted.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA GVP Module V; MHRA Guidance on PV

columns.name: authority_notification_required
columns.description: Indicates whether this pharmacovigilance action requires formal notification to one or more health authorities (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, etc.) prior to or upon implementation. Drives regulatory submission workflows.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA GVP Module V; ICH E2C(R2)

columns.name: benefit_risk_impact
columns.description: Assessment of how this pharmacovigilance action affects the overall benefit-risk balance of the medicinal product. Informs PSUR/PBRER benefit-risk conclusions and regulatory authority communications.
columns.reference: ICH E2C(R2); EMA GVP Module VII; FDA Benefit-Risk Framework

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this PV action record was first captured in the system (Argus Safety/Oracle AERS or Veeva Vault). Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); EMA GVP Module I

columns.name: dhpc_distribution_scope
columns.glossary_term: Dear Healthcare Professional Communication (DHPC) Distribution Scope
columns.description: Geographic scope of the Dear Healthcare Professional Communication (DHPC) distribution when action_type is dhpc. Indicates whether the communication is national, regional, or global. Not applicable for non-DHPC actions.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module XV; 21 CFR Part 200.5; MHRA DHCP Guidance

columns.name: effectiveness_assessment_date
columns.description: Date on which the effectiveness assessment of this pharmacovigilance action was completed or is scheduled. Supports periodic benefit-risk evaluation and regulatory reporting cycles.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module XVI; FDA REMS Assessment Guidance; ICH E2C(R2)

columns.name: effectiveness_assessment_outcome
columns.description: Outcome of the post-implementation effectiveness assessment, indicating whether the pharmacovigilance action successfully minimized the identified risk. Informs subsequent signal management and RMP update decisions.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module XVI; FDA REMS Assessment Guidance; ICH E2E

columns.name: effectiveness_assessment_status
columns.description: Status of the post-implementation effectiveness assessment for this pharmacovigilance action. Tracks whether the action achieved its intended risk minimization objective, as required by EMA GVP Module XVI and FDA REMS assessment requirements.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module XVI; FDA REMS Assessment Guidance; ICH E2E

columns.name: escalation_date
columns.description: Date on which this pharmacovigilance action was escalated to senior management or the QPPV. Nullable when escalation_flag is false. Supports governance and oversight reporting.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module I; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: escalation_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this pharmacovigilance action has been escalated due to missed deadlines, critical safety findings, or authority pressure. Triggers executive and QPPV notification workflows.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module I; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: implementation_evidence_ref
columns.description: Document reference number or Veeva Vault document ID for the evidence package demonstrating that the pharmacovigilance action has been implemented (e.g., updated label version, DHPC distribution confirmation, REMS modification approval letter).
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314.81; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: initiated_date
columns.description: The date on which the pharmacovigilance action was formally initiated or triggered. Represents the principal real-world business event timestamp (day-level precision) for regulatory timeline tracking and compliance reporting.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314.81; ICH E2E

columns.name: labeling_document_type
columns.description: Type of labeling document affected when action_type is labeling_update. Identifies whether the Company Core Data Sheet (CCDS), Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC), US Prescribing Information (USPI), Patient Information Leaflet (PIL), or package insert is being updated. Null or not_applicable for non-labeling actions.
columns.reference: ICH E2C(R2); EMA SmPC Guideline; 21 CFR Part 201; Directive 2001/83/EC

columns.name: labeling_section_affected
columns.description: Specific section(s) of the labeling document being updated (e.g., Section 4.4 Special Warnings, Section 4.8 Undesirable Effects, Boxed Warning, Contraindications). Applicable only for labeling_update action type.
columns.reference: EMA SmPC Guideline; 21 CFR Part 201.57; ICH E2C(R2)

columns.name: notified_authorities
columns.description: Comma-separated list of health authority codes (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA) that have been or must be notified of this action. Supports multi-jurisdictional regulatory tracking.
columns.reference: ICH E2C(R2); EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314.81; PMDA Pharmacovigilance Regulations

columns.name: priority_level
columns.description: Risk-based priority classification of the pharmacovigilance action, determining escalation urgency and resource allocation. Critical actions typically involve immediate patient safety risks requiring expedited regulatory response.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module V; ICH E2E; FDA Guidance on Signal Detection

columns.name: regulatory_deadline_date
columns.description: Mandatory deadline imposed by a health authority (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA) for completion or notification of this pharmacovigilance action. Distinct from the internally-set target_completion_date. Non-compliance may result in regulatory sanctions.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA GVP Module V; MHRA Guidance on PV; PMDA Regulations

columns.name: rems_program_name
columns.glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Program Name
columns.description: Name of the FDA-approved Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program being modified when action_type is rems_modification. Nullable for non-REMS actions.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.520; FDA REMS Guidance; FDAAA Section 505-1

columns.name: responsible_party
columns.description: Organizational unit or party accountable for implementing and completing this pharmacovigilance action. Determines workflow ownership and escalation paths within the safety management system. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pv_team|regulatory_affairs|medical_affairs|manufacturing|commercial|external_cro|external_cmo — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module I; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: target_completion_date
columns.description: Planned date by which the pharmacovigilance action must be fully implemented. Drives SLA monitoring, regulatory deadline tracking, and escalation workflows. Distinct from actual completion date.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314.81; ICH E2E

columns.name: triggering_event_reference
columns.description: Free-text or structured reference number identifying the specific triggering event (e.g., signal case number, PSUR submission number, authority correspondence reference). Provides cross-system traceability.
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module V; ICH E2C(R2); 21 CFR Part 314.81

columns.name: triggering_event_type
columns.description: Classification of the upstream event or finding that necessitated this PV action. Distinguishes between signal validation outcomes, PSUR/PBRER findings, RMP periodic reviews, health authority requests, SUSAR clusters, out-of-specification (OOS) trends, and literature review findings. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: signal_validation|psur_finding|rmp_review|authority_request|susar_cluster|oos_trend|literature_review — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: EMA GVP Module IX; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 314.81

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this PV action record. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module I.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; EMA GVP Module I; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: veeva_vault_doc_reference
columns.description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault RIM or QualityDocs for the regulatory submission package, labeling document, or DHPC associated with this action. Supports document management and regulatory submission traceability.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11; EMA GVP Module V

tables.name: pv_agreement
tables.description: Pharmacovigilance agreement record governing safety data exchange obligations between the MAH and partners. Covers SDEAs (Safety Data Exchange Agreements), PVAs (Pharmacovigilance Agreements), and co-vigilance arrangements with licensees, CROs, CMOs, co-promotion partners, and local affiliates. Captures agreement type, counterparty, effective/expiry dates, reporting timelines (days to exchange), product scope, responsible party designations (PSUR authorship, signal management, regulatory submission), and compliance monitoring status. Required under GVP Module I and ICH E2E for all outsourced PV activities.
tables.reference: EU GVP Module I SDEA / Safety Data Exchange Agreement

columns.name: pv_agreement_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the pharmacovigilance agreement record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity. Role: MASTER_AGREEMENT.

columns.name: approval_id

columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.business_partner. Business justification: The counterparty in a PV agreement is a registered business partner in the MDM system (licensee, co-marketing partner, CRO). Linking to business_partner enables counterparty data quality management, a

columns.name: licensing_agreement_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.licensing_agreement. Business justification: PV agreements are negotiated as part of or directly reference licensing agreements — ICSR exchange timelines, SUSAR reporting obligations, and PSUR responsibilities are defined within the licensing de

columns.name: mah_legal_entity_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Pharmacovigilance agreements are contracts between legal entities defining safety data exchange obligations. MAH legal entity linkage foundational for contract management, audit trail, and regulatory

columns.name: managing_org_unit_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.org_unit. Business justification: PV agreements are managed by specific PV org units (alliance management, PV operations). Org unit ownership is required for compliance review scheduling, ICSR exchange monitoring, and PV agreement aud

columns.name: project_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.project. Business justification: PV agreements with partners/licensees are negotiated per development program and govern safety data exchange obligations for a specific project. Compliance teams need to associate PV agreements with d

columns.name: pv_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.pv_product. Business justification: A PV agreement governs safety data exchange obligations for specific medicinal products. The pv_agreement table has territory_scope and counterparty fields but no structured FK to the product it cover

columns.name: royalty_agreement_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.royalty_agreement. Business justification: Pharmacovigilance agreements with licensors/licensees for in-licensed or out-licensed products often reference the same commercial relationship as royalty agreements. Linking enables tracking of safet

columns.name: site_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to manufacturing.site. Business justification: PV agreements with CMO/CDMO partners specify which manufacturing sites are covered by ICSR exchange and SUSAR reporting obligations (ICH E2D, EU GVP Module I). Linking pv_agreement to the manufacturin

columns.name: territory_country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: PV agreements have a defined territory scope and governing law country. counterparty_country and governing_law_country are plain-text denormalizations of country. A proper FK enables territory-based P

columns.name: agreement_number
columns.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique reference number assigned to the pharmacovigilance agreement (e.g., SDEA-2024-0042). Used in regulatory correspondence, audit trails, and partner communications. Maps to the document number in Veeva Vault RIM or Argus Safety agreement registry.
columns.reference: GVP Module I; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: agreement_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the pharmacovigilance agreement. DRAFT = under negotiation; ACTIVE = in force and binding; SUSPENDED = temporarily paused by mutual consent or regulatory action; TERMINATED = permanently ended before expiry; EXPIRED = reached end date without renewal; UNDER_REVIEW = undergoing periodic review or amendment.

columns.name: agreement_type
columns.description: Classification of the pharmacovigilance agreement by its legal and operational nature. SDEA = Safety Data Exchange Agreement; PVA = Pharmacovigilance Agreement; CO_VIGILANCE = co-vigilance arrangement; CO_PROMOTION = co-promotion partner PV agreement; AFFILIATE = local affiliate PV agreement. Determines the regulatory obligations and reporting obligations applicable to each party.
columns.reference: GVP Module I; ICH E2E; EMA/873138/2011

columns.name: amendment_date
columns.description: Date of the most recent amendment to the pharmacovigilance agreement. Nullable if no amendments have been made since original execution. Used to track agreement evolution and trigger re-review workflows.
columns.reference: GVP Module I; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2E

columns.name: argus_agreement_ref
columns.description: Reference identifier used in Argus Safety / Oracle AERS to link this pharmacovigilance agreement to the partner configuration for automated ICSR routing and exchange. Enables traceability between the agreement record and the operational safety system configuration.
columns.reference: Argus Safety; Oracle AERS; GVP Module VI; ICH E2B(R3)

columns.name: compliance_status
columns.description: Current compliance monitoring status of the pharmacovigilance agreement based on periodic reviews, audits, and KPI tracking. COMPLIANT = all obligations met; NON_COMPLIANT = one or more obligations breached; UNDER_REVIEW = compliance assessment in progress; PENDING_AUDIT = scheduled for compliance audit. Supports GVP Module I oversight requirements.
columns.reference: GVP Module I; GVP Module II; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: counterparty_pv_contact_email
columns.description: Email address of the designated pharmacovigilance contact at the counterparty organisation. Used for operational safety data exchange communications and escalation notifications.
columns.reference: GVP Module I; GDPR Article 4; ICH E2E

columns.name: counterparty_pv_contact_name
columns.description: Name of the designated pharmacovigilance contact person at the counterparty organisation responsible for safety data exchange under this agreement. Required for operational communication and escalation.

columns.name: counterparty_type
columns.description: Classification of the counterparty by their operational role in the pharmaceutical value chain. CRO = Contract Research Organization; CMO = Contract Manufacturing Organization; CDMO = Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization; LICENSEE = product licensee; CO_PROMOTER = co-promotion partner; AFFILIATE = local affiliate entity; DISTRIBUTOR = distribution partner. Drives applicable GVP obligations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CRO|CMO|CDMO|LICENSEE|CO_PROMOTER|AFFILIATE|DISTRIBUTOR — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: GVP Module I; GVP Module VI; ICH E2E

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this pharmacovigilance agreement record was first created in the system. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX per model conventions. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module I.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GVP Module I; ICH E2E

columns.name: data_exchange_format
columns.description: Specifies the technical format used for exchanging Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) between parties. E2B_R2 = ICH E2B(R2) XML format; E2B_R3 = ICH E2B(R3) FHIR-based format; PAPER = paper-based exchange; PROPRIETARY = system-specific format; NOT_SPECIFIED = format not yet defined. Drives technical integration requirements with Argus Safety/Oracle AERS.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); EMA/EMEA/H/20665/04; FDA 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: data_exchange_method
columns.description: Technical transmission method used for exchanging safety data between parties. EVWEB = EMA EudraVigilance Web Trader; GATEWAY = automated gateway-to-gateway; SFTP = secure file transfer; EMAIL = encrypted email; MANUAL = manual entry; API = direct API integration. Determines system configuration in Argus Safety.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3); EMA EudraVigilance; FDA FAERS; GVP Module VI

columns.name: effective_date
columns.description: Date on which the pharmacovigilance agreement becomes legally binding and operational obligations commence. Determines the start of mandatory safety data exchange timelines. Formatted as yyyy-MM-dd per model conventions.
columns.reference: GVP Module I; 21 CFR Part 314.81; ICH E2E

columns.name: expiry_date
columns.description: Date on which the pharmacovigilance agreement ceases to be in force unless renewed or extended. Nullable for open-ended agreements. Used to trigger renewal workflows and compliance alerts. Formatted as yyyy-MM-dd per model conventions.

columns.name: icsr_exchange_days
columns.glossary_term: Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) Exchange Timeline (Days)
columns.description: Number of calendar days within which Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) must be exchanged between the MAH and the counterparty following initial receipt. Typically 7 days for fatal/life-threatening SUSARs and 15 days for other serious cases per GVP Module VI. Drives compliance monitoring and SLA tracking.
columns.reference: GVP Module VI; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA/873138/2011

columns.name: is_gdpr_dpa_in_place
columns.glossary_term: GDPR Data Processing Agreement (DPA) In Place Flag
columns.description: Indicates whether a GDPR-compliant Data Processing Agreement (DPA) is in place with the counterparty covering the personal data exchanged as part of pharmacovigilance activities. Mandatory for EU-based safety data exchange under GDPR Article 28.
columns.reference: GDPR Article 28; GVP Module I; EMA/873138/2011

columns.name: language
columns.description: ISO 639-1 or ISO 639-2 language code of the governing language of the pharmacovigilance agreement document (e.g., EN for English, DE for German, FR for French). Relevant for legal interpretation and translation obligations.

columns.name: last_compliance_review_date
columns.description: Date of the most recent periodic compliance review conducted for this pharmacovigilance agreement. Used to track review frequency and identify overdue reviews per GVP Module I requirements for oversight of outsourced PV activities.
columns.reference: GVP Module I; GVP Module II; ICH E2E

columns.name: last_updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this pharmacovigilance agreement record. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX per model conventions. Supports change tracking and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GVP Module I; ICH E2E

columns.name: next_compliance_review_date
columns.description: Date on which the next periodic compliance review of this pharmacovigilance agreement is scheduled. Drives workflow scheduling and resource planning for the PV compliance team.
columns.reference: GVP Module I; GVP Module II; ICH E2E

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text field for capturing additional context, special conditions, derogations, or operational notes relevant to this pharmacovigilance agreement that are not captured in structured fields. Used by PV operations and regulatory affairs teams.

columns.name: psur_responsible_party
columns.glossary_term: Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) Responsible Party
columns.description: Designates which party bears primary responsibility for authoring and submitting Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs) / Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Reports (PBRERs) to regulatory authorities. MAH = Marketing Authorisation Holder; COUNTERPARTY = partner organisation; JOINT = shared responsibility; NOT_APPLICABLE = PSURs not in scope of this agreement.
columns.reference: GVP Module VII; ICH E2C(R2); 21 CFR Part 314.81

columns.name: qppv_contact_name
columns.glossary_term: Qualified Person for Pharmacovigilance (QPPV) Contact Name
columns.description: Name of the Qualified Person Responsible for Pharmacovigilance (QPPV) designated by the MAH under this agreement. The QPPV is a mandatory regulatory role under EU GVP legislation responsible for the PV system. Captured for regulatory compliance and audit purposes.
columns.reference: GVP Module I; Directive 2001/83/EC Article 8(3)(ia); EMA/873138/2011

columns.name: regulatory_submission_responsible_party
columns.description: Designates which party is responsible for submitting safety reports (ICSRs, SUSARs, PSURs, RMPs) to national competent authorities (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, etc.) for products in scope. Determines accountability in regulatory inspections and audits.
columns.reference: GVP Module I; GVP Module VI; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA/873138/2011

columns.name: renewal_notification_days
columns.description: Number of calendar days before the agreement expiry date that a renewal notification must be issued to the counterparty. Drives automated alerting in the PV agreement management system to prevent lapses in safety data exchange coverage.

columns.name: rmp_responsible_party
columns.description: Designates which party is responsible for maintaining and updating the Risk Management Plan (RMP) for products covered under this agreement. Relevant for EU-authorised products where RMP is mandatory per GVP Module V.
columns.reference: GVP Module V; EMA/838713/2011; ICH E2E

columns.name: signal_management_responsible_party
columns.description: Designates which party is responsible for signal detection, assessment, and management activities for products covered under this agreement. MAH = Marketing Authorisation Holder; COUNTERPARTY = partner; JOINT = shared; NOT_APPLICABLE = signal management not in scope. Aligns with GVP Module IX obligations.
columns.reference: GVP Module IX; ICH E2E; EMA/873138/2011

columns.name: susar_exchange_days

tables.name: signal_case_series
tables.description: This association product represents the Signal Case Series relationship between a safety_signal and an icsr. It captures the operational linkage between a pharmacovigilance safety signal and each Individual Case Safety Report that contributes to or supports that signal, as managed per GVP Module IX and ICH E2E. Each record documents one ICSR's participation in one signal detection run, including its contribution score, MedDRA match, and case contribution status. This is the authoritative source for case-level drill-down, regulatory queries, and signal validation workflows in the pharmacovigilance system.. Existence Justification: In pharmacovigilance, a safety signal is identified by aggregating and analyzing multiple ICSRs — a single signal can be supported by hundreds of individual case reports, and a single ICSR can contribute to multiple signals (e.g., the same adverse event case may contribute to a signal for Drug A alone and a signal for a Drug A + Drug B interaction). The business actively manages this 'signal case series' as a first-class operational concept in safety databases like Argus Safety and Oracle AERS, used for regulatory queries, signal validation, and case-level drill-down. The relationship carries its own data (contribution score, detection run date, MedDRA match flag) that belongs to neither the signal nor the ICSR alone.

columns.glossary_term: Signal Case Series - Signal Case Series Id

columns.description: Foreign key linking to the Individual Case Safety Report contributing to the signal

columns.name: case_contribution_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this ICSR is a contributing (numerator) case in the disproportionality analysis for the signal, as opposed to a background reference case. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

columns.name: case_count
columns.description: Total number of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) or adverse event cases contributing to this safety signal at the time of detection or most recent assessment. Used as a threshold criterion alongside disproportionality metrics. [Moved from safety_signal: The aggregate case_count on safety_signal is a derived summary of the signal_case_series records. While the aggregate may be retained on safety_signal for performance/reporting purposes, the authoritative case-level data now lives in signal_case_series. If retained, it should be treated as a denormalized cache, not the source of truth.]
columns.reference: GVP Module IX Signal Management; ICH E2C(R2); EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

columns.name: detection_run_date
columns.description: Date of the specific signal detection run during which this ICSR was identified as contributing to the safety signal. Belongs to the relationship, not to the signal or the ICSR alone. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

columns.name: disproportionality_contribution_score
columns.description: Per-case contribution score to the aggregate disproportionality metric (PRR/ROR/EBGM/IC) for this signal. Quantifies how much this individual ICSR influences the signal strength. Belongs to the relationship, not to either entity alone. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

columns.name: meddra_pt_code_matched
columns.description: The specific MedDRA Preferred Term code from the ICSR that matched the signal's MedDRA PT during the detection run. An ICSR may have multiple MedDRA terms; this records which one drove the case's inclusion in this signal's case series. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

columns.description: Human-readable name describing the packaging configuration, typically including container type, pack size, and market designation.
