columns.description: Method by which consent was obtained. Distinguishes between paper-based, electronic consent (eConsent), verbal consent, or telephonic consent.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2), 21 CFR Part 11, EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014

columns.name: consent_obtained_date
columns.description: Date when the informed consent was obtained from the patient or legally authorized representative (LAR). Primary business event timestamp for consent lifecycle.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2), 21 CFR Part 50.27, GDPR Article 7

columns.name: consent_obtained_timestamp
columns.description: Precise timestamp when consent was obtained. Used for eConsent systems and audit trail. Complements consent_obtained_date with time-of-day precision.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2), 21 CFR Part 11, GDPR Article 7

columns.name: consent_purpose
columns.description: Specific purpose for which consent was obtained. Examples: clinical_trial_participation, data_processing, research, marketing, data_sharing, pharmacovigilance, patient_support_program. Free-text or controlled vocabulary.
columns.reference: GDPR Article 6, HIPAA Privacy Rule 45 CFR 164.508, ICH GCP E6(R2)

columns.name: consent_signature_method
columns.description: Method by which the patient or LAR signed the consent. Examples: wet_signature (ink on paper), electronic_signature, digital_signature (PKI-based), biometric, verbal_recorded.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH GCP E6(R2), eIDAS Regulation (EU)

columns.name: consent_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the consent. Tracks whether consent is pending signature, obtained, withdrawn by patient, expired, declined, or revoked.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2), GDPR Article 7, HIPAA Privacy Rule 45 CFR 164.508

columns.name: consent_type
columns.description: Specific type or sub-category of consent. Examples: main_study, sub_study_genetic, sub_study_biomarker, future_research, data_processing, marketing, third_party_sharing. Provides granular classification within consent_category.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2), GDPR Article 6, HIPAA Privacy Rule

columns.name: consent_withdrawal_date
columns.description: Date when the patient withdrew consent. Null if consent has not been withdrawn. Critical for GCP compliance and data subject rights.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2) Section 4.3.4, GDPR Article 7(3), HIPAA Privacy Rule 45 CFR 164.508(b)(5)

columns.name: data_subject_rights_fulfillment_date
columns.description: Date when the data subject rights request was fulfilled or completed. Null if request is pending or no request exists.

columns.name: data_subject_rights_request_date
columns.description: Date when the data subject rights request was received. Null if no request. Critical for GDPR compliance (30-day response requirement).

columns.name: data_subject_rights_request_type
columns.description: Type of data subject rights request associated with this consent record. Examples: access, erasure, portability, rectification, restriction, objection. Null if no request. Applicable for GDPR compliance.

columns.name: econsent_platform
columns.description: Name or identifier of the eConsent platform or system used to capture electronic consent. Examples: Medidata Rave, Veeva Vault, Florence eBinders. Null for paper consents.

columns.name: future_use_consent_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the patient consented to future use of their data or biological samples for research purposes beyond the current study. True if consented, False if declined.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2), GDPR Article 6, 21 CFR Part 50

columns.name: gdpr_lawful_basis
columns.glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Lawful Basis
columns.description: GDPR Article 6 or Article 9 lawful basis for processing personal data. Examples: consent, legitimate_interest, legal_obligation, vital_interests, public_task, explicit_consent_special_category. Applicable for EU/EEA patients.

columns.name: genetic_substudy_consent_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the patient consented to participate in genetic or genomic sub-studies. True if consented, False if declined or not applicable.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2), GDPR Article 9 (Special Categories), 21 CFR Part 50

columns.name: hipaa_authorization_flag
columns.glossary_term: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Authorization Flag
columns.description: Indicates whether HIPAA authorization was obtained for use and disclosure of protected health information (PHI). True if authorization obtained, False if not applicable or declined. Applicable for US patients.

columns.name: icf_version
columns.description: Version number or identifier of the informed consent form document used. Critical for regulatory traceability and protocol amendment tracking. Applicable for clinical trial consents.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2) Section 4.8, 21 CFR Part 312.60

columns.name: lar_name
columns.description: Full name of the legally authorized representative or caregiver who provided consent on behalf of the patient. Applicable for pediatric populations or incapacitated patients.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2) Section 4.8.15, 21 CFR Part 50.3(l)

columns.name: lar_relationship
columns.description: Relationship of the LAR to the patient. Examples: parent, legal guardian, healthcare proxy, power of attorney, caregiver.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2) Section 4.8.15, 21 CFR Part 50.3(l)

columns.name: re_consent_reason
columns.description: Reason for re-consenting the patient. Examples: protocol_amendment, new_safety_information, icf_version_update, regulatory_requirement. Applicable when consent_category is re_consent.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2) Section 4.8.2, 21 CFR Part 312.60

columns.name: record_created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this consent record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance.

columns.name: record_updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this consent record was last updated in the system. Audit trail field for change tracking and compliance.

columns.name: withdrawal_reason
columns.description: Reason provided by the patient for withdrawing consent. Examples: adverse_event, personal_reasons, lack_of_efficacy, relocation, lost_to_followup. Free-text or controlled vocabulary.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2) Section 4.3.4, GDPR Article 7(3)

columns.name: withdrawal_scope
columns.description: Scope of consent withdrawal. Indicates whether patient withdrew from entire study, data use only, biological sample use only, or future contact. Critical for GCP compliance.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2) Section 4.3.4, 21 CFR Part 312.50

columns.name: witness_name
columns.description: Full name of the impartial witness who observed the consent process. Required when patient or LAR cannot read, or as per local regulations.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2) Section 4.8.9, 21 CFR Part 50.27

columns.name: witness_signature_date
columns.description: Date when the impartial witness signed the informed consent form. Null if no witness was required.
columns.reference: ICH GCP E6(R2) Section 4.8.9, 21 CFR Part 50.27

tables.name: concomitant_medication
tables.description: Records all concomitant medications taken by a participant during a study or program period. Captures WHO Drug-coded medication name, ATC classification code, dose, dose unit, route of administration, frequency, start date, stop date, ongoing flag, indication for use, and whether the medication is a prohibited concomitant per protocol. Critical for safety assessment, drug-drug interaction analysis, and pharmacovigilance case narratives.
tables.reference: WHO Drug Dictionary / ICH E2A Concomitant Medications

columns.name: concomitant_medication_id
columns.description: Unique identifier for the concomitant medication record. Primary key for this entity.

columns.name: adverse_event_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to patient.adverse_event. Business justification: The concomitant_medication table has a relationship_to_ae STRING field explicitly indicating a relationship to an adverse event. Normalizing this with an adverse_event_id FK replaces the free-text rel

columns.name: atc_classification_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: Concomitant medications are classified by ATC for drug interaction analysis, pharmacovigilance signal detection, and regulatory submission narratives (CDISC CM domain). The existing atc_code column is

columns.name: crf_form_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.crf_form. Business justification: CDISC SDTM CM domain submission requires source CRF traceability for concomitant medication records. Clinical data management and source data verification (SDV) processes depend on linking CM records

columns.name: material_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.material. Business justification: Concomitant medications are pharmaceutical products in material master for drug-drug interaction analysis, contraindicated medication detection, protocol deviation flagging, and safety signal detectio

columns.name: medicinal_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Concomitant medications must link to product master for drug-drug interaction analysis, contraindication checking, protocol deviation assessment, and safety signal detection in pharmacovigilance. Curr

columns.name: patient_enrollment_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to patient.patient_enrollment. Business justification: Concomitant medications are recorded during a specific study or program period. Linking to patient_enrollment provides the full enrollment context (treatment arm, protocol version, population flags) n

columns.name: patient_id
columns.description: Unique identifier for the clinical trial subject or patient taking the concomitant medication. Links to the patient or trial subject master record.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice (GCP), 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: prescribing_master_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.master. Business justification: Drug-drug interaction analysis and pharmacovigilance safety reporting require knowing which HCP prescribed each concomitant medication. In clinical trials and post-marketing surveillance, prescriber i

columns.name: protocol_deviation_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to patient.protocol_deviation. Business justification: The concomitant_medication table has a protocol_deviation_flag BOOLEAN field indicating whether the medication constitutes a protocol deviation. Normalizing this with a protocol_deviation_id FK replac

columns.name: trial_id
columns.description: Unique identifier for the clinical trial or study in which the concomitant medication was recorded. Links to the trial master record.

columns.name: visit_id
columns.description: Unique identifier for the clinical trial visit or encounter during which the concomitant medication was reported or recorded.

columns.name: action_taken
columns.description: Action taken with the concomitant medication in response to an adverse event or safety concern (e.g., none, dose reduced, dose increased, temporarily stopped, permanently stopped).
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR)

columns.name: comments
columns.description: Free-text comments or additional notes regarding the concomitant medication, including clarifications, special circumstances, or investigator remarks.

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the concomitant medication record was first created in the system. Part of audit trail for regulatory compliance and data lineage.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice (GCP)

columns.name: data_source
columns.description: The source from which the concomitant medication data was captured (e.g., Case Report Form (CRF), electronic diary, medical record, subject interview, pharmacy record).
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice (GCP), 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: dose
columns.description: The numeric dose amount of the concomitant medication administered per administration event. Used with dose_unit to specify complete dosing information.

columns.name: dose_unit
columns.description: The unit of measure for the medication dose (e.g., mg, g, mcg, mL, IU, tablets, capsules). Standardized units for dose quantification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mg|g|mcg|mL|L|IU|units|tablets|capsules|drops|puffs|patches — 12 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: UCUM (Unified Code for Units of Measure), ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: frequency
columns.description: The frequency or schedule of concomitant medication administration (e.g., once daily, twice daily, as needed, every 8 hours). Free-text or standardized frequency code.

columns.name: indication
columns.description: The medical condition, symptom, or reason for which the concomitant medication is being taken. Free-text description of the therapeutic indication.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ICH E2B(R3)

columns.name: medication_class
columns.description: The therapeutic or pharmacological class of the concomitant medication (e.g., antibiotic, antihypertensive, analgesic, anticoagulant). Used for safety signal detection and drug-drug interaction screening.
columns.reference: WHO ATC Classification System, FDA Established Pharmacologic Class (EPC)

columns.name: modified_by
columns.description: User identifier or name of the person who last modified the concomitant medication record. Part of audit trail for regulatory compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice (GCP)

columns.name: modified_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the concomitant medication record was last modified. Part of audit trail for regulatory compliance and data lineage.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice (GCP)

columns.name: ongoing_flag
columns.description: Boolean indicator of whether the concomitant medication is still being taken by the subject at the time of data capture or database lock. True if ongoing, False if stopped.

columns.name: prior_to_study_flag
columns.description: Boolean indicator of whether the concomitant medication was started before the subject enrolled in the clinical trial. True if started prior, False if started during study.

columns.name: prohibited_concomitant_flag
columns.description: Boolean indicator of whether the concomitant medication is prohibited per the clinical trial protocol. True if prohibited, False if allowed. Critical for protocol deviation tracking.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice (GCP), 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: record_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the concomitant medication record in the Electronic Data Capture (EDC) system (e.g., draft, submitted, verified, locked, query open, query resolved).
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice (GCP), 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: route_of_administration
columns.description: The route by which the concomitant medication is administered to the subject (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, topical, inhalation).
columns.reference: FDA Route of Administration Terminology, ICH E2B(R3)

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: The date on which the subject began taking the concomitant medication. Critical for temporal analysis of drug-drug interactions and adverse event causality assessment.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice (GCP), 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: stop_date
columns.description: The date on which the subject stopped taking the concomitant medication. Null if medication is ongoing at time of data capture.
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice (GCP), 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: who_drug_code
columns.description: Standardized WHO Drug Dictionary code for the concomitant medication. Used for global pharmacovigilance reporting and drug-drug interaction analysis.

columns.name: created_by
columns.description: User identifier or name of the person who created the concomitant medication record. Part of audit trail for regulatory compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice (GCP)

tables.name: adverse_event
tables.description: Captures all adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) reported by or for a participant during a clinical trial or post-market surveillance program. Records MedDRA-coded preferred term (PT) and system organ class (SOC), onset date, resolution date, severity grade (CTCAE), seriousness criteria (death, hospitalization, life-threatening, etc.), causality assessment, action taken with study drug, outcome, SAE flag, SUSAR flag, and reporting timeline compliance status. Feeds into Argus Safety / Oracle AERS for regulatory reporting.
tables.reference: ICH E2A/E2B AE Reporting / MedDRA / CTCAE

columns.name: adverse_event_id
columns.description: Primary key for adverse_event

columns.name: application_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.application. Business justification: Aggregate safety reporting (PSURs, PBRERs, annual reports) requires grouping AEs by regulatory application/product for signal detection, benefit-risk assessment, and label update decisions. Standard p

columns.name: batch_record_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to manufacturing.batch_record. Business justification: Regulatory pharmacovigilance requirement. When adverse events are reported post-market or in trials, FDA/EMA mandate traceability to manufacturing batch for investigation, recall assessment, and root

columns.name: brand_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand. Business justification: Adverse events must be tracked by commercial brand for pharmacovigilance, regulatory reporting (periodic safety updates), commercial risk assessment, and launch readiness. Supports brand safety profil

columns.name: compound_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.compound. Business justification: Pharmacovigilance requires linking adverse events to the specific investigational compound administered. Essential for safety signal detection, causality assessment, regulatory reporting (IND safety r

columns.name: country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Pharmacovigilance reporting timelines (15-day SUSAR, expedited ICSRs) are country-specific per ICH E2B(R3) and local regulations. A country FK on adverse_event enables country-level PV compliance repo

columns.name: crf_form_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.crf_form. Business justification: CDISC SDTM AE domain submission requires source CRF traceability. Patient-level AE records must link to the AE CRF page in the EDC for regulatory audit trail, SDV, and data reconciliation with the cli

columns.name: investigational_product_id
columns.description: Reference to the investigational product or study drug that the patient was receiving at the time of the adverse event.

columns.name: label_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.label. Business justification: Adverse event 'expectedness' classification — a core ICSR and PSUR requirement — is determined by comparing the AE against the current approved label. Pharmacovigilance teams must reference the label

columns.name: labeling_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.labeling. Business justification: Pharmacovigilance expectedness assessment (ICSR, SUSAR, PSUR) requires comparing each AE against the Reference Safety Information in the approved label version in force at event onset. Direct FK enabl

columns.name: licensing_agreement_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.licensing_agreement. Business justification: Licensing agreements mandate pharmacovigilance data exchange obligations between licensor and licensee. AEs on in-licensed products must be reported per agreement terms. Pharma PV teams track which li

columns.name: manufacturing_deviation_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to manufacturing.manufacturing_deviation. Business justification: Regulatory pharmacovigilance investigations (FDA, EMA) require direct linkage between patient adverse events and manufacturing deviations to determine if AE clusters are caused by out-of-spec batches

columns.name: medicinal_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Adverse events must link to medicinal product for ICSR reporting to FDA/EMA, product safety profiles, risk-benefit assessments, label updates, and post-market surveillance. Critical for pharmacovigila

columns.name: patient_enrollment_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to patient.patient_enrollment. Business justification: Adverse events must be contextualized within the specific enrollment episode for pharmacovigilance reporting. The enrollment context (treatment arm, randomization number, blinding status, population f

columns.name: patient_id
columns.description: Reference to the patient or clinical trial subject who experienced the adverse event.

columns.name: principal_investigator_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.principal_investigator. Business justification: ICH E6 GCP and FDA 21 CFR 312.64 require the reporting PI to be identified for each SAE/SUSAR. patient.adverse_event.master_id links to hcp.master (person identity) but not the trial-specific PI role;

columns.name: regulatory_submission_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) and expedited AE reports to health authorities are submitted as regulatory submissions. Pharmacovigilance operations require linking safety cases to their regula

columns.name: rems_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.rems. Business justification: FDA REMS assessments require analysis of adverse events for REMS-covered products to evaluate whether risk minimization elements are working. AEs must be linked to the REMS program to support periodic

columns.name: reporting_master_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.master. Business justification: Pharmacovigilance and MedWatch/EudraVigilance regulatory reporting require traceability of the HCP who reported the adverse event. The 'reported_by' plain-text field is a denormalization of hcp.master

columns.name: treatment_exposure_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to patient.treatment_exposure. Business justification: An adverse event is causally linked to a specific treatment exposure event (the dose/administration that triggered it). Adding treatment_exposure_id normalizes the treatment_administered string field

columns.name: trial_id
columns.description: Reference to the clinical trial during which the adverse event occurred. Null for post-market surveillance events.

columns.name: action_taken_study_drug
columns.description: Action taken with the investigational product or study drug in response to the adverse event.
columns.value_regex: None|Dose Reduced|Dose Increased|Drug Interrupted|Drug Withdrawn|Not Applicable
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: ae_term
columns.description: The verbatim description of the adverse event as reported by the patient, investigator, or healthcare professional.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: case_number
columns.glossary_term: Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) Case Number
columns.description: Unique case identifier assigned by the pharmacovigilance system for regulatory reporting. Used for tracking and submission to regulatory authorities.
columns.reference: ICH E2B(R3) Electronic Transmission of ICSR

columns.name: causality_assessment
columns.description: Investigator or sponsor assessment of the causal relationship between the adverse event and the investigational product or study drug.
columns.value_regex: Related|Probably Related|Possibly Related|Unlikely Related|Not Related|Not Assessable
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: duration_days
columns.description: The duration of the adverse event in days, calculated from onset date to resolution date. Null if ongoing or fatal.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: expectedness
columns.description: Indicates whether the adverse event was expected based on the current Investigator Brochure or product labeling.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: meddra_pt_code
columns.glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Code
columns.description: MedDRA preferred term code assigned to the adverse event for standardized medical terminology and regulatory reporting.

columns.name: meddra_pt_name
columns.glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Name
columns.description: MedDRA preferred term name describing the adverse event in standardized medical terminology.

columns.name: meddra_soc_code
columns.glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) Code
columns.description: MedDRA system organ class code representing the highest level of the MedDRA hierarchy for the adverse event.

columns.name: meddra_soc_name
columns.glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) Name
columns.description: MedDRA system organ class name representing the body system affected by the adverse event.

columns.name: onset_date
columns.description: The date when the adverse event first occurred or was first observed by the patient or investigator.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: outcome
columns.description: Final outcome of the adverse event at the time of reporting or study completion.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: record_created_timestamp
columns.description: The timestamp when this adverse event record was first created in the data system.

columns.name: record_updated_timestamp
columns.description: The timestamp when this adverse event record was last modified or updated in the data system.

columns.name: regulatory_report_date
columns.description: The date when the adverse event was reported to the regulatory authority (FDA, EMA, etc.). Applicable for SAEs and SUSARs.

columns.name: report_date
columns.description: The date when the adverse event was first reported to the sponsor or investigator.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: reporting_timeline_compliance_status
columns.description: Indicates whether the adverse event was reported to regulatory authorities within the required timeline (e.g., 7 days for fatal/life-threatening SAEs, 15 days for other SAEs).

columns.name: resolution_date
columns.description: The date when the adverse event resolved, recovered, or was no longer present. Null if ongoing or fatal.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: seriousness_criteria_congenital_anomaly
columns.glossary_term: Seriousness Criteria - Congenital Anomaly or Birth Defect
columns.description: Indicates whether the adverse event resulted in a congenital anomaly or birth defect.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: seriousness_criteria_death
columns.description: Indicates whether the adverse event resulted in death.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: seriousness_criteria_disability
columns.glossary_term: Seriousness Criteria - Persistent or Significant Disability
columns.description: Indicates whether the adverse event resulted in persistent or significant disability or incapacity.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: seriousness_criteria_hospitalization
columns.description: Indicates whether the adverse event resulted in initial or prolonged inpatient hospitalization.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: seriousness_criteria_life_threatening
columns.description: Indicates whether the adverse event was life-threatening at the time of the event.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: seriousness_criteria_medically_important
columns.glossary_term: Seriousness Criteria - Other Medically Important Condition
columns.description: Indicates whether the adverse event was considered medically important and may jeopardize the patient or require intervention to prevent one of the other serious outcomes.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

columns.name: seriousness_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the adverse event meets regulatory criteria for seriousness (death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, congenital anomaly, or other medically important condition).
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management - 21 CFR 312.32

columns.name: severity_grade
columns.glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Severity Grade
columns.description: Severity grade of the adverse event using CTCAE scale: Grade 1 (Mild), Grade 2 (Moderate), Grade 3 (Severe), Grade 4 (Life-threatening), Grade 5 (Death).

columns.name: source_system
columns.description: The operational system from which the adverse event record was captured (e.g., Argus Safety for pharmacovigilance, Medidata Rave for clinical trial EDC).
columns.value_regex: Argus Safety|Oracle AERS|Medidata Rave|Veeva Vault|Manual Entry

columns.name: study_day
columns.glossary_term: Study Day of Adverse Event (AE) Onset
columns.description: The study day (relative to first dose or randomization) on which the adverse event occurred. Negative values indicate pre-treatment events.

columns.name: susar_flag
columns.glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the adverse event qualifies as a SUSAR (serious, unexpected, and suspected to be related to the investigational product), requiring expedited reporting to regulatory authorities.
columns.reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management - EU Directive 2001/20/EC

Supports PK/PD analysis, dose-response modeling, and safety signal assessment.

columns.name: comments
columns.description: Free-text comments or notes from the laboratory or pathologist regarding the biomarker result, specimen quality, or interpretation.

columns.name: created_timestamp

columns.name: cutoff_value
columns.description: The threshold value used to determine positive vs negative result interpretation for this biomarker (e.g., PD-L1 ≥50% for pembrolizumab eligibility).
columns.reference: FDA Guidance on In Vitro Companion Diagnostic Devices

columns.name: data_source
columns.description: The source system or database from which this biomarker result was captured (e.g., LIMS, EDC, central laboratory portal).

columns.name: gene_name
columns.description: The name of the gene associated with this biomarker result, using HGNC nomenclature (e.g., EGFR, KRAS, BRCA1, TP53).

columns.name: laboratory_clia_number
columns.glossary_term: Laboratory Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) Number
columns.description: The CLIA certification number of the testing laboratory, required for clinical diagnostic testing in the United States.

columns.name: modified_by
columns.description: The user ID or system account that last modified this biomarker result record.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records and Signatures

columns.name: modified_timestamp
columns.description: The timestamp when this biomarker result record was last modified in the data system.

columns.name: mutation_type
columns.description: The type of genetic mutation detected (e.g., missense, nonsense, frameshift, deletion, insertion, amplification, fusion).
columns.reference: HGVS - Human Genome Variation Society Nomenclature

columns.name: quality_control_status
columns.description: Indicates whether the biomarker assay passed internal quality control checks (e.g., passed, failed, not applicable).

columns.name: reference_range_lower
columns.description: The lower bound of the normal or reference range for this biomarker, if applicable.

columns.name: reference_range_upper
columns.description: The upper bound of the normal or reference range for this biomarker, if applicable.

columns.name: result_date
columns.description: The date on which the biomarker result was finalized and reported by the laboratory.

columns.name: result_interpretation
columns.description: The clinical interpretation of the biomarker result (e.g., positive, negative, indeterminate, high, low, mutation detected, wild type). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: positive|negative|indeterminate|high|low|normal|abnormal|mutation_detected|wild_type — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: FDA Guidance on In Vitro Companion Diagnostic Devices

columns.name: result_status
columns.description: The current status of the biomarker result in the laboratory workflow (e.g., preliminary, final, corrected, cancelled, pending).

columns.name: result_value
columns.description: The quantitative or qualitative value of the biomarker result (e.g., 50%, positive, mutation detected, 10 mutations/Mb).

columns.name: specimen_collection_date
columns.description: The date on which the biological specimen was collected from the subject.

columns.name: specimen_type
columns.description: The type of biological specimen from which the biomarker was measured (e.g., tumor tissue, blood, plasma, serum, saliva). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tumor_tissue|blood|plasma|serum|saliva|urine|cerebrospinal_fluid|bone_marrow — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

columns.name: test_date
columns.description: The date on which the biomarker assay was performed by the laboratory.

columns.name: testing_laboratory
columns.description: The name of the laboratory or Contract Research Organization (CRO) that performed the biomarker assay.

columns.name: variant_annotation
columns.description: Detailed annotation of the genetic variant using HGVS nomenclature (e.g., c.2573T>G, p.L858R).
columns.reference: HGVS - Human Genome Variation Society Nomenclature

columns.name: created_by
columns.description: The user ID or system account that created this biomarker result record.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records and Signatures

domains.name: commercial
domains.description: Handles commercial operations including sales force management, healthcare professional (HCP) engagement, key opinion leader (KOL) relationships, promotional materials (Veeva PromoMats), territory management, product launch activities, sample distribution, and speaker programs. Integrates with Veeva CRM and Salesforce Health Cloud. Manages compliance with promotional regulations, PhRMA code, and Sunshine Act transparency reporting. Supports brand performance tracking and P&L reporting by brand.
domains.references: PhRMA Code / FDA Promotional Guidelines / Sunshine Act

tables.name: brand

Captures brand identity, therapeutic area, lifecycle stage (pre-launch, launch, growth, mature, LOE), brand strategy, target patient population, approved indications, ATC classification, INN/USAN, and P&L ownership. Serves as the commercial anchor entity linking all brand-level activities, performance tracking, promotional spend, and market share measurement.

columns.name: primary_market_country_id

columns.name: trademark_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.trademark. Business justification: Brand names are registered trademarks; legal protection, brand strategy, and market exclusivity depend on trademark registration. Core IP protection for commercial brands.

columns.name: transfer_price_id

columns.name: brand_code
columns.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the brand across commercial systems including Veeva CRM, SAP SD, and Salesforce Health Cloud. Used as the business key for cross-system reconciliation and reporting.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

columns.name: brand_name
columns.description: The proprietary trade name of the pharmaceutical product as approved by the regulatory authority (e.g., FDA, EMA) and used in commercial promotion, packaging, and market-facing communications.
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Guideline on Invented Name; ICH Q6A

columns.name: brand_status
columns.description: Current operational status of the brand within the commercial organization. Controls whether the brand is eligible for promotional spend, sales force detailing, and market access activities.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Product Configuration; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

columns.name: controlled_substance_schedule
columns.description: The DEA controlled substance schedule classification for the brand, if applicable. Determines distribution controls, sample restrictions, and reporting obligations under the Controlled Substances Act. 'not_scheduled' for non-controlled products.
columns.reference: DEA Controlled Substances Act; 21 CFR Part 1308; DEA Schedule Classification

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: The timestamp when the brand master record was first created in the commercial data platform. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and SOX data governance controls.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); SOX 302/404; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

columns.name: global_brand_owner
columns.description: The legal entity name of the global brand owner responsible for the NDA/BLA/MAA and global P&L accountability. Relevant for intercompany transfer pricing, royalty agreements, and IP ownership tracking.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO Module; ICH Q10; SOX Compliance

columns.name: global_launch_sequence
columns.description: Numeric sequence indicating the order in which this brand was launched globally relative to other brands in the portfolio. Used for portfolio prioritization, resource allocation, and launch excellence benchmarking.

columns.name: is_flagship_brand
columns.description: Indicates whether this brand is designated as a flagship or priority brand by commercial leadership, warranting elevated promotional investment, dedicated sales force, and executive-level performance reporting.
columns.reference: Internal Brand Portfolio Strategy; PhRMA Code

columns.name: launch_date
columns.description: The date on which the brand was first commercially available in its primary market following regulatory approval. Used as the anchor date for launch performance tracking, market share ramp analysis, and P&L reporting.
columns.reference: FDA Approval Letter; EMA Decision; Internal Commercial Launch Plan

columns.name: lifecycle_stage
columns.description: Current stage of the brand in its commercial lifecycle. Drives resource allocation, promotional investment levels, and strategic planning. Loss of exclusivity (LOE) stage triggers biosimilar/generic competition response planning.
columns.reference: PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals; Internal Brand Strategy Framework

columns.name: loss_of_exclusivity_date
columns.description: The projected or confirmed date on which the brand's market exclusivity expires, enabling generic or biosimilar competition. Critical for long-range financial planning, patent strategy, and lifecycle management decisions.
columns.reference: FDA Orange Book; 21 CFR Part 314 Subpart D; Hatch-Waxman Act; EMA Exclusivity Register

columns.name: orphan_drug_designation
columns.description: Indicates whether the brand has received Orphan Drug Designation from the FDA (ODD) or EMA (OMP), conferring 7-year US market exclusivity, 10-year EU exclusivity, and tax incentives. Affects pricing strategy and market access negotiations.
columns.reference: FDA Orphan Drug Act (21 CFR Part 316); EMA Regulation (EC) No 141/2000; Rare Diseases Act

columns.name: patent_expiry_date
columns.description: The expiry date of the primary composition-of-matter or method-of-use patent protecting the brand. Distinct from LOE date as patent term extensions (PTE) and data exclusivity may extend commercial protection beyond patent expiry.
columns.reference: USPTO Patent Records; FDA Orange Book; 35 USC 156 (Patent Term Extension); EMA SPC Regulation

columns.name: pl_cost_center
columns.glossary_term: Profit and Loss (P&L) Cost Center Code
columns.description: The SAP cost center code to which all brand-level revenues, promotional spend, and COGS are allocated for P&L reporting. Enables brand-level financial performance tracking and budget variance analysis.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Module; SOX 302/404 Financial Reporting

columns.name: primary_competitor_brands
columns.description: Comma-separated list of key competitor brand names in the same therapeutic class. Used for competitive intelligence, market share benchmarking, and sales force training. Classified as confidential competitive intelligence.
columns.reference: IQVIA Competitive Intelligence; Internal Market Research

columns.name: profit_center
columns.description: The SAP profit center assigned to the brand for internal management accounting and brand-level P&L reporting. Distinct from cost center; used for contribution margin analysis and brand portfolio performance reporting.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA Module; SOX Financial Reporting

columns.name: rems_required
columns.glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Required
columns.description: Indicates whether the FDA has mandated a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) for this brand due to serious safety risks. REMS programs impose specific distribution, prescribing, and patient monitoring requirements that affect commercial operations.
columns.reference: FDA REMS Program; 21 CFR Part 314.520; FDAAA 2007

columns.name: sample_eligible
columns.description: Indicates whether the brand is eligible for distribution of drug samples to healthcare professionals (HCPs) by the sales force. Controlled by PDMA regulations and PhRMA code. DEA scheduled products and REMS products may have restrictions.
columns.reference: Prescription Drug Marketing Act (PDMA); 21 CFR Part 203; PhRMA Code

columns.name: sap_material_number
columns.description: The SAP material master number assigned to the brand's primary commercial SKU in SAP S/4HANA MM/SD modules. Used for order management, COGS tracking, and supply chain integration.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module; SAP Material Master

columns.name: strategy_statement
columns.description: The overarching commercial strategy statement for the brand, capturing positioning, differentiation, and value proposition relative to competitors. Classified as confidential business strategy. Sourced from the brand plan approved by commercial leadership.
columns.reference: PhRMA Code; Internal Brand Planning Process; SOX Financial Reporting

columns.name: sunshine_act_reportable
columns.description: Indicates whether transfers of value associated with this brand (samples, speaker fees, meals, educational grants) are subject to Open Payments (Sunshine Act) reporting to CMS. Drives compliance workflows in Veeva CRM and SAP.
columns.reference: Physician Payments Sunshine Act (42 USC 1320a-7h); CMS Open Payments Program; PhRMA Code

columns.name: target_patient_population
columns.description: Description of the intended patient population for the brand, including disease stage, biomarker status, prior treatment history, and demographic criteria. Informs HCP targeting, patient support program design, and HEOR value dossier development.
columns.reference: FDA Prescribing Information; EMA SmPC; ICH E8 General Considerations for Clinical Studies

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: The timestamp of the most recent update to the brand master record. Used for change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver layer pipeline and audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); SOX 302/404; Databricks Delta Lake CDC

columns.name: veeva_crm_product_code
columns.description: The product identifier assigned to this brand in Veeva CRM (Salesforce Health Cloud), used to link brand records to HCP call activity, sample transactions, promotional material approvals (PromoMats), and speaker program events.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; Salesforce Health Cloud; Veeva Vault PromoMats

tables.name: territory
tables.description: Defines the geographic and organizational sales territories used to structure the field force. Captures territory code, name, geographic boundaries (zip codes, counties, states, regions), territory type (primary, secondary, specialty), alignment version, effective dates, and assigned district and region hierarchy. Used for call planning, target assignment, and performance attribution in Veeva CRM and Salesforce Health Cloud.

columns.name: territory_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the sales territory record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for the territory data product.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Management; Salesforce Health Cloud Territory Model

columns.name: budget_id

columns.name: country_id

columns.name: legal_entity_id

For in-licensed or co-promoted products, territories must be validated against licensing agreement geogr

columns.name: masterdata_cost_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: Territories are cost centers for budgeting and expense allocation. Required for promotional spend tracking, sales rep expense allocation, budget vs. actual reporting, and commercial operations P&L by

columns.name: org_unit_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.org_unit. Business justification: Territories are aligned to org_units (business units/regions) in pharma field force management for headcount reporting, budget allocation, and sales force effectiveness analysis. A commercial operatio

columns.name: patent_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: Territories are aligned to patented products; sales planning, quota setting, and resource allocation require patent/exclusivity awareness for strategic territory design.

columns.name: primary_brand_id
columns.description: FK to commercial.brand

columns.name: therapeutic_area_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.therapeutic_area. Business justification: Sales territories in pharma are aligned to therapeutic areas (oncology vs. immunology sales forces). territory.therapeutic_area is plain text. FK supports territory alignment reporting, sales force si

columns.name: alignment_version
columns.description: Version identifier of the territory alignment cycle that produced this territory definition (e.g., 'FY2024-Q1', 'ALIGN-2024-H2'). Enables tracking of territory changes across realignment cycles and supports historical performance attribution.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Alignment; Salesforce Health Cloud Territory Model

columns.name: area_code
columns.description: Code identifying the sales area (highest-level geographic grouping above region) to which this territory belongs. Supports national-level roll-up reporting and executive P&L attribution.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Hierarchy; Salesforce Health Cloud Territory Model

columns.name: brick_count
columns.description: Number of geographic 'bricks' (smallest geographic unit used in pharmaceutical territory alignment, typically a ZIP+4 or sub-ZIP unit) assigned to this territory. Used to measure territory size and workload balance during alignment planning.
columns.reference: IMS Health / IQVIA Brick Alignment Standard; Veeva CRM Territory Alignment

columns.name: call_plan_frequency
columns.description: Target number of calls (HCP visits) per representative per cycle (typically quarterly) for this territory as defined in the call plan. Used for field force productivity measurement and compliance tracking in Veeva CRM.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Call Planning; PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals

columns.name: county_list
columns.description: Semicolon-delimited list of county names or FIPS county codes included within this territory's geographic boundary. Complements ZIP code alignment for rural territory definitions and Sunshine Act county-level reporting.

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this territory record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and bi-temporal modeling requirements.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); SOX; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

columns.name: crm_territory_code
columns.description: Native territory identifier from the source CRM system (Veeva CRM or Salesforce Health Cloud). Used for cross-system reconciliation, data lineage tracing, and integration with call activity and sample distribution records.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Management; Salesforce Health Cloud Territory Model

columns.name: decile_rank
columns.description: Decile ranking (1–10) of the territory based on market potential or historical sales performance relative to all territories in the same alignment. Decile 1 represents the highest-potential territories. Used for resource allocation and call frequency prioritization.
columns.reference: IQVIA Territory Decile Methodology; Veeva CRM Target Segmentation

columns.name: effective_end_date
columns.description: Date on which this territory definition ceases to be operationally active. Null indicates an open-ended, currently active territory. Used for historical alignment queries and performance period attribution.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Management; Salesforce Health Cloud Territory Model

columns.name: effective_start_date
columns.description: Date from which this territory definition becomes operationally active for call planning, target assignment, and performance attribution. Supports bi-temporal modeling of territory changes.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Management; Salesforce Health Cloud Territory Model

columns.name: geographic_area_sq_miles
columns.description: Total geographic area of the territory in square miles. Used to assess travel burden for field representatives and to balance territory workload during alignment planning.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Alignment; IQVIA Geographic Analysis

columns.name: is_open_territory
columns.description: Indicates whether the territory is currently unassigned (open) with no active field representative. Open territories require coverage planning and may be temporarily covered by adjacent representatives or district managers.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Management; Salesforce Health Cloud Territory Model

columns.name: is_specialty_overlay
columns.description: Indicates whether this territory is a specialty overlay territory that operates in conjunction with a primary territory (e.g., an oncology specialist overlay on top of a primary care territory). Used to manage co-promotion and dual-rep call planning.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Management; PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals

columns.name: last_realignment_date
columns.description: Date on which this territory's boundaries, targets, or assignments were last modified as part of a formal territory realignment exercise. Used to track alignment cycle history and assess the currency of territory definitions.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Alignment; Salesforce Health Cloud Territory Model

columns.name: market_potential_index
columns.description: Normalized index score (typically 0.0000–9.9999) representing the estimated prescribing potential of the territory based on IQVIA/IQVIA data, patient population, and payer mix. Used for territory sizing, quota setting, and alignment optimization.
columns.reference: IQVIA (formerly IMS Health) Market Potential Methodology; Veeva CRM Territory Alignment

columns.name: state_province_code
columns.description: ISO 3166-2 state or province code for the primary state/province covered by this territory (e.g., 'NY', 'CA', 'ON'). Used for geographic boundary definition, Sunshine Act state-level reporting, and call planning.
columns.reference: ISO 3166-2; Sunshine Act (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7h); State Aggregate Spend Reporting

columns.name: sunshine_act_reporting_required
columns.description: Indicates whether HCP engagement activities within this territory are subject to mandatory Open Payments (Sunshine Act) transparency reporting to CMS. Typically true for US territories; false for territories outside US jurisdiction.
columns.reference: Sunshine Act (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7h); CMS Open Payments Program; 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: target_account_count
columns.description: Number of institutional accounts (hospitals, clinics, group practices, IDNs) designated as call targets within this territory. Used for key account planning and workload analysis.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Account Management; Salesforce Health Cloud Territory Model

columns.name: target_hcp_count
columns.description: Number of Healthcare Professionals (HCPs) designated as call targets within this territory for the current alignment cycle. Used for workload balancing, call planning, and field force sizing analysis.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Target List Management; PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals

columns.name: territory_code
columns.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the territory within the field force alignment system. Used as the business key in Veeva CRM and Salesforce Health Cloud for call planning and target assignment.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Management; Salesforce Health Cloud Territory Model

columns.name: territory_name
columns.description: Human-readable name of the sales territory (e.g., 'Northeast Oncology Zone 3'). Used for display in CRM dashboards, call planning tools, and performance reporting.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Management; Salesforce Health Cloud Territory Model

columns.name: territory_status

columns.name: territory_type

columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Management; PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals

columns.name: updated_timestamp

columns.name: urban_rural_classification
columns.description: Classification of the territory's geographic character as urban, suburban, rural, or mixed. Influences call planning strategy, travel time estimates, and field force resource allocation decisions.

columns.name: workload_index
columns.description: Composite index score measuring the estimated field representative workload for this territory, factoring in target HCP count, call frequency, geographic travel burden, and account complexity. Used for territory balancing during alignment cycles.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Alignment; IQVIA Workload Optimization Methodology

columns.name: zip_code_list
columns.description: Semicolon-delimited list of US ZIP codes (or equivalent postal codes) that define the geographic boundary of this territory. Used for HCP target assignment, call planning, and territory alignment in Veeva CRM. Stored as a delimited string per Silver Layer conventions; spatial decomposition occurs in the Gold Layer.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Alignment; USPS ZIP Code Standard; Salesforce Health Cloud Territory Model
