columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: Sales reps are assigned to cost centers for expense tracking and budget allocation. Required for headcount planning, promotional spend allocation, IC plan administration, and commercial operations P&L

columns.name: org_unit_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.org_unit. Business justification: Sales reps belong to an org_unit (business unit) for headcount management, budget allocation, and sales force effectiveness reporting. business_unit is a denormalized org_unit name. A field force mana

columns.name: territory_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to the territory to which the sales representative is assigned

columns.name: therapeutic_area_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.therapeutic_area. Business justification: Sales reps are hired, certified, and deployed by therapeutic area. sales_rep.therapeutic_area is plain text. FK supports rep certification tracking, TA-specific training compliance, incentive compensa

columns.name: annual_call_target
columns.description: Target number of HCP sales calls (details) the representative is expected to complete within the fiscal year, as set by the commercial operations team. Used for field force productivity tracking and performance management in Veeva CRM.

columns.name: call_plan_frequency_target
columns.description: Target number of HCP calls per cycle for this specific rep-territory assignment. Differs by rep role and territory type — an overlay rep may have a lower target than the primary rep for the same territory. Identified in detection phase as relationship-level data.

columns.name: certification_expiry_date
columns.description: Date on which the sales representative's current product or compliance certification expires. Triggers re-certification workflows and may restrict sample distribution or promotional activity if expired.
columns.reference: PhRMA Code; MasterControl/TrackWise; FDA 21 CFR Part 211

columns.name: effective_end_date
columns.description: Date on which the current territory, role, and business unit assignment for this sales representative ceases to be effective. Null indicates the current active assignment. Supports SCD Type 2 history tracking for territory realignments and role changes.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; SAP S/4HANA HR Module

columns.name: effective_start_date
columns.description: Date from which the current territory, role, and business unit assignment for this sales representative is effective. Supports slowly changing dimension (SCD) Type 2 history tracking for territory and role changes over time.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; SAP S/4HANA HR Module

columns.name: employment_status
columns.description: Current employment lifecycle status of the sales representative. Drives CRM access provisioning, territory assignment eligibility, sample authorization, and Sunshine Act reporting inclusion. Active = currently employed and field-active; On Leave = temporary absence (FMLA, medical, parental); Terminated = employment ended; Suspended = temporarily restricted from field activity; Pending Start = hired but not yet active.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Module; SOX Compliance; PhRMA Code

columns.name: first_name
columns.description: Legal given name of the sales representative as recorded in the HR system of record. Used for display, communication, and identity verification.

columns.name: gcp_certified
columns.description: Indicates whether the sales representative holds a current Good Clinical Practice (GCP) certification. Required for MSLs and reps supporting clinical trial site engagement or investigator-initiated study discussions. Sourced from the Learning Management System (LMS).
columns.reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Guidelines; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: hcp_engagement_tier
columns.description: Classification of the sales representative's HCP engagement level based on the complexity and strategic importance of their account portfolio. Tier 1 = high-value specialist/KOL accounts; Tier 2 = mid-level specialist accounts; Tier 3 = primary care/general accounts. Drives call frequency targets and resource allocation.

columns.name: hire_date
columns.description: Official date on which the sales representative was hired by the organization, as recorded in the HR system of record (SAP S/4HANA). Used for tenure calculations, vesting schedules, and compliance reporting.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Module; SOX Compliance

columns.name: job_title
columns.description: Official job title of the sales representative as recorded in the HR system (e.g., 'Senior Specialty Sales Representative', 'Oncology Territory Manager', 'Medical Science Liaison'). Used for organizational reporting and external business card / signature purposes.

columns.name: last_name
columns.description: Legal family name of the sales representative as recorded in the HR system of record. Used for display, reporting, and identity verification.

columns.name: product_certification_status
columns.description: Current status of the sales representative's product knowledge certification for their assigned brand(s). Reps must be certified before being authorized to promote a product or distribute samples. Sourced from the LMS or MasterControl/TrackWise training records.
columns.reference: PhRMA Code; FDA 21 CFR Part 211; MasterControl/TrackWise

columns.name: record_created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the sales representative master record was first created in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for data lineage, audit trail, and record lifecycle management per 21 CFR Part 11.

columns.name: record_updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the sales representative master record in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Used for change data capture (CDC), audit trail, and data freshness monitoring per 21 CFR Part 11.

columns.name: rep_role
columns.description: Commercial field force role classification defining the rep's function and engagement model. Territory Manager (TM) handles primary care accounts; Specialty Rep focuses on specialist HCPs; Key Account Manager (KAM) manages institutional/payer accounts; Medical Science Liaison (MSL) provides scientific exchange; Managed Care Specialist handles formulary access; National Account Manager handles national-level payer/GPO relationships. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: territory_manager|specialty_rep|key_account_manager|medical_science_liaison|managed_care_specialist|national_account_manager — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals; Veeva CRM

columns.name: sample_authorization_status
columns.description: Current authorization status of the sales representative to distribute drug samples to HCPs. Governed by the Prescription Drug Marketing Act (PDMA) and PhRMA Code. Suspended or revoked status prevents sample transactions in Veeva CRM.
columns.reference: Prescription Drug Marketing Act (PDMA); PhRMA Code; FDA 21 CFR Part 203

columns.name: speaker_program_eligible
columns.description: Indicates whether the sales representative is authorized to organize or facilitate HCP speaker programs on behalf of the company. Eligibility requires completion of speaker program compliance training and manager approval. Governed by PhRMA Code and OIG guidelines.
columns.reference: PhRMA Code; OIG Compliance Program Guidance; Sunshine Act

columns.name: state_province_code
columns.description: ISO 3166-2 state or province code for the primary operating geography of the sales representative (e.g., NY, CA, TX). Used for state-level compliance reporting, state Sunshine Act equivalents, and territory boundary management.

columns.name: sunshine_act_reportable
columns.description: Indicates whether this sales representative's HCP interactions and transfers of value are subject to Open Payments (Sunshine Act) reporting requirements under 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7h. MSLs and reps engaging in speaker programs or providing meals/gifts to HCPs are typically reportable.
columns.reference: Sunshine Act (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7h); CMS Open Payments Program

columns.name: termination_date
columns.description: Date on which the sales representative's employment was formally terminated. Null if currently employed. Used to deactivate CRM access, close territory assignments, finalize Sunshine Act reporting periods, and trigger sample reconciliation processes.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Module; Sunshine Act (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7h); PhRMA Code

columns.name: veeva_crm_user_code
columns.description: Unique user identifier assigned to the sales representative within Veeva CRM (Salesforce Health Cloud / Veeva CRM). Used to link field activity records, call logs, HCP interactions, and sample transactions back to the rep. Critical for CRM data lineage and compliance reporting.

columns.name: veeva_promomats_access
columns.description: Indicates whether the sales representative has active access to Veeva PromoMats for retrieving approved promotional materials. Access is role-based and tied to brand assignment and certification status. Ensures only MLR-approved content is used in HCP interactions.
columns.reference: Veeva PromoMats; FDA 21 CFR Part 202; PhRMA Code

columns.name: work_email
columns.description: Corporate email address of the sales representative used for official business communications, Veeva CRM login, and system notifications. Sourced from the enterprise directory (e.g., Active Directory / SAP S/4HANA).

columns.name: work_phone
columns.description: Primary corporate mobile or desk phone number assigned to the sales representative for field communications and HCP engagement. Sourced from HR or CRM system.

tables.name: hcp_target
tables.description: Commercial targeting and call planning record linking an HCP (owned by the hcp domain) to a brand, territory, and sales rep for a given targeting/planning cycle. Captures target tier (A/B/C), planned call frequency, call type mix (face-to-face vs. remote), specialty segment, prescribing potential decile, targeting rationale, priority rank, effective period, plan approval status, and targeting status. Drives field force activity scheduling, call planning, and promotional resource allocation in Veeva CRM. Distinct from the HCP master (owned by hcp domain) — this is the commercial segmentation and planning layer.

columns.name: hcp_target_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the HCP targeting and call planning record within the commercial segmentation and planning layer.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Data Model; Salesforce Health Cloud

columns.name: brand_id
columns.description: Reference to the pharmaceutical brand or product for which this HCP is being targeted. Supports brand-level P&L reporting and promotional resource allocation.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

columns.name: brand_plan_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand_plan. Business justification: hcp_target is the call planning record that operationalizes the brand_plan's targeting strategy. HCP targets are created as part of brand plan execution — the brand_plan defines target_hcp_segment, ca

columns.name: formulary_position_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to market.formulary_position. Business justification: HCP targeting considers formulary position to prioritize physicians where brand has favorable access. Targeting strategy and resource allocation process links targets to formulary status for call plan

columns.name: master_id
columns.description: Reference to the HCP master record (owned by the hcp domain) that is being targeted. This is the commercial segmentation layer — the HCP master itself is managed separately.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; Salesforce Health Cloud; PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals

columns.name: medicinal_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: HCP targeting strategies are product-specific. Call planning, territory design, and prescriber segmentation require product linkage. Real business process: targeting cycle planning and call plan optim

columns.name: principal_investigator_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.principal_investigator. Business justification: Commercial targeting identifies KOLs who are clinical investigators. Enables coordinated engagement strategy, speaker recruitment from trial sites, advisory board selection, and transparency reporting

columns.name: sales_rep_id
columns.description: Reference to the sales representative (field force employee) assigned to engage this HCP target within the territory for the planning cycle.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; Salesforce Health Cloud; PhRMA Code

columns.name: territory_id
columns.description: Reference to the sales territory to which this HCP target is assigned for the planning cycle. Drives field force routing and call planning in Veeva CRM.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Management; Salesforce Health Cloud

columns.name: therapeutic_area_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.therapeutic_area. Business justification: HCP targeting lists are built by therapeutic area for specialty segmentation and call planning. hcp_target.therapeutic_area is plain text. FK supports TA-level HCP segmentation reports, targeting anal

columns.name: trial_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.trial. Business justification: Trial participation is a primary HCP targeting criterion in pharma — investigators and trial-aware physicians are high-priority targets for commercial engagement post-approval. CRM targeting rationale

columns.name: approval_status
columns.description: Workflow approval status of the targeting plan record. Tracks whether the target assignment has been reviewed and approved by the regional or national sales manager before field force execution.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; PhRMA Code; Sunshine Act (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7h)

columns.name: approved_by
columns.description: Name or identifier of the sales manager or commercial operations approver who authorized this HCP target plan record. Supports audit trail and compliance review.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; PhRMA Code; SOX Compliance

columns.name: approved_date
columns.description: Date on which the targeting plan record was formally approved by the authorized sales manager or commercial operations team. Marks the transition from planning to execution.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; PhRMA Code; Sunshine Act

columns.name: call_type_mix_pct_f2f
columns.description: Percentage of total planned calls that are designated as face-to-face interactions (0.00–100.00). Used to monitor adherence to brand-level call mix strategy and field force deployment guidelines.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals

columns.name: competitor_prescriber
columns.description: Indicates whether the HCP is known to prescribe a competing product in the same therapeutic class. Used to prioritize conversion-focused engagement strategies and messaging.
columns.reference: IQVIA Market Data; Veeva CRM; Commercial Analytics

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this HCP target record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.

columns.name: current_brand_prescriber
columns.description: Indicates whether the HCP is currently an active prescriber of the targeted brand based on the most recent prescribing data. Distinguishes new-to-brand targets from existing prescribers for tailored engagement strategies.
columns.reference: IQVIA / APLD Prescribing Data; Veeva CRM; PhRMA Code

columns.name: cycle_call_count
columns.description: Number of completed sales calls made to this HCP for the targeted brand within the current cycle plan period. Used to measure in-cycle execution progress against planned_call_frequency.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Cycle Plan; Salesforce Health Cloud

columns.name: do_not_contact_flag
columns.description: Indicates that this HCP has requested no promotional contact or has been placed on a do-not-contact list. When true, field force must not initiate promotional calls. Critical for compliance with HCP opt-out preferences and applicable privacy regulations.
columns.reference: GDPR Article 21; HIPAA; PhRMA Code; Veeva CRM DNC Management

columns.name: effective_end_date
columns.description: Date on which this HCP target assignment expires or is no longer active. Nullable for open-ended targeting. Defines the end of the targeting period for the cycle.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Cycle Plan; Salesforce Health Cloud

columns.name: effective_start_date
columns.description: Date from which this HCP target assignment is active and the field force is authorized to engage the HCP for the specified brand and territory. Defines the start of the targeting period.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Cycle Plan; Salesforce Health Cloud

columns.name: engagement_channel_preference
columns.description: HCP's preferred channel for sales representative engagement as captured in Veeva CRM or Salesforce Health Cloud. Informs call type mix planning and omnichannel engagement strategy.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; Salesforce Health Cloud; PhRMA Code

columns.name: is_kol
columns.description: Indicates whether this HCP is designated as a Key Opinion Leader (KOL) for the targeted brand or therapeutic area. KOL status influences engagement strategy, speaker program eligibility, and medical affairs coordination.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; PhRMA Code; Sunshine Act (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7h)

columns.name: is_sample_eligible
columns.description: Indicates whether this HCP is eligible to receive drug samples for the targeted brand. Governed by the Prescription Drug Marketing Act (PDMA) and internal sample distribution policies.
columns.reference: Prescription Drug Marketing Act (PDMA); 21 CFR Part 203; PhRMA Code

columns.name: is_speaker_eligible
columns.description: Indicates whether this HCP is eligible to participate in brand speaker programs. Eligibility is governed by PhRMA Code compliance, Sunshine Act reporting requirements, and internal speaker bureau criteria.
columns.reference: PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals; Sunshine Act (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7h); OIG Compliance Guidance

columns.name: last_detail_date
columns.description: Date of the most recent promotional detail (sales call) made to this HCP for the targeted brand. Used to monitor call recency, identify lapsed targets, and prioritize field force scheduling.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Call Activity; PhRMA Code

columns.name: market_potential_segment
columns.description: Categorical assessment of the HCP's overall market potential for the brand, derived from prescribing volume, patient panel size, and payer mix. Used alongside prescribing_potential_decile for targeting decisions.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; IQVIA Market Data Standards

columns.name: modified_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this HCP target record was most recently updated. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver layer.

columns.name: planned_call_frequency
columns.description: Target number of sales calls (details) planned for this HCP during the cycle plan period. Drives field force scheduling and activity quotas in Veeva CRM.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Cycle Plan; PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals

columns.name: planned_f2f_calls
columns.description: Number of planned in-person (face-to-face) sales calls for this HCP within the cycle. Part of the call type mix alongside remote calls. Supports field force activity planning and compliance with call mix targets.

columns.name: planned_remote_calls
columns.description: Number of planned remote (virtual/telephone) sales calls for this HCP within the cycle. Complements planned_f2f_calls to define the full call type mix for the planning period.

columns.name: prescribing_potential_decile
columns.description: Decile ranking (1–10) of the HCP's estimated prescribing potential for the targeted brand's therapeutic area, derived from claims data or market research. Decile 10 = highest prescribing potential. Key input to target tier assignment.
columns.reference: IQVIA / APLD Data Standards; Veeva CRM; Sunshine Act Transparency Reporting

columns.name: priority_rank
columns.description: Numeric rank of this HCP target within the territory for the given brand and cycle plan. Lower rank = higher priority. Used to sequence call planning when field force capacity is constrained.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Cycle Plan; Salesforce Health Cloud

columns.name: specialty_segment
columns.description: Medical specialty segment of the HCP as used for commercial targeting purposes (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Immunology, Primary Care). May differ from the HCP master specialty if the brand targets a sub-specialty. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oncology|cardiology|immunology|primary_care|neurology|endocrinology|rheumatology|hematology|gastroenterology|pulmonology — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; ATC Classification; INN Standards

columns.name: sunshine_act_reportable
columns.description: Indicates whether interactions and transfers of value with this HCP target are subject to mandatory reporting under the U.S. Physician Payments Sunshine Act (Open Payments). Drives downstream aggregation for CMS Open Payments reporting.
columns.reference: Sunshine Act (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7h); CMS Open Payments Program; 21 CFR Part 312

columns.name: target_record_number
columns.description: Business-facing unique identifier for this HCP target record, used in Veeva CRM and downstream reporting. Distinct from the surrogate hcp_target_id.

columns.name: target_tier
columns.description: Segmentation tier assigned to the HCP for this brand and cycle, reflecting strategic priority for field force engagement. Tier A = highest priority, Tier D = lowest. Drives call frequency and resource allocation.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals

columns.name: targeting_rationale
columns.description: Free-text or structured justification for why this HCP has been selected and tiered for this brand and cycle. May reference prescribing behavior, patient population, KOL status, or market development opportunity.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM; PhRMA Code; Sunshine Act

columns.name: targeting_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of this HCP target record within the planning cycle. Active = currently targeted; Inactive = de-prioritized; Pending = awaiting approval; Suspended = temporarily paused; Removed = excluded from targeting.

columns.name: veeva_crm_record_code
columns.description: Source system record identifier from Veeva CRM corresponding to this HCP target record. Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and integration with the Veeva CRM operational system.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Data Model; 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records)

columns.name: ytd_call_count
columns.description: Number of completed sales calls (details) made to this HCP for the targeted brand in the current year-to-date period. Tracks field force execution against planned call frequency targets.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Call Activity; PhRMA Code

tables.name: call_activity
tables.description: Transactional record of each field force interaction (detail call) with an HCP or HCO, sourced from Veeva CRM. Captures call date, call type (face-to-face, remote, phone), HCP/HCO visited, products detailed, samples dropped, promotional materials presented, call outcome, next best action, signature captured flag, off-label discussion flag, and PhRMA code compliance status. Core to field force effectiveness measurement and Sunshine Act reporting.

columns.name: call_activity_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each field force call activity record in the Databricks Silver layer. Primary key for the call_activity data product.

columns.name: brand_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand. Business justification: call_activity records field force detail calls which are always conducted for a specific brand in pharma commercial operations. While drug_product_id and medicinal_product_id exist as product-level FK

columns.name: consent_record_id

columns.reference: Veeva CRM Product Catalog; ATC Classification (WHO)

columns.name: hco_master_id
columns.description: Reference to the Healthcare Organization (HCO) where the call took place or which is the primary target when the call is at an institutional level. Nullable when the call is exclusively HCP-targeted.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Account Object; PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals

columns.name: hcp_target_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.hcp_target. Business justification: A call_activity record is the execution of a planned interaction against an hcp_target (call planning record). Linking call_activity to hcp_target enables measurement of call plan attainment — how man

columns.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.investigational_site. Business justification: Medical science liaisons (MSLs) conduct site engagement visits for recruitment support, data dissemination, and investigator relations. Tracks commercial-clinical interface at trial sites, essential f

columns.name: master_id
columns.description: Reference to the Healthcare Professional (HCP) who was the primary target of this detail call. Links to the HCP master record.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Account Object; PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals

columns.name: medicinal_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Call activities detail medicinal products to HCPs. Call reporting, promotional effectiveness analysis, and reach/frequency metrics require product linkage. Real business process: call reporting and pr

columns.name: promo_material_id
columns.description: Reference to the primary promotional material (detail aid, leave-behind, or digital asset) presented during the call, as approved in Veeva PromoMats. Supports promotional compliance auditing.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault PromoMats; FDA 21 CFR Part 202 (Prescription Drug Advertising); PhRMA Code

columns.name: sales_rep_id
columns.description: Reference to the field sales representative (Medical Science Liaison, Sales Rep, or Key Account Manager) who conducted the call.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM User Object; Salesforce Health Cloud

columns.name: territory_id
columns.description: Reference to the sales territory in which this call activity occurred. Used for field force effectiveness measurement and territory performance reporting.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Territory Management; Salesforce Health Cloud Territory Model

columns.name: call_date
columns.description: The calendar date on which the field force interaction (detail call) took place. Principal business event date used for field force effectiveness reporting and Sunshine Act transparency reporting.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Call Object; 42 CFR Part 403 (Sunshine Act / Open Payments); PhRMA Code

columns.name: call_end_timestamp
columns.description: Precise date and time when the call interaction concluded, as recorded in Veeva CRM. Used together with call_start_timestamp to derive call duration for field force effectiveness analytics.

columns.name: call_notes
columns.description: Free-text narrative entered by the sales representative summarizing the content and outcome of the interaction. Classified as confidential due to potential inclusion of commercially sensitive HCP engagement details.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Call Object; PhRMA Code; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: call_objective
columns.description: Pre-call stated objective or purpose of the interaction as entered by the sales representative in Veeva CRM. Supports pre-call planning analytics and coaching.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Call Object; Salesforce Health Cloud

columns.name: call_outcome
columns.description: Result of the call attempt as recorded by the sales representative. 'No_see' indicates the HCP was unavailable. Used for field force effectiveness and access rate analytics.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Call Outcome Picklist; PhRMA Code

columns.name: call_start_timestamp
columns.description: Precise date and time when the call interaction began, as recorded in Veeva CRM. Used for call duration calculation and scheduling compliance.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Call Object; ICH E6(R2) GCP

columns.name: call_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the call activity record within Veeva CRM workflow. 'Submitted' indicates the rep has locked the record; 'Approved' indicates manager sign-off has been completed.

columns.name: call_type
columns.description: Classification of the interaction channel used for the detail call. Drives field force effectiveness segmentation and PhRMA code compliance checks. columns.reference: Veeva CRM Call Type Picklist; PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals

columns.name: channel_mix_code
columns.description: Categorizes the call within the omnichannel engagement model (field, inside sales, digital, or hybrid). Supports channel mix optimization analytics and commercial strategy reporting.

columns.name: crm_sync_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the call record was last synchronized from Veeva CRM into the Databricks Silver layer. Used for data freshness monitoring and pipeline audit.

columns.name: detail_priority_1_product
columns.description: Brand name of the first-priority product detailed during the call, as recorded in Veeva CRM. Retained as a denormalized field for reporting convenience and Sunshine Act submission.

columns.name: detail_priority_2_product
columns.description: Brand name of the second-priority product detailed during the call, if applicable. Supports multi-product detailing analysis and share-of-voice reporting.

columns.name: detail_priority_3_product
columns.description: Brand name of the third-priority product detailed during the call, if applicable. Supports multi-product detailing analysis and share-of-voice reporting.

columns.name: hcp_reaction
columns.description: Sales representative's assessment of the Healthcare Professional's reaction to the product detail during the call. Used for HCP engagement scoring and brand sentiment analytics.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Call Object; Salesforce Health Cloud

columns.name: kol_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the HCP visited during this call is classified as a Key Opinion Leader (KOL). Used for KOL engagement tracking and Medical Affairs coordination.

columns.name: last_modified_timestamp

columns.name: meal_cost_usd
columns.description: Actual cost in US dollars of the meal or refreshment provided during the call. Used for PhRMA Code per-person meal cap compliance monitoring and Sunshine Act reporting.

columns.name: meal_provided_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether a meal or refreshment was provided to the HCP or HCO staff during this call. Required for PhRMA Code compliance and Sunshine Act transfer-of-value reporting.
columns.reference: PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals; 42 CFR Part 403 (Sunshine Act)

columns.name: next_best_action
columns.description: Recommended follow-up action for the sales representative as determined by the CRM system or rep input (e.g., schedule follow-up call, send clinical reprint, invite to speaker program). Supports field force coaching and CRM-driven engagement planning.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Next Best Action; Salesforce Health Cloud Einstein Analytics

columns.name: off_label_discussion_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether any off-label (unapproved indication) discussion occurred during the call. Classified as confidential due to regulatory sensitivity. Triggers compliance review workflow when True.
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 202; FDA Guidance on Off-Label Communications; PhRMA Code; OIG Compliance Guidance

columns.name: phrma_code_compliant_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the call activity was conducted in full compliance with the PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals. Used for internal compliance monitoring and audit reporting.
columns.reference: PhRMA Code on Interactions with Healthcare Professionals (2022 Edition); OIG Compliance Guidance

columns.name: promo_material_version

tables.name: brand_plan
tables.description: Annual or multi-year commercial brand plan serving as the unified planning, budgeting, and execution tracking entity for a brand's commercial strategy. Captures strategic objectives, positioning, competitive differentiation, promotional mix, channel strategy, and KPI targets. Includes detailed promotional spend tracking by tactic (personal promotion, non-personal, digital, samples, speaker programs, congress) with planned budget, actual spend, variance, cost center, and brand P&L line attribution. Also tracks launch activity milestones for new product/indication launches including activity name, launch phase (pre-launch, launch, post-launch), activity type (field force training, formulary pull-through, KOL engagement, patient support activation), planned/actual dates, owner, status, and dependencies on regulatory approval milestones. Serves as the single commercial planning, financial execution, launch management, and brand P&L entity.

columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA SD; Salesforce Health Cloud

columns.name: approval_date
columns.description: Date on which this market access strategy was formally approved by the designated approver. Marks the transition from under_review to approved lifecycle status.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault QualityDocs; 21 CFR Part 11; SOX

columns.name: approved_by
columns.description: Name or employee identifier of the senior leader (e.g., VP Market Access, Chief Commercial Officer) who formally approved this access strategy.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault QualityDocs; 21 CFR Part 11; SOX

columns.name: copay_assistance_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether a copay assistance or copay card program is included in this access strategy to reduce patient out-of-pocket costs and improve commercial insurance access.
columns.reference: CMS Anti-Kickback Statute Safe Harbors; OIG Guidance

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this market access strategy record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking in compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 and SOX requirements.

columns.name: effective_from_date
columns.description: Date from which this market access strategy becomes operative and binding for downstream access activities including HTA submissions, payer contracting, and patient support programs.

columns.name: effective_until_date
columns.description: Date on which this market access strategy expires or is superseded. Nullable for open-ended strategies. Used to manage strategy lifecycle and trigger renewal workflows.

columns.name: gross_to_net_target_pct
columns.description: Target gross-to-net revenue reduction percentage for this access strategy, representing the expected aggregate discount, rebate, and allowance burden relative to gross list price. Critical for P&L planning and net revenue forecasting. Confidential financial data.

columns.name: heor_study_plan
columns.glossary_term: Health Economics and Outcomes Research (HEOR) Study Plan
columns.description: Summary of the Health Economics and Outcomes Research (HEOR) study plan, including cost-effectiveness models, budget impact analyses, and quality-of-life studies planned to support payer value dossiers and HTA submissions. Confidential strategic content.
columns.reference: ISPOR Good Practices for Outcomes Research; NICE Methods Guide; EMA HTA Regulation (EU) 2021/2282

columns.name: hta_body_code
columns.description: Code identifying the primary HTA body responsible for evaluating this product in the target geography (e.g., NICE, G-BA, HAS, PBAC, CADTH, AIFA). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NICE|G-BA|HAS|PBAC|CADTH|AIFA|SMC|NCPE|TLV|ZIN — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: EMA HTA Regulation (EU) 2021/2282; ISPOR HTA Compendium

columns.name: hta_outcome
columns.description: Outcome of the HTA review by the primary HTA body: pending (under review), positive (recommended), positive_with_restriction (recommended with clinical/population restrictions), negative (not recommended), withdrawn (submission withdrawn), or not_applicable.
columns.reference: NICE Technology Appraisal; G-BA AMNOG; EMA HTA Regulation (EU) 2021/2282

columns.name: hta_strategy
columns.description: Description of the Health Technology Assessment (HTA) strategy including target HTA bodies (e.g., NICE, G-BA, HAS, PBAC), submission sequencing, evidence package approach, and comparator selection rationale. Confidential strategic content.
columns.reference: EMA HTA Regulation (EU) 2021/2282; NICE STA Process; G-BA AMNOG; HAS; PBAC

columns.name: hta_submission_actual_date
columns.glossary_term: Health Technology Assessment (HTA) Submission Actual Date
columns.description: Actual date on which the HTA dossier was submitted to the primary HTA body. Compared against hta_submission_planned_date to track submission timeliness.
columns.reference: EMA HTA Regulation (EU) 2021/2282; NICE STA Process; G-BA AMNOG

columns.name: hta_submission_planned_date
columns.glossary_term: Health Technology Assessment (HTA) Submission Planned Date
columns.description: Planned date for submission of the HTA dossier or value dossier to the primary HTA body. Used for launch sequencing and access readiness milestone tracking.
columns.reference: EMA HTA Regulation (EU) 2021/2282; NICE STA Process; G-BA AMNOG

columns.name: icer_threshold_amount
columns.glossary_term: Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (ICER) Willingness-to-Pay Threshold Amount
columns.description: Payer or HTA body willingness-to-pay threshold per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) or other health outcome unit in the target geography. Used to assess pricing headroom and value-based pricing strategy. Confidential strategic financial data.
columns.reference: NICE Methods Guide; ICER Value Assessment Framework; EMA HTA Regulation (EU) 2021/2282

columns.name: icer_threshold_currency
columns.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the ICER willingness-to-pay threshold applicable in the target geography (e.g., GBP for NICE, EUR for G-BA/HAS, USD for ICER US).
columns.reference: ISO 4217; NICE Methods Guide; ICER Value Assessment Framework

columns.name: lifecycle_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the access strategy document: draft (being authored), under_review (in approval workflow), approved (signed off), active (being executed), on_hold (paused), superseded (replaced by a newer version), or retired (no longer applicable). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|under_review|approved|active|on_hold|superseded|retired — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

columns.name: list_price_amount
columns.description: Gross list price (WAC — Wholesale Acquisition Cost in the US, or equivalent list price in other geographies) for the product in the target geography. Confidential commercial pricing data.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA SD; CMS Drug Pricing Transparency; EU Transparency Directive 89/105/EEC

columns.name: list_price_currency
columns.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the gross list price of the product in the target geography (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

columns.name: patient_support_program_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether a patient support program (copay assistance, patient assistance program, hub services) is included as a component of this access strategy to improve patient access and adherence.
columns.reference: CMS Anti-Kickback Statute Safe Harbors; HIPAA; GDPR

columns.name: payer_segment
columns.description: Specific payer segment or channel targeted by this access strategy (e.g., Commercial, Medicare Part D, Medicaid, VA/DoD, Private Insurance, NHS, Statutory Health Insurance). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Commercial|Medicare Part D|Medicaid|VA/DoD|NHS|Statutory Health Insurance|Private Insurance|Integrated Delivery Network — promote to reference product]

columns.name: planned_launch_date
columns.description: Target date for commercial product launch in the specified geography and payer segment, as defined in the launch sequencing plan. Drives milestone planning and access readiness timelines.
columns.reference: ICH E3; FDA PDUFA; EMA Procedural Guidance

columns.name: reimbursement_pathway
columns.description: Regulatory and payer reimbursement pathway pursued for this product: standard (routine formulary review), accelerated (expedited review), managed_entry (conditional coverage), risk_sharing (payer-manufacturer risk agreement), outcomes_based (payment linked to clinical outcomes), named_patient, or compassionate_use. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: standard|accelerated|managed_entry|risk_sharing|outcomes_based|named_patient|compassionate_use — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: EMA HTA Regulation (EU) 2021/2282; CMS Coverage Determination; NICE Technology Appraisal

columns.name: remediation_plan
columns.description: Description of planned remediation actions to address identified access barriers, including evidence generation plans, payer engagement activities, managed entry agreement negotiations, and patient support program design. Confidential strategic content.

columns.name: rwe_rwd_plan
columns.glossary_term: Real-World Evidence (RWE) and Real-World Data (RWD) Generation Plan
columns.description: Description of the Real-World Evidence (RWE) and Real-World Data (RWD) generation plan supporting payer negotiations, HTA submissions, and outcomes-based contracting. Includes study designs, data sources, and timelines. Confidential strategic content.
columns.reference: FDA Real-World Evidence Framework (21st Century Cures Act); EMA RWE Framework; ISPOR

columns.name: strategy_code
columns.description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the access strategy, used in cross-functional communications, HTA submissions, and payer contracting documents. Format: MAS-<ProductCode>-<Year>.

columns.name: strategy_name
columns.description: Human-readable name of the market access strategy, typically including the product name, indication, and geography (e.g., 'Oncology Product X — US Formulary Access Strategy 2025').

columns.name: strategy_owner
columns.description: Name or employee identifier of the Market Access lead or director accountable for developing and executing this access strategy.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; SAP S/4HANA HR

columns.name: strategy_type
columns.description: Classification of the access strategy by its business purpose: launch (initial market entry), lifecycle (ongoing management), indication_expansion (new indication), line_extension (new formulation/dosage), or biosimilar_defense (protecting market share against biosimilar entry).
columns.reference: ISPOR; ICER; EMA Guideline on Market Access

columns.name: strategy_version
columns.description: Version number of the access strategy document following major.minor versioning convention (e.g., 1.0, 2.3). Supports document lifecycle management and audit trail requirements.

columns.name: target_formulary_tier
columns.description: Desired formulary tier placement targeted by this access strategy for the specified payer segment. Tier 1 represents preferred/lowest cost-share; specialty and non_formulary represent restricted access positions.
columns.reference: CMS Medicare Part D Formulary Guidelines; PBAC; NICE

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this market access strategy record was last modified. Used for change tracking, audit trail, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver layer.

columns.name: value_proposition
columns.description: Narrative summary of the clinical, economic, and humanistic value proposition communicated to payers and HTA bodies to justify formulary placement and reimbursement. Confidential strategic content.

tables.name: payer_account
tables.description: Master record for payer organizations including commercial health plans, government payers (Medicare, Medicaid, NHS, statutory health insurers), pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), and group purchasing organizations (GPOs). Captures payer type, tier, covered lives, formulary influence, contracting authority, and geographic coverage. SSOT for payer identity within the market access domain.

columns.name: payer_account_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the payer account record within the market access domain. Serves as the primary key and system-of-record identifier for all downstream joins and references.

columns.name: business_partner_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.business_partner. Business justification: Payer accounts are registered as business partners in MDM (SAP BP) for master data governance, deduplication, and financial settlement. Linking enables contract-to-payment reconciliation, credit limit

columns.name: country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Payer accounts are geographically scoped for market access segmentation, formulary analytics, and country-level rebate reporting. hq_country_code is a plain denormalized attr; FK to country master ena

columns.name: parent_payer_account_id
columns.description: Self-referencing identifier pointing to the parent payer organization in a payer hierarchy (e.g., a regional health plan rolling up to a national parent). Enables hierarchical covered-lives aggregation and enterprise-level contracting.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA Customer Hierarchy; Veeva CRM Account Hierarchy

columns.name: account_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the payer account record. Drives eligibility for contracting, rebate processing, and formulary negotiations. Active accounts are eligible for all market access activities.
columns.reference: Veeva CRM Account Status; SAP S/4HANA Customer Account Group

columns.name: cms_payer_code
columns.glossary_term: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Payer ID
columns.description: Official CMS-assigned payer identifier used in Medicare and Medicaid claims processing and enrollment data. Enables cross-referencing with CMS plan finder, Part D enrollment, and government reimbursement data.
columns.reference: CMS Payer ID Registry; 42 CFR Part 423; CMS Plan Finder

columns.name: contract_type
columns.description: Type of commercial arrangement governing the relationship with this payer. Determines the financial model for gross-to-net deductions and market access obligations.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Contract Management; AMCP Value-Based Contracting Framework

columns.name: contracting_authority
columns.description: Indicates whether this payer account holds direct contracting authority (True) or operates under a parent/umbrella contract managed by another payer entity. Determines whether a direct rebate or pricing agreement can be executed.

columns.name: copay_accumulator_policy
columns.description: Indicates whether this payer has implemented a copay accumulator adjustment program that prevents manufacturer copay assistance from counting toward patient deductibles and out-of-pocket maximums. Impacts gross-to-net and patient affordability.
columns.reference: CMS Copay Accumulator Policy; PCMA Industry Standards; 45 CFR Part 156

columns.name: copay_assistance_accepted
columns.description: Indicates whether this payer accepts manufacturer copay assistance cards or patient support programs for its commercially insured members. Government payers (Medicare, Medicaid) are prohibited from accepting copay assistance under Anti-Kickback Statute.
columns.reference: OIG Anti-Kickback Statute; 42 CFR Part 1001; CMS Copay Accumulator Policy

columns.name: covered_lives
columns.description: Total number of beneficiaries or members covered under the payer's health plan(s). Key metric for assessing payer reach and prioritizing market access investment. Sourced from CMS enrollment data or payer-reported figures.
columns.reference: CMS Enrollment Data; IQVIA Payer Covered Lives Database

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this payer account record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5(2); SOX Section 404

columns.name: effective_date
columns.description: Date on which this payer account became active and eligible for market access activities, contracting, and formulary engagement. Marks the start of the formal payer relationship.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA Customer Master Valid From; Veeva CRM Account Start Date

columns.name: formulary_decision_cycle
columns.description: Frequency at which the payer's pharmacy and therapeutics (P&T) committee reviews and updates formulary coverage decisions. Critical for planning HTA submission and contracting timelines.
columns.reference: AMCP Formulary Management Guidelines; Internal Market Access Calendar

columns.name: formulary_influence_score
columns.description: Proprietary numeric score (0–100) reflecting the payer's ability to drive formulary adoption and steer prescribing behavior across its covered lives. Used in payer prioritization and contracting strategy.
columns.reference: Internal Market Access Scoring Model; IQVIA Payer Influence Analytics

columns.name: formulary_tier_position
columns.description: Current formulary tier placement of the company's lead product(s) on this payer's formulary. Reflects the outcome of market access negotiations and directly impacts patient access and copay levels.
columns.reference: AMCP Formulary Management Guidelines; CMS Part D Formulary Requirements

columns.name: geographic_coverage_scope
columns.description: Scope of the payer's geographic coverage indicating whether the plan operates nationally, regionally, at state/province level, locally, or across multiple countries. Informs market access strategy and contracting jurisdiction.
columns.reference: CMS Plan Finder; EMA Reimbursement Framework

columns.name: gpo_membership
columns.description: Name of the Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) to which this payer or its affiliated health system belongs (e.g., Vizient, Premier, HealthTrust). Relevant for hospital and institutional formulary contracting.
columns.reference: HSCA GPO Standards; Internal Market Access Account Mapping

columns.name: hta_body
columns.description: Name of the Health Technology Assessment (HTA) body associated with this payer's reimbursement decision-making process (e.g., NICE, HAS, G-BA, AIFA, SMC). Drives value dossier format and HEOR evidence requirements.
columns.reference: EUnetHTA Core Model; NICE Technology Appraisal Guidance; G-BA AMNOG Process

columns.name: last_contract_review_date
columns.description: Date of the most recent formal contract or rebate agreement review with this payer. Used to track contracting cycle compliance and trigger renewal workflows.
columns.reference: Internal Market Access Contracting SOP; SAP S/4HANA SD Contract Management

columns.name: naic_code
columns.glossary_term: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) Code
columns.description: Five-digit NAIC company code assigned to licensed insurance entities in the United States. Used for regulatory identification, state insurance filings, and cross-referencing with insurance regulatory databases.
columns.reference: NAIC Company Code Registry; State Insurance Regulatory Filings

columns.name: payer_account_code
columns.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code assigned to the payer organization, used in contracting, SAP SD customer master, and Veeva CRM account records for cross-system reconciliation.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Customer Master; Veeva CRM Account Object

columns.name: payer_name
columns.description: Full legal name of the payer organization as registered with regulatory or governmental authorities (e.g., 'UnitedHealthcare Insurance Company', 'Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services'). Used as the primary identity label for the payer.
columns.reference: CMS Payer Registry; Veeva CRM Account Name; SAP S/4HANA Customer Master

columns.name: payer_subtype
columns.description: Further granular classification within the payer type (e.g., Medicare Advantage, Medicaid Managed Care, Part D Plan Sponsor, NHS England, Statutory Health Insurer, PBM Formulary Manager). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: medicare_advantage|medicaid_managed_care|part_d_sponsor|fee_for_service|nhs|statutory_health_insurer|pbm_formulary — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: CMS Plan Finder; EMA Payer Classification; IQVIA Payer Taxonomy

columns.name: payer_type
columns.description: Classification of the payer organization by business model. Drives contracting strategy, rebate structure, and market access approach. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: commercial_health_plan|government_payer|pbm|gpo|integrated_delivery_network|managed_care_organization — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: IQVIA Payer Taxonomy; CMS Payer Classification

columns.name: pbm_affiliation
columns.description: Name of the Pharmacy Benefit Manager (PBM) affiliated with or contracted by this payer to manage drug benefit administration, formulary design, and rebate negotiations (e.g., Express Scripts, CVS Caremark, OptumRx).
columns.reference: PCMA PBM Industry Standards; Internal Market Access Account Mapping

columns.name: primary_contact_email
columns.description: Business email address of the primary contact at the payer organization. Used for contracting correspondence, formulary submission notifications, and market access communications.
columns.reference: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA Privacy Rule; Veeva CRM Contact Email

columns.name: primary_contact_name
columns.description: Full name of the primary business contact at the payer organization (e.g., Director of Pharmacy, VP of Formulary Management). Used for relationship management and contracting communications.
columns.reference: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA Privacy Rule; Veeva CRM Contact Object

columns.name: primary_contact_phone
columns.description: Business phone number of the primary contact at the payer organization. Used for direct payer relations outreach and contracting negotiations.
columns.reference: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA Privacy Rule; Veeva CRM Contact Phone

columns.name: primary_therapeutic_focus
columns.description: The primary therapeutic area(s) or disease categories that the payer's formulary and coverage policies emphasize (e.g., oncology, immunology, rare diseases, cardiovascular). Informs product-specific formulary positioning strategy.
columns.reference: ATC Classification System; Internal Therapeutic Area Taxonomy

columns.name: prior_authorization_required
columns.description: Indicates whether this payer requires prior authorization (PA) for coverage of the company's products. PA requirements create patient access barriers and are tracked for market access strategy and REMS compliance.
columns.reference: CMS Prior Authorization Policy; AMCP Access & Reimbursement Guidelines

columns.name: pt_committee_meeting_month
columns.glossary_term: Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee Meeting Month
columns.description: Calendar month (1–12) in which the payer's Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) committee typically convenes for formulary review. Used to time value dossier submissions and contracting negotiations.
columns.reference: AMCP Format for Formulary Submissions; Internal Market Access Planning

columns.name: rebate_eligible
columns.description: Indicates whether this payer account is eligible to participate in pharmaceutical rebate programs. Drives gross-to-net revenue calculations and rebate contract eligibility in SAP SD.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Rebate Management; CMS Anti-Kickback Statute Safe Harbors; 42 CFR Part 1001

columns.name: reimbursement_authority
columns.description: Name of the governmental or statutory body that holds formal authority over reimbursement listing decisions for this payer (e.g., CMS, NHS England, GKV-Spitzenverband, CNAM). Distinct from HTA body which assesses clinical value.
columns.reference: CMS Reimbursement Policy; NHS England Commissioning Framework; EMA Reimbursement Guidance

columns.name: rwe_data_sharing_agreement
columns.glossary_term: Real-World Evidence (RWE) Data Sharing Agreement Flag
columns.description: Indicates whether a Real-World Evidence (RWE) or Real-World Data (RWD) data sharing agreement is in place with this payer. RWE partnerships support value-based contracting, outcomes-based agreements, and payer negotiations.
columns.reference: HIPAA Data Use Agreement; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA RWE Framework Guidance

columns.name: step_therapy_required
columns.description: Indicates whether this payer mandates step therapy (fail-first) protocols before approving coverage of the company's products. Step therapy requirements are key barriers tracked in market access and patient support programs.
columns.reference: CMS Step Therapy Policy; AMCP Step Therapy Guidelines

columns.name: termination_date
columns.description: Date on which this payer account was terminated or deactivated. Null for currently active accounts. Used for historical reporting and gross-to-net reconciliation of closed payer relationships.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA Customer Master Valid To; Veeva CRM Account End Date

columns.name: tier
columns.description: Strategic tier classification assigned by the market access team reflecting the payer's relative importance based on covered lives, formulary influence, and revenue impact. Tier 1 represents highest-priority national accounts.

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this payer account record. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and data quality monitoring in the Silver layer.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5(2); SOX Section 404

columns.name: value_based_contract_eligible
columns.description: Indicates whether this payer has the infrastructure and willingness to enter into outcomes-based or value-based contracting arrangements. Drives HEOR evidence generation strategy and RWE data requirements.
columns.reference: AMCP Value-Based Contracting Framework; CMS Innovation Center Models

Records formulary tier, prior authorization requirements, step therapy requirements, quantity limits, preferred/non-preferred status, and effective dates. columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for a formulary position record representing the placement status of a pharmaceutical product within a specific payer formulary at a point in time.

columns.description: The primary type of utilization management restriction applied to this formulary position. columns.description: The patient coinsurance rate (expressed as a decimal, e.g., 0.20 for 20%) applicable to this formulary tier position. Used when the plan applies percentage-based cost-sharing rather than a fixed copay.

columns.reference: CMS Medicare Part D Cost-Sharing Guidelines; ERISA Plan Design Standards

columns.name: data_source
columns.description: The originating system or data feed from which this formulary position record was sourced. Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation across Salesforce Health Cloud/Veeva CRM, PBM data feeds, and third-party market intelligence providers. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: salesforce_crm|veeva_crm|payer_portal|pbm_feed|iqvia|symphony_health|manual_entry — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: Internal Data Governance Policy; 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records

columns.name: effective_date
columns.description: The date on which this formulary position becomes effective and the payer begins applying the associated coverage terms, tier placement, and utilization management requirements.
columns.reference: CMS Medicare Part D Formulary Guidelines; NCPDP Formulary and Benefit Standard

columns.name: formulary_position_code
columns.description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for this formulary position record, used in payer communications, contracting systems, and gross-to-net reconciliation workflows.

columns.name: formulary_review_date
columns.description: The scheduled or actual date of the next payer formulary review cycle for this product. Used by market access teams to plan payer engagement, evidence submissions, and contracting activities.
columns.reference: Internal Market Access Calendar; CMS Annual Formulary Review Requirements

columns.name: lives_covered
columns.description: The estimated number of covered lives (plan members) under the payer formulary associated with this position. Used to weight formulary access metrics and estimate revenue impact of tier placement changes.
columns.reference: IQVIA Payer Coverage Analytics; CMS Enrollment Data

columns.name: market_share_impact_pct
columns.description: The estimated percentage of total addressable market share attributable to this formulary position, based on covered lives and payer segment weight. Used in market access scenario modeling and launch readiness assessments.
columns.reference: Internal Market Access Analytics Standard; IQVIA Market Dynamics Framework

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text field for market access team annotations regarding this formulary position, including payer negotiation context, clinical criteria nuances, or exceptions not captured in structured fields.

columns.name: payer_segment
columns.description: The market segment classification of the payer administering this formulary. Enables segmented gross-to-net revenue analysis and access gap reporting across commercial, government, and exchange channels.
columns.reference: CMS Payer Segment Definitions; IQVIA Payer Segmentation Framework

columns.name: plan_year
columns.description: The benefit plan year (e.g., 2024) to which this formulary position applies. Payer formularies are typically updated annually and this field enables year-over-year access trend analysis.
columns.reference: CMS Annual Notice of Change Requirements; ERISA Plan Year Definition

columns.name: prior_authorization_required
columns.description: Indicates whether the payer requires prior authorization (PA) before the product will be covered under this formulary position. A value of True signals a utilization management barrier that may impact patient access.
columns.reference: CMS Prior Authorization Transparency Rule; NCPDP Formulary and Benefit Standard

columns.name: quantity_limit_days
columns.description: The number of days supply over which the quantity_limit_value applies. For example, a limit of 30 units per 30 days. Enables precise modeling of dispensing restrictions for patient access programs.
columns.reference: NCPDP Formulary and Benefit Standard; CMS Formulary Reference File

columns.name: quantity_limit_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the payer imposes a quantity limit on dispensing of this product under this formulary position. When True, the quantity_limit_value and quantity_limit_days fields define the specific restriction.
columns.reference: NCPDP Formulary and Benefit Standard; CMS Formulary Reference File

columns.name: quantity_limit_value
columns.description: The maximum quantity (in dispensing units) of the product that the payer will cover within the quantity limit period defined by quantity_limit_days. Used for access gap and utilization management analysis.
columns.reference: NCPDP Formulary and Benefit Standard; CMS Formulary Reference File

columns.name: rebate_percentage
columns.description: The contractually agreed rebate percentage (expressed as a decimal, e.g., 0.15 for 15%) payable to the payer or PBM for this formulary position. A key input to gross-to-net revenue calculations and P&L reporting.
columns.reference: OIG Discount Safe Harbor (42 CFR Part 1001); Internal Gross-to-Net Revenue Management Policy; SOX Financial Reporting

columns.name: rebate_tier
columns.description: The rebate tier designation associated with this formulary position as negotiated in the payer or PBM contract. Determines the rebate percentage or per-unit rebate amount owed to the payer in exchange for preferred formulary placement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: base|preferred|exclusive|performance|supplemental — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: Internal Gross-to-Net Revenue Management Policy; OIG Discount Safe Harbor (42 CFR Part 1001)

columns.name: record_created_timestamp
columns.description: The timestamp when this formulary position record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and SOX compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records and Signatures; SOX Section 404

columns.name: record_updated_timestamp
columns.description: The timestamp when this formulary position record was last modified in the data platform. Enables change detection, incremental processing, and audit trail maintenance per 21 CFR Part 11 and SOX compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records and Signatures; SOX Section 404

columns.name: specialty_drug_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the payer classifies this product as a specialty drug under this formulary, which typically triggers specialty tier placement, specialty pharmacy channel requirements, and higher patient cost-sharing.
columns.reference: CMS Specialty Drug Definition; NCPDP Formulary and Benefit Standard

columns.name: specialty_pharmacy_required
columns.description: Indicates whether the payer mandates dispensing through a designated specialty pharmacy network for this formulary position. Impacts patient access and distribution channel strategy.
columns.reference: NCPDP Formulary and Benefit Standard; Specialty Pharmacy Accreditation Standards (URAC)

columns.name: step_therapy_criteria
columns.description: Narrative description of the step therapy requirements imposed by the payer, including which agents must be tried first and the duration or failure criteria required before this product is covered.
columns.reference: CMS Step Therapy Policy; Payer Formulary Management Guidelines

columns.name: step_therapy_required
columns.description: Indicates whether the payer requires step therapy (fail-first protocol), meaning the patient must try and fail one or more alternative therapies before this product will be covered. A key access barrier metric.
columns.reference: CMS Step Therapy Policy; NCPDP Formulary and Benefit Standard

columns.name: termination_date
columns.description: The date on which this formulary position ceases to be effective. A null value indicates the position is currently active and open-ended. Used for point-in-time formulary access analysis.
columns.reference: CMS Medicare Part D Formulary Guidelines; NCPDP Formulary and Benefit Standard

columns.name: therapeutic_area
columns.description: The therapeutic area classification of the product for which this formulary position applies (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Disease). Enables cross-portfolio formulary access analysis by disease area.
columns.reference: WHO ATC Classification System; Internal Therapeutic Area Taxonomy

tables.name: hta_submission
tables.description: Master record for the full lifecycle of Health Technology Assessment (HTA) submissions to bodies such as NICE (UK), HAS (France), G-BA (Germany), CADTH (Canada), and PBAC (Australia). Captures submission planning, dossier preparation, submission date, HTA body, therapeutic indication, comparator, clinical evidence package, economic model type, submission status, and the resulting formal decision including recommendation type (positive, negative, restricted, conditional), benefit rating, added therapeutic benefit classification, recommended price range, and reimbursement conditions. Owns both the submission event and the decision outcome as lifecycle stages of a single HTA engagement. Drives downstream payer contracting and pricing decisions.

columns.name: hta_submission_id
columns.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the HTA submission record. Serves as the primary key for the full lifecycle of a single HTA engagement from planning through decision.

columns.description: Foreign key linking to market.access_strategy. Business justification: An HTA submission is executed as part of a broader market access strategy. The access_strategy record contains the planned HTA submission dates (hta_submission_planned_date, hta_submission_actual_date

columns.description: Reference to the primary HEOR study record that underpins the economic model and value dossier submitted to the HTA body. Links to the medical affairs HEOR study asset.
columns.reference: Internal HEOR Study Registry; ISPOR Guidelines

columns.description: Reference to the specific therapeutic indication for which HTA is being sought. A single product may have multiple HTA submissions across different indications.
columns.reference: ICH E8; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials

columns.name: inn_registry_id

columns.name: medicinal_product_id
columns.description: Reference to the drug product (DP) or finished dosage form (FDF) that is the subject of this HTA submission. Links to the master product record.

columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.orange_book_listing. Orange Book status and paragraph IV dates are relevant to HTA economic mo
