domains.name: intellectual
domains.description: SSOT for intellectual property portfolio including patents (NCE, NBE, formulations, processes), patent expiry timelines, exclusivity periods (orphan drug, data exclusivity, pediatric), trademark registrations, drug master files, freedom-to-operate analyses, and licensing agreements. Supports lifecycle management decisions, generic/biosimilar entry defense strategies, and coordination with legal counsel on patent litigation.
domains.references: USPTO / EPO / WIPO Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)

tables.name: patent
tables.description: Core master record for all pharmaceutical patents owned or licensed by the company. Captures patent number, title, filing/grant/expiry dates, patent family reference, jurisdiction, patent type (composition of matter, method of use, formulation, process, polymorph, salt form), covered compound (INN/USAN), therapeutic area, legal status, and assignee. Also serves as the anchor for trade secrets and know-how records via asset classification. SSOT for the IP portfolio — anchors lifecycle management, LOE planning, litigation defense, and generic/biosimilar entry strategy.

columns.name: patent_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each patent record in the IP portfolio. Primary key for the patent master data product.

columns.name: country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Patents are jurisdiction-specific; essential for freedom-to-operate analysis, market entry planning, and regulatory strategy in global pharmaceutical operations.

columns.name: legal_entity_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Patents are owned by legal entities; critical for IP ownership tracking, portfolio valuation, M&A due diligence, and financial reporting of intangible assets.

columns.name: masterdata_atc_classification_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: Patents are classified by therapeutic area; essential for portfolio analysis, competitive benchmarking, and therapeutic area-specific IP strategy.

columns.name: masterdata_cost_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: Patents incur maintenance costs allocated to cost centers; required for IP budget management, financial planning, and cost allocation in pharmaceutical R&D.

columns.name: masterdata_inn_registry_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.inn_registry. Business justification: Patents claim specific INNs; essential for patent landscaping, FTO analysis, and molecule-patent linkage in pharmaceutical IP management.

columns.name: masterdata_profit_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.profit_center. Business justification: Patents are assigned to therapeutic areas/product lines represented by profit centers; critical for portfolio valuation, segment reporting, and strategic IP management.

columns.name: material_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.material. Business justification: Patents cover specific materials (APIs, formulations); essential for product development, supply chain planning, and patent-product linkage in pharmaceutical operations.

columns.name: patent_family_id
columns.description: Identifier grouping all related patent applications and grants that share a common priority filing across multiple jurisdictions. Used to manage global IP portfolio coherence and track international prosecution strategy.
columns.reference: WIPO PCT; EPO DOCDB Patent Family Definition

columns.name: plant_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.plant. Business justification: Manufacturing process patents are associated with specific plants; required for technology transfer, GMP compliance, and site-specific IP protection.

columns.name: adjusted_expiry_date
columns.description: Final effective expiry date after applying all patent term adjustments (PTA), patent term extensions (PTE) for regulatory review delays, and supplementary protection certificates (SPC). Represents the true end of patent exclusivity for commercial planning purposes.

columns.name: annuity_paid_through_date
columns.description: Date through which patent annuity (maintenance) fees have been paid, confirming the patent is in good standing. Used by IP operations to monitor fee payment compliance and prevent unintentional lapse.

columns.name: asset_classification
columns.description: Broader intellectual property asset classification for this record. Primarily 'patent' for this product, but also supports trade secrets and know-how records anchored to the patent master per the SSOT design. Enables unified IP portfolio reporting across asset types.
columns.reference: Internal IP Policy; TRIPS Agreement Article 39; 18 U.S.C. § 1839 (Defend Trade Secrets Act)

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this patent record was first created in the IP portfolio system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.

columns.name: data_exclusivity_expiry
columns.description: Date on which regulatory data exclusivity (RDE) expires, preventing generic/biosimilar applicants from referencing the originator's clinical data. In the US, NCEs receive 5 years; biologics receive 12 years under BPCIA. In the EU, the 8+2+1 rule applies. Complements patent expiry in LOE planning.

columns.name: expiry_date
columns.description: Calculated or legally determined date on which patent protection lapses, typically 20 years from the filing date subject to patent term adjustments (PTA), patent term extensions (PTE), and supplementary protection certificates (SPC). The primary LOE (Loss of Exclusivity) planning anchor for lifecycle management and generic/biosimilar entry strategy.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 154(b); EPC Article 63; EU Regulation 469/2009 (SPC); FDA 21 CFR § 314.53

columns.name: external_counsel_ref
columns.description: Reference identifier or name of the external law firm or patent attorney managing prosecution, maintenance, or litigation for this patent. Supports coordination between in-house IP team and outside counsel.
columns.reference: Internal IP Policy; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct

columns.name: filing_date
columns.description: Date on which the patent application was formally submitted to the patent office. Establishes the priority date for novelty assessment and is the anchor for calculating patent term and exclusivity periods.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 111; EPC Article 80; WIPO PCT Rule 20

columns.name: fto_clearance_status
columns.description: Current freedom-to-operate (FTO) analysis status for this patent relative to the company's commercial activities. Cleared indicates no infringement risk identified; at_risk indicates potential third-party patent conflict; blocked indicates active infringement concern; under_review indicates ongoing FTO analysis. Critical for launch readiness and litigation risk management.

columns.name: grant_date
columns.description: Date on which the patent was officially granted by the patent office, conferring enforceable rights to the assignee. Null for applications still under examination. Used to calculate patent term adjustments (PTA) and supplementary protection certificate (SPC) eligibility.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 154; EPC Article 97; FDA Orange Book

columns.name: legal_status
columns.description: Current legal standing of the patent in its jurisdiction lifecycle. Pending indicates application under examination; granted indicates active protection; abandoned/lapsed indicates failure to prosecute or maintain; opposed indicates third-party challenge; litigated indicates active court proceedings. Drives LOE planning and portfolio valuation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|granted|abandoned|expired|lapsed|opposed|litigated — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: USPTO PAIR; EPO Register; 35 U.S.C. § 154; EPC Article 63

columns.name: litigation_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this patent is currently subject to active litigation, including Paragraph IV ANDA challenges, inter partes review (IPR), post-grant review (PGR), or district court infringement proceedings. Triggers escalated monitoring and legal counsel coordination.

columns.name: maintenance_fee_due_date
columns.description: Next scheduled date by which maintenance (annuity) fees must be paid to the patent office to keep the patent in force. Failure to pay results in lapse of patent rights. Critical for IP portfolio maintenance operations.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 41; EPC Rule 51; USPTO Fee Schedule

columns.name: orange_book_listed
columns.description: Indicates whether this patent is listed in the FDA Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations (Orange Book). Orange Book listing triggers Paragraph IV certification obligations for ANDA filers and is central to Hatch-Waxman litigation strategy.
columns.reference: 21 CFR § 314.53; FDA Orange Book; Hatch-Waxman Act (21 U.S.C. § 355)

columns.name: orphan_drug_exclusivity_expiry
columns.description: Date on which orphan drug market exclusivity expires, granting 7 years (US) or 10 years (EU) of market protection for drugs treating rare diseases. Distinct from patent expiry and critical for rare disease portfolio lifecycle planning.
columns.reference: Orphan Drug Act (21 U.S.C. § 360bb); EU Regulation 141/2000; FDA ODE; EMA COMP

columns.name: ownership_type
columns.description: Classification of the company's relationship to the patent. Owned indicates full proprietary ownership; licensed_in indicates rights acquired from a third party; licensed_out indicates rights granted to a third party; co_owned indicates joint ownership; assigned indicates transfer of ownership has occurred.

columns.name: patent_number
columns.description: Officially assigned patent number issued by the relevant patent office (e.g., USPTO, EPO, WIPO). Serves as the primary external business identifier for the patent. Format varies by jurisdiction (e.g., US10123456B2, EP3456789A1).

columns.name: patent_type
columns.description: Classification of the patent by the nature of the invention. Composition of matter covers the active molecule (NCE/NBE); method of use covers therapeutic indications; formulation covers drug product design; process covers manufacturing methods; polymorph and salt form cover physical-chemical variants. Critical for LOE (Loss of Exclusivity) strategy and generic/biosimilar entry defense.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 101; ICH Q6A; FDA Orange Book

columns.name: pediatric_exclusivity_expiry
columns.description: Date on which the 6-month pediatric exclusivity extension expires, granted by the FDA under the Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA) for conducting pediatric studies. Attaches to and extends both patent and data exclusivity periods.
columns.reference: Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA); 21 U.S.C. § 355a; FDA

columns.name: priority_date
columns.description: Earliest claimed priority date, typically the date of the first-filed application in the patent family (provisional or national phase). Determines prior art cutoff and is critical for freedom-to-operate (FTO) analyses and validity challenges.
columns.reference: Paris Convention Article 4; WIPO PCT; 35 U.S.C. § 119

columns.name: prosecution_status
columns.description: Detailed status of the patent application within the prosecution workflow at the patent office. Provides granular tracking beyond legal_status for IP counsel and patent attorneys managing active applications. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: filed|examination|office_action|response_pending|allowed|granted|abandoned — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: USPTO PAIR; EPO Online Filing; MPEP

columns.name: purple_book_listed
columns.description: Indicates whether this patent is listed in the FDA Purple Book (List of Licensed Biological Products). Relevant for biologics and biosimilar entry defense under the Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act (BPCIA).

columns.name: spc_expiry_date
columns.description: Date on which the Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC) expires, representing the final end of patent-based market exclusivity in the relevant EU jurisdiction. Null if no SPC applies.

columns.name: spc_number
columns.description: Reference number of the Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC) granted in EU member states to extend patent protection beyond the standard 20-year term to compensate for regulatory review time. Null if no SPC has been granted.

columns.name: term_adjustment_days
columns.description: Number of days added to the patent term by the USPTO as Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) to compensate for delays in patent prosecution caused by the USPTO. Directly impacts the effective expiry date calculation.

columns.name: term_extension_days
columns.description: Number of days added to the patent term under 35 U.S.C. § 156 (US) to compensate for time lost during FDA regulatory review of the drug product. Maximum extension is 5 years; total remaining term cannot exceed 14 years post-approval.

columns.name: therapeutic_area
