columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: LOE (loss of exclusivity) defense activities and exclusivity maintenance costs are tracked against cost centers for IP budget management and financial planning. No existing cost_center FK on exclusivi

columns.name: masterdata_inn_registry_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.inn_registry. Business justification: Exclusivity is granted for specific INNs; critical for lifecycle management, molecule-specific LOE planning, and regulatory exclusivity tracking.

columns.name: masterdata_ndc_code_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.ndc_code. Business justification: Exclusivity protects specific NDC-coded products; critical for LOE forecasting, generic entry planning, and product-specific revenue protection.

columns.name: medicinal_product_id
columns.description: Reference to the pharmaceutical product (Drug Product or Drug Substance) to which this exclusivity period applies.
columns.reference: FDA Orange Book; EMA Product Register

columns.name: patent_id
columns.description: FK to intellectual.patent.patent_id — Exclusivity periods are often tied to specific patents — linking enables IP lifecycle management and loss-of-exclusivity (LOE) planning critical for commercial strategy.

columns.name: approval_date
columns.description: The date on which the NDA, BLA, or MAA was approved by the granting authority, which typically triggers the start of the exclusivity period. Serves as the anchor date for exclusivity calculations.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314; FDA Orange Book; EMA EPAR; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: brand_name
columns.description: The proprietary/trade name of the drug product under which the exclusivity was granted and the product is marketed. Used for commercial lifecycle management and trademark coordination.
columns.reference: FDA Orange Book; EMA EPAR; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: challenge_status
columns.description: Indicates whether this exclusivity period is subject to a legal or regulatory challenge. Paragraph IV = ANDA Paragraph IV certification challenge under Hatch-Waxman; Inter Partes = IPR/PGR challenge at USPTO; Court Order = court-ordered modification; Under Review = authority-initiated review. Critical for generic entry defense strategy.
columns.reference: Hatch-Waxman Act 21 USC 355(j); 35 USC 315 (IPR); FDA Orange Book

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this exclusivity period record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and SOX compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; SOX; GDPR Article 5; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: data_package_type
columns.description: Type of regulatory data package submitted with the application. Full = complete standalone dossier (NCE/NBE); 505(b)(2) = hybrid relying on published literature or prior approvals; Hybrid = EU hybrid application; Bibliographic = based on published scientific literature. Determines applicable exclusivity type and duration.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.54 (505(b)(2)); EMA Directive 2001/83/EC Article 10; ICH M4

columns.name: dmf_number
columns.description: FDA Drug Master File (DMF) number associated with the drug substance or drug product covered by this exclusivity, where applicable. Supports CMC (Chemistry Manufacturing and Controls) linkage and regulatory audit.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: dosage_form
columns.description: The pharmaceutical dosage form of the product covered by this exclusivity (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, solution, patch). Relevant because exclusivity may be dosage-form specific.
columns.reference: FDA Orange Book; ICH Q6A; EMA Guideline on Pharmaceutical Development

columns.name: exclusivity_category
columns.description: Broad category of the exclusivity period indicating whether it applies to a small molecule (NCE/NME), biologic (NBE), orphan drug designation, pediatric extension, or combination product.
columns.reference: FDA CDER/CBER Guidance; ICH Q6A; EMA Guideline on Orphan Medicinal Products

columns.name: exclusivity_code
columns.description: Internally assigned unique alphanumeric code identifying this exclusivity period record, used for cross-system referencing and lifecycle management tracking.
columns.reference: Internal IP Management Standard; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: exclusivity_duration_months
columns.description: Total duration of the exclusivity period expressed in months as granted by the regulatory authority (e.g., 84 months for US orphan drug, 120 months for EU orphan drug, 144 months for US biologics). Supports duration validation and comparison across jurisdictions.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.108; Hatch-Waxman Act; BPCIA 42 USC 262; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000

columns.name: exclusivity_expiry_date
columns.description: The date on which the regulatory exclusivity period expires, after which generic or biosimilar applicants may reference the innovator data. Critical for lifecycle management and generic/biosimilar entry defense planning.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.108; Hatch-Waxman Act; BPCIA 42 USC 262; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000

columns.name: exclusivity_start_date
columns.description: The date on which the regulatory exclusivity period commences, typically aligned with the date of first approval (NDA/BLA/MAA approval date) or orphan designation date depending on exclusivity type.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.108; FDA Orange Book; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000

columns.name: exclusivity_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the exclusivity period. Active = currently in force; Expired = past expiry date; Withdrawn = voluntarily or involuntarily revoked by authority; Challenged = subject to legal or regulatory challenge; Pending = granted but not yet effective; Suspended = temporarily halted pending review.
columns.reference: FDA Orange Book; EMA Orphan Register; 21 CFR Part 314; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: exclusivity_type
columns.description: Classification of the regulatory exclusivity type granted. NCE = New Chemical Entity (5 years US); ODE = Orphan Drug Exclusivity (7 years US / 10 years EU); PED = Pediatric Exclusivity Extension (6 months); DATA = Data Exclusivity for new indication (3 years US); BIOL = Biologics Exclusivity (12 years US); REMS = Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy exclusivity. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NCE|ODE|PED|DATA|BIOL|REMS|NME|PATENT_LINKAGE — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.108; Hatch-Waxman Act; BPCIA 42 USC 262; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000

columns.name: first_generic_entry_date
columns.description: The projected or actual date on which the first generic (ANDA) or biosimilar (351(k) BLA) product may enter the market following expiry or challenge of this exclusivity. Used for lifecycle management, revenue forecasting, and LOE (Loss of Exclusivity) planning.
columns.reference: Hatch-Waxman Act; BPCIA 42 USC 262; FDA Orange Book; EMA Biosimilar Guidelines

columns.name: granting_authority
columns.description: Regulatory authority that granted this exclusivity period (e.g., FDA for US market, EMA for EU market, PMDA for Japan, MHRA for UK post-Brexit). Determines jurisdiction and applicable exclusivity rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|PMDA|MHRA|NMPA|WHO|DEA — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: FDA Orange Book; EMA Orphan Register; ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: indication
columns.description: The specific disease or condition for which the product is approved and for which this exclusivity was granted. Particularly important for new indication (3-year data exclusivity) and orphan drug exclusivity where exclusivity is indication-specific.
columns.reference: FDA Orange Book; EMA EPAR; ICH E8; 21 CFR Part 314.108

columns.name: is_orphan_designated
columns.description: Indicates whether the product holds an orphan drug designation from FDA (Orphan Drug Act) or EMA (Regulation EC 141/2000), which is a prerequisite for orphan drug exclusivity (ODE). Distinct from exclusivity_type as designation may exist without exclusivity being granted.
columns.reference: FDA Orphan Drug Act 21 CFR Part 316; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000

columns.name: last_updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this exclusivity period record, supporting change tracking and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records regulations.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; SOX; GDPR Article 5; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: legal_counsel_notes
columns.description: Free-text notes from legal counsel regarding this exclusivity period, including litigation strategy, challenge responses, and coordination with patent attorneys. Classified as confidential due to potential attorney-client privilege content.
columns.reference: Internal IP Legal Policy; SOX Compliance; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: lifecycle_stage
columns.description: Current lifecycle management stage of the product relative to this exclusivity period. Pre-Approval = exclusivity anticipated but not yet granted; Active Protection = exclusivity in force; LOE Watch = within 24 months of expiry requiring active monitoring; Post-Expiry = exclusivity has lapsed.
columns.reference: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System; Internal Lifecycle Management Policy

columns.name: loe_risk_level
columns.description: Assessed risk level for Loss of Exclusivity (LOE) based on proximity to expiry, challenge status, and competitive pipeline. Critical for commercial lifecycle management and strategic planning.
columns.reference: Internal IP Lifecycle Management Policy; ICH Q10

columns.name: orphan_designation_number
columns.description: Official orphan drug designation number assigned by FDA (ODA) or EMA (EC Regulation 141/2000) when exclusivity_type is ODE. Required for orphan drug exclusivity validation and regulatory reporting.
columns.reference: FDA Orphan Drug Act 21 CFR Part 316; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: patent_linkage_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this exclusivity period is linked to a listed patent in the FDA Orange Book or equivalent patent register, enabling coordination between patent protection and regulatory exclusivity for lifecycle management.
columns.reference: Hatch-Waxman Act; FDA Orange Book; 21 CFR Part 314.53

columns.name: pediatric_extension_expiry_date
columns.description: The adjusted expiry date reflecting the 6-month pediatric exclusivity extension, if granted. Null if pediatric_extension_granted is False.
columns.reference: Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA); EU Paediatric Regulation EC 1901/2006

columns.name: pediatric_extension_granted
columns.description: Indicates whether a 6-month pediatric exclusivity extension (PED) has been granted under the Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA) or EU Paediatric Regulation, extending the base exclusivity or patent term by 6 months.
columns.reference: Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA); EU Paediatric Regulation EC 1901/2006; 21 CFR Part 314.108

columns.name: regulatory_basis
columns.description: The specific statutory or regulatory provision under which this exclusivity was granted (e.g., 21 CFR 314.108(b)(2) for NCE, Orphan Drug Act Section 527, BPCIA Section 7002, EU Regulation 141/2000 Article 8). Supports legal and regulatory audit trails.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.108; Orphan Drug Act; BPCIA; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000; Hatch-Waxman Act

columns.name: rems_required
columns.glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Required
columns.description: Indicates whether a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) is required as a condition of approval for this product, which may confer additional exclusivity protections or market access restrictions relevant to generic entry.
columns.reference: FDA REMS Guidance; 21 USC 355-1; 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: route_of_administration
columns.description: The route by which the drug product is administered (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, topical). Exclusivity may be route-specific, particularly for new indication or new formulation exclusivity.
columns.reference: FDA Orange Book; ICH M4; EMA SmPC Guideline

columns.name: source_system
columns.description: The operational system of record from which this exclusivity period data was sourced (e.g., Veeva Vault RIM, FDA Orange Book feed, EMA EPAR, SAP S/4HANA). Supports data lineage and Silver layer provenance tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; Internal Data Governance Policy; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

columns.name: therapeutic_area
columns.description: The therapeutic area or disease category associated with the approved indication (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neurology, Cardiovascular). Used for portfolio segmentation and LOE impact analysis by therapeutic area.
columns.reference: ICH E8; ATC Classification; FDA CDER Therapeutic Area Classification

tables.name: trademark
tables.description: Master record for all pharmaceutical trademark registrations including brand names, logos, trade dress, and slogans. Captures trademark name, registration number, filing date, registration date, expiry/renewal date, jurisdiction, Nice classification, goods and services description, trademark type (word mark, figurative, combined), owner entity, and current status (pending, registered, opposed, cancelled). Supports brand protection strategy and commercial launch activities.

columns.name: trademark_id
columns.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each trademark registration record in the pharmaceutical intellectual property portfolio.
columns.reference: ISO 15836 (Dublin Core Metadata); Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Trademarks are registered by jurisdiction; required for brand protection strategy, market entry planning, and global brand portfolio management.

columns.name: legal_entity_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Trademarks are registered to legal entities; required for brand ownership tracking, legal compliance, and M&A due diligence in pharmaceutical branding.

columns.name: licensing_agreement_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.licensing_agreement. Business justification: trademark has licensing_flag (BOOLEAN) indicating the trademark is subject to a licensing arrangement. The governing licensing agreement is tracked in licensing_agreement, which covers all IP licensin

columns.name: masterdata_atc_classification_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: Trademarks are associated with therapeutic categories; required for brand strategy, market positioning, and therapeutic area-specific brand portfolio management.

columns.name: masterdata_cost_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: Trademark maintenance costs (annuity fees, watch services, opposition proceedings) are tracked against cost centers for IP budget management and financial reporting. A pharma IP controller expects tra

columns.name: masterdata_inn_registry_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.inn_registry. Business justification: Trademarks are brand names for INN-based drugs. EMA and FDA require INN alongside brand name on packaging; regulatory submissions map trademark to INN. inn_name on trademark is a denormalized represen

columns.name: masterdata_profit_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.profit_center. Business justification: Trademarks are associated with profit centers for brand P&L reporting and licensing revenue attribution under IFRS. Brand management requires profit-center-level trademark portfolio reporting. No exis

columns.name: material_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.material. Business justification: Brand trademarks are associated with specific materials (finished drug products) for packaging artwork management and supply chain labeling compliance. Artwork approval workflows require trademark-to-

columns.name: application_number
columns.description: The official application number assigned by the trademark office at the time of filing, prior to registration. Used to track the application through examination and opposition proceedings.
columns.reference: USPTO TEAS; EUIPO eSearch; WIPO Madrid System

columns.name: colour_claim
columns.description: Description of any specific colour or colour combination claimed as a feature of the trademark (e.g., Pantone codes, RGB values, or textual colour descriptions). Relevant for figurative and combined marks where colour is a distinctive element.
columns.reference: WIPO Nice Agreement; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 4; USPTO TEAS

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: The timestamp when the trademark record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); GDPR Article 5(2); SOX; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: disclaimer_text
columns.description: Any disclaimer of exclusive rights to specific elements of the trademark (e.g., generic or descriptive terms within a combined mark) as required or accepted by the trademark office during examination.
columns.reference: 15 U.S.C. § 1056; USPTO TEAS; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001

columns.name: expiry_date
columns.description: The date on which the current trademark registration term expires and renewal must be filed to maintain protection. Critical for lifecycle management and brand protection continuity.
columns.reference: WIPO Madrid System; 15 U.S.C. § 1058; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 53

columns.name: external_counsel_firm
columns.description: Name of the external law firm or IP agent responsible for managing the trademark prosecution and maintenance in the relevant jurisdiction. Supports coordination with legal counsel on prosecution strategy and renewal deadlines.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; Pharmaceutical IP management best practices; SOX compliance

columns.name: filing_date
columns.description: The date on which the trademark application was officially filed with the relevant trademark office. Establishes priority date for the mark in the jurisdiction.
columns.reference: WIPO Paris Convention Art. 4; 15 U.S.C. § 1051; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 32

columns.name: goods_services_description
columns.description: Detailed textual description of the goods and/or services covered by the trademark registration, as specified in the application. For pharmaceutical trademarks, typically describes the therapeutic area, dosage form, and indication of the drug product covered.
columns.reference: WIPO Nice Agreement; 15 U.S.C. § 1051(a)(2); EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 33

columns.name: internal_reference_code
columns.description: Internal company reference code or docket number assigned to the trademark record in the company's IP management system (e.g., Veeva Vault RIM or internal IP docketing system). Enables cross-referencing with internal IP portfolio management tools.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; SAP S/4HANA IP Module; Internal IP Docketing Standards

columns.name: litigation_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the trademark is currently involved in active litigation or legal proceedings (True), such as infringement actions, cancellation proceedings, or inter partes disputes. Triggers coordination with legal counsel.
columns.reference: 15 U.S.C. § 1114; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 130; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: madrid_international_number
columns.description: The WIPO-assigned international registration number for trademarks filed under the Madrid Protocol. Populated only when madrid_protocol_flag is True.
columns.reference: WIPO Madrid System; WIPO Madrid Protocol Art. 3

columns.name: madrid_protocol_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this trademark registration was obtained through the WIPO Madrid Protocol international registration system (True) or through a direct national/regional filing (False). Affects renewal procedures and management workflows.
columns.reference: WIPO Madrid Protocol (1989); WIPO Madrid System

columns.name: mark_type
columns.description: Classification of the trademark by its nature: word mark (text only), figurative mark (logo/image only), combined mark (text and image), three-dimensional mark (shape), sound mark, or colour mark. Drives brand protection strategy and enforcement scope. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: word_mark|figurative_mark|combined_mark|three_dimensional_mark|sound_mark|colour_mark — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: WIPO Nice Agreement; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 4; 15 U.S.C. § 1127

columns.name: nice_class_codes
columns.description: Comma-separated list of Nice Classification class numbers (1–45) under which the trademark is registered. For pharmaceutical trademarks, typically includes Class 5 (pharmaceutical preparations) and potentially Class 10 (medical devices) or Class 44 (medical services). Defines the scope of goods and services covered by the mark.
columns.reference: WIPO Nice Agreement (11th Edition); 15 U.S.C. § 1112; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 33

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text field for capturing additional remarks, prosecution history notes, strategic comments, or legal observations relevant to the trademark record that are not captured in structured fields.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; Internal IP Management Best Practices

columns.name: office_code
columns.description: Code identifying the trademark office or registry where the application was filed or registration is held (e.g., USPTO for United States, EUIPO for European Union, UKIPO for United Kingdom, JPO for Japan, CNIPA for China, WIPO for international registrations). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: USPTO|EUIPO|UKIPO|JPO|CNIPA|WIPO|CIPO|IP_AUSTRALIA — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: WIPO Madrid System; USPTO; EUIPO; UKIPO; JPO; NMPA/CNIPA; PMDA

columns.name: opposition_deadline_date
columns.description: The date by which third parties may file an opposition to the trademark application in the relevant jurisdiction. Critical for monitoring the application's progress toward registration and for assessing third-party challenge risk.
columns.reference: 15 U.S.C. § 1063; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 46; WIPO Madrid System

columns.name: opposition_status
columns.description: Current status of any opposition proceedings against the trademark application: not_opposed (no opposition filed), opposition_filed (third-party opposition pending), opposition_withdrawn (opponent withdrew), or opposition_decided (proceeding concluded by the trademark office).
columns.reference: 15 U.S.C. § 1063; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 46–47; WIPO Madrid System

columns.name: owner_country_code
columns.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the trademark owner's country of domicile or incorporation, as recorded in the trademark register.

columns.name: priority_claim_country_code
columns.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction in which the priority application was originally filed, as claimed under the Paris Convention.

columns.name: priority_claim_date
columns.description: The date of the earliest priority application claimed under the Paris Convention, if the trademark application claims priority from a prior filing in another jurisdiction. Establishes the effective priority date for multi-jurisdictional filings.
columns.reference: WIPO Paris Convention Art. 4; 15 U.S.C. § 1126; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 34

columns.name: product_launch_country_code
columns.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the primary market where the associated pharmaceutical drug product is commercially launched or planned for launch under this trademark. Links trademark protection to commercial launch activities.
columns.reference: ISO 3166-1; FDA; EMA; PMDA; NMPA; Commercial Launch Best Practices

columns.name: registration_date
columns.description: The date on which the trademark was officially registered by the trademark office. Marks the start of the initial registration term and triggers renewal obligation tracking.
columns.reference: WIPO Madrid System; 15 U.S.C. § 1057; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 45

columns.name: registration_number
columns.description: The official registration number assigned by the trademark office upon successful registration of the mark. Serves as the externally-known unique identifier for the trademark in the relevant jurisdiction.
columns.reference: WIPO Madrid System; USPTO TEAS; EUIPO eSearch; 15 U.S.C. § 1057

columns.name: registration_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the trademark registration: pending (application filed, under examination), registered (officially granted), opposed (subject to third-party opposition proceedings), cancelled (registration revoked), expired (lapsed due to non-renewal), or abandoned (application withdrawn or lapsed). Critical for brand protection and commercial launch readiness.
columns.reference: WIPO Madrid System; 15 U.S.C. § 1058; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 47

columns.name: renewal_date
columns.description: The date by which the renewal application must be submitted to the trademark office to avoid lapse of the registration. May differ from expiry_date due to grace period provisions.
columns.reference: WIPO Madrid System Rule 30; 15 U.S.C. § 1059; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 53

columns.name: renewal_reminder_date
columns.description: The internal reminder date set for initiating the trademark renewal process, typically set a defined number of months before the official renewal_date. Supports proactive renewal management and avoidance of unintentional lapse.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; Internal IP Docketing Standards; WIPO Madrid System

columns.name: therapeutic_area
columns.description: The therapeutic area or disease category for which the associated drug product is indicated (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Supports portfolio segmentation and brand strategy analytics.
columns.reference: ATC (Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical) Classification System; WHO ATC Index; ICH E8

columns.name: trademark_name
columns.description: The brand name, word mark, or slogan that is the subject of the trademark registration (e.g., a proprietary drug brand name). Serves as the primary human-readable identity label for the trademark record.
columns.reference: WIPO Madrid System; 15 U.S.C. § 1051 (Lanham Act); EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: The timestamp when the trademark record was last modified in the system. Supports audit trail requirements, change tracking, and incremental data processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); GDPR Article 5(2); SOX; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: use_anywhere_date
columns.description: The date on which the trademark was first used anywhere (not necessarily in commerce) in connection with the identified goods/services. Relevant for establishing priority in use-based trademark systems.

columns.name: use_in_commerce_date
columns.glossary_term: Trademark First Use in Commerce Date
columns.description: The date on which the trademark was first used in commerce in connection with the goods/services identified in the registration. Required for use-based trademark systems (e.g., USPTO) and relevant for establishing priority and defending against cancellation for non-use.

columns.name: watch_service_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether a trademark watch service is active for this mark (True), monitoring for conflicting third-party applications in the relevant jurisdictions. Supports proactive brand protection strategy.
columns.reference: WIPO Madrid System; USPTO; EUIPO; Pharmaceutical IP best practices

tables.name: drug_master_file
tables.description: Master record for Drug Master Files (DMFs) submitted to regulatory authorities. Covers Type I-V DMFs (manufacturing site, drug substance/API, packaging, excipient, reference information). Captures DMF number, type, holder, submission/amendment dates, regulatory authority, active status, and associated substance. Supports CMC submissions and third-party API/excipient qualification for regulatory filings.
tables.reference: FDA DMF / EDMF (European Drug Master File)

columns.name: drug_master_file_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the Drug Master File record in the enterprise data platform (Silver Layer). Primary key for this entity.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420; ICH M4 eCTD Guidance

columns.name: country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: DMFs are filed with country-specific regulatory authorities; required for regulatory compliance, supply chain qualification, and market-specific manufacturing authorization.

columns.name: legal_entity_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: DMFs are held by legal entities; required for regulatory submissions, supply chain qualification, and vendor management in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

columns.name: licensing_agreement_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.licensing_agreement. Business justification: Drug Master Files (DMFs) contain confidential manufacturing and formulation information. DMF holders often grant access to third parties (e.g., generic manufacturers, partners) via licensing agreement

columns.name: masterdata_atc_classification_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: DMFs are classified by ATC for regulatory portfolio management and therapeutic area reporting. atc_code on drug_master_file is a denormalized representation of atc_classification.atc_code. Proper FK e

columns.name: masterdata_cost_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: DMF maintenance costs (annual updates, regulatory submissions, amendment fees) are tracked against cost centers for regulatory affairs budget management and R&D cost capitalization under IAS 38. No ex

columns.name: masterdata_inn_registry_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.inn_registry. Business justification: DMFs describe specific INNs; required for regulatory submissions, molecule-DMF linkage, and supply chain qualification in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

columns.name: masterdata_profit_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.profit_center. Business justification: DMFs support commercial products; their costs and associated revenues are attributed to profit centers for product P&L reporting and segment financial reporting. No existing profit_center FK on drug_m

columns.name: material_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.material. Business justification: DMFs describe specific materials; required for regulatory compliance, procurement, and material-DMF linkage in pharmaceutical supply chain management.

columns.name: plant_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.plant. Business justification: DMFs reference manufacturing sites; essential for regulatory submissions, supply chain qualification, and site-specific manufacturing authorization.

columns.name: api_manufacturer_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the DMF holder is the manufacturer of the Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) covered by this DMF. True for Type II DMFs where the holder manufactures the drug substance. Used to distinguish API manufacturers from intermediates suppliers, excipient suppliers, and packaging material suppliers.
columns.reference: ICH Q7 (API GMP); 21 CFR Part 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019)

columns.name: cas_number
columns.description: CAS Registry Number uniquely identifying the chemical substance covered by the DMF. Used for substance identification in regulatory submissions, safety databases, and supply chain qualification. Applicable primarily to Type II (API/DS) and Type IV (excipient) DMFs.
columns.reference: CAS Registry (American Chemical Society); ICH Q11; FDA Substance Registration System (SRS)

columns.name: cmc_section_reference
columns.glossary_term: Chemistry Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) Section Reference
columns.description: Reference to the specific CMC (Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls) section of the eCTD submission (Module 3) that this DMF supports. Used to map the DMF to the corresponding regulatory dossier section for NDA/BLA/ANDA/MAA submissions.
columns.reference: ICH M4Q (R1) CTD Module 3; FDA eCTD Guidance; EMA eCTD Guidance

columns.name: confidentiality_commitment_date
columns.description: Date on which the regulatory authority acknowledged the confidential nature of the DMF content. The FDA treats DMF content as confidential trade secret information. This date records when the confidentiality commitment was formally established, supporting IP protection and trade secret management.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420(c); FDA Trade Secret Policy; GDPR Article 9; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this DMF record was first created in the enterprise data platform. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); SOX; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: cross_reference_count
columns.description: Number of active regulatory applications (NDA, BLA, ANDA, IND, MAA) that currently cross-reference this DMF. Indicates the commercial and regulatory criticality of the DMF; a high count signals high supply chain dependency and elevated risk if the DMF is withdrawn or goes inactive.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019)

columns.name: dmf_number
columns.description: Official DMF number assigned by the regulatory authority (e.g., FDA) upon receipt of the DMF submission. Serves as the primary external identifier used in cross-references within NDA, BLA, ANDA, and IND applications. Format varies by authority (e.g., FDA assigns a numeric DMF number).
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019)

columns.name: dmf_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the DMF with the regulatory authority. 'active' indicates the DMF is in good standing and available for cross-reference; 'inactive' indicates it has not been updated within the required period; 'withdrawn' indicates the holder has formally withdrawn the file; 'under_review' indicates a pending agency review; 'closed' indicates the file has been administratively closed.
columns.reference: FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019); 21 CFR Part 314.420

columns.name: dmf_type
columns.description: Classification of the DMF per FDA categorization: Type I (Manufacturing Site, Facilities, Operating Procedures, and Personnel — discontinued by FDA but retained for legacy), Type II (Drug Substance, Drug Substance Intermediate, and Material Used in Their Preparation, or Drug Product), Type III (Packaging Material), Type IV (Excipient, Colorant, Flavor, Essence, or Material Used in Their Preparation), Type V (FDA-Accepted Reference Information). Drives CMC submission strategy and third-party qualification workflows.
columns.value_regex: Type I|Type II|Type III|Type IV|Type V
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019); ICH Q11

columns.name: dosage_form
columns.description: Physical form of the drug product or substance covered by the DMF (e.g., tablet, capsule, injectable solution, lyophilized powder, cream, patch). Relevant primarily for Type II (Drug Product) and Type III (Packaging) DMFs. Aligns with FDA/EMA dosage form terminology. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|injectable_solution|lyophilized_powder|cream|patch|suspension|gel|suppository|inhalation_powder — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: FDA Dosage Form Terminology; EMA EDQM Standard Terms; ICH M4Q CMC Guidance

columns.name: ectd_sequence_number
columns.glossary_term: Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Sequence Number
columns.description: Four-digit eCTD sequence number assigned to the DMF submission or amendment within the eCTD lifecycle. Used to track the submission history and version control of the DMF in the regulatory authority's electronic submission gateway.
columns.reference: ICH M8 eCTD Guidance; FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide; EMA eCTD Guidance

columns.name: effective_date
columns.description: Date on which the DMF became effective and available for cross-reference by applicants in regulatory submissions (NDA, BLA, ANDA, IND). May differ from submission date if the authority requires a review period before the file is deemed active.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019)

columns.name: fda_establishment_identifier
columns.description: FDA Establishment Identifier (FEI) number assigned to the manufacturing facility by the FDA. Used to link the DMF to the FDA's establishment registration database, enabling GMP inspection history lookup and import alert monitoring.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 207; FDA Establishment Registration and Drug Listing; FDA FEI Database

columns.name: gmp_certificate_expiry_date
columns.glossary_term: Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Certificate Expiry Date
columns.description: Expiry date of the current GMP certificate for the manufacturing site associated with this DMF. Triggers renewal workflows and supplier qualification reviews. An expired GMP certificate may block use of the DMF in new regulatory submissions.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Parts 210/211; ICH Q7; PIC/S GMP Guide; EMA GMP Certificate Database

columns.name: gmp_certificate_number
columns.description: Certificate number of the current GMP certificate issued by a recognized regulatory authority or inspection body (e.g., FDA, EMA, PIC/S member authority) for the manufacturing site associated with this DMF. Used for supplier qualification and regulatory compliance verification.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Parts 210/211; ICH Q7; PIC/S GMP Guide; EMA GMP Certificate Database

columns.name: last_amendment_date
columns.description: Date of the most recent amendment or annual update submitted to the regulatory authority for this DMF. FDA requires annual updates to maintain active status. Tracks currency of the file and triggers compliance alerts when updates are overdue.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019)

columns.name: letter_of_authorization_date
columns.description: Date on which the DMF holder issued the Letter of Authorization (LOA) permitting the company to cross-reference this DMF in its regulatory submissions. Relevant when the company is the applicant referencing a third-party DMF.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420(d); FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019)

columns.name: letter_of_authorization_required
columns.description: Indicates whether a Letter of Authorization (LOA) from the DMF holder is required before an applicant can cross-reference this DMF in their regulatory submission. True for most Type II and Type IV DMFs where the holder controls access to confidential manufacturing information.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420(d); FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019)

columns.name: manufacturing_site_country_code
columns.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the country where the manufacturing site is located. Used for import/export compliance, country-of-origin tracking, supply chain risk management, and regulatory jurisdiction determination.
columns.reference: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; 21 CFR Parts 210/211; ICH Q7; GDP Guidelines

columns.name: next_annual_update_due_date
columns.glossary_term: DMF Next Annual Update Due Date
columns.description: Calculated due date for the next mandatory annual update submission to maintain active DMF status with the regulatory authority. Derived from the last amendment date plus 12 months. Used for compliance monitoring and proactive submission planning.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019)

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text field for capturing additional regulatory, operational, or strategic notes related to this DMF. May include information about pending amendments, agency correspondence, supplier negotiations, or lifecycle management decisions not captured in structured fields.
columns.reference: Internal Data Governance Policy; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: proprietary_holder_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the company itself (Pharmaceuticals) is the holder of this DMF (True) or whether it is a third-party supplier DMF that the company cross-references (False). Drives different workflows: internal DMFs require internal maintenance; third-party DMFs require supplier management and LOA tracking.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019)

columns.name: regulatory_authority
columns.description: The regulatory authority to which the DMF was submitted (e.g., FDA for US, EMA for EU, PMDA for Japan, MHRA for UK, NMPA for China). Determines applicable regulatory requirements, format standards (e.g., eCTD vs. paper), and review timelines. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|PMDA|MHRA|NMPA|WHO|Health Canada|TGA — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 314.420; EMA CMDh Guidance; ICH M4 eCTD; PIC/S

columns.name: rims_tracking_number
columns.glossary_term: Regulatory Information Management System (RIMS) Tracking Number
columns.description: Internal tracking number assigned to this DMF record within the company's Regulatory Information Management System (RIMS), such as Veeva Vault RIM. Used for internal workflow management, submission tracking, and audit trail purposes.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH M4 eCTD; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: route_of_administration
columns.description: Intended route of administration for the drug substance or product covered by the DMF (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, topical, inhalation). Applicable for Type II DMFs. Aligns with FDA/EMA route of administration terminology. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intramuscular|topical|inhalation|transdermal|intrathecal — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: FDA Route of Administration Terminology; EMA EDQM Standard Terms; ICH M4Q

columns.name: submission_date
columns.description: Date on which the DMF was first submitted to the regulatory authority. Establishes the official filing date and is used to calculate review timelines, annual update obligations, and IP/exclusivity period calculations.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019)

columns.name: submission_format
columns.description: Format in which the DMF was submitted to the regulatory authority: 'eCTD' (Electronic Common Technical Document — mandatory for FDA since 2017 for most submissions), 'paper' (legacy paper-based submission), or 'NeeS' (Non-eCTD Electronic Submission — used in some jurisdictions). Determines document management and archival requirements.
columns.reference: ICH M8 eCTD Guidance; FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide; 21 CFR Part 314.420

columns.name: therapeutic_area
columns.description: Primary therapeutic area or disease indication associated with the drug substance covered by this DMF (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular, Neurology). Used for portfolio management, lifecycle planning, and IP strategy alignment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oncology|immunology|rare_diseases|cardiovascular|neurology|infectious_diseases|metabolic|respiratory|dermatology|hematology — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: ICH E3; FDA Therapeutic Area Guidance; EMA Therapeutic Area Classification

columns.name: title
columns.description: Official descriptive title of the DMF as submitted to the regulatory authority. Typically includes the substance or material name, manufacturer name, and scope of the file (e.g., 'Drug Substance DMF for [INN] manufactured at [Site]').
columns.reference: FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019); 21 CFR Part 314.420

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this DMF record was most recently updated in the enterprise data platform. Used for change tracking, audit trail, and data freshness monitoring in compliance with 21 CFR Part 11.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); SOX; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: veeva_vault_document_reference
columns.description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault RIM (Regulatory Information Management) system where the DMF submission package and associated correspondence are stored. Enables traceability between the enterprise data platform record and the source regulatory document management system.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); FDA eCTD Guidance

columns.name: withdrawal_date
columns.description: Date on which the DMF holder formally withdrew the DMF from the regulatory authority. Populated only when dmf_status is 'withdrawn'. Triggers downstream impact assessment for any NDA/BLA/ANDA applications that cross-reference this DMF.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry (2019)

tables.name: licensing_agreement
tables.description: Records all IP licensing agreements (in-licensing, out-licensing, cross-licensing, co-development, collaboration) including deal terms, milestone obligations, and milestone payment tracking. Captures agreement type, parties, licensed assets, territory, field of use, exclusivity scope, royalty structure, milestone events (regulatory filing, IND submission, phase completion, NDA approval, first commercial sale, sales thresholds), milestone descriptions, trigger events, milestone due dates, achieved dates, milestone payment amounts, currency, payment status, responsible party, sublicensing rights, and termination conditions. Supports deal management, milestone tracking, revenue recognition (ASC 606), royalty accounting, and partner relationship management.

columns.name: licensing_agreement_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the licensing agreement record in the intellectual property portfolio system.

columns.name: licensee_business_partner_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.business_partner. Business justification: The licensee in a licensing agreement is a business partner in the vendor/customer master. Linking enables royalty payment processing, credit management, and partner relationship management. licensee_

columns.name: licensor_legal_entity_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Licensing agreements require tracking licensor legal entity for contract management, revenue recognition, and intercompany royalty accounting in pharmaceutical partnerships.

columns.name: masterdata_atc_classification_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: Licensing portfolio is segmented by ATC therapeutic class for business development reporting, deal valuation, and portfolio strategy. BD teams report licensing deal value by therapeutic area using ATC

columns.name: masterdata_cost_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: License agreements generate costs/revenues allocated to cost centers; required for P&L reporting, royalty expense tracking, and business unit accountability.

columns.name: masterdata_inn_registry_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.inn_registry. Business justification: Licensing agreements for pharmaceutical compounds are tied to specific INNs (active substances). Royalty calculation, FTO analysis, and regulatory compliance tracking require substance-level licensing

columns.name: masterdata_profit_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.profit_center. Business justification: License agreements are assigned to business segments; required for revenue recognition, segment P&L reporting, and royalty income allocation.

columns.name: territory_country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: License territories define geographic scope; essential for revenue allocation, royalty calculation, and compliance with territorial restrictions in pharmaceutical licensing.

columns.name: agreement_number
columns.description: Externally-known, human-readable reference number assigned to the licensing agreement, used in correspondence with counterparties, legal counsel, and regulatory filings. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this MASTER_AGREEMENT entity.

columns.name: agreement_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the licensing agreement. Draft: under negotiation. Active: fully executed and in force. Suspended: temporarily paused by mutual consent or breach notice. Terminated: ended before natural expiry. Expired: reached end of term without renewal. Drives deal management workflows and financial reporting.

columns.name: agreement_type
columns.description: Classification of the licensing agreement by deal structure. In-licensing: rights acquired from a third party. Out-licensing: rights granted to a third party. Cross-licensing: mutual exchange of IP rights. Co-development: joint development with shared IP. Collaboration: broad research or commercialization partnership. Drives revenue recognition treatment under ASC 606.

columns.name: change_of_control_provision
columns.description: Indicates whether the agreement contains a change-of-control clause that grants termination or renegotiation rights upon acquisition or merger of either party. True = change-of-control provision exists; False = no such provision. Critical for M&A due diligence and IP portfolio valuation.
columns.reference: SOX Section 302; SEC Regulation S-K; ICH Q10

columns.name: commercial_milestone_value
columns.description: Aggregate value of all commercial milestone payments (e.g., first commercial sale, annual net sales thresholds) defined in the agreement, expressed in the agreement currency. Supports commercial launch planning and ASC 606 variable consideration estimation.

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the licensing agreement record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED audit trail required for 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and SOX financial reporting controls.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; SOX Section 302; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: currency_code
columns.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which all financial obligations under the agreement (upfront payments, milestones, royalties) are denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY, GBP). Required for multi-currency royalty accounting and foreign exchange hedging.

columns.name: development_milestone_value
columns.description: Aggregate value of all development-stage milestone payments (e.g., IND submission, Phase I/II/III completion) defined in the agreement, expressed in the agreement currency. Supports clinical development budget planning and ASC 606 variable consideration estimation.
columns.reference: ASC 606; IFRS 15; 21 CFR Part 312; ICH E6(R2)

columns.name: diligence_obligations
columns.description: Narrative description of the commercially reasonable efforts or best efforts diligence obligations imposed on the licensee to develop and commercialize the licensed product. Failure to meet diligence obligations may trigger termination rights. Used for partner relationship management and compliance monitoring.

columns.name: dispute_resolution_mechanism
columns.description: Contractually agreed mechanism for resolving disputes between the parties. Arbitration: binding arbitration under specified rules (e.g., ICC, AAA). Litigation: resolution through courts of the governing jurisdiction. Mediation: non-binding mediation before escalation. Expert-determination: technical disputes resolved by independent expert.
columns.reference: ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 314; SOX Section 302

columns.name: effective_date
columns.description: Date on which the licensing agreement becomes legally binding and operative. Marks the start of the agreement term for royalty accrual, exclusivity period calculation, and milestone tracking. Corresponds to EFFECTIVE_FROM for the MASTER_AGREEMENT role.

columns.name: exclusivity_type
columns.description: Scope of exclusivity granted under the license. Exclusive: licensee is the sole permitted user in the territory/field. Non-exclusive: licensor may grant same rights to others. Co-exclusive: limited number of licensees permitted. Semi-exclusive: licensor retains right to practice but not to license others. Critical for generic/biosimilar entry defense strategy.
columns.reference: USPTO Patent Rules; 21 CFR Part 314; ICH Q10

columns.name: execution_date
columns.description: Date on which the licensing agreement was formally signed and executed by all parties. May differ from the effective date if the agreement has a retroactive or future effective date. Used for legal record-keeping and audit trails.

columns.name: expiry_date
columns.description: Date on which the licensing agreement naturally expires at the end of its agreed term. Nullable for perpetual or open-ended agreements. Drives lifecycle management alerts, renewal negotiations, and IP exclusivity planning. Corresponds to EFFECTIVE_UNTIL for the MASTER_AGREEMENT role.

columns.name: field_of_use
columns.description: Specific therapeutic area, indication, or application domain within which the licensee is permitted to use the licensed IP. Examples: 'oncology', 'rare diseases', 'human therapeutics only', 'diagnostic use'. Restricts the scope of the license and is critical for exclusivity analysis and sublicensing rights management.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314; ICH E6(R2); USPTO Patent Rules

columns.name: governing_law
columns.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction whose laws govern the interpretation and enforcement of the agreement. Determines applicable contract law, dispute resolution procedures, and regulatory compliance obligations.

columns.name: last_updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when the licensing agreement record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED audit trail required for 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and change control tracking.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; SOX Section 302; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: legal_counsel_reference
columns.description: Name or identifier of the internal or external legal counsel responsible for drafting, negotiating, and maintaining the agreement. Used for coordination on patent litigation, IP enforcement, and contract amendments.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314; USPTO Patent Rules; SOX Section 302

columns.name: licensed_asset_description
columns.description: Narrative description of the intellectual property assets covered by the license, including compound names (INN/USAN), patent numbers, know-how, trade secrets, trademarks, or biological sequences. Supports IP portfolio management and freedom-to-operate analysis.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314; ICH Q10; USPTO Patent Rules

columns.name: licensed_asset_type
columns.description: Classification of the primary intellectual property asset type covered by the agreement. Patent: granted patent rights. Know-how: proprietary technical knowledge. Trademark: brand or trade name rights. Data-package: regulatory data exclusivity or clinical data. Biological-sequence: gene or protein sequence rights. Trade-secret: confidential proprietary information. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: patent|know-how|trademark|data-package|biological-sequence|trade-secret|formulation|process — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: USPTO Patent Rules; 21 CFR Part 314; ICH Q10

columns.name: milestone_count
columns.description: Total number of contractually defined milestone events (development, regulatory, and commercial) specified in the agreement. Used for milestone tracking dashboards, deal management reporting, and ASC 606 performance obligation identification.

columns.name: regulatory_milestone_value
columns.description: Aggregate value of all regulatory milestone payments (e.g., NDA/BLA/MAA submission, FDA/EMA approval) defined in the agreement, expressed in the agreement currency. Supports regulatory affairs planning and ASC 606 variable consideration estimation.
columns.reference: ASC 606; IFRS 15; 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

columns.name: responsible_party
columns.description: Identifies which party bears primary responsibility for conducting development activities (clinical trials, regulatory submissions, manufacturing scale-up) under the agreement. Licensor: licensor retains development responsibility. Licensee: licensee assumes development responsibility. Joint: shared responsibility as defined in the agreement.

columns.name: right_of_first_negotiation
columns.description: Indicates whether the agreement grants either party a right of first negotiation (ROFN) for additional territories, indications, or follow-on compounds. True = ROFN exists; False = no ROFN. Relevant for lifecycle management and business development strategy.
columns.reference: USPTO Patent Rules; ICH Q10; SOX Section 302

columns.name: royalty_base
columns.description: The contractual basis on which royalties are calculated. Net-sales: royalties applied to net sales after standard deductions. Gross-sales: royalties applied to gross sales before deductions. Net-revenue: royalties applied to net revenue. Units-sold: royalties calculated per unit sold. Determines the royalty accounting methodology.

columns.name: royalty_rate
columns.description: Contractual royalty rate expressed as a decimal fraction of net sales (e.g., 0.050000 = 5.0%) payable by the licensee to the licensor. Used for royalty accrual calculations, revenue recognition under ASC 606/IFRS 15, and P&L forecasting. Null if the agreement uses a tiered royalty structure captured in a separate milestone/royalty schedule.

columns.name: sap_contract_number
columns.description: Contract number assigned in SAP S/4HANA (SD or FI module) for financial processing of royalty payments, milestone invoicing, and upfront fee recognition. Enables reconciliation between the IP portfolio system and the ERP for royalty accounting and revenue recognition.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA SD/FI; ASC 606; SOX Section 302

columns.name: sublicensing_permitted
columns.description: Indicates whether the licensee has the contractual right to sublicense the licensed IP to third parties (e.g., CMOs, CDMOs, or sub-distributors). True = sublicensing permitted; False = sublicensing prohibited. Impacts CMO/CDMO engagement and supply chain structuring.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314; ICH Q10; USPTO Patent Rules

columns.name: termination_conditions
columns.description: Summary of the contractual conditions under which either party may terminate the agreement, including material breach cure periods, insolvency triggers, regulatory failure events, and convenience termination rights. Used by legal counsel for contract management and risk assessment.
columns.reference: ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 314; SOX Section 302

columns.name: termination_date
columns.description: Date on which the licensing agreement was terminated prior to its natural expiry, whether by mutual consent, breach, or exercise of termination rights. Null if the agreement has not been terminated. Used for financial close-out and IP rights reversion tracking.

columns.name: total_deal_value
columns.description: Total potential deal value including upfront payments, all milestone payments, and estimated royalties over the agreement term, expressed in the agreement currency. Used for deal valuation, P&L forecasting, and investor disclosure. Represents the gross deal value before probability-weighting.
columns.reference: ASC 606; IFRS 15; SOX Section 302; SEC Regulation S-K

columns.name: total_milestone_value
columns.description: Sum of all contractually defined milestone payment amounts across all milestone events in the agreement, expressed in the agreement currency. Represents the maximum milestone-based consideration achievable under the agreement. Used for deal valuation and revenue recognition planning.

columns.name: upfront_payment_amount
columns.description: One-time upfront license fee or signing payment due at execution of the agreement, expressed in the agreement currency. Recognized as revenue or capitalized as an intangible asset depending on the nature of the license under ASC 606/IFRS 15. Part of the MONETARY_TRIPLET for this MASTER_AGREEMENT.

columns.name: veeva_vault_document_reference
columns.description: Reference identifier of the fully executed agreement document stored in Veeva Vault (RIM or QualityDocs module). Enables direct navigation from the data product record to the source legal document for audit, due diligence, and regulatory inspection purposes. Aligns with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault RIM; SOX Section 302

tables.name: royalty_payment
tables.description: Transactional record of royalty payments made or received under licensing agreements. Captures payment date, payment direction (inbound/outbound), royalty basis (net sales, units sold), royalty rate applied, calculation period, gross sales, net sales, deductions, royalty amount, currency, payment status, and reconciliation status. Supports financial reporting, royalty audits, and compliance with licensing agreement terms.

columns.name: royalty_payment_id
columns.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each royalty payment transaction record within the intellectual property portfolio management system.

columns.name: drug_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_product. Business justification: Royalty payments are calculated on net sales of specific drug products (by dosage form and strength). Finance and BD teams need drug_product-level granularity for royalty reporting, audit reconciliati

columns.name: journal_entry_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.journal_entry. Business justification: Every royalty payment (in or out) generates a GL posting for revenue/expense recognition. Finance links royalty payments to journal entries for reconciliation, audit trail, SOX compliance, and revenue

columns.name: licensing_agreement_id
columns.description: Reference to the licensing agreement under which this royalty payment is made or received. Links the payment to the governing contract terms.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; ICH Q10

columns.name: masterdata_cost_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: Royalty payments are posted to cost centers for financial controlling and budget variance analysis. cost_center_code on royalty_payment is a denormalized representation of cost_center.cost_center_code

columns.name: masterdata_profit_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.profit_center. Business justification: Royalty payments are attributed to profit centers for product P&L reporting and segment financial reporting under IFRS 15 revenue recognition. Finance requires profit-center-level royalty income/expen

columns.name: medicinal_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Royalty payments calculated on product-specific net sales. Essential for financial reporting, deal reconciliation, and product-level P&L attribution. Removes denormalized licensed_product_name.

columns.name: patent_id
columns.description: Reference to the patent or intellectual property asset (NCE, NBE, formulation, or process patent) that is the subject of the royalty-bearing license.

columns.name: payment_run_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.payment_run. Business justification: Royalty disbursements are executed via treasury payment runs. Linking royalty_payment to payment_run enables reconciliation of IP royalty payments against bank payment batches — required for treasury

columns.name: primary_royalty_business_partner_id
columns.description: Reference to the party granting the license (the entity receiving royalty payments in an outbound scenario or paying in an inbound scenario).

columns.name: royalty_agreement_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.royalty_agreement. Business justification: Royalty payments are calculated under a specific finance royalty_agreement governing rates, tiers, and territory. This FK enables royalty accounting reconciliation, audit trail, and rate-tier validati

columns.name: adjustment_amount
columns.description: Any adjustments applied to the calculated royalty amount, such as corrections from prior period reconciliations, audit findings, or contractual true-ups. Positive values increase the payment; negative values reduce it.
columns.reference: GAAP/IFRS; SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX

columns.name: audit_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this royalty payment record has been flagged for formal royalty audit review, typically triggered by discrepancies between reported sales and expected royalty amounts or by contractual audit rights.

columns.name: bank_reference_number
columns.description: Bank-issued transaction reference number or wire transfer confirmation number associated with the royalty payment. Used for bank reconciliation and payment verification.

columns.name: calculation_period_end_date
columns.description: End date of the royalty calculation period for which net sales or units sold are being reported and royalties computed. Together with start date defines the reporting window per the licensing agreement.

columns.name: calculation_period_start_date
columns.description: Start date of the royalty calculation period (e.g., quarter or year) for which net sales or units sold are being reported and royalties computed. Aligns with licensing agreement reporting obligations.

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this royalty payment record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under SOX and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
columns.reference: SOX; 21 CFR Part 11; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

columns.name: currency_code
columns.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the royalty payment transaction (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY). Determines the denomination of all monetary amounts in this record.
columns.reference: ISO 4217; SAP S/4HANA FI Module; GAAP/IFRS

columns.name: deductions_amount
columns.description: Total allowable deductions applied to gross sales to arrive at net sales, as defined in the licensing agreement. Typically includes chargebacks, rebates, returns, freight, and applicable taxes.
columns.reference: GAAP/IFRS; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; SOX

columns.name: dispute_reason
columns.description: Free-text description of the reason for disputing the royalty payment amount, applicable when payment_status is 'disputed'. Documents the basis for disagreement between licensor and licensee for legal and audit purposes.

columns.name: due_date
columns.description: Contractual deadline by which the royalty payment must be made as specified in the licensing agreement. Used to track overdue payments and trigger escalation workflows.

columns.name: exchange_rate
columns.description: Foreign exchange rate applied to convert the transaction currency to the company's functional reporting currency at the time of payment. Required for multi-currency licensing agreements and consolidated financial reporting.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; GAAP/IFRS IAS 21

columns.name: functional_currency_amount
columns.description: Total payment amount converted to the company's functional reporting currency using the applicable exchange rate. Used for consolidated P&L reporting and SOX financial controls.
columns.reference: GAAP/IFRS IAS 21; SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX

columns.name: gl_account_code
columns.description: SAP General Ledger account code to which this royalty payment is posted for financial reporting purposes. Distinguishes royalty income (inbound) from royalty expense (outbound) in the P&L.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO Module; GAAP/IFRS; SOX

columns.name: gross_sales_amount
columns.description: Total gross sales revenue generated from the licensed product during the calculation period, before any deductions. Used as the starting point for net sales calculation per the licensing agreement definition.
columns.reference: GAAP/IFRS; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; SOX

columns.name: licensed_territory
columns.description: Geographic territory or market for which the royalty payment applies, as defined in the licensing agreement. May be a country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3), region, or 'GLOBAL'. Supports territory-level royalty analytics.
columns.reference: ISO 3166-1; Licensing Agreement Terms; FDA; EMA

columns.name: minimum_royalty_amount
columns.description: Contractual minimum royalty amount guaranteed per period as specified in the licensing agreement, regardless of actual sales performance. Applicable when the calculated royalty falls below this floor.

columns.name: net_sales_amount
columns.description: Net sales revenue for the licensed product during the calculation period, calculated as gross sales minus allowable deductions per the licensing agreement definition. Forms the royalty basis for net-sales-based agreements.
columns.reference: GAAP/IFRS; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; SOX

columns.name: payment_date
columns.description: The actual date on which the royalty payment was executed (funds transferred or received). Represents the principal real-world business event date for this transaction.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX; GAAP/IFRS

columns.name: payment_direction
columns.description: Indicates whether the royalty payment is inbound (received by the company as licensor) or outbound (paid by the company as licensee). Critical for P&L classification and financial reporting.

columns.name: payment_method
columns.description: The financial instrument or mechanism used to execute the royalty payment (e.g., wire transfer, ACH, check, offset against receivables, or netting against other obligations).

columns.name: payment_reference_number
columns.description: Externally-known business identifier for this royalty payment transaction, typically matching the SAP FI document number or bank remittance reference used for reconciliation and audit trail.

columns.name: payment_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the royalty payment transaction. Tracks progression from draft calculation through approval, payment execution, and final settlement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending|approved|paid|disputed|cancelled — promote to reference product if additional statuses are required]

columns.name: reconciliation_status
columns.description: Current status of the royalty payment reconciliation process, indicating whether the payment has been matched against the licensee's royalty report and confirmed as accurate. Supports royalty audit workflows.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX; GAAP/IFRS

columns.name: royalty_amount
columns.description: Calculated royalty amount due for the calculation period, derived by applying the royalty rate to the applicable royalty basis (net sales, gross sales, or units sold). This is the principal monetary fact of the transaction.
columns.reference: GAAP/IFRS; SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX

columns.name: royalty_report_reference
columns.description: Reference number or identifier of the royalty statement or sales report submitted by the licensee that forms the basis for this royalty payment calculation. Links the payment to the supporting documentation.

columns.name: royalty_tier_label
columns.description: Label identifying the applicable royalty tier when the licensing agreement specifies tiered rates based on cumulative net sales thresholds (e.g., 'Tier 1: 0-$100M', 'Tier 2: $100M-$500M'). Null if the agreement uses a flat rate.

columns.name: therapeutic_area
columns.description: Therapeutic area classification of the licensed drug product (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases). Supports portfolio-level royalty analytics and strategic lifecycle management decisions.

columns.name: total_payment_amount
columns.description: Final net royalty payment amount after applying the royalty rate to the basis, enforcing any minimum royalty floor, and incorporating adjustments. This is the amount actually paid or received.
columns.reference: GAAP/IFRS; SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX

columns.name: units_sold
columns.description: Number of units of the licensed product sold during the calculation period. Used as the royalty basis for unit-based royalty agreements. Expressed as DECIMAL to accommodate partial units or volume-based measures.
columns.reference: Licensing Agreement Terms; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this royalty payment record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements, and data lineage in the Databricks Silver Layer.
columns.reference: SOX; 21 CFR Part 11; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

columns.name: withholding_tax_amount
columns.description: Amount of withholding tax deducted from the royalty payment at source, as required by applicable tax treaties between the licensor and licensee jurisdictions. Relevant for cross-border licensing arrangements.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; OECD Tax Treaties; GAAP/IFRS

columns.name: withholding_tax_rate
columns.description: Applicable withholding tax rate (expressed as a decimal fraction) applied to the royalty payment based on the tax treaty between the relevant jurisdictions. Used to validate withholding tax amount calculations.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; OECD Tax Treaties

tables.name: fto_analysis
tables.description: Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) analysis and competitive IP watch records. Covers FTO assessments determining whether a product, process, or technology can be commercialized without infringing third-party IP rights, plus ongoing monitoring of competitor IP activities (patent filings, ANDA/505(b)(2) submissions, biosimilar applications, patent challenges). Captures analysis title, scope, requestor, conducting attorney or firm, analysis date, product or technology assessed, jurisdictions covered, identified blocking patents, risk level, recommended actions, final opinion, watch type, competitor identity, filing dates, reference numbers, technology area, affected products, and threat assessment. Supports go/no-go decisions for product development, commercial launch, and proactive IP defense strategy.

columns.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) analysis or competitive IP watch record. Primary key for this entity.

columns.name: country_id

columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.formulation. Business justification: FTO analyses are conducted for specific formulations before technology transfer and manufacturing scale-up. IP teams need to link FTO analyses to formulations to assess freedom-to-operate for formulat

columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.business_partner. Business justification: FTO analysis law firms are business partners in the vendor master. Linking enables legal spend tracking, AP payment processing, and outside counsel management. law_firm_name is a denormalized business

columns.name: masterdata_cost_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: FTO analyses are charged to requesting business units; required for cost allocation, chargeback processing, and legal spend tracking in pharmaceutical IP.

columns.name: masterdata_inn_registry_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.inn_registry. Business justification: FTO analyses are conducted for specific active ingredients (INNs) to assess freedom to operate before product launch. Substance-level FTO portfolio management and regulatory clearance tracking require
