columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_family. Business justification: FTO analyses in pharma are commonly scoped to entire patent families rather than individual patents, since a competitor product must clear all family members across jurisdictions. fto_analysis has no

columns.name: patent_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: Freedom-to-Operate analyses are conducted with respect to specific blocking patents. fto_analysis currently has no FK to patent despite being the core IP asset being analyzed. One patent can be the su

columns.name: affected_product_names
columns.description: Comma-separated list of proprietary product names or INNs that are commercially affected by the FTO analysis findings or the competitor IP watch activity. Supports portfolio-level impact assessment and lifecycle management decisions.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA Orange Book; FDA Purple Book

columns.name: analysis_date
columns.description: The date on which the FTO analysis was formally conducted or the opinion was rendered by the responsible attorney or firm. Represents the principal business event date for this record.

columns.name: analysis_number
columns.description: Externally-known unique reference number assigned to the FTO analysis or IP watch record, used for tracking across legal, regulatory, and business functions. Format: FTO-YYYY-NNNNN.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: analysis_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle state of the FTO analysis record: draft (initiated, not yet reviewed), in_review (under attorney or committee review), completed (final opinion issued), superseded (replaced by a newer analysis), or cancelled.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10

columns.name: analysis_title
columns.description: Descriptive title of the Freedom-to-Operate analysis or competitive IP watch record, summarizing the product, technology, or process under assessment.

columns.name: analysis_type
columns.description: Classification of the analysis record: FTO assessment (go/no-go commercialization opinion), IP watch (ongoing competitor monitoring), patent landscape (broad mapping), clearance opinion (legal freedom-to-use), or freedom-to-use. Drives workflow and reporting.

columns.name: competitor_filing_date
columns.description: Date on which the competitor filed the patent application, ANDA, biosimilar application, or other regulatory/IP submission being monitored. Critical for calculating response timelines and exclusivity defense windows.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; Hatch-Waxman Act; BPCIA

columns.name: competitor_name
columns.description: Name of the competitor company whose IP activities are being monitored in this watch record (e.g., generic manufacturer filing an ANDA, biosimilar applicant, or third-party patent filer). Central to competitive intelligence.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA Orange Book; FDA Purple Book

columns.name: competitor_reference_number
columns.description: Official reference number of the competitor's filing being monitored, such as an ANDA application number, biosimilar BLA number, patent publication number, or IPR petition number. Enables direct lookup in regulatory and patent databases.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA; USPTO; EPO; WIPO

columns.name: conducting_attorney
columns.description: Name of the internal patent attorney or external legal counsel responsible for conducting and signing off on the FTO analysis. Critical for attorney-client privilege tracking and legal accountability.

columns.name: confidentiality_level
columns.description: Data classification level assigned to the FTO analysis record, governing access controls and information sharing: restricted (attorney-client privilege, highly sensitive), confidential (internal legal/IP team only), internal (general internal use), or public. Aligns with enterprise data governance policy.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5; HIPAA; Veeva Vault RIM; SOX

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this FTO analysis record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.

columns.name: design_around_required
columns.description: Indicates whether the FTO analysis concluded that a design-around strategy is required to avoid infringement of identified blocking patents before commercialization can proceed.

columns.name: dmf_reference_number
columns.description: Reference number of the Drug Master File (DMF) associated with the drug substance or manufacturing process under FTO assessment, if applicable. Links the IP analysis to the CMC regulatory submission package.
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 314.420; Veeva Vault RIM; ICH Q10

columns.name: exclusivity_expiry_date
columns.description: Date on which the relevant regulatory exclusivity period (orphan drug, data exclusivity, pediatric, NCE, etc.) expires for the assessed product. Determines the earliest date a competitor could receive approval for a generic or biosimilar.
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; Hatch-Waxman Act; BPCIA; EMA; Orphan Drug Act

columns.name: exclusivity_type
columns.description: Type of regulatory exclusivity relevant to the FTO analysis or IP watch record: orphan_drug, data_exclusivity, pediatric, new_chemical_entity (NCE), biological, or market exclusivity. Informs the window of protection against generic or biosimilar entry. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: orphan_drug|data_exclusivity|pediatric|new_chemical_entity|biological|market — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; Orphan Drug Act; BPCIA; Hatch-Waxman Act; EMA Regulation (EC) No 141/2000

columns.name: final_opinion
columns.description: The formal legal opinion rendered by the conducting attorney: clear (free to operate without infringement risk), conditional_clear (free to operate subject to design-arounds or licensing), blocked (cannot commercialize without infringing), inconclusive (insufficient information), or pending (opinion not yet issued).
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10

columns.name: licensing_required
columns.description: Indicates whether the FTO analysis concluded that a license must be obtained from a third-party patent holder before the assessed product or technology can be commercialized.

columns.name: litigation_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the FTO analysis or IP watch record is associated with active or anticipated patent litigation (e.g., Paragraph IV ANDA challenge, IPR petition, patent infringement suit). Triggers escalation to senior legal counsel.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; Hatch-Waxman Act; 35 USC; 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: patent_expiry_relevance_date
columns.description: The earliest expiry date among the blocking patents identified in the FTO analysis, representing the date after which the primary IP barrier may no longer apply. Critical for lifecycle management and generic/biosimilar entry defense planning.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; USPTO; EPO; 35 USC; ICH Q10

columns.name: recommended_actions
columns.description: Narrative description of recommended next steps arising from the FTO analysis, such as design-around strategies, licensing negotiations, patent challenge (IPR/PGR), freedom-to-use licensing, or further legal investigation. Drives IP strategy execution.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH Q10; 35 USC (US Patent Act)

columns.name: requestor_department
columns.description: Business department or function that initiated the FTO analysis request (e.g., R&D, Commercial, Regulatory Affairs, Legal). Used for workload tracking and cross-functional reporting.

columns.name: review_due_date
columns.description: Scheduled date by which the FTO analysis or IP watch record must be reviewed and updated to reflect changes in the patent landscape, competitor activities, or product development status. Supports proactive IP portfolio management.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: risk_level
columns.description: Overall IP infringement risk level assigned by the conducting attorney following the FTO analysis: high (significant blocking IP identified, commercialization at risk), medium (some risk, mitigation possible), low (minor risk, manageable), or negligible (no material blocking IP found).
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH Q10; FDA 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: risk_rationale
columns.description: Narrative explanation supporting the assigned risk level, summarizing the key blocking patents, claim analysis findings, and legal reasoning that led to the risk determination. Supports legal review and business decision-making.

columns.name: scope_description
columns.description: Detailed narrative describing the scope of the FTO analysis, including the specific product features, process steps, formulation parameters, or technology elements assessed for potential third-party IP infringement.

columns.name: technology_area
columns.description: Broad technology or therapeutic area classification of the subject matter under FTO assessment (e.g., oncology, immunology, rare diseases, formulation, manufacturing process, delivery device). Supports portfolio-level IP analytics.
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; ATC Classification; ICH Q10

columns.name: threat_assessment
columns.description: Assessment of the competitive threat posed by the monitored competitor activity: critical (immediate commercial impact expected), high (significant risk to market exclusivity), medium (moderate risk requiring active response), low (limited near-term impact), or monitoring (no immediate action required).
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH Q10; Hatch-Waxman Act; BPCIA

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this FTO analysis record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail, version control, and change management per 21 CFR Part 11.

columns.name: version_number
columns.description: Version number of the FTO analysis document (e.g., 1.0, 2.1), tracking revisions and updates to the analysis over time. Supports document control and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault RIM; ICH Q10

columns.name: watch_type
columns.description: For competitive IP watch records, classifies the type of competitor activity being monitored: patent_filing (new patent applications), anda_submission (Abbreviated New Drug Application), biosimilar_application (biosimilar filing), patent_challenge (IPR/PGR/opposition), regulatory_filing, or trademark. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: patent_filing|anda_submission|biosimilar_application|patent_challenge|regulatory_filing|trademark — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: Veeva Vault RIM; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; Hatch-Waxman Act; BPCIA

tables.name: patent_litigation
tables.description: Tracks active and historical patent litigation cases including Paragraph IV ANDA challenges, inter partes review (IPR) petitions, post-grant review (PGR), patent infringement suits, and declaratory judgment actions. Captures case number, court or tribunal, case type, filing date, parties (plaintiff, defendant), asserted patents, accused products, litigation status, key milestones, outside counsel, estimated liability, and outcome. Critical for generic/biosimilar entry defense strategy and legal budget management.
tables.reference: Hatch-Waxman Paragraph IV / BPCIA Patent Dance

columns.name: actual_legal_spend_usd
columns.description: Cumulative actual legal fees and costs incurred to date for this litigation matter, expressed in US dollars. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA FI/CO module legal spend tracking. Used for legal budget management and P&L reporting.
columns.reference: ASC 450; SOX Section 302; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

columns.name: appeal_court
columns.description: Name of the appellate court or tribunal hearing the appeal (e.g., U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, U.S. Supreme Court, EPO Board of Appeal). Null if no appeal has been filed.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 141; Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure

columns.name: appeal_filed
columns.description: Indicates whether an appeal has been filed following the trial court or PTAB judgment. True if an appeal is pending or has been decided; False if no appeal was filed.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 141; Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure

columns.name: asserted_patent_numbers
columns.description: Semicolon-delimited list of patent numbers (e.g., US9,123,456; US10,234,567) asserted or challenged in this litigation. These are the Orange Book-listed or Blue Book-listed patents at issue. Links to the patent portfolio for expiry and claim analysis.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.53; 35 U.S.C. § 271(e)(2); Orange Book (FDA Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations)

columns.name: case_notes
columns.description: Free-text field for internal legal team notes, strategic observations, and case-specific commentary. May include attorney work product summaries, risk assessments, and strategic recommendations. Classified as confidential due to potential attorney-client privilege content.
columns.reference: Attorney-Client Privilege; Federal Rules of Evidence Rule 502; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: case_number
columns.description: Official court-assigned or tribunal-assigned docket number uniquely identifying the litigation case (e.g., civil action number, IPR petition number, PGR petition number). Serves as the primary external business identifier for cross-referencing with legal counsel and court records.
columns.reference: USPTO Rules of Practice; 35 U.S.C. § 311 (IPR); 35 U.S.C. § 321 (PGR); 21 CFR Part 314.53

columns.name: case_priority
columns.description: Internal priority classification assigned to the litigation case based on revenue at risk, strategic importance, and likelihood of adverse outcome. Critical cases receive executive-level oversight; high cases are monitored by senior IP counsel; medium and low cases follow standard legal management processes.

columns.name: case_type
columns.description: Classification of the litigation case by legal mechanism. Paragraph IV ANDA challenges arise under Hatch-Waxman; IPR and PGR are USPTO trial proceedings; patent infringement suits are district court actions; declaratory judgment actions are filed by generic/biosimilar challengers; biosimilar patent dance refers to BPCIA exchange proceedings. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: paragraph_iv_anda|inter_partes_review|post_grant_review|patent_infringement|declaratory_judgment|biosimilar_patent_dance — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. §§ 271, 311, 321; 21 CFR Part 314.53; Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act (BPCIA)

columns.name: court_or_tribunal
columns.description: Name of the judicial or administrative body presiding over the case (e.g., U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, USPTO Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, European Patent Office Opposition Division).
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. §§ 141, 311; USPTO Trial Practice Guide; EPC Article 99

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this patent litigation record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); SOX Section 302; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: estimated_liability_usd
columns.description: Management's best estimate of the potential financial exposure or liability associated with this litigation case, expressed in US dollars. Used for legal reserve provisioning, financial disclosure under ASC 450 (contingencies), and SOX compliance. Includes potential damages, lost profits, and legal costs.
columns.reference: ASC 450 (Contingencies); SOX Section 302; IAS 37 (Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets)

columns.name: filing_date
columns.description: Date on which the complaint, petition, or challenge was formally filed with the court or tribunal. For Paragraph IV ANDA challenges, this is the date the ANDA filer notified the NDA holder. Critical for calculating the 30-month stay period and litigation timelines.

columns.name: first_filer_status
columns.description: Indicates whether the ANDA challenger is the first filer entitled to 180-day generic exclusivity under the Hatch-Waxman Act. True if the defendant holds first-filer status; False otherwise. Relevant for assessing the competitive landscape and timing of generic entry.
columns.reference: 21 U.S.C. § 355(j)(5)(B)(iv); Hatch-Waxman Act; FDA Orange Book

columns.name: institution_decision_date
columns.description: Date on which the PTAB issued its decision on whether to institute the IPR or PGR trial. A decision to institute means the petition met the threshold for review. Null for non-PTAB proceedings.

columns.name: ipr_petition_number
columns.description: USPTO-assigned petition number for Inter Partes Review proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB). Format follows USPTO convention (e.g., IPR2023-01234). Null for non-IPR case types.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 311; 37 CFR Part 42; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

columns.name: judgment_date
columns.description: Date on which the court or tribunal issued its final judgment, final written decision (for PTAB proceedings), or order. Null if the case has not yet reached judgment.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. §§ 318, 328; Federal Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 58

columns.name: lead_outside_counsel
columns.description: Full name of the lead attorney at the outside counsel firm responsible for managing this litigation matter. Used for escalation, communication, and legal budget accountability.
columns.reference: SOX Section 302; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct

columns.name: legal_budget_usd
columns.description: Approved annual or total budget allocated for legal fees and costs associated with this litigation matter, expressed in US dollars. Used for variance analysis against actual legal spend and budget reforecasting.
columns.reference: ASC 450; SOX Section 302; SAP S/4HANA CO Module

columns.name: litigation_status
columns.description: Current procedural status of the litigation case reflecting its lifecycle stage. Active cases are ongoing; settled cases have reached agreement; dismissed cases were terminated without judgment; judgment_entered reflects a court ruling; appealed cases are under appellate review; stayed cases are paused pending other proceedings; closed cases are fully resolved. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|settled|dismissed|judgment_entered|appealed|stayed|closed — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

columns.name: next_key_milestone
columns.description: Description of the next significant procedural or substantive milestone in the litigation (e.g., claim construction hearing, expert discovery deadline, summary judgment motion, PTAB oral argument, appellate briefing deadline). Used for litigation calendar management.
columns.reference: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

columns.name: next_milestone_date
columns.description: Scheduled date for the next key procedural or substantive milestone in the litigation. Used for proactive legal calendar management and escalation triggers.
columns.reference: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

columns.name: outcome
columns.description: Final outcome or resolution of the litigation case. Patent upheld means the challenged patent survived; patent invalidated means the patent was found invalid or unenforceable; infringement found or non-infringement found reflects district court rulings; settled indicates out-of-court resolution; dismissed indicates termination without merits ruling; consent judgment reflects agreed court order. Null for active cases. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: patent_upheld|patent_invalidated|infringement_found|non_infringement_found|settled|dismissed|consent_judgment — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. §§ 282, 318, 328; Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

columns.name: paragraph_iv_notice_date
columns.description: Date on which the company received the formal Paragraph IV certification notice from the ANDA filer, as required under the Hatch-Waxman Act. Triggers the 45-day window to file suit and the 30-month stay. Null for non-Paragraph IV case types.

columns.name: plaintiff_name
columns.description: Legal name of the party initiating the litigation (typically the innovator/NDA holder asserting patent rights, or the generic/biosimilar applicant filing a declaratory judgment action). May be the company itself or a subsidiary.
columns.reference: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 10; 21 CFR Part 314.53

columns.name: revenue_at_risk_usd
columns.description: Estimated annual revenue at risk if the litigation outcome is unfavorable and generic or biosimilar entry occurs earlier than the patent expiry date. Expressed in US dollars. Critical input for lifecycle management decisions and commercial strategy.
columns.reference: ASC 450; SOX Section 302; ICH Q10 (lifecycle management)

columns.name: settlement_date
columns.description: Date on which a settlement agreement was executed between the parties, if the case was resolved through settlement rather than judgment. Null for cases resolved by judgment or still active.
columns.reference: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 41; FTC Act (reverse payment settlement scrutiny); 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: settlement_entry_date
columns.description: Agreed date on which the generic or biosimilar entrant is permitted to launch its product under the terms of the settlement agreement. Critical for lifecycle management and revenue forecasting. Null for non-settlement outcomes.
columns.reference: Hatch-Waxman Act; FTC Act; 21 CFR Part 314.53

columns.name: suit_filed_date
columns.description: Date on which the NDA holder filed the patent infringement suit in response to the Paragraph IV notice, within the 45-day statutory window. Null for case types where the company is the defendant or for non-Hatch-Waxman proceedings.

columns.name: therapeutic_area
columns.description: Therapeutic area or disease category associated with the drug product at the center of the litigation (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular, Neuroscience). Enables portfolio-level analysis of litigation exposure by therapeutic area.
columns.reference: ATC Classification System (WHO); ICH E6 (GCP); FDA Therapeutic Area Guidance

columns.name: thirty_month_stay_expiry_date
columns.description: Date on which the automatic 30-month stay of FDA approval of the ANDA expires under the Hatch-Waxman Act. Calculated from the date the NDA holder received the Paragraph IV certification notice. Null for non-Hatch-Waxman case types. Critical for generic entry defense strategy.

columns.name: trial_date
columns.description: Scheduled or actual date of the trial or oral hearing before the court or tribunal. For PTAB proceedings, this is the oral argument date. Null if trial has not been scheduled or the case settled prior to trial.
columns.reference: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this patent litigation record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking for compliance purposes.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); SOX Section 302; GDPR Article 5

tables.name: patent_prosecution
tables.description: Tracks patent application prosecution workflow from filing through grant or abandonment, including all annuity and maintenance fee payment obligations across all jurisdictions. Captures application number, prosecution stage, patent office, examiner, office actions received, response deadlines, prosecution attorney, prosecution strategy, and complete annuity/maintenance fee history (fee year, due dates, amounts, currencies, payment status, paying agents, confirmation receipts, grace periods, surcharge amounts). Failure to pay annuities results in patent lapse. Supports docketing, deadline management, fee compliance, cost tracking, portfolio maintenance operations, and annuity budget forecasting.

columns.name: patent_prosecution_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each patent prosecution record in the portfolio management system. Primary key for the patent_prosecution data product.

columns.name: country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Patent prosecution is jurisdiction-specific; each prosecution record corresponds to a national/regional patent office. Prosecution cost tracking by jurisdiction and regulatory authority mapping requir

columns.name: internal_order_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Patent prosecution costs (annuity fees, filing fees, attorney costs) are tracked against SAP internal orders for IP cost controlling and capitalization decisions. Pharma IP finance teams require this

columns.name: legal_entity_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Patent prosecution is conducted on behalf of a specific legal entity (the patent applicant/owner). Legal entity-level IP asset reporting and transfer pricing of IP rights require this link. No existin

columns.name: masterdata_cost_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: Patent prosecution costs (annuity fees, attorney fees, filing fees) are tracked against cost centers for IP budget management and R&D cost capitalization under IAS 38. IP controllers require cost-cent

columns.name: patent_family_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_family. Business justification: Patent prosecution records track individual patent applications. Patent families group related applications filed across multiple jurisdictions that share a common priority. Each prosecution record sh

columns.name: patent_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: Patent prosecution tracks the application process from filing through grant. When a patent is granted, the prosecution record should link to the resulting patent master record. The grant_number in pat

columns.name: paying_agent_business_partner_id
columns.glossary_term: Paying Agent Business Partner Id (Foreign Key)
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.business_partner. Business justification: Annuity paying agents are business partners in the vendor master; linking enables automated annuity payment processing and vendor spend analytics. paying_agent_name is a denormalized business_partner.

columns.name: abandonment_date
columns.description: Date the application was formally abandoned, either expressly by the applicant or by operation of law (e.g., failure to respond to office action within statutory period or failure to pay issue fee). Null unless prosecution_stage = 'abandoned'.

columns.name: annuity_due_date
columns.description: Date by which the annuity or maintenance fee for the current fee year must be paid to maintain the patent in force. Failure to pay by this date (or within the grace period) results in patent lapse. Critical docketing field.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 41; EPC Article 86; 37 CFR 1.362; PCT Rule 57

columns.name: annuity_fee_amount
columns.description: Base annuity or maintenance fee amount due for the current fee year, in the currency specified by annuity_fee_currency. Used for IP budget forecasting and cost tracking across the patent portfolio.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 41; EPC Article 86; USPTO Fee Schedule; EPO Fee Schedule

columns.name: annuity_fee_currency
columns.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the annuity fee amount (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY, GBP, CNY). Required for multi-currency portfolio cost consolidation and budget reporting.

columns.name: annuity_fee_year
columns.description: The renewal/annuity year number for which the most recent maintenance fee obligation applies (e.g., year 3, year 7, year 12). Annuity years are counted from the filing date in most jurisdictions. Used for fee schedule management and budget forecasting.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 41 (USPTO Maintenance Fees); EPC Article 86 (Renewal Fees); PCT Rule 57

columns.name: annuity_grace_period_end_date
columns.description: Last date on which the annuity fee can be paid with a surcharge before the patent lapses. Typically 6 months after annuity_due_date in most jurisdictions. After this date, the patent is irrevocably lapsed unless restoration procedures are available.

columns.name: annuity_payment_date
columns.description: Actual date on which the annuity or maintenance fee was paid to the patent office or paying agent. Used to confirm timely payment and to calculate any applicable surcharges.

columns.name: annuity_payment_status
columns.description: Current payment status of the annuity/maintenance fee obligation for the current fee year. Pending = not yet due or awaiting payment; Paid = confirmed payment received; Overdue = past due date, within grace period; Lapsed = grace period expired without payment; Waived = fee waived per applicable rules.

columns.name: annuity_surcharge_amount
columns.description: Late payment surcharge amount applied when the annuity fee is paid after the due date but within the grace period. Tracked separately from the base fee for cost analysis and to identify patterns of late payment.

columns.name: application_number
columns.description: Official application number assigned by the patent office upon filing (e.g., US16/123456, EP21700001.2, PCT/US2023/012345). Serves as the primary external identifier for tracking prosecution status across jurisdictions.
columns.reference: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1; EPO Rule 41 EPC; PCT Rule 26bis

columns.name: application_type
columns.description: Classification of the patent application by filing type. Utility = standard non-provisional; Provisional = 12-month placeholder; PCT = Patent Cooperation Treaty international; Continuation/Divisional/CIP = derived from parent application. Determines prosecution rules and term calculations. CIP = Continuation-In-Part.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. §§ 111, 119, 120, 121; PCT Article 11; EPO Rule 36 EPC

columns.name: claim_count
columns.description: Total number of claims in the current version of the patent application or granted patent, including independent and dependent claims. Affects official filing fees in many jurisdictions and indicates the breadth of IP protection sought.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 112; 37 CFR 1.75; EPC Rule 43; PCT Rule 6

columns.name: cpc_classification
columns.description: Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) code assigned by USPTO or EPO (e.g., A61K 31/4745). More granular than IPC; used for patent analytics, freedom-to-operate (FTO) searches, and competitive landscape mapping.

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this patent prosecution record was first created in the IP docketing system. Supports audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and SOX compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5(2)

columns.name: examiner_art_unit
columns.description: Patent office art unit or examination division to which the application is assigned (e.g., USPTO Art Unit 1627 for pharmaceutical compositions). Informs prosecution strategy based on art unit allowance rates and examiner tendencies.
columns.reference: USPTO MPEP § 903; EPO Technical Board of Appeal classification

columns.name: examiner_name
columns.description: Name of the patent examiner assigned to the application at the patent office. Used for prosecution strategy planning, examiner history analysis, and interview request management.
columns.reference: USPTO MPEP § 408; EPO Guidelines for Examination Part C

columns.name: expiry_date
columns.description: Calculated date on which the patent expires, typically 20 years from the filing date subject to any patent term extensions (PTE), supplementary protection certificates (SPC), or pediatric exclusivity extensions. Critical for lifecycle management, generic entry forecasting, and LOE (loss of exclusivity) planning.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 154; EPC Article 63; TRIPS Agreement Article 33; 21 CFR Part 60 (PTE)

columns.name: filing_date
columns.description: Date the patent application was officially filed with the patent office. Establishes the priority date for prior art purposes and is the anchor for calculating the 20-year patent term under most jurisdictions. Critical for patent term extension (PTE) and supplementary protection certificate (SPC) calculations.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 111; PCT Article 11; EPC Article 80; TRIPS Agreement Article 33

columns.name: grant_date
columns.description: Date the patent was officially granted by the patent office. Marks the start of enforceable patent rights and triggers the annuity/maintenance fee schedule in most jurisdictions. Null until prosecution_stage = 'granted'.

columns.name: independent_claim_count
columns.description: Number of independent claims in the application or granted patent. Independent claims define the broadest scope of protection and are the primary focus of validity and infringement analyses.

columns.name: invention_type
columns.description: Pharmaceutical classification of the invention being patented. NCE (New Chemical Entity) = novel small molecule; NBE (New Biological Entity) = biologic/biosimilar; formulation = drug product composition; process = manufacturing/synthesis method; method_of_use = therapeutic indication; combination = multi-component therapy. Critical for lifecycle management and generic/biosimilar entry defense strategy.
columns.reference: ICH Q6A/Q6B; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Guideline on Summary of Product Characteristics

columns.name: ipc_classification
columns.description: International Patent Classification (IPC) code assigned to the application (e.g., A61K 31/00 for pharmaceutical preparations). Used for patent landscape analysis, prior art searches, and competitive intelligence. Multiple codes may be stored as a comma-separated string.
columns.reference: WIPO IPC (International Patent Classification) 8th Edition; Strasbourg Agreement 1971

columns.name: last_office_action_date
columns.description: Date of the most recent office action received from the patent office. Used to calculate the statutory response deadline and to trigger docketing alerts for prosecution attorneys.

columns.name: law_firm_name
columns.description: Name of the external patent law firm engaged for prosecution of this application, if applicable. Used for vendor management, cost tracking, and conflict-of-interest monitoring across the IP portfolio.

columns.name: office_action_count
columns.description: Total number of office actions (rejections, objections, or requirements) received from the patent office during prosecution of this application. Indicates prosecution complexity and is used for cost estimation and strategy assessment.
columns.reference: USPTO MPEP Chapter 700; EPO Guidelines for Examination Part C Chapter IV

columns.name: office_action_type
columns.description: Classification of the most recent office action received. Restriction = requirement to elect claims; Non-final = first substantive rejection; Final = final rejection after response; Advisory = after final response; Allowance/Notice of Allowance = claims approved for grant.
columns.reference: USPTO MPEP §§ 706, 821; EPO Guidelines for Examination Part C

columns.name: parent_application_number
columns.description: Application number of the parent patent application from which this application claims priority (applicable for continuation, divisional, or CIP applications). Used to reconstruct the patent family hierarchy and assess claim scope relative to the parent.

columns.name: patent_office_code
columns.description: Two- or three-letter code identifying the national or regional patent office handling the application (e.g., US = USPTO, EP = EPO, JP = JPO/PMDA, CN = CNIPA, WO = WIPO PCT). Drives jurisdiction-specific deadline rules and annuity schedules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: US|EP|JP|CN|WO|GB|DE|FR|CA|AU|IN|KR|BR|MX|RU — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: WIPO ST.3 (Two-letter codes for countries); PCT Rule 4.9

columns.name: payment_confirmation_reference
columns.description: Official confirmation or receipt reference number issued by the patent office or paying agent upon successful annuity fee payment. Serves as proof of payment for audit and compliance purposes.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 41; EPC Article 86; 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records)

columns.name: pct_application_number
columns.description: PCT international application number (e.g., PCT/US2023/012345) if this national/regional application entered the national phase from a PCT filing. Links the national phase application to the international PCT prosecution record.
columns.reference: PCT Article 11; PCT Rule 4.9; WIPO ST.10/C

columns.name: priority_date
columns.description: Earliest claimed priority date for the application, typically the filing date of the first-filed provisional or parent application in the priority chain. Governs prior art cutoff and is used in freedom-to-operate (FTO) analyses and patent validity assessments.
columns.reference: Paris Convention Article 4; PCT Article 8; 35 U.S.C. § 119; EPC Article 87

columns.name: prosecution_stage
columns.description: Current stage of the patent application in the prosecution workflow lifecycle. Drives docketing actions, deadline calculations, and portfolio status reporting. Values: filed, examination, office_action_received, response_submitted, allowance, granted, abandoned. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: filed|examination|office_action_received|response_submitted|allowance|granted|abandoned — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
columns.reference: USPTO MPEP Chapter 700; EPO Guidelines for Examination; 35 U.S.C. § 131–135

columns.name: prosecution_strategy
columns.description: Free-text description of the prosecution strategy adopted for this application, including claim amendment approach, interview strategy, appeal considerations, and alignment with the broader IP lifecycle management plan. Attorney-client privileged content.
columns.reference: USPTO MPEP § 713 (Examiner Interviews); ICH Q10 (Pharmaceutical Quality System)

columns.name: publication_date
columns.description: Date the patent application was published by the patent office, typically 18 months after the earliest priority date. Marks the point at which the application enters the public domain and becomes citable prior art.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 122(b); PCT Rule 48; EPO Rule 68 EPC

columns.name: publication_number
columns.description: Official publication number assigned by the patent office upon publication of the application (e.g., US20230123456A1, WO2023/012345A1). Distinct from the application number; used for public citation and prior art searches.
columns.reference: USPTO 37 CFR 1.211; EPO Rule 68 EPC; WIPO ST.10/C

columns.name: response_deadline
columns.description: Statutory or extended deadline by which a response to the most recent office action must be filed to avoid abandonment. Calculated from last_office_action_date per jurisdiction-specific rules. Critical docketing field — failure to meet this deadline results in application abandonment.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 133; 37 CFR 1.134–1.136; EPC Rule 132; PCT Rule 26

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this patent prosecution record. Used for change tracking, data synchronization with source docketing systems (e.g., Veeva Vault RIM, Anaqua), and audit compliance.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); SOX Section 404

tables.name: patent_term_extension
tables.description: Records all patent term extension and supplementary protection mechanisms across global jurisdictions that compensate for regulatory review time lost during drug approval. Covers US Hatch-Waxman Patent Term Extension (PTE), EU/UK Supplementary Protection Certificates (SPC), Japanese patent term extension, and equivalent national mechanisms. Captures application number, mechanism type (PTE, SPC, national equivalent), filing date, patent reference, product reference, marketing authorization reference, regulatory review period, calculated/granted extension duration, adjusted expiry date, granting authority, decision status, SPC-specific fields (basic patent, product definition per Article 1(b)), and pediatric extension eligibility. Single source of truth for all patent term adjustments — critical for accurate LOE date calculation across all markets.

columns.name: patent_term_extension_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each patent term extension or supplementary protection certificate record in the intellectual property portfolio. Primary key for this entity.

columns.name: country_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: PTEs are jurisdiction-specific; critical for patent expiry forecasting, lifecycle management, and market-specific exclusivity planning in pharmaceutical commercialization.

columns.name: drug_product_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_product. Business justification: PTEs granted for specific approved drug products (formulation-level precision beyond existing medicinal_product_id). Essential for LOE forecasting and regulatory strategy. Removes denormalized inn.

columns.name: drug_substance_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_substance. Business justification: Patent term extensions are granted for the active ingredient (drug substance) that was subject to regulatory review. FDA PTE and EU SPC applications reference the specific drug substance. Regulatory a

columns.name: legal_entity_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: PTE/SPC applications are filed by the Marketing Authorization Holder (a specific legal entity). Legal entity-level IP asset reporting and regulatory submission tracking require this link. No existing

columns.name: masterdata_cost_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: PTE/SPC application costs and associated legal fees are tracked against cost centers for IP budget management and R&D capitalization. IP finance teams require cost-center-level PTE spend reporting. No

columns.name: masterdata_inn_registry_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.inn_registry. Business justification: PTEs and SPCs are granted for specific active substances (INNs). Substance-level exclusivity management and LOE planning require INN linkage. atc_code on patent_term_extension is a classification, not

columns.name: medicinal_product_id
columns.description: Reference to the drug product (Drug Product / Finished Dosage Form) for which the marketing authorization was obtained and which forms the basis of the extension application. Links the extension to the commercial product in the master data.
columns.reference: Internal Master Data Standard; ICH Q6A; FDA 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: patent_id
columns.description: Reference to the underlying base patent record in the IP portfolio for which this term extension or SPC is being sought. Links the extension to the specific patent being extended.

columns.name: adjusted_expiry_date
columns.description: The new patent expiry date after application of the granted term extension or SPC. Calculated as base_patent_expiry_date plus granted_extension_days. This is the Loss of Exclusivity (LOE) date for the product in this jurisdiction and is the primary output used in lifecycle management and generic/biosimilar entry defense strategies.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 156; EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 Art. 13; ICH Q8; FDA Guidance on LOE

columns.name: applicant_delay_days
columns.description: Number of days deducted from the regulatory review period due to delays attributable to the applicant (e.g., failure to respond to FDA requests within the prescribed period). Reduces the calculated extension duration under 35 U.S.C. § 156(c)(1). Tracked for audit and dispute resolution purposes.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 156(c)(1); FDA 21 CFR Part 60.22; USPTO PTE Examination Guidelines

columns.name: application_number
columns.description: The official application number assigned by the granting authority (e.g., USPTO, EPO, UKIPO, JPO) when the patent term extension or SPC application was filed. Serves as the primary external business identifier for tracking the application through the regulatory process.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 156 (US PTE); EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 (SPC); UK Patents Act 1977 s.128B; Japanese Patent Act Art. 67

columns.name: approval_phase_start_date
columns.description: For US PTE calculations: the date on which the regulatory approval phase began, typically the date of NDA/BLA submission to the FDA. Used to calculate the approval phase component of the regulatory review period under 35 U.S.C. § 156(g)(1)(B).
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 156(g)(1)(B); FDA 21 CFR Part 314; FDA 21 CFR Part 60

columns.name: atc_code
columns.description: The WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code assigned to the active substance covered by the extension. Provides standardized classification for cross-portfolio analytics, competitive intelligence, and regulatory reporting.
columns.reference: WHO ATC/DDD Index; EMA Product Information; FDA Orange Book

columns.name: base_patent_expiry_date
columns.description: The original expiry date of the underlying base patent before any term extension or adjustment is applied. Used as the baseline for calculating the adjusted expiry date and the duration of the extension period.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 154; EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 Art. 13; Japanese Patent Act Art. 67

columns.name: base_patent_number
columns.description: The official patent number of the underlying patent for which the term extension or SPC is sought (e.g., US10,123,456 or EP1234567). For SPC purposes, this is the 'basic patent' as defined under Article 1(c) of EU Regulation 469/2009. Retained as a denormalized field for direct reference without joining to the patent table.
columns.reference: EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 Art. 1(c); 35 U.S.C. § 156(f)(2); WIPO ST.9

columns.name: calculated_extension_days
columns.description: The number of days of patent term extension calculated based on the regulatory review period formula. For US PTE: one-half of the testing phase plus the approval phase, capped at 5 years with remaining patent life not exceeding 14 years post-approval. For EU SPC: period between IND filing and MA grant minus 5 years, capped at 5 years.

columns.name: created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this patent term extension record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking in compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.

columns.name: data_exclusivity_expiry_date
columns.description: The date on which regulatory data exclusivity (also known as data protection) expires for the product in this jurisdiction. In the EU, this is 8+2+1 years from first authorization; in the US, 5 years for NCEs or 12 years for biologics. Tracked alongside PTE/SPC to determine the complete exclusivity landscape.

columns.name: decision_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the patent term extension or SPC application. Tracks the application from initial drafting through filing, examination, and final decision by the granting authority. Critical for LOE (Loss of Exclusivity) date calculation and portfolio management. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|filed|under_review|granted|refused|withdrawn|appealed|lapsed|invalidated — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 156; EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009; Veeva Vault RIM

columns.name: external_counsel_reference
columns.description: Reference identifier or name of the external patent law firm or legal counsel managing this patent term extension or SPC application. Used for coordination of legal strategy, correspondence tracking, and matter management. Marked confidential as it reflects privileged legal relationships.
columns.reference: Internal IP Governance Policy; Attorney-Client Privilege

columns.name: filing_date
columns.description: The date on which the patent term extension or SPC application was formally filed with the granting authority. For US PTE, must be filed within 60 days of first marketing approval. For EU SPC, must be filed within 6 months of marketing authorization grant. Critical for determining application validity.

columns.name: grant_date
columns.description: The date on which the granting authority officially granted the patent term extension or SPC. Null if the application has not yet been decided or was refused/withdrawn. Used to confirm the effective start of the extended protection period.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 156; EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009; USPTO; EPO

columns.name: granted_extension_days
columns.description: The actual number of days of patent term extension officially granted by the granting authority. May differ from the calculated extension if the authority applies different determinations of the regulatory review period or applicant delay deductions. Null until the extension is formally granted.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 156; EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 Art. 13; USPTO; EPO

columns.name: granting_authority
columns.description: Name of the national or regional intellectual property office responsible for examining and granting the patent term extension or SPC (e.g., USPTO, EPO, UKIPO, JPO, CIPO, IP Australia). Determines procedural rules and timelines.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 156; EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009; Japanese Patent Act Art. 67; WIPO

columns.name: loe_date
columns.description: The effective Loss of Exclusivity (LOE) date for the product in this jurisdiction, accounting for all applicable exclusivity mechanisms (PTE/SPC, pediatric extension, orphan drug exclusivity, data exclusivity). This is the single most critical date for commercial planning, generic/biosimilar entry defense, and lifecycle management strategy. Represents the date after which generic or biosimilar competition may legally enter the market.
columns.reference: FDA Orange Book; EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009; 35 U.S.C. § 156; ICH Q8; EMA Guidance on Biosimilars

columns.name: marketing_authorization_date
columns.description: The date on which the first marketing authorization for the product was granted in the relevant jurisdiction. This date is critical for calculating the regulatory review period and the permissible extension duration under Hatch-Waxman PTE and EU SPC frameworks.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 156(g); EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 Art. 13; FDA 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: marketing_authorization_number
columns.description: The official marketing authorization number (NDA number, BLA number, EU MA number, or national equivalent) that forms the regulatory basis for the extension application. For EU SPC, this is the first authorization to place the product on the market in the Community per Article 3(b) of Regulation 469/2009.
columns.reference: EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 Art. 3(b); 35 U.S.C. § 156(a)(5)(A); FDA 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: mechanism_type
columns.description: Classification of the patent term extension mechanism. PTE = US Hatch-Waxman Patent Term Extension under 35 U.S.C. § 156; SPC = EU/UK Supplementary Protection Certificate under EC Regulation 469/2009; national_equivalent = country-specific analogous mechanisms (e.g., Japan, Canada, Australia); pediatric_extension = additional 6-month pediatric exclusivity; data_exclusivity = regulatory data protection period. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PTE|SPC|national_equivalent|pediatric_extension|data_exclusivity|regulatory_data_protection — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 156; EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009; Japanese Patent Act Art. 67; ICH E11

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text field for capturing additional context, legal strategy notes, authority correspondence summaries, or other relevant information pertaining to this patent term extension or SPC record that is not captured in structured fields. Used by IP counsel and regulatory affairs teams.

columns.name: opposition_date
columns.description: The date on which a third-party opposition, invalidity action, or equivalent challenge was filed against this patent term extension or SPC. Null if no opposition has been filed. Used to track litigation timelines and coordinate with legal counsel.
columns.reference: EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 Art. 15; EPC Art. 105; 35 U.S.C. § 156

columns.name: opposition_filed
columns.description: Indicates whether a third party (e.g., generic manufacturer, biosimilar applicant) has filed an opposition, invalidity action, or equivalent challenge against this patent term extension or SPC. True triggers escalation to the legal team for litigation management and LOE date reassessment.
columns.reference: EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 Art. 15; 35 U.S.C. § 156; EPC Art. 105; CJEU SPC litigation precedents

columns.name: orphan_drug_exclusivity
columns.description: Indicates whether the product covered by this extension also benefits from orphan drug exclusivity (7 years in the US under the Orphan Drug Act, 10 years in the EU under Regulation (EC) No 141/2000). Used in conjunction with PTE/SPC to determine the effective exclusivity cliff date.
columns.reference: 21 U.S.C. § 360cc (Orphan Drug Act); EU Regulation (EC) No 141/2000; FDA Office of Orphan Products Development

columns.name: pediatric_extension_eligible
columns.description: Indicates whether this patent term extension or SPC is eligible for an additional 6-month pediatric extension under the US Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA) or EU Paediatric Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006. True if a Written Request (US) or Paediatric Investigation Plan (EU) has been completed and accepted.
columns.reference: 21 U.S.C. § 505A (BPCA); EU Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006 Art. 36; FDA Pediatric Exclusivity Guidance

columns.name: pediatric_extension_granted
columns.description: Indicates whether the additional 6-month pediatric extension has been formally granted on top of the base PTE or SPC. Distinct from eligibility — this flag confirms the authority has approved the pediatric supplement. When True, the adjusted_expiry_date should reflect the additional 6 months.
columns.reference: 21 U.S.C. § 505A; EU Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006 Art. 36; FDA Orange Book

columns.name: regulatory_review_period_days
columns.description: The total number of days of the regulatory review period as determined by the granting authority. For US PTE, this is the period from IND filing to NDA/BLA approval, reduced by any applicant-caused delays. Directly determines the maximum permissible extension duration under 35 U.S.C. § 156.
columns.reference: 35 U.S.C. § 156(g); FDA 21 CFR Part 60; EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 Art. 13

columns.name: spc_product_definition
columns.description: For EU/UK SPC applications only: the definition of the 'product' as per Article 1(b) of EU Regulation 469/2009, specifying the active ingredient or combination of active ingredients of a medicinal product. This definition determines the scope of SPC protection and is critical for freedom-to-operate analyses and generic entry defense.

'Delisted' indicates the NDA holder has removed the listing. 'Withdrawn' indicates FDA-initiated removal. 'Pending' indicates submission under review. 'Corrected' indicates an amendment was filed.

columns.name: litigation_status

Tracks whether litigation is active, settled, or resolved by court judgment. Informs LOE risk assessment and legal strategy. 'US' for FDA Orange Book; 'EU' for EMA Article 10 reference product listing; 'UK' for MHRA; 'JP' for PMDA; 'CN' for NMPA. Enables multi-market IP portfolio management. columns.name: nda_number

columns.name: orphan_drug_designation_flag

columns.name: paragraph_iv_date
columns.description: Date on which the first Paragraph IV certification was received by the NDA holder for this listed patent. Initiates the 45-day window to file patent infringement suit and triggers the 30-month stay clock if suit is filed.

columns.name: paragraph_iv_flag

columns.name: patent_expiry_date
columns.description: Date on which the listed patent expires as published in the FDA Orange Book. This date directly governs the earliest date a generic applicant may receive final approval absent a Paragraph IV challenge or court ruling.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.53; Hatch-Waxman Act; FDA Orange Book

columns.name: patent_type
columns.description: Classification of the listed patent as covering the drug substance (active ingredient), drug product (formulation/composition), or method of use. Determines the nature of Paragraph IV challenges and carve-out labeling strategies.

columns.name: patent_use_code

columns.name: pediatric_exclusivity_flag

columns.name: reference_listed_drug_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether this NDA product is designated as the Reference Listed Drug (RLD) against which ANDA applicants must demonstrate bioequivalence. True if the product is the RLD; False if it is a non-RLD listed product.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.3; FDA Orange Book RLD Designation; Hatch-Waxman Act

columns.name: rems_flag

columns.description: Indicates whether the listed drug product is subject to an FDA-approved Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). REMS requirements may affect generic applicant ability to demonstrate shared REMS compliance, impacting generic entry timelines.
columns.reference: 21 U.S.C. § 355-1 (REMS); FDA REMS Database; 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: route_of_administration
columns.description: Route by which the drug product is administered (e.g., oral, intravenous, topical, subcutaneous). Used in therapeutic equivalence evaluations and generic entry assessments. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intramuscular|topical|inhalation|transdermal|ophthalmic — promote to reference product]
columns.reference: FDA Orange Book; ICH M4 (CTD); 21 CFR Part 314

columns.name: spc_expiry_date
columns.description: Date on which the Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC) expires in the relevant EU/UK jurisdiction. Represents the effective end of patent-based market protection for the listed product in that market.

columns.name: spc_number
columns.description: Reference number of the Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC) granted in EU/UK jurisdictions to extend patent protection beyond the standard 20-year term for medicinal products. Applicable for EU and UK market listings; null for US Orange Book entries.
columns.reference: EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 (SPC for Medicinal Products); MHRA SPC Guidance

columns.name: strength
columns.description: Labeled strength of the drug product as listed in the Orange Book (e.g., '10 mg', '500 mg/5 mL'). Strength is a key differentiator for therapeutic equivalence and generic substitution eligibility.

columns.name: submission_date
columns.description: Date on which the NDA holder submitted the patent or exclusivity information to the FDA for Orange Book listing. Must occur within 30 days of NDA approval or patent grant per 21 CFR Part 314.53(d).

columns.name: therapeutic_equivalence_code

'A' codes indicate therapeutically equivalent to the RLD; 'B' codes indicate not therapeutically equivalent. Drives pharmacy substitution decisions and formulary management.

columns.name: thirty_month_stay_expiry_date
columns.description: Date on which the 30-month stay of ANDA approval expires following a timely-filed patent infringement suit in response to a Paragraph IV certification. After this date, FDA may grant final ANDA approval regardless of ongoing litigation outcome.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 314.107(b)(3); Hatch-Waxman Act Section 505(j)(5)(B)(iii); FDA Orange Book

columns.name: updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this Orange Book listing record was last modified in the data product. Supports change tracking, audit compliance under 21 CFR Part 11, and Silver Layer data freshness monitoring.
columns.reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); ICH Q10

columns.name: veeva_vault_doc_reference

tables.name: licensed_patent_schedule
tables.description: This association product represents the Contract between licensing_agreement and patent. It captures the formal schedule of intellectual property assets covered under each licensing agreement, recording the specific patents licensed, the per-patent royalty rate, the scope of licensed claims, exclusivity type, and sublicensing rights for each patent-agreement combination. Each record links one licensing_agreement to one patent with attributes that exist only in the context of this contractual relationship — they cannot reside on the agreement (which spans multiple patents) nor on the patent (which may be licensed under multiple agreements with different terms).. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical IP management, a single licensing agreement routinely covers a portfolio of multiple patents (e.g., a composition-of-matter patent plus a method-of-use patent plus a formulation patent), and a single patent can be licensed under multiple separate agreements to different licensees in different territories or fields of use. The business actively manages this relationship as a 'Licensed Patent Schedule' — a formal exhibit attached to every licensing agreement that lists each covered patent with its own royalty rate, effective dates, and exclusivity scope. This is not an analytical correlation; it is an operationally managed, legally binding schedule that deal managers create, amend, and terminate throughout the agreement lifecycle.

columns.name: licensed_patent_schedule_id
columns.glossary_term: Licensed Patent Schedule - Licensed Patent Schedule Id
columns.description: Primary key for the licensed_patent_schedule association

columns.name: licensing_agreement_id
columns.glossary_term: Licensed Patent Schedule - Licensing Agreement Id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to the licensing agreement under which this patent is licensed. Identifies the deal, parties, territory, and financial terms governing this patent's inclusion.

columns.name: patent_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to the specific patent covered under this licensing agreement. Identifies the IP asset whose rights are being granted.

columns.name: effective_date
columns.description: Date on which this specific patent's coverage under the licensing agreement becomes operative. May differ from the agreement's overall effective_date when patents are added to an existing agreement via amendment (e.g., a continuation patent granted after deal signing is added to the schedule mid-term).

columns.name: exclusivity_type
columns.description: Scope of exclusivity granted for this specific patent under this agreement. A single licensing agreement may grant exclusive rights to one patent and non-exclusive rights to another in the same schedule. Cannot reside on licensing_agreement (which captures overall deal exclusivity) or on patent (which may be licensed exclusively to one partner and non-exclusively to another).

columns.name: expiry_date
columns.description: Date on which this patent's coverage under the agreement terminates. May be driven by the patent's own expiry, the agreement's expiry, or a negotiated earlier termination for this specific patent. Enables LOE planning at the patent-agreement intersection level.

columns.name: licensed_scope
columns.description: Narrative or structured description of which patent claims, fields of use, or indications are licensed under this agreement for this specific patent. A patent may be partially licensed (e.g., only method-of-use claims, not composition claims). Cannot reside on the agreement (varies per patent) or on the patent (varies per agreement).

columns.name: royalty_rate_per_patent
columns.description: The royalty rate (expressed as a percentage of net sales or a fixed per-unit amount) applicable specifically to this patent under this agreement. In multi-patent deals, individual patents may carry different royalty rates reflecting their relative commercial importance. Cannot reside on licensing_agreement (which may aggregate rates) or on patent (which may be licensed at different rates to different partners).

columns.name: schedule_status
columns.description: Current lifecycle status of this patent's inclusion in the licensed patent schedule. Supports tracking of patents added, removed, or suspended from coverage during the agreement term without requiring deletion of the historical record.

columns.name: sublicensing_permitted
columns.description: Indicates whether the licensee is contractually permitted to sublicense this specific patent to third parties under this agreement. Sublicensing rights may be granted for some patents in a schedule but not others, particularly where the licensor retains tighter control over foundational composition-of-matter patents.

domains.name: finance
domains.description: Owns enterprise financial data including general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, cost accounting, budgeting, R&D capitalization, COGS by product, royalty accounting, and SOX-compliant financial reporting. Integrates with SAP FI/CO modules. Supports P&L by therapeutic area, brand, and geography, return on investment (ROI) for R&D programs, and capital expenditure tracking.

tables.name: general_ledger
tables.description: Central repository for all financial accounting entries across the enterprise, representing the authoritative chart of accounts, account balances, and period-end ledger positions. Captures account master data (account number, account type, account group, currency), period balances (opening, debit totals, credit totals, closing balance by period), company code, profit center allocations, cost center references, and currency translations as sourced from SAP FI module. Serves as SSOT for trial balance, balance sheet, income statement, and SOX-compliant period-end close processes across all legal entities in the pharmaceutical group. Supports consolidation eliminations, multi-GAAP reporting (US GAAP and IFRS), and financial close status tracking. Does NOT own individual postings (owned by journal_entry) — owns aggregate balances and account structure.

columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.profit_center. Business justification: GL accounts are assigned to profit centers for segment P&L reporting by therapeutic area in pharma. The plain profit_center column is a denormalized code; proper FK enables segment reporting and manag

columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module — Table T077S; US GAAP ASC 730 (R&D); IFRS IAS 38

columns.description: Current lifecycle status of the GL account master record: active (postings allowed), blocked (postings temporarily prevented), or marked_for_deletion (pending archival). Supports SOX-compliant account master data governance.

columns.description: Identifier for the chart of accounts framework applied to this GL account (e.g., 'INT1' for international, 'USGP' for US GAAP). Supports multi-GAAP reporting across the pharmaceutical group.

columns.name: group_currency_code

columns.name: intercompany_flag

columns.name: last_posted_date
columns.description: The most recent date on which a journal entry posting was made to this GL account within the fiscal period. Used for account activity monitoring, dormant account identification, and period-end close validation.

columns.name: opening_balance
columns.description: The GL account balance at the start of the fiscal period in transaction currency. Represents the carried-forward closing balance from the prior period. Used in trial balance preparation and period-end close processes.

columns.name: period_close_status

Supports SOX-compliant financial close tracking.

columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module — Table SKB1 field XSPEB; SOX Section 404

columns.name: rd_capitalization_flag
columns.description: Indicates whether the GL account balance is subject to R&D capitalization rules under IFRS IAS 38 (True) or expensed as incurred under US GAAP ASC 730 (False). Critical for pharmaceutical companies managing the boundary between R&D expense and intangible asset capitalization.
columns.reference: IFRS IAS 38 Intangible Assets; US GAAP ASC 730 Research and Development; SOX Section 404

columns.name: recon_account_type
columns.description: Indicates if this GL account is a reconciliation account and its type: D=Accounts Receivable (Customers), K=Accounts Payable (Vendors), A=Assets, or empty for non-reconciliation accounts. Reconciliation accounts aggregate subledger balances into the GL.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module — Table SKB1 field MITKZ; US GAAP ASC 210; IFRS IAS 1

columns.name: record_created_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this GL account balance record was first created in the Silver layer data product. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and SOX-compliant record-keeping requirements.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 302/404; 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: record_updated_timestamp
columns.description: Timestamp when this GL account balance record was last modified in the Silver layer data product. Supports incremental data loading, change tracking, and SOX-compliant audit trail requirements.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 302/404; 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records; GDPR Article 5

columns.name: segment
columns.description: Segment identifier for IFRS 8 / ASC 280 segment reporting (e.g., 'Oncology', 'Immunology', 'Rare Disease', 'Consumer Health'). Enables disaggregated P&L and asset reporting by operating segment for external financial disclosures.
columns.reference: IFRS 8 Operating Segments; US GAAP ASC 280; SAP S/4HANA FI-GL Segment

columns.name: sox_relevant
columns.description: Indicates whether this GL account is in scope for SOX Section 302/404 internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR). SOX-relevant accounts require documented controls, testing, and sign-off during the annual audit cycle.
columns.reference: SOX Section 302 and 404; PCAOB AS 2201; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

columns.name: tax_code
columns.description: SAP tax code associated with the GL account for VAT/GST and withholding tax determination. Relevant for pharmaceutical entities operating across multiple tax jurisdictions. Supports indirect tax reporting and compliance.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-TX Module; IFRS IAS 12 Income Taxes; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: trading_partner
columns.description: Company code of the intercompany trading partner for balances involving intercompany transactions. Used to identify and eliminate intercompany balances during group consolidation. Populated only when intercompany_flag is True.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-GL Intercompany — Table FAGLFLEXT field RASSC; IFRS 10; US GAAP ASC 810

tables.name: journal_entry
tables.description: Individual accounting transactions posted to the general ledger with full header and line-item detail, including tax-specific postings. Header captures posting date, document type, reference number, fiscal year/period, currency, and posting user. Line items capture GL account, cost center, profit center, debit/credit amounts in transaction and local currency, tax code, tax jurisdiction, taxable base amount, tax amount, withholding tax, assignment field, and line item text. Encompasses all subledger postings (AP, AR, asset, tax) and manual adjustments. Tax postings carry additional attributes: tax jurisdiction, tax return reference, VAT/sales tax/deferred tax classification, and indirect tax reporting period for multi-jurisdiction compliance. Supports audit trails required under SOX and 21 CFR Part 11, financial close processes, and granular P&L analysis by therapeutic area, brand, and geography.
tables.reference: SAP FI Journal Entry / Accounting Document

columns.name: journal_entry_id
columns.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each journal entry record in the general ledger. Primary key for the journal_entry data product in the Databricks Silver Layer.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; 21 CFR Part 11; SOX Section 302/404

columns.name: accounts_payable_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.accounts_payable. Business justification: Journal entries generated by AP postings should reference the source AP document. This is a nullable FK since not all journal entries are AP-related. Strengthens accounts_payable connections to journa

columns.name: cost_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: Cost center on journal entries drives R&D capitalization decisions, overhead absorption, and pharma program cost reporting. The plain cost_center column is denormalized; FK enables cost center hierarc

columns.name: fixed_asset_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: Journal entries related to fixed asset transactions (acquisition, depreciation, disposal, impairment) should reference the specific asset. This is a nullable FK since not all journal entries are asset

columns.name: general_ledger_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: Journal entries post to specific GL accounts. Each JE line item must reference the GL account it impacts. The existing gl_account field is a STRING code; adding general_ledger_id establishes the prope

columns.name: internal_order_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Journal entries that charge costs to internal orders should reference the internal order. This is a nullable FK since not all journal entries are internal-order-related. Connects internal_order to jou

columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.invoice. Business justification: Invoice posting in SAP FI creates journal entries. Linking journal_entry to invoice provides direct traceability from accounting transactions to the originating invoice document. This supports revenue

columns.name: legal_entity_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Journal entries are posted within a legal entity for statutory reporting, intercompany elimination, and tax filing. Pharma companies post entries across multiple legal entities; this FK is required fo

columns.name: payment_run_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.payment_run. Business justification: Payment runs in SAP FI generate clearing journal entries when vendor payments are executed. Linking journal_entry to payment_run enables reconciliation between payment execution records and the result

columns.name: profit_center_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.profit_center. Business justification: Profit center on journal entries is required for segment P&L reporting by therapeutic area and product line. The plain profit_center column is denormalized; FK enables management reporting and IFRS 8

columns.name: royalty_agreement_id
columns.description: Foreign key linking to finance.royalty_agreement. Business justification: Journal entries are posted for royalty accruals, royalty payments, and sublicense fee recognition. Linking journal_entry directly to royalty_agreement enables traceability from individual accounting t

columns.name: amount_group_currency
columns.description: Monetary amount of the journal entry translated into the corporate group reporting currency (typically USD or EUR) for consolidated P&L reporting by therapeutic area, brand, and geography.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IFRS 10; IAS 21; SOX Section 302

columns.name: amount_local_currency
columns.description: Monetary amount of the journal entry translated into the company code's local (functional) currency using the applicable exchange rate. Used for statutory financial reporting and local tax compliance.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IAS 21; IFRS; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: amount_transaction_currency
columns.description: Gross monetary amount of the journal entry in the original transaction currency. For debit entries this is positive; for credit entries this is negative (SAP sign convention). Core monetary fact for the posting.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IAS 21; IFRS 15; SOX Section 404

columns.name: assignment_field
columns.description: SAP assignment field (ZUONR) used for sorting and matching open items in accounts payable, accounts receivable, and bank reconciliation. Typically populated with invoice number, payment reference, or contract number for automated clearing.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 404

columns.name: business_area
columns.description: SAP business area code representing an organizational unit for which an internal balance sheet and P&L can be drawn up. Used for segment reporting across geographies and therapeutic areas.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IFRS 8; US GAAP ASC 280

columns.name: company_code
columns.description: SAP company code identifying the legal entity for which the journal entry is posted. Enables P&L reporting by legal entity and supports multi-entity consolidation across the pharmaceutical group.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements; SOX Section 302

columns.name: debit_credit_indicator
columns.description: SAP indicator specifying whether the line item is a debit (S=Soll/Debit) or credit (H=Haben/Credit) posting. Fundamental double-entry bookkeeping attribute required for GL balance validation and trial balance generation.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IFRS; US GAAP; Double-Entry Bookkeeping Principles

columns.name: document_date
columns.description: The date of the original source document (invoice date, payment date, contract date) that triggered the journal entry. May differ from posting_date; used for aging analysis and vendor/customer terms calculation.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IAS 1; IFRS 15

columns.name: document_number
columns.description: SAP-assigned unique accounting document number within the company code and fiscal year. Serves as the externally-known business identifier for the journal entry, used in audit trails and reconciliation.
columns.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 404; 21 CFR Part 11

columns.name: document_type
